Users may need to manually locate and add files that are already open, making the PDF combining workflow less efficient.

title: Zoom level resets when opening or switching to another PDF
author: ravindusp
body:
PDFCraft does not retain the user's previously selected zoom level when viewing another PDF document.

When a user adjusts the zoom to a preferred level and opens another document, the application does not remember that preference.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open a PDF document in PDFCraft.
2. Change the zoom level to a custom value (e.g., 125% or 150%).
3. Open another PDF document.
4. Observe the zoom level of the newly opened document.

### Expected Behavior
PDFCraft should remember the user's last selected zoom level and apply it when opening another document.

Ideally, the application could also provide an option to choose between:
- **Remember last used zoom:** Apply the last selected zoom level to newly opened documents.
- **Default zoom:** Always open PDFs at a predefined zoom level (e.g., Fit Width, Fit Page, or 100%).

### Actual Behavior
The previously selected zoom level is not retained when viewing another PDF, requiring the user to adjust it again.

### Additional Information
- **Platform:** macOS 27.0.1
- **Feature:** PDF Viewer → Zoom
- **Frequency:** Reproducible when opening another document

### Impact
Users who regularly work with multiple PDFs must repeatedly adjust their zoom level, disrupting the document viewing workflow.

title: Prompt before opening absolute local paths from GoToR PDF links
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

PdfCraft currently supports local PDF `GoToR` links, including targets specified using absolute filesystem paths.

For absolute local paths, PdfCraft should require explicit user confirmation before opening the target file.

This would better match Adobe Acrobat/Reader’s security behavior, where links that attempt to access local filesystem locations can trigger a warning asking the user to allow or block the action.

## Background

Support for opening local `GoToR` PDF links was added in #1265.

The implementation currently accepts both relative and absolute local paths, subject to the existing file validation and safety checks.

One remaining security/UX question from #1265 was whether absolute paths should require confirmation before they are opened.

An absolute path can point anywhere accessible to the current user, for example:

- `/Users/alice/Documents/private.pdf`
- `/home/alice/private.pdf`
- `C:\Users\Alice\Documents\private.pdf`
- a local or mounted filesystem location

Allowing an untrusted PDF to silently follow such a path is more security-sensitive than resolving a relative link beside the source document.

Adobe Acrobat/Reader treats local filesystem access as a potentially sensitive operation and may display a warning asking the user to explicitly allow or block access.

PdfCraft should adopt similar behavior for absolute-path `GoToR` targets.

## Proposed behavior

When the user clicks a `GoToR` link whose target resolves to an absolute local filesystem path, PdfCraft should display a confirmation prompt before opening the target.

The prompt should clearly show the destination path and allow the user to choose whether to continue.

Example:

> This document is trying to open a local file:
>
> `/Users/alice/Documents/target.pdf`
>
> Do you want to allow this?

Possible actions:

- **Open / Allow**
- **Cancel / Block**

If the user cancels, the source PDF should remain open and unchanged.

## Relative paths

Relative `GoToR` paths that …

title: M12: Auto-tag PDFs with a reviewable structure proposal
author: earlvanze
body:
## Goal
Create real PDF structure tags for untagged PDFs in PdfCraft's Rust engine, with a headless tool and a reviewable UI action. This is the missing core behind `a11y.autotag` and the guided remediation workflow in #1202. The visual Tags panel remains #982.

## Scope
- Build a valid `/StructTreeRoot`, `/ParentTree`, `/MarkInfo`, page `/StructParents`, marked-content IDs, and parent links. Preserve visible page content and existing annotations, forms, links, and metadata.
- Classify text runs into paragraphs and candidate headings using layout evidence; detect lists, tables, and figures only when evidence is strong enough. Ambiguous items must be marked for review, not silently assigned confident semantics. Expose proposed tags and confidence/review reasons before applying.
- Keep reading order explicit and editable through the existing tag-order API. Let users correct tag type, heading level, figure alt text, and decorative status after applying.
- For scanned pages, run the existing local OCR path first only with user authorization. Do not invent alt text. Optional local AI descriptions belong in a later reviewed step.
- Never report accessibility compliance based on auto-tagging alone. Run the checker afterward and retain manual findings.

## Delivery
1. Engine API with bounded parsing, cycle-safe object walks, and atomic failure behavior on malformed PDFs.
2. `accessibility_autotag_preview` and `accessibility_autotag_apply` automation tools, including an end-to-end synthetic PDF test.
3. GUI preview/apply action and visual review handoff to #982 and #1202.
4. Update `parity/acrobat-features.toml`, roadmap and gap status with exact shipped scope.

- Synthetic multi-page PDF with headings, paragraphs, a list, a table, an image, and an untagged annotation keeps its rendered appearance. Its tag tree, marked content, parent tree and reading order validate after save/reopen; checker findings improve without false passes.

title: Proposal: open-licence document fonts for non-Latin scripts (Thai first): Sarabun, Edit text fallback, ToUnicode fix
author: POBIM
body:
## Summary

Several open issues report the same underlying gap for Thai (#398, #1379, #420, #218, #664, #440, #1035, #506). Users can't edit Thai text in existing PDFs. They can't choose a Thai font, and they see tofu boxes when craft-fonts is missing. I tested a prototype locally and the approach below works. I'm proposing it as a general pattern for **document fonts in non-Latin scripts**, with Thai as the first case.

## What fails today (main @ 84a75ea, built with craft-fonts)

To reproduce, print a short Thai HTML page in Tahoma to PDF with Edge or Chrome; Word exports behave the same way.

- **Edit text on Thai.** The edit fails with `complex text needs the complete source TrueType/OpenType face; load that font before editing`. The v0.6 release instead says `the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+0E37`. Word and Edge embed Thai as Identity-H subsets that can't be shaped, and the only Type 3 fallback faces are Japanese and Hebrew. "Load font…" doesn't help, because the common Thai document fonts (Angsana, Cordia, Tahoma, Leelawadee, TH Sarabun PSK/New) are not openly licensed.
- **Add Text font menu.** It offers only Helvetica, Times and Courier. Thai uses Noto Sans Thai regular, with no bold or italic.
- **Search and copy after a shaped edit.** `embedding::embed_mapping` writes `<cid> <>` (an empty destination) for mark glyphs that share their letter's cluster. Readers then drop the whole ToUnicode map, so an edited Thai line with tone or vowel marks can no longer be searched or copied. Lines without marks still work.
- **Reading Thai PDFs from Word or Edge.** The render text extractor returns broken mark order, for example `ชอืโครงการ` for `ชื่อโครงการ`. The Edit text reader gets it right.

## Proposed approach

### 1. craft-fonts: add static, OFL document faces per script

- For Thai, add **Sarabun** (Cadson Demak, OFL-1.1) in Regular, Bold, Italic and Bold Italic, from [google/fonts@88058c7](https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/88058c714073e72bb…

### What happens
`text_edit` on a paragraph set in an embedded TrueType font (Type0 / Identity-H) always swaps the font for a standard 14 substitute (Helvetica, Helvetica-Bold or Times-Roman). This happens even when the new text only **deletes** characters, so every glyph it needs is already in the embedded font. It happens with both subset and fully embedded fonts.

The tool's own description says *"Its own font is reused when it can show every character; otherwise the line is set in Helvetica"*, so I expected the original font to be kept here.

Side effect: the substitute has different metrics, so the paragraph rewraps. On a real designed document, a 2-line, 40 pt title became 3 lines in Helvetica-Bold and overlapped the paragraph below it, even though the edit only deleted text.

Most PDFs exported from Word, InDesign, Chrome or Typst embed TrueType/OpenType as Type0 Identity-H, so in practice almost any edit to a real document changes its typeface.

Hello,

**Error details:**

```text
Faulting application name: pdfcraft.exe
Faulting application version: 0.6.0.0
Faulting module name: nvdxgiwrapx.dll
Faulting module version: 10.18.13.5362
Exception code: 0xc0000005

Application path: C:\Program Files\PdfCraft\pdfcraft.exe

The exception code `0xc0000005` indicates an access violation.

title: Support for CAdES-signed PDFs (.pdf.p7m): file is opened as "broken" and repaired
author: flavioleggio
body:
### Description

When I open a CAdES-signed PDF (.pdf.p7m), PdfCraft reports that the file is broken and repairs it. A .p7m file is a CMS/PKCS#7 envelope (DER-encoded) that contains the original PDF together with the signature and the signer's certificates. This format is widely used in Italy for legally binding digital signatures (firma digitale).

### Repair details reported

The top alert bar presented a "Details" button that opens the Advanced tab of document properties. In the footer of the dialog we have the following repair details.

> xref at 23080 unreadable (syntax error at byte 23080: expected object header); retrying relative to the header

My guess is that PdfCraft parses the envelope as if it were a plain PDF. The PDF is found inside it, but the CMS data that follows (signature, certificates) stops the parser from finding startxref, so the cross-reference table gets rebuilt.

### Steps to reproduce

A test file can be generated from any PDF with OpenSSL (3.0 or later):

1. Create a throwaway self-signed certificate

```shell
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -subj "/CN=PdfCraft Test" -days 1
```

2. Wrap any PDF in a CAdES-BES attached signature (DER-encoded .p7m)

```shell
openssl cms -sign -binary -nodetach -cades -md sha256 \
    -in test.pdf -signer cert.pem -inkey key.pem \
    -outform DER -out test.pdf.p7m
```

3. (Optional) Check that the embedded PDF can be extracted intact
```shell
openssl cms -verify -noverify -inform DER -in test.pdf.p7m -out extracted.pdf
cmp test.pdf extracted.pdf && echo "identical"
```

Then open test.pdf.p7m in PdfCraft. The file is reported as broken and repaired, with a message like the one below (the byte offset depends on the file):

> cross-reference data unreadable (syntax error at byte NNNNN: no startxref); rebuilding from object headers
> rebuilt cross-reference index from NN object headers

The same happens with real .p7m files produced by Italian qualified signature tools…

title: Windows: a PDF path passed unquoted with spaces doesn't open (Acrobat opens it)
author: magdale76
body:
**What happens.** Some Windows programs (office/practice-management software with a "PDF reader command line" setting) start the reader with the file path unquoted:

```
"C:\Program Files\PdfCraft\pdfcraft.exe" P:\Archive\00042A26 Contract.PDF
```

Windows splits that into two arguments, `P:\Archive\00042A26` and `Contract.PDF`. Neither exists, so PdfCraft shows "Couldn't read 00042A26: … (os error 2)" and opens nothing. With such a program's "open all PDFs" button, only the files without spaces in their names open.

**Expected.** The file opens. Acrobat accepts this command line, so users switching the setting from Acrobat to PdfCraft hit it straight away; the program's setting has no way to add quotes.

**Seen on** Windows 11, PdfCraft 0.6.0 installed with the MSI. The file association itself is fine (`"%1"` is quoted); this only affects programs that build the command line themselves.

**Workaround until fixed:** point the program at a one-line batch file, `@start "" "C:\Program Files\PdfCraft\pdfcraft.exe" "%*"`.

**Proposed fix:** when an argument names no file but it and the following arguments, joined with a space, name an existing file, rejoin them (longest run first). Everything else is kept as given. PR follows.

title: Windows Explorer: create one PDF from multiple selected images
author: KevinAR-18
body:
The Windows MSI already registers “Create PDF with PdfCraft…” for supported
image types, but it currently uses `MultiSelectModel=Single`, so it is only
available for one image at a time.

Requested behaviour:
- Select one or multiple supported images in Windows File Explorer.
- Choose “Create PDF with PdfCraft…”.
- PdfCraft receives the entire selection as one create-from-images job.
- The existing DPI chooser is shown once.
- The result is one unsaved PDF with one page per image.
- Original image files remain unchanged.

A registry-only `MultiSelectModel=Player` change is not sufficient: for a
legacy command verb Explorer still invokes the command per selected file,
rather than passing one complete selection. We likely need a Shell/COM command
handler or a deliberately designed launcher/IPC mechanism.

Questions:
1. Is a Windows Shell/COM handler acceptable for this project?
2. If yes, is there a preferred safe Rust wrapper/library?
3. Should the first implementation target the legacy “Show more options” menu
   only, or the Windows 11 first-level context menu as well?

title: Render: Type 3 glyphs are drawn bold under text rendering mode 2 (fill + stroke), although the rendering mode has no effect on Type 3 fonts
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
## Summary
Pages that set `2 Tr` before showing text in a Type 3 font render visibly bolder in PdfCraft than in poppler. Print-stream PDFs do this routinely: a bank statement produced by "303l Linux" (Ricoh Production Print) sets `2 Tr` for all 149 text runs of its Type 3 bitmap font, and the whole page looks semi-bold in PdfCraft 0.5.0 and 0.6.0. ISO 32000-1 §9.3.6: "The text rendering mode shall have no effect on text displayed in a Type 3 font." title: Large documentation PDFs: text_find retains an unbounded PageText cache and discards partial results when page text extraction fails
author: cyfung1031
body:
## Summary

PdfCraft's automation text path keeps extracted `PageText` objects in a per-document cache with no byte, page-count, or LRU budget.

This is useful for repeated text operations, but on large documents the retained cache can grow with every page touched during the lifetime of the current document version. An exhaustive search, a late-match search, or repeated searches across different parts of a large document can therefore retain text and glyph geometry for a substantial part of the document even after those pages are no longer needed.

There is a separate robustness problem in the same path: if text extraction fails for one page that a search reaches, `page_texts` returns an error and `text_find` aborts the entire call. Matches already found on readable pages are not returned, and there is no machine-readable page-level warning or partial-result state.

These two behaviors are especially relevant for large technical manuals and imperfect PDFs, where automation clients need both bounded memory use and useful partial search results.

Audited against current `main`:

```text

```

  - `page_texts`
  - `text_find`

- `crates/automation/src/tools.rs`

title: Comments and editing improvements and bugs (detailed suggestions)
author: geckolinux
body: Hi there, first of all thanks for PdfCraft. As a Linux user who is extremely dependent on PDFs, this app in my opinion fills one of the most important gaps in functionality for Linux on the desktop. The biggest limitation by far of current PDF viewers for Linux are the limited and clunky commenting options (text boxes, arrows, text callouts, ped/pencil scribbling, typewriter text, watermarks, pasted images, etc.) Currently I think PDF-XChange Editor running on Wine is still the best option, but it looks like PdfCraft is already viable as an alternative in many situations. Here are some suggestions and issues based on my testing thus far: ### Text boxes - Inline editing a text box would be much better, instead of a popup editing field. - Font style settings are missing for text boxes. - No border thickness/color/style controls are available. ---------------- - In addition to text boxes, a "typewriter" function for adding quick text anywhere with no bounding boxes would also be useful. It appears this was attempted to be implemented here, but it has the same limitations as described above, and doesn't seem to be much different from a text box. ### Arrows and text callouts - Rotation does not seem to be possible. - Arrows and text callouts do not allow for rotating or changing their length/angle after creation.

title: Faux-redaction audit misses covers drawn as a rectangle path (m/l/h + f) instead of `re`
author: Mart95Dev
body:
## Summary

`pdfcraft-cli audit` (and `doc_audit_redactions`) reports a faux redaction when the opaque cover is drawn with the `re` operator, but reports nothing when the same rectangle is drawn as a closed path (`m`/`l`/`h` + `f`). The covered text is still extractable in both cases.

Rectangles drawn as paths are common in real files. For example, VectorCraft exports its rectangle shapes this way (`55 140 m 415 140 l 415 168 l 55 168 l 55 140 l h f`), so a "redaction" made in VectorCraft and exported to PDF passes PdfCraft's audit.

`crates/audit/src/cover.rs` documents arbitrary filled paths as out of scope, so this is a known limitation. An axis-aligned rectangle path is the same shape as `re`, though, so it seems worth covering.

## Reproduction

Two one-page PDFs with identical text (`SECRET-12345`, Helvetica 14 pt at 20,45) and an identical black cover. Only the fill operator differs.

`cover-re.pdf` content stream:
```
BT /F1 14 Tf 20 45 Td (SECRET-12345) Tj ET
0 0 0 rg
15 38 140 24 re f
```

`cover-path.pdf` content stream:
```
BT /F1 14 Tf 20 45 Td (SECRET-12345) Tj ET
0 0 0 rg
15 38 m 155 38 l 155 62 l 15 62 l h f
```

```
$ pdftotext cover-re.pdf -     →  SECRET-12345
$ pdftotext cover-path.pdf -   →  SECRET-12345

$ pdfcraft-cli audit cover-re.pdf
{"count":1,"findings":[{"covered_text":"SECRET-12345","kind":"covered-text","page":1,"rect":[15.0,38.0,155.0,62.0]}]}

$ pdfcraft-cli audit cover-path.pdf
{"count":0,"findings":[]}
```

title: [Feature Request] Add a non-destructive background color and inversion mode for PDF reading
author: brunoteixeira042
body:

The current background customization feature is useful for improving visual comfort when reading PDF documents. However, changing the background through document editing may permanently alter the document's appearance.

This can be undesirable when users simply want a darker background or different colors for comfortable reading without modifying the original file.

Some PDF viewers provide a reading mode that applies color transformations only during rendering, preserving the original document.

Proposed Solution

Introduce a non-destructive reading mode that allows users to customize or invert PDF colors temporarily, without modifying the underlying document.

Potential features include:

Reading mode: Apply color transformations only to the displayed PDF.
Color inversion: Support dark backgrounds with light text for improved readability in low-light environments.
Alternative color schemes: Optionally provide sepia, grayscale, or customizable background and text colors.
Quick toggle: Allow users to enable or disable the reading mode at any time.
Original document preservation: Ensure that temporary color changes do not modify the PDF's contents or appearance when saved or exported.
Keep existing editing functionality: Preserve the current background editing tool for users who intentionally want to modify the document.
Expected Benefits
Improved visual comfort during extended reading sessions.
Preservation of the original PDF.
Reduced risk of unwanted changes to images, diagrams, charts, and other visual elements.
Greater flexibility for users with different reading preferences.
Expected Behavior

Users should be able to enable a reading mode, view the document using their preferred color scheme, and disable the mode to return to the original appearance.

title: Telugu interface language can't be drawn: no Telugu font in craft-fonts or the system-font fallback
author: bmh129
body:
## Summary

Telugu (తెలుగు) is offered as an interface language, but no build can draw Telugu script. Its name in Preferences ▸ Interface language shows as missing-glyph boxes, and so, presumably, does the whole interface when Telugu is chosen.

## Environment

- Fedora 44 (Silverblue), GNOME 50, Wayland. PdfCraft runs in a Fedora 44 toolbox that has no Telugu font installed.
- Local build of `main` (0.7.1) with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` set to craft-fonts `3d9ab3a`, the revision `release.yml` pins.

## Steps

1. Open Preferences.
2. Open the Interface language menu.

**Expected:** తెలుగు, as in the language's own script.
**Actual:** a row of boxes, just above Magyar. Every other language name renders (Simplified Chinese misses one character, 简, which is #498).

## Cause

- `theme.rs` adds craft-fonts' `Telu` faces as the UI's Telugu fallback (`pdfcraft_fonts::ui_telugu_fonts()`), but craft-fonts has no Telugu face, neither at `3d9ab3a` nor on `main`. It has BIZ UD Gothic and Mincho, Shippori Mincho, Noto Sans Arabic, Noto Sans CJK SC (not embedded, AGENTS.md §1.1) and Noto Sans Thai.
- The installed-font fallback (`system_fonts.rs`) only looks for Arabic (probe U+0627), Devanagari and Han faces, so an installed Telugu font is never used either.

So I believe official release builds show the same boxes on any system, but I haven't checked an official build.

## Possible fixes

1. Add an openly licensed Telugu face to craft-fonts, for example Noto Sans Telugu (OFL-1.1, not an Adobe design), with its `ATTRIBUTION` entry. The existing `ui_telugu_fonts()` path would then pick it up with no code change here.
2. And/or teach `system_fonts.rs` a Telugu need: probe U+0C15 (క), with candidates such as Fedora's `google-noto-sans-telugu-fonts` and Debian's `fonts-noto-core` and `fonts-telu`. Builds without craft-fonts (local, distro, Flatpak) would then use an installed font.
3. Until one of these lands, consider hiding a language from the menu when no face can draw its name, so it do…

title: Reading colours: dark modes hide highlighted text (band multiplies to black)
author: edurbs
body:
## What happens

With Reading colours set to a dark preset (Preferences ▸ Reading colours ▸ *White on black*, *Yellow on black*, *Green on black*), every **highlight annotation renders as a solid dark bar and the text under it is invisible** (contrast ≈ 1:1). Introduced by #1270 (reading colours, closes #897).

Pixel analysis of the dark screenshot: page background black `(0,0,0)`, normal text correctly remapped to white, but inside each highlight the fill is `(29,29,29)` with **zero** light pixels — the glyphs are gone. In the light-mode render the same three highlights are yellow `(255,240,0)` with readable black text.

## Why

`ColorReplacement::map` remaps every solid paint by luminance, and annotation appearance paints are classified as **line art** (`is_text = false`):

- Yellow highlight `(255,240,0)` is luminance-light (t ≈ 0.886) → remapped toward the dark background → `(29,27,0)`.
- The highlight then composites with **Multiply** (both the `/AP` ExtGState `/BM /Multiply` and the no-`/AP` fallback in `draw_highlight_without_appearance`): remapped-white text × near-black fill = near-black. Words and band both vanish.

A second contributor is described in the comment below: the page background was painted outside the page's transparency group, so Multiply never blended with it.

## Expected

Reading colours replace **document** colours (page text, line art, images), never **annotation** colours — the Acrobat model ("change the color of black text or line art"). With annotations exempt, a yellow highlight stays yellow: on a dark page the words under it render yellow (multiply), readable, matching Acrobat's Replace Document Colors look.

## Fix direction

Bracket the `/Annots` loop in `interpret_page` with an annotation-context signal (default no-op on the `Device` trait), and make `replaced()` return paints unchanged while inside it. Regression test: highlight + `WHITE_ON_BLACK`, assert the glyphs inside the quad stay bright.

Screenshots (light vs dark render…

title: edit: chained page operations name the wrong missing page
author: Nmarello
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1 (macOS universal release), Apple M4.

`edit` applies its operations in order and renumbers pages after each one. That's fine, but when a later operation points past the end, the error names the wrong page.

With any 5-page PDF:

```sh
pdfcraft-cli edit in.pdf --out out.pdf --delete 4 --move 5:1
# pdfcraft-cli: page 4 does not exist
```

Page 4 does exist. After `--delete 4` the document has four pages, so the out-of-range page is 5, from `--move 5:1`. These variants work:

```sh
pdfcraft-cli edit in.pdf --out out.pdf --move 5:1 --delete 4   # ok, 4 pages
pdfcraft-cli edit in.pdf --out out.pdf --delete 4 --move 4:1   # ok, 4 pages
```

Suggestion: name the page and the operation that's out of range (e.g. `--move 5:1: page 5 does not exist; after the earlier operations the document has 4 pages`). `--help` could also say that page numbers refer to the document after the preceding operations.

title: M10 : PostScript (.ps) / EPS (.eps) export
author: edurbs
body:
# M10 : PostScript (.ps) / EPS (.eps) export

**Tracking issue for `create.export-ps` and `create.export-eps`** (parity `planned`, P2, M10).
Not to be confused with the reverse direction — PostScript/EPS **to** PDF (Distiller, `create.distiller`, P3/M14, deferred) — which stays out of scope here.

> **Status: in progress (2026-10-12).** Layer A implementation is starting on a dedicated branch; the design spec and task-by-task implementation plan travel with the Layer A PR. Comment here before starting parallel work on this feature (see #1176).

## What Acrobat does

Export PDF ▸ PostScript writes Level 2/3 `.ps` (one file, all pages) and per-page `.eps` with a `%%BoundingBox`, keeping text as text where fonts cooperate and flattening what PostScript cannot express (transparency). Used for print/RIP workflows, Illustrator/InDesign/TeX interchange, and Distiller round-trips.

## Current state

- `parity/acrobat-features.toml`: `create.export-ps` (line ~7061), `create.export-eps` (line ~7073) — `planned`, no commands/tools/evidence.
- `crates/engine/src/catalog.rs:80`: UI placeholder `export.ps`, `Planned("M10")`.
- `docs/gaps.md` §8 and `docs/file-format-parity.md` (Export PDF to ▸ PostScript, EPS): listed as missing.
- Before 2026-10-12: no code, no branch, no PR, nobody else in flight. Layer A work now tracks here.

## Estimate honesty

Gap 8's 55–100 h covers **all** of Office export/import **plus** SVG/XML/EPS/PS/JPEG 2000 export. A correct PS writer alone is bigger than a proportional slice of that budget:

title: Feature Request: Option to export PDF to MD (markdown format)
author: davidzyph
body:
Currently, PDFCraft is an excellent tool for managing and manipulating PDF files. However, it would be incredibly useful to have a native feature that allows exporting or extracting the content of a PDF document directly to Markdown format (.md).

The idea is for the tool to interpret the basic structure of the PDF (such as headers, lists, bold text, and links) and translate it into clean Markdown syntax, making it easier to extract text without the classic broken formatting issues.

Benefits & Use Cases
Implementing this feature would bring great value to users for the following reasons:

1. Integration with note-taking systems: Many users manage their knowledge and notes in Markdown-based applications (like Obsidian, Logseq, Notion, or Neovim). Being able to go from a PDF to Markdown natively would greatly speed up the workflow.

2. Handling dense and study documents: For those working with lengthy texts, technical manuals, or complex legal documents, having the content in Markdown makes reading, searching for terms, highlighting, and structuring personal summaries much easier.

3. Version control friendly: Unlike PDFs, Markdown files are plain text, making them perfect for tracking changes using Git.

4. Accessibility and editing: Text extracted in .md is much easier to edit, modify, and adapt for other formats in the future (using tools like Pandoc) or for publishing on the web.

Proposed Solution
Add an option in the interface called Export to Markdown or Convert to .md.

Alternatives Considered
Currently, the only way to achieve this is by manually copying and pasting text (which breaks line breaks and structure) or relying on third-party external tools, which interrupts the all-in-one experience PDFCraft offers.

author: babstar99
body:
### Motivation / Real-world use case
- Document: Aircraft FCOM, 30MB, 2000+ pages, highly complex vector + bookmarks
- Workflow: OEM issues Rev 24 -> Rev 25 monthly. User has 200+ highlights, notes, ink on Rev 24.
- Problem: Acrobat's "Compare Files" + "Import Comments" loses anchor when pagination shifts. PdfCraft's Organize view is perfect for extracting Limitations/MEL sections, but annotations are lost on revision increment.
- Value: Core workflow for aviation, legal, engineering, medical - any controlled document where your notes must survive the next revision.
- Tested: PdfCraft v0.7.1 macOS universal, 30MB FCOM opens fine, Organize view works, 0 crashes.

As a tech pubs user, I want to:
1. Open Old.pdf (with my comments) and New.pdf (clean OEM rev)

title: OCR: multilingual recognition (starting with Traditional Chinese) via PaddleOCR ONNX models on rten
author: philip-tam
body:
## Summary
Scan & OCR reads only unaccented Latin (the `ocrs` model; `docs/gaps.md` gap 7, #524, #744, #1104, #146). I ran a small spike to see whether PaddleOCR's multilingual models, which are Apache-2.0, can run in pure Rust through `rten`, which `pdfcraft-ocr` already uses. They can. Before writing a PR I'd like your view on model sourcing, size and packaging.

## What I tried
- `rten` 0.26 with the `onnx_format` feature loads the `.onnx` files directly, so no Python or conversion step is needed.
- Text finding uses a PaddleOCR DB detection model (2.4 MB). The reader is the Chinese CTC recognition model (84 MB, 18,383-character dictionary). Preprocessing is DB-style resize, a threshold, connected components and box expansion. Decoding is greedy CTC.
- I used a throwaway program of about 120 lines, with no changes in the repo.
- The files came from a community ONNX conversion (Hugging Face `monkt/paddleocr-onnx`, licence listed as Apache-2.0). That is fine for a spike, not for shipping.

## Results
On a synthetic 3-line Traditional Chinese and English image (installed system font):
- The clean image read 2 of 3 lines exactly. In the third, 參 came out as 参.
- A degraded copy (shrunk to 55%, blurred, noisy, rotated 1.2°) read all three lines correctly.
- Digits and Latin inside Chinese lines were right. The model does not output spaces, so word spacing would be rebuilt from the gaps between characters.
- Speed: about 60 ms to load the reader, about 60 ms to detect text, and 65–120 ms per line.

Not tested: real scans, rotated or curved text, dense layouts, vertical text.

## Questions
1. **Model source.** Are PaddleOCR models acceptable? Which verifiable source should we use: official Paddle exports converted by us (with the conversion recorded), or a mirror? I'd add a `kind = "model"` entry with a licence, SHA-256 and credit to `ATTRIBUTION.toml`, as for the current `ocrs` models.
2. **Size and packaging.** The Chinese reader is 84 MB. Other scripts are 8–13 MB ea…

title: page_add_text refuses Central European Latin (Č Ć Đ ř Ł ő); generalize #1513 beyond Turkish?
author: alesk
body:
## Summary

`page_add_text` refuses Central European Latin letters, which blocks generating documents in Slovenian, Croatian, Czech, Polish, Hungarian and other languages.

## Environment

- `pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1` (release zip, SHA-256 checked), macOS arm64, run through `pdfcraft-cli run --script`. First seen on 0.6.0.

## Repro

```json
[
 {"tool":"doc_create","args":{"from":"blank","pages":1,"width":595,"height":842}},
 {"tool":"page_add_text","args":{"doc":1,"page":1,"at":[20,30],"font":"courier","text":"Račun"}}
]
```

```
pdfcraft-cli: step 2 (page_add_text): the standard fonts can't draw "Č" (U+010C); only Western European characters can be added as text for now
```

I tested each character on its own (0.7.1):

| Char | Result |
|---|---|
| Š U+0160, Ž U+017D | ok (in WinAnsi) |
| Č U+010C, Ć U+0106, Đ U+0110 (Slovenian/Croatian) | refused |
| ř U+0159 (Czech), Ł U+0141 (Polish), ő U+0151 (Hungarian) | refused |

`doc_create from=text` refuses the same characters with a clear error (since #1030).

## Use case

I generate Slovenian UPN payment slips (fixed-position text plus a QR image on an A4 page). `page_add_text` with `at` and `courier` would fit this well, but about 80% of my real records contain `č`/`Č` in street names, cities or descriptions, so I can't use it.

## Relation to #1513

Open PR #1513 fixes this for Turkish (Ğ İ Ş ğ ı ş) with a `/Differences` encoding over WinAnsi plus a ToUnicode CMap, but the six characters and their byte codes are hard-coded. Generalizing that approach would cover this issue: Adobe's Core 14 AFMs have glyphs for all of Latin Extended-A (`Ccaron`, `cacute`, `dcroat`, `rcaron`, `Lslash`, `ohungarumlaut`, …), and the remapped codes could be chosen from the characters actually used in the text.

One limit of fixed slots: #1513 puts the Turkish letters at 0xD0/0xDD/0xDE/0xF0/0xFD/0xFE, so a single run can't contain both `İ` and `Ý` (or `ð`). Choosing slots per font avoids that. Embedding a Latin font subset (#906) would still be…

title: XFA: draw barcode fields (PDF417 on Government of Canada immigration forms) instead of their value as text
author: CouchRiv
body:
## Summary

Every Government of Canada immigration (IRCC) PDF form is a dynamic XFA form with **PDF417** barcode fields.
- **What they hold.** The "Validate" button fills them with the applicant's data, and IRCC scans them from the printed or uploaded form.
- **What PdfCraft 0.7.1 does.** It lays these forms out well: IMM 5257 gives 6 pages and 173 fields, and fill + incremental save through MCP keeps the encryption and the usage-rights signature (tested). But it draws barcode fields as their value in plain text and warns: *"barcode fields show their value as text, not as bars"* (`crates/xfa/src/layout.rs`, `Ui::Barcode`).
- **Effect.** A form validated and printed or saved with PdfCraft has no scannable barcode.

The template uses:

```xml
<barcode type="pdf417" errorCorrectionLevel="5" moduleHeight="0.676mm" moduleWidth="0.338mm">
```

All 7 barcode fields across the IRCC forms I checked use exactly that: IMM 5257, 5709, 5710 and 1294.

## Repro (public blank form)

```sh
curl -LO https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/ircc/documents/pdf/english/kits/forms/imm5257/01-09-2023/imm5257e.pdf
pdfcraft-cli info imm5257e.pdf     # xfa_layout.warnings: "barcode fields show their value as text, not as bars" (once a value is set)
```

## Proposed fix

1. **Encoder.** Use [`rxing`](https://github.com/rxing-core/rxing) (Apache-2.0, maintained, ZXing port) with only its encoders enabled, or a small in-tree encoder.
   - PDF417: byte compaction, Reed-Solomon at the template's `errorCorrectionLevel`, columns from `dataColumnCount`/`rowColumnRatio` when present.
   - Code 128, QR and Data Matrix come almost for free.
2. **Drawing.** In `layout.rs`, at `Ui::Barcode`, build the module matrix and emit filled rectangles in the page content stream (vector, so it prints sharp).
   - Size: `moduleWidth` × `moduleHeight`, inside the field's content box, with the quiet zone.
   - Keep today's text fallback (and the warning) for types that aren't supported.
3. **Data.** Encode the field's forma…

title: XFA: BMP and TIFF pictures (image/bmp, image/tif) are left out
author: CouchRiv
body:
## Summary

XFA templates often embed pictures as BMP or TIFF. PdfCraft 0.7.1 leaves them out with *"a image/bmp image is not a JPEG, PNG or GIF and is left out"* (same for `image/tif`).
- **Where.** `crates/xfa/src/image.rs` only sniffs JPEG, PNG and GIF, and `crates/xfa/Cargo.toml` enables only the `gif` feature of `image`.
- **Seen on.** The Government of Canada immigration forms: IMM 5257 has 2 BMP and 2 TIFF pictures, IMM 5710 has 2 BMP and 5 TIFF. They are logos and section graphics, missing from the rendered pages.

Note the content type: the templates say `contentType="image/tif"`, not `image/tiff`.

## Repro (public blank form)

```sh
curl -LO https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/ircc/documents/pdf/english/kits/forms/imm5257/01-09-2023/imm5257e.pdf
pdfcraft-cli info imm5257e.pdf | jq .xfa_layout.warnings
# ["a image/bmp image is not a JPEG, PNG or GIF and is left out", "a image/tif image is not a JPEG, PNG or GIF and is left out", ...]
```

## Proposed fix

1. **Dependency.** `crates/xfa/Cargo.toml`: `image = { version = "0.25", default-features = false, features = ["gif", "bmp", "tiff"] }`.
2. **Sniffing** (`image.rs`): add `Kind::Bmp` (`BM`) and `Kind::Tiff` (`II*\0` / `MM\0*`).
   - Sniff the bytes and don't trust the declared type.
   - Accept `image/bmp`, `image/x-ms-bmp`, `image/tif` and `image/tiff` when the bytes agree.
3. **Decoding.** Decode them like GIF, to 8-bit RGB plus an optional alpha soft mask.
   - Keep `MAX` dimension checks and decoder limits.
   - For TIFF: first page only, with `Limits` set (as #665 did for page decode).
4. **Test.** Add tiny BMP (24-bit and 8-bit palette) and TIFF (uncompressed, LZW) fixtures. Assert no warning and the expected pixel at a known spot.

title: CLI: render/text/info use the placeholder page of dynamic XFA forms (MCP uses the layout); text ignores copy:no
author: CouchRiv
body:
## Summary

On a dynamic XFA form, the CLI works on the PDF's placeholder page, while the MCP/automation path (`doc_open`) uses the XFA layout. On the public IRCC form IMM 5257 (PdfCraft 0.7.1):

| | MCP (`doc_open`, `doc_info`, `form_fields`) | CLI |
|---|---|---|
| pages | 6 | `info`: `"pages": 1`; `render --page 2`: *"page 2 does not exist"* |
| fields | 174 | `info`: `"fields": 1` (only `xfa_layout.fields` says 173) |
| text | `text_extract` refuses: *"the document's security settings don't allow copying text"* (`copy:no`) | `text` prints the "Please wait... upgrade to Adobe Reader" placeholder, ignoring the copy permission |

## Repro

```sh
curl -LO https://www.canada.ca/content/dam/ircc/documents/pdf/english/kits/forms/imm5257/01-09-2023/imm5257e.pdf
pdfcraft-cli info imm5257e.pdf | jq '{pages, fields, xfa_layout}'
pdfcraft-cli render imm5257e.pdf --page 2 --dpi 50 --out p2.png
pdfcraft-cli text imm5257e.pdf | head -3
```

## Proposed fix

1. **Same document model as automation.** `apps/pdfcraft-cli` `render`, `text` and `info` should open documents through the same path as automation, so a dynamic XFA form is its laid-out pages.
   - `info`: report the layout's page and field counts at top level, and keep the raw counts under e.g. `pdf_pages`/`acroform_fields`.
2. **Permissions.** `text` (and `render` export, if it's treated as copying) should apply the same permission check as `text_extract`. Without the owner password, the CLI then gives the same answer as the MCP.
3. **Test.** On a dynamic-XFA fixture: `info.pages` equals the layout's pages, `render --page N` works for every layout page, and `text` respects `copy:no`.

(For what it's worth, the automation path is great on these forms: `form_fill` on the XFA fields plus `doc_save {"full": false}` keeps the encryption and the usage-rights signature, and the values land in `datasets`.)

title: `edit --rotate` fails with "page 0 does not exist" on a PDF that info, text and render all read
author: gozzy-nwogbo
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1 (release build), macOS 27.0.1, Apple Silicon

**What happens**

For a PDF with damaged metadata, the read path recovers the page tree but the edit path does not. `info` reports 3 pages, `text` and `render` work, then `edit` fails on the first page.

**Repro** (public file: [py-pdf/sample-files `017-unreadable-meta-data/unreadablemetadata.pdf`](https://github.com/py-pdf/sample-files/blob/main/017-unreadable-meta-data/unreadablemetadata.pdf))

```sh
pdfcraft-cli info unreadablemetadata.pdf      # "pages": 3
pdfcraft-cli edit unreadablemetadata.pdf --out out.pdf --rotate 1:90
# pdfcraft-cli: page 0 does not exist
```

**Expected:** the edit succeeds on the 3 pages the reader already found, or fails with a message that names the damage.
**Actual:** `page 0 does not exist`, no output file.

The same `edit --rotate 1:90` works on the other 38 unencrypted PDFs in our sample. From the outside it looks like `edit` opens the document without the repair step that `info`/`text`/`render` use, but I have not confirmed that in the source.

*Found with an automated test harness (Claude Code agents, MuPDF and PyMuPDF as independent checks) while evaluating the Craft apps for local agent use. I re-ran the repro above by hand.*

title: Feature: Drag to check or uncheck multiple checkboxes
author: Gamedirection
body:
### Description

Allow checking or unchecking several checkboxes in one drag, as in the other Craft apps. All Craft apps must work the same way.

- VectorCraft: storytold/vectorcraft#1477, PR storytold/vectorcraft#1600
- PhotoCraft: storytold/photocraft#3333, PR storytold/photocraft#3521

### Requested behaviour

- Press on a checkbox and drag over its neighbours. Each checkbox that the pointer goes over takes the new state of the first one, until you release the button.
- A click toggles one checkbox, as before.
- A mixed (dash) checkbox stays as it is during a drag.
- Put the change in the shared checkbox widget, so Preferences, dialogs and panels all get it at the same time.

### Scope

This applies to the checkboxes of the app's own interface (Preferences, dialogs, panels). It does not apply to checkbox form fields in a PDF document. Those are document content (see #180, #231, #449).

### Reference

VectorCraft PR #1600 and PhotoCraft PR #3521 use the same design: a `drag_toggle` helper in the shared checkbox keeps the new state in the egui context while the primary button is down, and every checkbox that the pointer goes over takes that state.

title: Windows: no "Print" on File Explorer's right-click menu when PdfCraft is the default PDF app
author: mtlcl410
body:
### Problem

When PdfCraft is the default app for PDF files on Windows, right-clicking a PDF in File Explorer shows no **Print** entry. Explorer builds that entry from the default app's `shell\print` verb, and the MSI registers only `shell\open` for `PdfCraft.Document` (`packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs`):

```
HKCR\PdfCraft.Document\shell\
    open      <- the only verb
```

So once a user makes PdfCraft their PDF default, printing a file from Explorer is no longer possible without opening it first. Other PDF apps register this verb, and with Acrobat as the default, Explorer's Print sends the file straight to the default printer without showing a dialog.

### Proposal

1. **`pdfcraft.exe --print <file>…`**: before any window is created, open each file, impose it with the Print dialog's defaults, send it to the system default printer through the existing spooler path (the same one `doc_print` uses with `printer: "default"`), and exit. No window appears, and in release builds no console appears, because the app uses the `windows` subsystem.
2. **Fall back to the Print dialog, never fail silently.** If the file can't be printed unattended, PdfCraft opens it in the app with the Print dialog showing, so the user can see what happened. Cases:
   - the file needs a password;
   - its permissions forbid printing (still enforced through `print_pdf`);
   - there is no default printer;
   - the spooler reports an error (also logged).
3. **Paper size.** The dialog defaults to US Letter, which is wrong for A4 users when there is no dialog to correct it. For unattended printing, use the standard size matching the first page (`print::matching_paper`). If the first page is not a standard size, fall back to the printer's default paper.
4. **MSI.** Add `PdfCraft.Document\shell\print\command` = `"pdfcraft.exe" --print "%1"`. As with "Edit with PdfCraft" (#1180), Windows 11 shows it under "Show more options".
5. **Tests and docs.** Unit tests for argument parsing and for each fallback d…

title: Save: a full rewrite that fails its reopen check still replaces the file — `doc_save` in place turned a readable 139 KB PDF into an unreadable 500-byte file
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
## Summary
`doc_save` writes the new bytes to the target (`write_atomic`) before it checks that they reopen (`mark_saved`). When the check fails, the tool reports an error, but the file on disk is already the new, unreadable version. Saved in place, the original is gone: with `full: true`, a 139,713-byte PDF that PdfCraft opens fine (1 page, with its annotations) became a 500-byte file that neither PdfCraft nor poppler can open. Saving to another path leaves that broken file behind.

## Steps to reproduce
Input: pdfplumber's public oss-fuzz sample [`tests/pdfs/from-oss-fuzz/load/5317294594523136.pdf`](https://github.com/jsvine/pdfplumber/blob/stable/tests/pdfs/from-oss-fuzz/load/5317294594523136.pdf) (139,713 bytes; poppler reads 1 page).
```
copy 5317294594523136.pdf x.pdf
steps.json: [{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"x.pdf"}},{"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"full":true}}]
pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root .
```

## Expected
A readable rewrite, or, if the result can't be reopened, the error and `x.pdf` unchanged.

## Actual (0.7.1 and main @ dfa43be)
`pdfcraft-cli: step 2 (doc_save): the edited document could not be reopened: the file is not a readable PDF: no readable page tree or cross-reference data was found`, exit 1. `x.pdf` is now 500 bytes: header `%PDF-256`, a catalog whose `/Pages 3 0 R` is the array `[ 0 ]`; poppler: "Top-level pages object is wrong type (array)".

## Analysis
Two problems:
1. Write before verify. In `doc_save` (`crates/automation/src/lib.rs`), `write_atomic(&target, &bytes)?` runs before `self.session.mark_saved(…)`, which is where the reopen fails. The desktop path `save_doc_to` (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs`) has the same order and reports "Saved, but reopening failed"; it saves incrementally, so there the original bytes should survive as the prefix (not tested). Checking the bytes before writing (the `inspect`/`check_pages` that `mark_saved` and `refresh` run) would keep the original whenever the check fails ("none of…

title: Render: Type 3 image-mask glyphs shrunk by less than 2:1 lose strokes (pixels are picked, not averaged); #1586 averages only beyond 2:1
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
## Summary
A 1-bit image mask shrunk by between 1:1 and 2:1 is drawn by picking single source pixels. For Type 3 bitmap glyphs with 1-pixel strokes (TeX pk fonts, fax-era and OCR fonts) that deletes strokes outright: at 150 dpi the 8×14 px glyphs of `type3_imagemask_tr2.pdf` (the #1469 fixture) at 10 pt read `-:||:-||:-:||` instead of `HolloHlloHoll`, and at 96 dpi the 12 pt Type 3 line of `mask_downscale.pdf` loses parts of most glyphs. Poppler averages the covered source pixels and every glyph stays legible. #1586 (open) averages non-interpolated images shrunk by more than 2:1 and keeps picking up to 2:1 on purpose (#624, crisp screenshots). For 1-bit masks that range is where thin strokes vanish, and it is hit at ordinary zoom levels: a 300 dpi pk font shown at 200 % (192 dpi) is 1.6:1.

## Steps to reproduce
Fixture [`mask_downscale.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/mask_downscale.pdf) ([raw](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/main/pdfcraft/mask_downscale.pdf), 12 KB, generator [`make_mask_fixtures.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/make_mask_fixtures.py)): a line of text as (1) an `/ImageMask` stencil of a 300 dpi bitmap, (2) the same bitmap as a DeviceGray 1-bit image, (3) a Type 3 font whose glyphs are 16 px image masks; each at 12 pt and 9 pt. Also [`type3_imagemask_tr2.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/type3_imagemask_tr2.pdf).
```
pdfcraft-cli render mask_downscale.pdf --page 1 --dpi 96 --out pc96.png
pdftoppm -r 96 -png -singlefile mask_downscale.pdf pop96
pdfcraft-cli render type3_imagemask_tr2.pdf --page 1 --dpi 150 --out pc150.png
```

![comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/main/pdfcraft/mask_downscale_compare.png)

title: No kinetic (momentum) scrolling with touchpad
author: Thaer99ob
body:
## Description:
When scrolling with a touchpad, scrolling stops immediately when fingers are lifted. There is no momentum, unlike in web browsers and  other PDF apps.

## Steps to reproduce:

1. Open a multi-page PDF.
2. Do a fast two-finger swipe on the touchpad.
2. Lift your fingers mid-motion.

## Expected behavior
Scrolling continues and decelerates smoothly, matching OS-level behavior.

## Actual behavior
Scrolling stops instantly on release.

## Environment:

- OS: Linux Wayland
- App version: Latest

title: Edit text & images: alignment guides while moving a paragraph or image
author: ch0kemeister
body:
### What

While a paragraph or image is being dragged in Edit text & images (or nudged with the arrow keys), draw alignment guides against the other paragraphs and images on the page, as Acrobat, Affinity and Figma do: thin magenta lines when the dragged box's left, right, top or bottom edge, or its centre, lines up with an edge or centre of another box, and the drag snaps to that line within a few screen pixels (Shift to drag freely). The guides vanish on release.

### Why

Moving text today is blind: the only reference is the eye. A heading dragged next to a paragraph ends up a point or two off its left edge, which shows in print. Acrobat's Edit PDF shows these guides for exactly this reason.

### Scope

- Candidates: the other text blocks and images on the same page, plus the page's own edges and centre.
- Edges and centres on both axes; nearest line wins when several are within the snap distance.
- Existing machinery: `edit_text_ui.rs` already has the boxes of every paragraph (`boxes`) and the drag preview rect (`BlockDrag`, `ImageSelection::drag`), so the guides are a pure overlay plus a snap offset applied to the preview.
- Not in scope: distributing objects, smart spacing between three boxes, guides across pages.

Tested on macOS 26 (Apple Silicon) with a debug build of main (7437bde3): the drag preview moves freely with no guides.

title: macOS 26+: Chinese UI renders in Hiragino Sans GB instead of PingFang (PingFang.ttc moved out of /System/Library/Fonts)
author: TinXiwei
body:
### Summary

On macOS 26+ the Simplified Chinese UI is drawn by **Hiragino Sans GB W3 (华文黑体)** instead of PingFang (苹方), so all Chinese text looks dated and washed out. Glyphs are correct (no tofu — this is the follow-up to #826 / #925); the wrong installed face is being picked.

`han_candidates()` looks for `/System/Library/Fonts/PingFang.ttc`, which no longer exists on current macOS — Apple moved PingFang into the reserved system-font directory, leaving only Hiragino Sans GB / STHeiti in `/System/Library/Fonts`.

### Environment

- PdfCraft 0.7.1 (latest release, macos-universal dmg)
- macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M2, arm64, interface language 简体中文

### Evidence

Log (`~/Library/Application Support/PdfCraft/logs/pdfcraft.log`):

```
INFO [main] pdfcraft_ui_egui::system_fonts: interface font fallback: /System/Library/Fonts/Hiragino Sans GB.ttc (face 0)
```

`face 0` of that collection is Hiragino Sans GB **W3**, the thin pre-PingFang-era face.

```
$ ls /System/Library/Fonts/PingFang.ttc
ls: /System/Library/Fonts/PingFang.ttc: No such file or directory

$ ls /System/Library/Fonts/ | grep -iE 'ping|heiti|hiragino'
Hiragino Sans GB.ttc
STHeiti Light.ttc
STHeiti Medium.ttc
```

PingFang is instead at:

```
/System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/FontServices.framework/Resources/Reserved/PingFangUI.ttc
-rw-r--r--  root:wheel  61,473,880 bytes      # world-readable TTC, 268 faces
```

Its face 0 is `.PingFang UI Text SC Regular Text` — the face the system UI itself uses — and it covers both the Hans probe 欢 (U+6B22) and the Hant probe 說 (U+8AAA), so `face_with()` accepts it unchanged. CoreText also still resolves the family by name here (`CTFontCreateWithName("PingFang SC", …)` → "PingFang SC Regular"), so only the hard-coded path misses.

No workaround exists locally: `PDFCRAFT_SYSTEM_FONTS=0` disables the fallback entirely and the embedded craft-fonts faces are Japanese (BIZ UD Gothic / BIZ UD Mincho / Shippori Mincho, no 欢), so the UI returns to tofu; nothing in `app.ron` …

title: Detect form fields finds nothing on scanned (image-only) forms
author: alexanderalber
body:
Prepare a form ▸ Detect form fields (`form.detect`, tool `form_detect_fields`) finds nothing on a scanned form.

**Seen in a user report:** a local authority published a business registration form only as a photo-scanned PDF. Acrobat's field detection found the fields, PdfCraft found none.

**Why:** detection (#93) works on vector data only: words from the text layer and rectangle/line paths from the content stream (`pdfcraft_forms::detect::page_shapes`). A scanned page is a single image, so there are no words and no paths, and detection finds nothing by construction. Running Recognize Text first does not help much either: it adds words but no lines or boxes.

**Expected:** on a page that is a picture, the rules, boxes and check boxes are read from the pixels, and the labels come from the text layer or from OCR when the models are installed. Without OCR models, fields should still be created (with default names) rather than none. Pages stored sideways with `/Rotate` (common for scans) should get fields that read upright.

title: Linux: opening a PDF with xdg-open starts a new process and window every time (single-instance not working)
author: braenmachio
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.6.0 (`pdfcraft-0.6.0-linux-x86_64.AppImage`, also reproduced with the extracted `squashfs-root/usr/bin/pdfcraft`)

**Environment:** Omarchy (Arch Linux), Hyprland, Wayland, Intel UHD Graphics 620 (wgpu/Vulkan)

**Setup:** PdfCraft is the default handler for `application/pdf` (`ai.storyteller.pdfcraft.desktop`, `Exec=... %F`). `xdg-open file.pdf` launches it correctly.

**Problem:** Each `xdg-open` or direct invocation starts a new process and opens a new window, even when PdfCraft is already running. The file is not forwarded to the running instance.

**Expected:** The new invocation hands the path to the running instance and exits, and the file opens there (new tab or window in the same process).

**Steps to reproduce:**
```bash
pdfcraft ~/Documents/a.pdf &
sleep 4
pdfcraft ~/Documents/b.pdf     # different file
```
Repeating with the same file (`a.pdf` twice) gives the same result. The log shows a full second startup (version line, wgpu adapter, font fallback) with no message about an existing instance or file forwarding.

**Observations:**
- The binary contains the path `apps/pdfcraft/src/single_instance.rs`, so the module is compiled in.
- With one instance running, `ss -xlp | grep -i pdfcraft` prints nothing, and there is no pdfcraft/artcraft entry in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. No socket or lock is visible from outside the process.
- Running the extracted binary from a fixed path behaves the same as the AppImage, so the AppImage mount path is not the cause.
- `pdfcraft --help` logs `unknown option help` and starts the GUI. The binary strings show `--new-window`, `--control` and `--version`, but I could not find a documented list of options.

**Questions:**
1. Is single-instance supported on Linux, and does it forward file arguments?
2. Is there a flag or setting to enable it?
3. Could `--help` print the supported options?

title: [Bug] `text_paragraphs` merges a heading and body lines into one paragraph; `text_edit` on it wipes all of them and the page's watermark
author: stobados
body:
Lines with different sizes are grouped into one paragraph. Replacing that paragraph replaces every line in it and also removes a watermark added on the same page. Editing a single line with `line` works and keeps the watermark.

**Environment:** macOS 27.2 (26B5101f), Apple M1, 8 GB. PdfCraft 0.7.1. Mode: Headless MCP.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page PDF with a 20 pt heading and three 12 pt lines. We used WordCraft: Heading 1 "Public notice", then "Deadline: 4 March 2026", "Fund A - small productions", "Fund B - large productions", saved as PDF (font: subset HelveticaNeue)

5. `tool_call text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "Public notice (edited)"}`

**Expected:** The heading and each body line (different size and spacing) are separate paragraphs. Editing text never removes other content on the page.

**Actual:** All four lines are replaced by the new text, and `text_paragraphs` afterwards lists one paragraph only: the DRAFT watermark is gone.

**Notes:** Also seen on a real 27-page Word-generated PDF, in 0.6.0 and 0.7.1: an edit replaced unrelated lines, the replacement used Helvetica instead of the embedded Calibri subset, and the wrapped text overlapped the next line.

Related: #1680 (side-by-side table cells grouped into one paragraph). This case has no table: a heading and plain body lines.

title: Render: a JPX image drawn with an out-of-range integer in `cm` panics in hayro-jpeg2000 (`attempt to divide by zero`, codestream.rs:150)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
## Summary
A JPEG 2000 image drawn with `100 0 0 9223372036854775807 0 0 cm` makes the page renderer panic inside `hayro-jpeg2000` 0.3.5 (`src/j2c/codestream.rs:150:30: attempt to divide by zero`). The page safety net catches it, so the app keeps running, but the page does not render (`check-one`: `renderer crashed on page 1`, `render` fails). Found by mutation fuzzing; the fixture below rebuilds it from scratch.

## Steps to reproduce
Fixture [`jpx_cm_i64max.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/jpx_cm_i64max.pdf) (2 KB, generator [`make_jpx_cm_overflow.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/make_jpx_cm_overflow.py)): a 64×64 grey JP2 (Pillow/OpenJPEG) drawn with `q 100 0 0 9223372036854775807 0 0 cm /Im1 Do Q`. Control: [`jpx_cm_ok.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/jpx_cm_ok.pdf), same image at `100 0 0 100 50 50`.
```
pdfcraft-cli check-one jpx_cm_i64max.pdf
pdfcraft-cli render jpx_cm_i64max.pdf --page 1 --dpi 72 --out x.png
```

## Expected
No panic: the image is skipped or drawn degenerate, and the rest of the page renders.

## Actual (0.7.1 Windows and main @ dfa43be)
```
thread 'main' panicked at …/hayro-jpeg2000-0.3.5/src/j2c/codestream.rs:150:30:
attempt to divide by zero
{"detail":"p1: renderer crashed on page 1: attempt to divide by zero","failed_pages":1,…,"status":"page-errors"}
```
Backtrace: `hayro_jpeg2000::j2c::codestream::read_header` ← `hayro_syntax::filter::jpx::decode` ← `hayro_interpret::x_object::decoded_raster` ← `hayro::renderer::Renderer::draw_image`.

## Analysis
`draw_image` (`vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs`, around line 1358) derives the decode target as `(transform * Point::new(w, 0.0)).to_vec2().length().ceil() as u32` (and the same for the height). With this matrix one of those lengths is not finite; `NaN as u32` is 0. `read_header` then divides the image size by the target (`size_data.image_height() / target_height`, codestream.rs:150) …

title: Open: Standard security handler V 2 / R 3 with `/Length 256` panics in hayro-syntax (`range end index 32 out of range for slice of length 16`, crypto/mod.rs:591)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
## Summary
An encryption dictionary `/Filter /Standard /V 2 /R 3 /Length 256` makes the key computation panic: Algorithm 2 truncates the 16-byte MD5 output to `Length / 8` = 32 bytes (`hash[..byte_length as usize]`, `vendor/hayro-syntax/src/crypto/mod.rs:591`, and line 595 for the final key). The open safety net catches it and reports "the file is not a readable PDF: the parser crashed". `/Length` above 128 is not valid for V 2, so the file is malformed; it should be refused with an encryption error (qpdf and poppler report a wrong password) instead of a panic. Found by mutation fuzzing; the fixture rebuilds it from scratch.

## Steps to reproduce
Fixture [`rc4_r3_length256.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/rc4_r3_length256.pdf) (653 bytes; control [`rc4_r3_length128.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/rc4_r3_length128.pdf), same with `/Length 128`; generator [`make_fuzz_rebuilds.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/make_fuzz_rebuilds.py)).
`pdfcraft-cli check-one rc4_r3_length256.pdf`

## Expected
`open-error` for an unsupported or invalid key length (as with `/Length 128`: "the document is protected by a password"), no panic.

## Actual (0.7.1 Windows and main @ dfa43be)
```
thread 'main' panicked at vendor/hayro-syntax/src/crypto/mod.rs:591:40:
range end index 32 out of range for slice of length 16
{"detail":"the file is not a readable PDF: the parser crashed: range end index 32 out of range for slice of length 16", … "status":"open-error:the-file-is-not"}
```

## Analysis
`byte_length` comes from `/Length` unchecked. For the RC4/AESV2 algorithms (R 2–4) the key is at most 16 bytes; clamping to 5..=16 (or returning a `DecryptionError` for anything else) fixes both slices.

## Environment
PdfCraft 0.7.1 (`pdfcraft-0.7.1-windows-x64-portable.zip`), Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200); same on a Linux build of `main` @ dfa43be.

title: Render: a tiling pattern whose /BBox is far larger than its step panics in vello_common (`index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 4294967295`)
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
## Summary
A tiling pattern with `/BBox [0 0 100000 10] /XStep 10 /YStep 10` makes the page renderer panic in `vello_common` 0.0.8 (`src/pixmap.rs:332:17`). The page safety net catches it, but the page does not render. With `/BBox [0 0 10 10]` the same page renders, and poppler renders both. Found by mutation fuzzing; the fixture rebuilds it from scratch.

## Steps to reproduce
Fixture [`tiling_bbox_wide.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/tiling_bbox_wide.pdf) (705 bytes; control [`tiling_bbox_ok.pdf`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/tiling_bbox_ok.pdf); generator [`make_fuzz_rebuilds.py`](https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures/blob/main/pdfcraft/make_fuzz_rebuilds.py)).
`pdfcraft-cli check-one tiling_bbox_wide.pdf`

## Expected
The page renders; the pattern fills the rectangle (or is skipped), no panic.

## Actual (0.7.1 Windows and main @ dfa43be)
```
thread 'main' panicked at …/vello_common-0.0.8/src/pixmap.rs:332:17:
index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 4294967295
{"detail":"p1: renderer crashed on page 1: index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 4294967295", … "status":"page-errors"}
```
Backtrace: `hayro::render_into` ← `pdfcraft_render::raster::render_page`.

## Analysis
In the `Pattern::Tiling` branch of `vendor/hayro/src/renderer.rs` the cell scale is capped by `MAX_PIXMAP_SIZE / bbox.width()` (3000 / 100000 = 0.03), so `x_step = xs * t.x_step` = 0.3 and `pix_width = x_step.abs().round() as u16` = 0. A 0 × N cell pixmap then underflows an index in vello_common. Suggest `max(1)` on `pix_width`/`pix_height` (or skipping the pattern when a cell is under one pixel), and a regression test next to the ones for patch (3) (`tiling_cells_stay_small_whatever_the_step`).

## Environment
PdfCraft 0.7.1 (`pdfcraft-0.7.1-windows-x64-portable.zip`), Windows 11 25H2 (build 26200); same on a Linux build of `main` @ dfa43be. vello_common 0.0.8 from crates.io.

title: Redact: redacting part of a scanned (JPEG) page leaves a blank page with black boxes
author: magdale76
body:
**What happens.** On a PDF made from images (a scan or camera photo, so each page is one JPEG), mark an area for redaction and apply it. The whole page picture disappears: the result is a white page with only the black redaction boxes.

**Expected.** Only the marked areas are removed; the rest of the scanned page stays visible, as Acrobat does.

**Why.** `crates/redact/src/image.rs` clears the covered pixels of a partly covered image, but only for lossless filters (Flate, LZW, RunLength, ASCII85/Hex). A `DCTDecode` image is removed whole (fail-closed), and scanned pages are almost always DCT.

**Proposed fix:** decode grey and RGB JPEGs, clear the covered pixels, and write a new JPEG from the cleared pixels only (nothing of the original stream, such as an EXIF thumbnail, carried over). Keep removing whole what can't be handled safely (CMYK JPEG, JPX, JBIG2, CCITT, a colour space that disagrees with the JPEG). PR follows.

Seen on Windows 11 with a PDF built from photographed pages.

Description

Many organizations, including public administrations, still publish official forms as XFA (XML Forms Architecture) dynamic PDFs created with Adobe LiveCycle Designer. [PROGRAM NAME] cannot render them. Instead of the form, it only shows the fallback page that these files contain, which reads "Please wait... title: Optimize: a page printed as thousands of one-pixel image strips isn't reduced at all; no Mobile preset
author: magdale76
body:
**What happens.** Some PDF printers (seen with Bullzip PDF Printer, which an office program uses to archive its documents) draw a page picture as thousands of images, each one pixel row high, stacked edge to edge: on one real A4 page, 3,300 strips (JPEG and Flate mixed), 4.3 MB in total. Reduce File Size and the PDF Optimizer leave it at 4.3 MB (2 bytes saved). The optimizer works one image at a time, a one-row image can't be resampled, and every JPEG strip repeats its own headers.

**Expected.** Acrobat's optimizer merges image fragments: with its Mobile settings the same page becomes one 795 × 1125 image, 147 KB.

**Also missing:** the optimizer's Settings menu with ready-made presets. Acrobat's Standard matches our Reduce File Size choices (above 225 ppi to 150 ppi, JPEG medium). Its Mobile preset uses colour and greyscale images above 144 ppi to 96 ppi, JPEG high (monochrome above 900 to 600 ppi, CCITT G4).

**Proposed fix:** merge runs of stacked image fragments into one image before the image settings run, and add Standard and Mobile presets to the dialog and to `doc_optimize`. PR follows. Related: #490 (Reduce File Size well behind Acrobat on scans).

The real document is private, so the tests use synthetic pages built the same way.

title: web: host save dispatch marks a document clean and may close it without persistence acknowledgement
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- pdfcraft-readonly-audit:7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a:H8 -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** High
- **Confidence:** High
- **Source revision:** https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/commit/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a (upstream main verified during review).
- **Evidence status:** Static source/caller review. No runtime reproduction, builds, tests, exploit development, or destructive testing was performed. Regression tests below are proposed, not executed.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [`apps/pdfcraft-web/src/main.rs:210–217`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/apps/pdfcraft-web/src/main.rs#L210-L217)
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs:623–640`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs#L623-L640)

The host save callback reports successful postMessage dispatch as Ok. The UI then calls mark_saved and runs its continuation, including close-after-save, without an acknowledgement that the host persisted the bytes.

## Conditions
A same-origin embedding host has no listener, fails an upload/write, or navigates away after the message is dispatched. Inbound origin/source checks are present; this is not an origin-bypass report.

## Impact
PdfCraft can clear unsaved warnings and close the only edited document before any durable copy exists. A later host error cannot restore a closed editor.

## Recommended remediation
Add save request IDs and explicit success/error acknowledgement. Keep the document dirty and defer close until success. Bind acknowledgement to the saved generation so subsequent edits remain dirty.

## Suggested regression coverage
Test absent acknowledgement, host write rejection, close-after-save, and edits while acknowledgement is pending. Ensure a successful acknowledgement cleans only the acknowledged generation.

- [`crates/model/src/lib.rs:85–108`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/model/src/lib.rs#L85-L108)

The seen set is checked only when a node is popped, while every Kids entry is queued with attrs.clone(). Dict owns a vector of objects, so large direct inherited Resources values are deeply cloned for every queued duplicate.

## Assessment

- [`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:4263–4275`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L4263-L4275)

## Root cause and source evidence
- [`crates/automation/src/lib.rs:2323–2334`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/automation/src/lib.rs#L2323-L2334)

The common write_atomic helper writes the staging file, drops the File and renames it without sync_all or sync_data. doc_save then marks the document saved. Desktop saving and the new doc_batch publisher have stronger staging sync behavior.

author: PierrunoYT
body:

## Assessment

- **Source revision:** https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/commit/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a (upstream main verified during review).

The EKU parser leaves extended_key_usage as None when parsing/children extraction fails. signing_problem only rejects a present purpose set lacking a permitted purpose. EKU is on the processed-critical allowlist, so a malformed critical value also evades the unknown-critical gate.

A correctly issuer-signed certificate contains a malformed EKU extnValue. Certificate-signature verification must still succeed; arbitrary forged certificates are not implied.

## Impact
A malformed usage restriction can disappear and allow a Valid verdict instead of a non-Valid/Unknown result.

## Recommended remediation
Record EKU presence before parsing, validate ASN.1 tags/structure, and retain an explicit malformed-extension problem or rejecting purpose set on failure.

## Suggested regression coverage
Issuer-signed certificates with malformed critical and non-critical EKU must be non-Valid. Include valid document-signing EKU and valid disallowed-purpose controls.

## Assessment

## Root cause and source evidence
- [`crates/a11y/src/alt.rs:283–289`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/a11y/src/alt.rs#L283-L289)

clear_parent_tree uses chunks_mut(2), checks pair[0], then indexes pair[1]. A final one-element chunk matching the page key reaches that bounds access. mark_decorative has already replaced page Contents before calling the helper.

## Conditions

## Assessment

- **Source revision:** https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/commit/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a (upstream main verified during review).
- **Evidence status:** Static source/caller review. No runtime reproduction, builds, tests, exploit development, or destructive testing was performed. Regression tests below are proposed, not executed.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [`crates/optimize/src/images.rs:82–90`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/optimize/src/images.rs#L82-L90)
- [`crates/optimize/src/images.rs:101–108`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/optimize/src/images.rs#L101-L108)

The Form walk skips a previously seen reference when depth > 4, and the same seen set spans every page. Effective PPI depends on each invocation transform, so reference deduplication is not sufficient.

## Conditions
A nested shared Form is first invoked at a small displayed size and then at a larger size, including on another page. The deeper later invocation is skipped.

## Impact
The computed minimum PPI misses the largest display use. Optimization can downsample the shared image below that use requirements and permanently blur content.

## Recommended remediation
Use active-path cycle detection separately from transform-sensitive invocation traversal. Bound total work and conservatively preserve images when analysis cannot account for all uses.

## Suggested regression coverage
A deeply nested shared Form invoked at asymmetric scales on one page and across pages. Require PPI/dimensions to reflect the largest use; include cycle and direct repeated-image controls.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [`crates/optimize/src/images.rs:283–296`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/optimize/src/images.rs#L283-L296)

process builds a resized soft mask associated with its original ObjRef; run replaces that original mask object via doc.set(mr, ...). There is no copy-on-write when other image objects share the same SMask.

## Conditions
Two image objects share a soft mask but require different output resolutions, or only one qualifies for downsampling. The size-saving branch publishes the resized result.

## Impact

Allocate a new resized mask and update only the optimized image SMask reference, preserving the shared original for other users.

## Suggested regression coverage

title: cos: object-stream offset casts and addition can wrap on 32-bit targets
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- pdfcraft-readonly-audit:7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a:M15 -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Confidence:** High
- **Source revision:** https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/commit/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a (upstream main verified during review).
- **Evidence status:** Static source/caller review. No runtime reproduction, builds, tests, exploit development, or destructive testing was performed. Regression tests below are proposed, not executed.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [`crates/cos/src/document.rs:843–850`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/cos/src/document.rs#L843-L850)

objstm casts nonnegative i64 First/member offsets to usize and computes first + off without checked conversion/addition or validating the resulting object start against the decoded stream.

## Conditions
On wasm32 or another 32-bit target, large positive values truncate or overflow. On 64-bit usize, adding two nonnegative i64 values does not create this particular addition overflow.

## Impact
Overflow-checked builds can panic; release wrapping can point at a different in-range position and parse the wrong object. Lexer clamping cannot detect an already-wrapped in-range result.

## Recommended remediation
Use checked conversions/addition and validate object-stream offsets against actual decoded extents before indexing.

## Suggested regression coverage
Boundary-value offsets with architecture-independent checked helpers plus wasm32 coverage. Require actionable refusal, retain valid object-stream loading, and avoid architecture-independent claims of a 64-bit overflow.

title: print: synchronous printer option lookup can block the GUI indefinitely
author: PierrunoYT
body:
<!-- pdfcraft-readonly-audit:7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a:M18 -->
## Assessment
- **Severity:** Medium
- **Confidence:** High
- **Source revision:** https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/commit/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a (upstream main verified during review).
- **Evidence status:** Static source/caller review. No runtime reproduction, builds, tests, exploit development, or destructive testing was performed. Regression tests below are proposed, not executed.

## Root cause and source evidence
- [`crates/ui-egui/src/print_ui.rs:689–698`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/ui-egui/src/print_ui.rs#L689-L698)
- [`crates/print/src/spool.rs:40–55`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a/crates/print/src/spool.rs#L40-L55)

The Properties button handler calls spool::printer_options synchronously. On Unix, printer_options_via waits on lpoptions.output() without a deadline or cancellation. The pinned craft-print dependency also uses unbounded submission waits, although desktop submission normally runs off the GUI thread.

## Conditions
lpoptions/CUPS stops responding when the user opens printer Properties. Other spooler hangs can retain background submission resources.

## Impact
The option lookup blocks the GUI thread indefinitely. Background submission hangs do not by themselves establish a GUI-wide freeze; their impact is retained jobs/processes/resources.

## Recommended remediation
Run discovery/options off the UI thread and impose bounded subprocess lifetimes with cancellation and kill/reap handling. Apply an explicit lifetime policy to dependency submission too.

## Suggested regression coverage
Use an injected nonresponding command in a disposable test to verify bounded error delivery and GUI responsiveness; include normal successful options and cancellation cleanup. Do not require a real printer or stuck system service.
