title: Feature Request: Reusable Dynamic Image Stamps with Automatic Date and Time
author: gabglus
body:
**Title:** Feature Request: Reusable Dynamic Image Stamps with Automatic Date and Time

### Description

I would like to request a feature that allows users to create and save reusable custom stamps combining a PNG image with an automatically generated date and time.

This would be particularly useful for business documents, invoices, approvals, and administrative workflows.

### Proposed functionality

- **Custom PNG image:** Allow users to import a PNG image, preserving its transparency.
- **Automatic date and time:** Automatically insert the current date and time when the stamp is applied to a PDF.
- **Customizable format:** Allow users to configure the date and time format, for example, `2026-10-13 15:30`.
- **Flexible positioning:** Allow users to position and resize the stamp on the PDF page.
- **Reusable templates:** Allow users to save custom stamps and reuse them across multiple PDF documents without having to configure them each time.
- **Date and time persistence:** Once applied, the date and time should remain fixed in the document and should not change when the PDF is reopened.
- **Preview:** Display the complete stamp, including the PNG image and generated date and time, before placing it.

### Example use case

I have a company stamp stored as a transparent PNG image. When reviewing or approving an invoice, I want to select my saved stamp, place it on the PDF, and have PdfCraft automatically add the current date and time.

Ideally, this should be available as a single action, without manually inserting a separate text box for the date and time.

### Expected benefit

This feature would make PdfCraft more practical for professional document workflows and reduce repetitive manual work when processing multiple PDFs.

Thank you for your work on PdfCraft and for considering this feature request.

title: [Accessibility] Expose PDF document text and structure to screen readers through AccessKit
author: keyang556
body:
PdfCraft already uses AccessKit and exposes accessibility information for various UI controls. However, the PDF document canvas does not appear to expose the actual document text and structure to assistive technologies in the same way.
Although PdfCraft can extract, search, select, and copy PDF text internally, these capabilities do not necessarily make the document readable through screen readers such as NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, or Orca.
I would like to request an accessible document representation for the PDF viewer, similar to the implementation recently added to WordCraft in PR #489, which fixed WordCraft issue #488.

title: Feature Request: Toggle Line Weights / Thin Lines View (Parity with Acrobat's Ctrl+5)
author: eranco7
body:
### Problem Description
When viewing complex mechanical drawings, blueprints, or CAD-generated PDFs, vector line weights can appear incredibly thick or muddy on-screen. This makes it difficult to read detailed schematics or select precise elements when zooming in or out.

### Proposed Solution
I would love to see a "Toggle Line Weights" feature added to PdfCraft, mapping to the **Ctrl + 5** keyboard shortcut (or **Cmd + 5** on macOS) to match Adobe Acrobat's behavior. When toggled off, it should force the rendering engine to display all vector strokes at a uniform, minimal width (1 pixel on screen) regardless of the zoom level or the stroke width specified in the document metadata.

### Alternatives Considered
Currently, I have to jump back into Adobe Acrobat or a full CAD suite just to inspect fine details in technical and mechanical drawings, which breaks the workflow of using PdfCraft as a daily-driver PDF workbench.

### Additional Context
As noted in the roadmap, the application aims for Acrobat Pro workflow parity. A "thin lines" view is a must-have for engineers, architects, and anyone dealing with precise drafting or vector blueprints.

author: musaad-sharikh
body:
PdfCraft draws its whole interface in the embedded Inter, whatever the desktop's default interface font is, and Preferences has no setting to change it. On a desktop where every other application follows the fontconfig default, PdfCraft is the one that does not.

### Use case

My fontconfig defaults are Rubik for `sans-serif` and Vazirmatn for Arabic. GTK and Qt applications follow them. I would like PdfCraft's menus, panels and dialogs to do the same, or to let me pick the interface font.

### Current limitation

- Preferences offers "Interface size" but no interface font.
- The Flatpak sandbox already sees the user's fonts: `fc-match sans-serif` run inside it returns Rubik, and `fc-match sans-serif:lang=ar` returns Vazirmatn.
- The only installed face PdfCraft loads is a last-resort fallback taken from a fixed file list, not from fontconfig. The log shows:
  `interface font fallback: /usr/share/fonts/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf (face 0)`
  which is the runtime's DejaVu Sans, not a font the user chose.

### Desired outcome

Either of:

- an "Interface font" setting in Preferences (system default, or a chosen installed family), with Inter kept as the default; or
- on Linux, resolve the interface font and its fallbacks through fontconfig, so the user's defaults apply.

### Environment

- PdfCraft 0.7.1, Flatpak (`org.freedesktop.Platform` 25.08), x86_64
- CachyOS Linux, niri 26.04, Wayland

### Where it comes from (v0.7.1)

- `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` inserts Inter first in the proportional family.
- `candidates()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs` probes fixed file names under `/usr/share/fonts` and `/usr/local/share/fonts`.

Related: storytold/gridcraft#229, storytold/photocraft#2291.

title: Crash on window close on Touch Bar MacBooks (NSTouchBarFinderObservation KVO exception)
author: shaiar
body:
## Description
PdfCraft crashes every time the window is closed, with "PdfCraft quit unexpectedly".

## Environment
- PdfCraft 0.7.1
- macOS 26.7 (25G229)
- MacBook Pro 16" 2019 (MacBookPro16,1), Intel, **has Touch Bar**

## Steps to reproduce
1. Launch PdfCraft
2. Close the window
3. App crashes (100% reproducible)

## Crash details
`EXC_BAD_INSTRUCTION (SIGILL)` on the main thread, caused by an uncaught Objective-C exception during the display-cycle flush:

```
-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]
-[NSObject(NSKeyValueObserverRegistration) removeObserver:forKeyPath:context:]
-[NSObject(NSKeyValueObserverRegistration) _removeObserver:forProperty:]
objc_exception_throw
...
+[NSApplication _crashOnException:]
```

AppKit's Touch Bar subsystem tries to remove a KVO observer from a view/window that's already been torn down (or was never registered). This looks like a winit window-teardown ordering issue on Touch Bar Macs, so updating eframe/winit may fix it.

Possibly related to #1690 (same KVO exception on Apple Silicon; that machine may also have a Touch Bar).


Full crash report attached.

[PdfCraft-crash-report.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33385669/PdfCraft-crash-report.txt)

title: Greek characters cannot be rendered when adding new text to a PDFcraft
author: itdepartment-ux
body:
### Problem

Existing Greek text in PDFs displays correctly, but adding new Greek text fails.

The Add Text font selector offers Helvetica, Times and Courier. Typing Greek characters produces this warning:

“The PDF text fonts can't draw ‘Μ’ (U+039C). Choose supported text.”

In another text insertion workflow, the text is saved but Greek characters appear as `?`, with a warning that the appearance remains incorrect in every PDF viewer.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a PDF containing existing Greek text.
2. Select Add Text.
3. Type `Βασίλης — Ελληνικά: ά έ ή ί ό ύ ώ ς`.
4. Attempt to commit and save the new text.

### Expected behavior

New Greek text should render correctly after saving and reopening the PDF. It should also remain searchable and copyable.

### Actual behavior

Depending on the insertion tool, Greek text is either refused or saved with `?` in its visual appearance.

### Possible implementation direction

An initial review of main suggests that:

- `crates/edit/src/added.rs` writes ordinary added text using standard-14 fonts and WinAnsiEncoding.
- `crates/fonts/src/script.rs` already uses the bundled Inter font as a fallback for Greek signature text.
- `crates/fonts/src/embedding.rs` already provides Unicode font embedding.

Could Add Text reuse the existing embedding support with a Greek-capable bundled font such as Inter? Text measurement, wrapping, alignment and Unicode extraction would also need to use the selected font correctly.

FreeText annotation appearances may need a corresponding change in `crates/annot/src/appearance.rs`.

This is a suggested implementation direction, not a tested patch.

### Environment

- PdfCraft version: Latest
- Operating system: Windows 11

title: Please cut a release with 759cfa6 (redaction, signature validation) and f9d7aa7, plus an advisory
author: oracola91
body:
v0.7.1 (7163ba3) is the latest release. Two security fixes landed on `main` after it:

- **759cfa6** (#1631), "Security: fix three audit findings in redaction and signature validation". From its message:
  - Apply Redactions and Remove Hidden Information could leave removed image samples and form text in the saved file, through inherited or shared `/Resources`, "while the operation reported success".
  - The reader that judges post-signing changes and the renderer could treat a set-aside cross-reference entry differently, so the validator "reported the signature Valid while the page showed the new content".
- **f9d7aa7** (#1653), the line-length cap before `auth` on the `--control` channel.

Neither commit is in v0.7.1 (compare v0.7.1...759cfa6 and v0.7.1...f9d7aa7 both show "ahead, behind 0"), so every published build still has these.

Requests:

1. Cut a release that contains both.
2. Publish a GitHub Security Advisory that names the affected versions, so users and dependency scanners notice.
3. Until then, a short README note: don't rely on redaction or signature verdicts in v0.7.1 or earlier. "Where it stands" currently lists "passwords, redaction and sanitizing" and "basic digital signatures" under **Good today**.
4. 759cfa6 also lists what it doesn't cover yet: "originals named by a form XObject's own /Resources, by an annotation appearance or by a pattern". An issue tracking those would tell users where redaction is still incomplete.

title: Releases: document the expected signer identities, add build provenance and an SBOM
author: oracola91
body:
I verified the v0.7.1 downloads and they check out. The macOS DMG, app and CLI carry Developer ID "Learning Machines LLC (DJ6XS33FX8)" and are notarized (ticket stapled on the DMG and the app). The Windows MSI and both exes are Authenticode-signed through Trusted Signing as "Learning Machines Inc". It took some digging to establish that, and a few additions would make it easy for anyone:

1. **Name the expected identities** in the README downloads section: the Apple Developer ID name and Team ID, and the Windows signer subject. The README says "Installers and executables are code-signed" and "Signed and notarized" without saying by whom, so nobody can pin them or notice a change.
2. **Build provenance.** `actions/attest-build-provenance` in the release job would let anyone run `gh attestation verify <file> -R storytold/pdfcraft`. Signing `SHA256SUMS.txt` (Sigstore/cosign) would also work. Today `SHA256SUMS.txt` sits next to the files it covers and isn't signed, so it shows a file is intact, not who built it.
3. **An SBOM per release**, for example CycloneDX via `cargo cyclonedx`, listing the vendored forks (hayro, lopdf, winit, egui-wgpu) with their upstream base versions.
4. **Signed Linux packages** (deb/rpm repository metadata or detached signatures). `docs/releasing.md` notes the Linux and FreeBSD packages have no code signing.

title: Hardening ideas: isolate parsing and rendering, coverage-guided fuzzing, script time limit, stronger digital ID files
author: oracola91
body:
The README says fuzzing "still turns up crashes and hangs on hostile files". Some suggestions, roughly by impact:

1. **Isolation.** Parse and render in a separate low-privilege process: an XPC service with App Sandbox on macOS, an AppContainer or low-integrity process on Windows. Today only the Flatpak build is confined, and `packaging/macos/entitlements.plist` says the app "is not sandboxed". The vendored hayro renderer enables its `unsafe` feature (SIMD JPEG, JPEG 2000 and JBIG2 decoders), so `unsafe_code = "forbid"` in the first-party crates doesn't cover the most exposed code.
2. **Fuzzing.** Coverage-guided targets (cargo-fuzz / libFuzzer with AddressSanitizer) for the parser, stream filters, fonts and image decoders, and possibly OSS-Fuzz. Hangs could fail the nightly run. Crash reproducers could stay out of public workflow artifacts until they're fixed. Related: #997.
3. **Form JavaScript.** A wall-clock limit for AcroForm scripts (XFA already has a timeout), and perhaps a per-document prompt before scripts run.
4. **Digital ID files.** New .p12 identities use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 2048 iterations (`crates/sign/src/pkcs12.rs`, `const ITER: u32 = 2048`) and a 6-character minimum password (`crates/ui-egui/src/sign_ui.rs`). Raising both, in line with current OWASP password-storage guidance, would make a copied .p12 much harder to brute-force.
5. **Helper tools by absolute path.** On macOS, `/usr/bin/defaults` is called by absolute path, with a comment explaining why. The CUPS tools (`lpoptions` in `crates/print/src/spool.rs`; `lpstat` and `lp` per the v0.7.1 binary) are called by bare name. When the app or CLI is started from a terminal, a user-writable folder early in `PATH` decides which one runs.
6. **Windows build flags.** The v0.7.1 exes have ASLR and DEP but not Control Flow Guard. `-C control-flow-guard` would add it.

title: OCR downsample setting does not shrink a page box stored in pixels, so recognition saturates CPU and memory
author: ihsanmokhlisse
body:
## What happened

Recognize Text on an image-only PDF pegs every performance core and holds about 2 GB, then gives the memory back when the job ends. The "Downsample to" choices (72, 150, 300, 600 dpi) do not change the bitmap for this file.

PdfCraft 0.7.1, commit `7163ba3dee8becfff6871c9a65d0d8314314742b`, macOS arm64, Apple M3 Pro (6 performance cores + 6 efficiency cores, 36 GB RAM).

## The file

66 pages, PDF 1.6, no text layer on any page, so "skip pages that already have text" skips nothing. Each page is one full-page JPEG.

- MediaBox `2263 × 3200` pt (about 31 × 44 in). A letter page is `612 × 792` pt.
- Page content is only `2263 0 0 3200 0 0 cm` / `Do`.
- 64 pages: image `2263 × 3200` px, placed at 1 pixel per point (7.2 megapixels, about 29 MB of RGBA).
- 4 pages: image `3789 × 5359` px, about 1.66 px/pt.

The page box is the bitmap's pixel size, so "72 dpi" is already the full image.

## Process evidence

One live run of Recognize Text on all pages:

| When | CPU | RSS |
|---|---|---|
| Job running | about 306% | 1.82 GB |
| Workers just finished | 0%, cumulative CPU time 7:52 | 1.94 GB |
| Next 25 seconds | 0% | 605 MB down to 411 MB |

`ps -M` during the run showed six threads with about 1:12 of user time each. That matches rten's pool, which uses `hw.perflevel0.physicalcpu` (6 on this machine). Idle PdfCraft afterwards sits near 400 MB, so this is the job's working set, not a leak that keeps growing.

## Where the scale is chosen

`crates/engine/src/ocr.rs`, `OcrJob::run`:

```rust
let wanted = self.settings.dpi.clamp(72.0, 600.0) / 72.0;
let scale = self.native.get(page).copied().flatten().map_or(wanted, |n| n.clamp(1.0, wanted));
```

`n` is the image's pixels per point. Here `n` is `1.0` and `wanted` is at least `1.0`, so every dpi choice renders the same `2263 × 3200` bitmap. The `1.0` floor is right for a low-resolution letter page (scale 1 there is only `612 × 792`). On a page box this large, the same floor is the full scan, and the dialog can…

title: Feature Request: Search Across All Open PDF Documents
author: bereaarrow
body:
**Title: Feature Request: Search Across All Open PDF Documents**

**Description**

It would be very useful to add a feature that allows users to search for keywords across all currently open PDF documents at once.

For example, Foxit PDF Reader supports searching for a keyword across multiple open PDF documents, allowing users to find relevant information without searching each document individually.

**Proposed Feature**

- Allow users to search for a keyword across all currently open PDF documents.
- Display matching results from all open documents, ideally showing the document name, page number, and matching text.
- Allow users to navigate directly to a search result in the corresponding document.

**Use Case and Benefits**

When working with multiple PDF documents, users often need to find the same keyword or piece of information across several files. Currently, searching each document individually can be time-consuming and inefficient.

A global search across all open PDFs would significantly improve productivity and make it easier to compare information across documents.

Foxit PDF Reader is an example of an application that already provides this functionality.

Thank you for considering this feature request!

title: Redaction: `pattern=phone` also marks parts of other numbers
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `redact_mark pattern=phone` marks the two phone numbers in the fixture but also parts of an IBAN, a SIRET and a French social security number (NIR). The result is a half-redacted identifier that still shows its first digits.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1, Windows 11 x64 portable.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```
python -c "import fitz;d=fitz.open();p=d.new_page();[p.insert_text((50,80+30*i),t) for i,t in enumerate(['NIR 1 85 05 78 006 084 36 end','IBAN FR76 3000 6000 0112 3456 7890 189','SIRET 123 456 782 00010','tel 01 23 45 67 89 / +33 1 23 45 67 89'])];d.save('ids.pdf')"
```
(example numbers.) `steps.json`: `doc_open path=ids.pdf`, `redact_mark doc=1 pattern=phone`, `redact_apply doc=1`, `doc_save doc=1 path=out.pdf`.

**Actual.** `marked: 5`. PyMuPDF text of `out.pdf`: `NIR 1 85 / end / IBAN FR76 3000 6000 / SIRET 123 / tel / `. The two phone numbers are removed (good), plus the trailing digit groups of the NIR, IBAN and SIRET.

**Expected.** Only the two phone numbers are marked. A digit group that continues a longer run of digit groups (as in an IBAN or SIRET) is not taken for a phone number; how to detect that is up to you.

**Why / use case.** French administrative documents, redacted by an agent without a GUI. A phone pattern that leaves the start of an IBAN visible is worse than none, because the agent assumes the identifier is gone.

**Notes.** `phone` is a heuristic and I understand some false positives are accepted; the case here is a partial match inside a longer number. Related: #162.

python -c "import fitz;d=fitz.open();p=d.new_page();p.insert_text((50,80),'Call 01 23 45 67 89');d.save('m2.pdf')"
```

```
[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"m2.pdf"}},
 {"tool":"redact_mark","args":{"doc":1,"pattern":"phone"}},
 {"tool":"redact_apply","args":{"doc":1}},
 {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"path":"m2_out.pdf"}}]
```
```
pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root .
pdfcraft-cli audit m2_out.pdf        # exit code 1
```

**Actual.** `{"count":1,"findings":[{"covered_text":"Call","kind":"covered-text","page":1,"rect":[72.0,759.8,145.392,770.8]}]}` then `audit: 1 faux redaction(s) found`. The digits are not extractable from `m2_out.pdf` (PyMuPDF gives `Call`), and the reported rectangle starts where `Call ` ends.

title: redact_mark: accept a caller-supplied regex (optionally with a checksum validator)
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `redact_mark` can find content in three ways: `find` / `words` (literal strings), `rect` (a position), or `pattern` (one of five fixed values: `phone`, `email`, `credit-card`, `ssn`, `date`). There is no way to give a regular expression. Any identifier that is not one of the five (a national ID number, a company registry number, a tax number, an internal reference) can only be redacted if the caller already knows its exact value.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1, Windows 11 x64 portable (the `redact_mark` schema in `pdfcraft-cli tools`).

**Steps to reproduce.** A page containing two fictitious numbers in the same format, `ids.pdf`:
```
python -c "import fitz;d=fitz.open();p=d.new_page();[p.insert_text((50,80+30*i),t) for i,t in enumerate(['Ref 1 85 05 78 006 084 36 end','Ref 2 91 12 34 567 890 12 end'])];d.save('ids.pdf')"
```
`steps.json`: `doc_open path=ids.pdf`, `redact_mark doc=1 pattern=ssn`.

**Actual.** `nothing matched, so nothing was marked`. `ssn` is the US format. To redact both numbers the caller has to extract the text, find them with its own regex, and pass the exact strings in `words`.

**Suggestion.** An optional `regex` argument on `redact_mark` (same page scoping as `find`), marking every match. Optionally a `validate` value (for example `luhn`, `mod97`) that keeps a match only if its checksum is valid, which cuts false marks on digit sequences. The existing `pattern` values stay as they are. The naming and the regex flavour are your call; the point is that a caller can supply its own pattern, so region-specific formats do not need to be built in one by one.

**Why / use case.** pdfcraft is driven by an agent through `run --script` / MCP, on administrative documents from several countries (for example French social security numbers and company registry numbers, which follow a fixed format and a checksum). Each country has its own formats; a caller-supplied pattern covers all of them without pdfcraft maintaining a list, and keeps t…

title: Field detection: comb boxes are missed, or turned into check boxes
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `form_detect_fields` does not recognise a row of adjacent drawn boxes (comb field: postcode, date, number written one character per box). Depending on box size the row gives no field, or one check box per cell.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1, Windows 11 x64 portable. #93 notes that comb boxes were not detected yet.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```
python -c "
import fitz
d=fitz.open();p=d.new_page(width=595,height=842)
p.insert_text((40,80),'Postcode A',fontsize=10)
for i in range(5): p.draw_rect(fitz.Rect(120+i*18,62,138+i*18,84),color=(0,0,0))
p.insert_text((40,180),'Postcode B',fontsize=10)
for i in range(10): p.draw_rect(fitz.Rect(120+i*16,162,136+i*16,182),color=(0,0,0))
d.save('comb.pdf')"
```
`steps.json`: `doc_open path=comb.pdf`, `form_detect_fields doc=1 add=false`.

**Actual.** Row A (5 boxes, 18x22 pt): no field. Row B (10 boxes, 16x20 pt): 10 fields of kind `checkbox`, `Check Box1` ... `Check Box10`.

**Expected.** One `text` field per row spanning the row. Suggestion: report the cell count, and when added set `max_length` to it and the comb flag (`form_set_props` already supports comb). A single isolated square stays a check box; the minimum number of adjacent cells that makes a comb is your call.

**Why / use case.** French administrative forms (CERFA-style) use comb boxes for postcodes, phone numbers, dates and IBAN. An agent filling a form with `form_detect_fields` + `form_fill` cannot know that ten check boxes are one number, or gets nothing, and has to read the content stream itself.

**Notes.** Related: #93 (closed), #294, #1721 (scans), #1596 (merged; I have not retested on main).

title: `form_add_field`: text fields always get a fixed 12 pt font, so text is clipped in a short box
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** Text fields created by `form_add_field` (and by `form_detect_fields add=true`) get `/DA (/Helv 12 Tf 0 g)`. In a box shorter than the font, the text is cut off. `form_set_props font_size=0` (auto) fixes it afterwards.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1, Windows 11 x64 portable.

**Steps to reproduce.** `steps.json`:
```
[{"tool":"doc_create","args":{"from":"blank","pages":1,"width":300,"height":100}},
 {"tool":"form_add_field","args":{"doc":1,"type":"text","page":1,"rect":[20,20,200,28],"name":"t8"}},
 {"tool":"form_add_field","args":{"doc":1,"type":"text","page":1,"rect":[20,50,200,62],"name":"t12"}},
 {"tool":"form_set_props","args":{"doc":1,"field":"t12","font_size":0}},
 {"tool":"form_fill","args":{"doc":1,"values":{"t8":"Hello world","t12":"Hello world"}}},
 {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"path":"ff.pdf"}}]
```
Then read the widgets' font size (PyMuPDF `widget.text_fontsize`) and render `ff.pdf`.

**Actual.** `t8` (8 pt high): font size 12, text cut at the box edges. `t12` (set to auto): font size 0, text fitted. Fields added by `form_detect_fields add=true` are also size 12.

**Expected.** Suggestion: automatic font size by default for new text fields, or a `font_size` argument (0 = auto) on `form_add_field`. Whichever you prefer; an explicit size should not change.

**Why / use case.** An agent creates many fields in one script and cannot look at a render to see the clipping, so a default that clips fails silently.

**Notes.** Related: #294 (field detection and defaults).

title: `doc_optimize`: optional target size (suggestion)
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `doc_optimize` takes fixed settings, so a caller with an upload limit has to retry with other settings until the file is small enough. Would an optional target size fit the tool? If `doc_reduce` and `doc_batch` are considered enough, feel free to close.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1, Windows 11 x64 portable.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```
python -c "
import fitz,random
random.seed(1)
pm=fitz.Pixmap(fitz.csRGB,fitz.IRect(0,0,1600,1200),False);pm.set_rect(pm.irect,(200,100,50))
for i in range(0,1200,7): pm.set_rect(fitz.IRect(0,i,1600,i+3),(random.randint(0,255),random.randint(0,255),random.randint(0,255)))
d=fitz.open();p=d.new_page();p.insert_image(p.rect,pixmap=pm);d.save('img.pdf')"
```
`steps.json`: `doc_open path=img.pdf`, `doc_optimize doc=1 path=out.pdf` gives `bytes_after` 626717 (from 5763577); with `color={"downsample":true,"ppi":72,"compression":"jpeg","quality":30}` it gives 407293.

**Suggestion.** An optional `target_bytes`: the tool tries stronger settings until the output fits, reports the settings used, and says explicitly (`target_reached: false`) when it cannot get there. Without it, nothing changes.

**Why / use case.** Online portals and mail gateways impose size limits (for example 2 MB per attachment). An agent otherwise guesses settings and loops.

**Notes.** `bytes_before` / `bytes_after` are already reported, which helps the loop. Different from #1783.

title: Relative path not found: the error does not show the resolved path
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** With `--root DIR`, relative paths resolve against `--root`, as the schema says. When one does not exist, the error shows the path as typed plus a raw OS message, not where it looked.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1, Windows 11 x64 portable (the OS message follows the system language).

**Steps to reproduce.** In a directory `work` containing `sub/a.pdf`, with `work` as current directory:
```
echo '[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"sub/a.pdf"}}]' > steps.json
pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root sub
```

**Actual.** `pdfcraft-cli: step 1 (doc_open): sub/a.pdf: Le chemin d'accès spécifié est introuvable. (os error 3)`. It looked for `sub/sub/a.pdf`; with `"path":"a.pdf"` the run works.

**Expected.** Suggestion: name the resolved path and the root in the message, for example `sub/a.pdf not found (looked for <abs>/sub/sub/a.pdf, --root <abs>/sub)`.

**Why / use case.** An agent often builds a script from a working directory that differs from `--root`; a localised OS error with no resolved path gives it nothing to correct from.

**Notes.** Minor.

title: Script runner: one structured result for the whole run (suggestion)
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `pdfcraft-cli run --script` prints each step's JSON result as a separate pretty-printed object on stdout, and a failure as one plain-text line on stderr. A caller cannot tell from stdout alone which step failed, nor parse the output as one document.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.7.1, Windows 11 x64 portable.

**Steps to reproduce.**
```
python -c "import fitz;d=fitz.open();d.new_page();d.save('a.pdf')"
```
`steps.json`:
```
[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"a.pdf"}},
 {"tool":"page_rotate","args":{"doc":1,"pages":[999],"degrees":90}},
 {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"path":"b.pdf"}}]
```
```
pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root . > out.txt 2> err.txt ; echo $?
```

**Actual.** Exit code 1. `out.txt` has the result of step 1 only (12 lines, one object); `err.txt` has `pdfcraft-cli: step 2 (page_rotate): page 999 is out of range: the document has 1 pages`. With several successful steps, stdout is several concatenated JSON objects. The step index and tool name appear only in the stderr text.

**Expected.** Suggestion: an opt-in way (a flag, so existing output stays identical) to get one JSON document for the run, with per step the index, tool, status and result or error, so the failed step is identifiable. How later steps are reported is up to you. Exit codes unchanged.

**Why / use case.** pdfcraft is driven by an agent that builds a multi-step script and reads the outcome. With concatenated objects and a text error line, the agent has to split the stream and parse the message to learn which step failed and whether an earlier `doc_save` ran.

**Notes.** The `doc_batch` report (on main) already returns a structured per-file result; this asks for the same for `run --script`.

title: Flatpak: Print dialog finds no printers (no CUPS tools or socket in the sandbox) – tracking issue for the print portal
author: chilllla
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.7.1 (Flatpak bundle, runtime `org.freedesktop.Platform` 25.08), Fedora 44, KDE Plasma, Wayland

**What happens:** The host has working CUPS queues (`lpstat -p` lists three, `lpstat -e` seven more destinations), but in the Print dialog only "Print to PDF" is available. No local printers are listed.

**Cause:** `craft-print` finds printers by running `lpstat -p -d` and `lpstat -e` (and `lpoptions`/`lp` for options and submitting). Inside the sandbox these commands don't exist and neither do `/run/cups/cups.sock` or `/etc/cups`, so the printer list is empty. I checked with `flatpak run --command=sh ai.storyteller.pdfcraft -c 'command -v lpstat'`.

The Flatpak manifest already says so (`packaging/linux/flatpak/ai.storyteller.pdfcraft.bundle.yml`): "No CUPS socket either: printing runs the `lp` command, which the freedesktop runtime doesn't ship, so Print reports that the spooler is unavailable until it goes through the print portal." I couldn't find an issue tracking that, so this is meant as one. It probably affects every Craft app with a Print command, since they share `craft-print`; I only tested PdfCraft.

**Suggested direction (as in the manifest):** use `org.freedesktop.portal.Print` for the Flatpak build, so printing works without extra permissions. A fallback could be to bundle the CUPS client tools and talk to the host's CUPS, but that needs socket access.

**Workaround that worked for listing printers:** wrapper scripts named `lpstat`, `lpoptions` and `lp` that run `flatpak-spawn --host --env=LC_ALL=C --env=LANG=C <cmd> "$@"`, placed first in `PATH` via `flatpak override`, together with `--talk-name=org.freedesktop.Flatpak`. The `LC_ALL=C` is needed because `flatpak-spawn --host` doesn't forward the app's environment and the parser only understands English output. With this, `lpstat -p -d` inside the sandbox lists the host's printers. I haven't tested actually submitting a job. This also gives the app permission to run arbitrary host co…

title: Single Page view: scrolling past the bottom of a zoomed-in page should go to the next page
author: codyvogt
body:
**Description**

In Single Page view, when a page is zoomed in far enough to be taller than the window (common with large multipage drawings), the mouse wheel and trackpad only pan within the page. Once you reach the bottom, further scrolling does nothing: you have to use the page box, the arrow keys or the rail buttons to get to the next page.

Acrobat turns the page in this case: keep scrolling down at the bottom edge and it shows the next page, scrolled to its top. Scrolling up at the top edge shows the previous page, scrolled to its bottom.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. Open a multipage PDF (e.g. a drawing set).
2. View → Page Display → Single Page.
3. Zoom in until the page is taller than the window.
4. Scroll down with the wheel or trackpad until the bottom of the page.
5. Keep scrolling.

**Actual:** the view stays at the bottom of the current page.
**Expected:** the next page is shown, at its top. In reverse, scrolling up at the top shows the previous page at its bottom.

**Notes**

- Today, wheel paging in Single Page view (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs`, `wheel_pager.rs`) only runs when the whole page fits (`fits && ...`). Zoomed in, the wheel goes to the `ScrollArea` instead and stops at the edge.
- One wheel notch or trackpad gesture at the edge should turn one page, so momentum from a swipe that reaches the bottom doesn't skip several pages. `WheelPager` already handles this for pages that fit.
- Continuous view already scrolls across pages, but it isn't a workaround for long because the layout choice doesn't persist (#289, #1495).

Related: #289, #1742, #752

I'm happy to take a crack at this if nobody else picks it up.

title: Feature request: Drag pages from Organize Pages grid to file manager to extract them
author: CubicleNate
body:
**Summary**

In the Organize Pages view, allow selected page thumbnails to be dragged out of the application window and dropped into a file manager (Windows Explorer, Linux file managers, etc.). The dropped pages should become PDF files.

**Desired behavior**

- Select one or more pages in the Organize Pages grid.
- Drag the selection out of the PdfCraft window and drop it into a folder in the file manager.
- Result:
  - Single page → a single-page PDF.
  - Multiple pages → either one multi-page PDF containing the selection, or one PDF per page as an option (either is fine; the former is probably more useful by default).
- Feature works on Windows and Linux Desktop (and ideally macOS if the same mechanism can support it).

**Current workaround**

Select pages → use the Extract command → save the new document manually.

**Why this is useful**

Quick extraction of individual pages or small selections without going through the Extract dialog and Save As. Very useful for organizing out large scans of PDFs into their individual files. This is a feature that you can do in Adobe's PDF application.

**Additional notes**

- Should respect the current selection and page order.
- Nice-to-have: holding a modifier key (example: Shift or Ctrl) could switch between “one PDF per page” vs “one multi-page PDF” and when the key is not held a menu pops up..
- The reverse of supporting dragging into the grid from the file manager would be nice but that can be separate request.

title: [BUG] Visual layout glitch when rotating pages
author: SezarTheGreat
body: ### Bug Description A visual layout glitch occurs in PdfCraft when attempting to rotate the **very first page** of a PDF document. While subsequent pages seem to rotate or display correctly, applying rotation to Page 1 causes the page content container to distort, overflow, or render with improper aspect ratios/orientation clipping relative to the surrounding UI. The point is that the rotation applies to the subsequently next page but not to the first page. ### Steps to Reproduce 1. Open **PdfCraft** and load a multi-page PDF document (e.g., `Unit 1 Data Mining.pdf`). 2. Go to the **Edit** mode panel. 3. Select the **1st page**. 4. title: MCP: form_set_props puts oneOf at the top level of its input schema, so Claude-based clients reject the whole tool list
author: andreero0
body:
## What happens

With `pdfcraft-cli mcp` (without `--compact`) attached to an agent that runs on Claude, every prompt fails before the model sees it. In Kiro the error is:

```
Error sending prompt: tools.408.custom.input_schema: input_schema does not support oneOf, allOf, or anyOf at the top level
```

The index changes with how many other tools the client has loaded, but it lands on `form_set_props`. Anthropic's tool API refuses a request if any one tool's `input_schema` has `oneOf`, `anyOf` or `allOf` at the top level, so a single tool takes down the whole session, including conversations that never touch forms.

## Cause

`crates/automation/src/tools.rs`, in the `form_set_props` definition (added in #650):

```rust
input["oneOf"] = json!([{ "required": ["field"] }, { "required": ["fields"] }]);
```

It is the only tool that does this. I checked by asking `pdfcraft-cli mcp` for `tools/list` and filtering for top-level `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf`: 161 tools, one hit, `form_set_props`. `--compact` avoids it only because `form_set_props` is not in the core list.

## Why removing it loses nothing

The handler already enforces the rule. `form_set_props` in `crates/automation/src/forms.rs` returns "give either field or fields, not both" when both or neither are given, and the descriptions of `field`, `fields` and the tool already tell the agent to use one or the other.

## Reproduce

1. Add `pdfcraft-cli mcp --root <dir>` to an MCP client backed by a Claude model (Kiro, Claude Code or Claude Desktop).
2. Send any prompt.
3. The request is rejected with the error above. Removing pdfcraft from the client makes it work again.

## Suggested fix

Drop the top-level `oneOf` and keep the check in the handler. A check in `tool_table_is_well_formed` that no tool has a top-level `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` would stop it coming back. I have a PR ready that does both.

Environment: macOS (Apple silicon), PdfCraft 0.7.1, `pdfcraft-cli` built from main.

title: ui-egui: `commands::a_tool_chosen_with_no_document_asks_for_one_and_runs_on_it` fails on main on every platform
author: snipeTR
body:
On `main` at 7437bde378f43856eada40af25b983812e615e8a, `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test commands` fails on every CI platform. This turns every open PR's test jobs red, whatever the PR changes.

**Failing test:** `commands::a_tool_chosen_with_no_document_asks_for_one_and_runs_on_it`, at `crates/ui-egui/tests/commands.rs` around line 188–190. It fails at one of two assertions:
- `the picked file is open`: `h.state().active` is still `None` after `run_command("export.text")` with `pick_override` set and `run_steps(3)`. Seen on Windows and FreeBSD.
- `and the tool runs on it: None`: the file opened, but the Export dialog didn't. Seen on Ubuntu.

**Sometimes also failing:** `commands::the_open_recent_menu_lists_files_and_opens_one`, at line 292: `the recent file opened in a new tab`, `left: 1, right: 2`.

**Where it was seen:**
- `main` CI: run https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/38360385134
  - test (ubuntu-latest): both tests fail;
  - test (windows-latest): the first test fails.
- `main` FreeBSD: run https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/38360385993. Both tests fail.
- PR #1181: run https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/38365349909. The same first test fails on ubuntu and windows.
- Locally on Linux (no GPU, lavapipe), `upstream/main` checked out on its own: the first test fails on every run, and the second fails sometimes.

**Reproduce:** `cargo test -p pdfcraft-ui-egui --test commands a_tool_chosen_with_no_document_asks_for_one_and_runs_on_it`

The root cause hasn't been investigated. Either opening the picked file and then running the deferred command no longer happens within the frames the test steps, or the test no longer matches how the command now opens files. Per AGENTS.md the test shouldn't be skipped; the fix is either in the deferred open-then-run path or in how the test waits for it.

title: render: two raster tests hit their time limits on the FreeBSD qemu runner
author: snipeTR
body:
On PR #1181, the FreeBSD job failed in `pdfcraft-render --lib`: 267 tests passed and 2 failed after 284 s. The PR doesn't touch `crates/render`. Both failures are deadline assertions on the slow emulated VM.

**Failing tests:**
- `raster::tests::waiting_worker_can_cancel_before_initializer_returns`
  - Panic at `crates/render/src/raster.rs:1369`: `assertion failed: std::time::Instant::now() < deadline`.
  - Follow-on panic in another thread at `raster.rs:1343`: `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: RecvError`.
- `raster::tests::page_contents_and_nested_forms_share_one_budget`
  - Panic at `raster.rs:4427`: `a self-painting form must not stall the renderer: Timeout`.

In the same run, `raster::tests::user_unit_scales_the_page_and_everything_on_it` ran for more than 60 s and still passed. That suggests the VM is simply slow, not that the renderer stalls.

**Job:** https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/actions/runs/38365350904. FreeBSD 15 (build + test), job 115189036869.

On `main` at 7437bde, the FreeBSD job failed earlier, in `pdfcraft-ui-egui --test commands` (see the issue for that test). Its log doesn't show whether these render tests pass there.

**Suggestion:** make the time limits robust to slow runners rather than skip the tests. Two options:
- Measure progress instead of wall-clock time.
- Scale the deadlines with an environment variable that the FreeBSD workflow sets.

Either way, a real stall should still fail.

title: [Bug] PDF to DOCX conversion loses paragraph breaks and formatting

title: Print: remember two-sided, grayscale, scaling and comments & forms across restarts
author: magdale76
body:
## Problem

The Print dialog keeps its choices only for as long as the app is open (`open_print` rebuilds the draft with `..keep`), and `persist`/`restore` save none of them. Every launch starts from the factory defaults: Two-sided off, colour, Fit, Document and markups.

That hurts most where PdfCraft is opened once per document. In a small office I help with, another program opens each PDF in a fresh PdfCraft to print it, so an office that always prints two-sided, or always in grayscale, has to set the same options again for every single document.

The paper size is already covered by #1103 (#1212 for a remembered default, #1692 for paper by PDF page size, both persisted). This issue is about the rest of the dialog.

## Proposal

Persist the last used value of the options that describe *how this office prints*, and keep resetting the ones that describe *this one job*:

| Remember across restarts | Keep per job (reset as today) |
|---|---|
| Two-sided (off / long edge / short edge) | Copies (a leftover "5" from yesterday is an expensive surprise) |
| Grayscale | Pages to print (all / current / range / selected) |
| Size mode (Fit, Actual size, Shrink, Custom %) and the custom % | Orientation: stays **Auto**, so each page follows the PDF; a remembered Portrait would turn every later landscape document wrong |
| Comments & forms | Multiple / Booklet / Poster layouts (one-off imposition jobs) |
| Collate | |

Details:

- Settings are untrusted input: an unknown or malformed value is ignored and the default used, as for the other entries in `restore`.
- Two-sided is remembered as the user's choice; with a printer whose driver can't print two-sided the existing warning still applies.
- Open question for maintainers: should the last **printer** be remembered too, when it isn't the system default? It would help offices printing to a non-default queue, but falls back badly when that printer is gone (it would have to fall back to the default silently).

body:
## Summary

The native Add Header and Footer dialog accepts Russian Cyrillic text and renders it correctly in its page preview, with OK enabled. Applying the same settings fails because the fixed Helvetica output font cannot draw Cyrillic. There is no font selector in this dialog, so a bilingual Russian/English footer cannot be added.

## Environment

title: [Bug] Windows: Printing to PostScript cloud printer spools massive uncompressed EMF (1.4GB for 8 pages) and fails with Win32 Error 1
author: bobby0316
body:
### Environment
- **OS**: Windows 11 x64
- **PdfCraft Version**: 0.7.1
- **Printer**: DingTalk Smart Cloud Printer (`钉钉智能云打印机`)
  - **Driver**: `DingTalk PDF Printer` (Uses Windows PostScript driver `PSCRIPT5.DLL` + `ghostpdf.ppd`)
  - **Port Monitor**: `DTPRINTERMON:`
  - **Print Processor**: `winprint`

---

### Description
When printing an 8-page PDF document to a PostScript-based virtual/cloud printer (DingTalk Cloud Printer) via PdfCraft, the print spool file balloons to **1.42 GB** and the job fails mid-transfer. Printing the exact same document using Adobe Acrobat Pro works normally with minimal spool size (a few MBs).

---

### Event Log & Diagnostic Details

From `Microsoft-Windows-PrintService/Admin` (Event ID 372):
```text
TimeCreated      : 2026/10/13 18:22:16
Id               : 372
LevelDisplayName : Error
Message          : The document 打印文档, owned by user, failed to print on printer 钉钉智能云打印机. 
                   Data type: NT EMF 1.008. 
                   Size of the spool file in bytes: 1426195908 (~1.42 GB). 
                   Number of bytes printed: 1424792820. 
                   Total number of pages in the document: 8. 
                   Number of pages printed: 7. 
                   Win32 error code returned by the print processor: 1 (ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION).
Root Cause Analysis
Uncompressed High-DPI GDI Rasterization: In crates/print/README.md, it is noted:

"Windows renders sheets through Windows.Data.Pdf and spools them... Not yet: PostScript output."

author: sampaiodias
body:
## Problem

With Preferences > Reading colours > White on black enabled, scrolling down to a page that has not rendered yet briefly displays a completely white page. Once rendering finishes, the page turns black with white text. This bright flash is uncomfortable and defeats the purpose of dark reading colours.

Reported by the user on Windows. The flash lasts fractions of a second. No personal document is required to describe the issue.

## Reproduction

1. Open a multi-page PDF.
2. Set Reading colours to White on black.
3. Scroll down to a page whose render is not cached.
4. Observe the page background while rendering is pending.

## Expected

The page placeholder should immediately use the configured reading background, including custom colours, and remain consistent until the rendered page appears. Reading colours disabled should retain white paper.

## Code inspection

The reading canvas currently fills every page rectangle with Color32::WHITE before drawing its cached texture or rendering placeholder (crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs). This is a likely cause, based on source inspection; the agent has not reproduced the GUI symptom.

## Related

#1548 concerns highlighted text in dark reading colours. #187 concerns flashes of earlier pages in a two-page spread. This report concerns the white loading background specifically.

title: Masking
author: ABEL243
body:
# Mask and cutout quality across the Craft apps — field report and proposal

**From:** a LightCraft / PhotoCraft user (non-commercial use, Windows)
**Apps tested:** LightCraft 0.7.1, PhotoCraft 0.8.2, EffectCraft 0.9.2, FilmCraft 0.7.2, VectorCraft 0.10.0 (installed through the ArtCraft launcher)
**Source read:** `storytold/lightcraft` @ `b3d392b4` (2026-10-13), `storytold/photocraft` `main` (2026-10-13)
**Machine:** Intel Core Ultra 7 255H (16 cores), Intel Arc 140T iGPU (15 GB shared, driver 32.0.101.8826), 31 GB RAM, Windows 11 Pro

## TL;DR

In every app of the suite, automatic masks fail to extract shapes reliably: the subject is found roughly, edges are
soft or bleed into the background, and fine structures (hair, fingers, thin objects) are lost. The causes are
structural, not tuning issues:

1. **No learned segmentation model is used for Subject / Background / Remove Background** in any app. LightCraft and
   PhotoCraft use saliency heuristics (PhotoCraft adds GrabCut). The code says so itself.
2. **The one learned model in the suite (SAM 3 in LightCraft) runs on the CPU on Windows and Linux**, with a
   288 × 288 output and a non-letterboxed 1008² input: about 1.5–2.5 minutes per photo here, and coarse edges.
3. **Each app re-implements segmentation separately** (PhotoCraft and EffectCraft each ship their own GMM + max-flow),
   so improvements in one app never reach the others.

I prototyped a fix in a LightCraft fork (BiRefNet, MIT licence, through the existing DNG-matte path). Results and
pitfalls are below, with a proposal for a shared segmentation component.

| Mask | Result | Time |

| **Background** | the inverse of the above, same errors | instant |

title: Allow installed system fonts (incl. .ttc collections) for editing existing PDF text, honouring fsType
author: spoonek8
body:
### Summary

When editing text in an existing PDF, *Load font…* / *Installed fonts…* only accepts fonts whose name table declares an open licence. On Windows this rules out the fonts most CJK business documents are actually set in (e.g. Microsoft JhengHei `msjh.ttc`, PMingLiU `mingliu.ttc`), so edited paragraphs can never match the surrounding text. I'd like to request an opt-in way to use installed fonts, gated on the font's own embedding permissions.

### Environment

- PdfCraft 0.7.1 (official Windows build)
- Use case: Traditional Chinese (zh-Hant, Taiwan) office documents exported from Word

### Current behaviour

Selecting an installed Windows font fails with:

> select an openly licensed font whose name table declares its licence (OFL, Apache, Ubuntu, Bitstream Vera or MIT)

As far as I can tell from the source, two separate checks block this:

1. `crates/fonts/src/embedding.rs` → `validate_document_input()` requires an open-licence string in name ID 13 (and excludes some families by name).
2. `validate()` rejects font collections ("select a standalone TrueType/OpenType font (not a font collection)"), so even with the licence check removed, `.ttc` system fonts can't be loaded.

Since PDFs exported from Word typically embed only a subset of the original font, adding any character not already in the document is impossible without changing the paragraph to a different typeface.

### Why this seems feasible

- **PhotoCraft already does this.** Its font database (`crates/text/src/fonts.rs`) scans the platform font directories and reads faces from collections via `skrifa::FontRef::from_index`. PdfCraft already depends on skrifa, so collection support looks like a small change.
- **PdfCraft already reads installed fonts at runtime** for the UI fallback (`crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs`, which even probes `msjh.ttc` for zh-Hant). A user-chosen font read from the user's own machine at runtime would likewise never be bundled or shipped with PdfCraft, consistent wit…

title: Cannot input Chinese text, incomplete font enumeration & improper fallback logic
author: siberzhang
body: Bug: Error message: PDF文本字体无法显示“我”(U+6211)。请选择支持的文本。 the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+XXXX Reproduce steps: 1. Create a new blank PDF in PDFCraft. 2. Add a new text box, the default font is Helvetica. There is NO font selection dropdown for this new text box. 3. Type common Simplified Chinese character like "我" (U+6211), error pops up immediately. 4. Check the font list in edit panel: only a tiny number of fonts show up (SimSun, Calibri, Helvetica etc.), most system-installed Chinese fonts (Microsoft YaHei, Noto Sans SC) are missing from the list, even they are properly installed on Windows. Root cause analysis: 1. When creating new text, it defaults to Helvetica (Latin-only font), and there is no prompt/UI to switch to a CJK font. 2. The program fails to enumerate all system fonts, so user cannot pick available Chinese fonts manually. 3. Once glyph missing, it falls back to hard-coded BIZ UDPGothic (Japanese font), which does not contain many simplified Chinese glyphs, resulting in failure to save edits. Suggestions: 1. Fix system font enumeration, list all installed valid fonts, including Chinese CJK fonts. 2. For Chinese locale: set a CJK font as default for new text box, instead of Helvetica. 3. Always provide font selector when creating/editing text. 4. Replace BIZ UDPGothic fallback font with full CJK font such as Noto Sans CJK SC. 5. Gracefully handle missing glyph, avoid blocking text saving.

title: Bug: RTL (Hebrew/Arabic) text rendering is reversed and cursor positioning is broken
author: gold-360
body:
**Describe the bug**
There are two major issues when working with RTL text (such as Hebrew or Arabic) in tools like **"Fill & Sign"** and **"Edit PDF"**:

1. **Reversed Text:** The characters are rendered left-to-right. For example, typing "שלום" results in visually reversed text ("םולש").
2. **Broken Cursor Positioning:** When clicking in the middle of an existing RTL sentence to insert a new word, the newly typed text appears in a completely different location within the sentence. The visual cursor placement does not match the logical text index.

**Steps to Reproduce**
1. Open any PDF in PdfCraft.
2. Go to the **Fill & Sign** or **Edit PDF** tool.
3. Type Hebrew or Arabic characters. See that the text is written left-to-right (reversed).
4. Try clicking in the middle of a sentence you just typed to add a word.
5. Notice that the text is inserted at the wrong position.

**Expected behavior**
- RTL text should be rendered right-to-left in its correct visual order.
- Clicking in the middle of an RTL sentence should place the cursor at the correct logical index so text is inserted exactly where clicked.

**Proposed Solution / Context**
These are classic symptoms of missing Complex Text Layout (CTL) and Bidirectional (Bidi) text support. Most underlying open-source PDF manipulation libraries draw strings sequentially LTR by default and lack logical-to-visual cursor mapping.

A common workaround without rewriting the core PDF library is to utilize a lightweight bidi algorithm library (such as `bidi-js`). This can be used to:
1. Compute the correct visual order before drawing the text to the canvas.
2. Map visual mouse clicks to their correct logical character indices.

Here is a conceptual implementation for the text-rendering pipeline:

title: Feature request: faster text editing, symbol insertion, and object duplication
author: Xeen404
body:
## Problem Statement
Current editing workflows require high mouse precision and excessive clicking to perform repetitive tasks like inserting arrows/checkmarks or duplicating layout elements. This slows down annotation and formatting significantly.

## Proposed Solutions

### 1. Quick Symbol & Action Insertion
Introduce a lightweight UI component (e.g., floating toolbox) with a dedicated small toggle button to show/hide the toolbox, allowing users to:

- **Resize Handles:** Expand the clickable area of corner/edge handles by ~4-8px outward.
- **Move Zone:** Allow dragging from anywhere within the expanded margin, not just the visible border/text content.
- *Visual Feedback:* Optionally highlight the active zone on hover to indicate interactivity.

Implement standard OS-level editing behaviors for selected objects (text boxes, shapes, images):
- **Copy/Paste:** `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+V` (macOS: `Cmd+C` / `Cmd+V`).

title: Support detached CAdES signatures (.pdf.p7s): open and verify the pair
author: edurbs
body:
Title: Support detached CAdES signatures (.pdf.p7s): open and verify the pair

## Context

#1449 added attached CAdES envelope support (`.pdf.p7m`, PR #2126): the envelope opens as its embedded PDF, read-only, with the signer identified and the content digest checked. Detached signatures were deliberately deferred: a `.p7s` holds only the signature and certificates — the signed document sits *beside* it (`determina.pdf.p7s` next to `determina.pdf`), the shape written by `openssl cms -sign` without `-nodetach` and used in some PEC and EU workflows.

## Current behaviour (after #2126)

- Opening the `.p7s` alone → precise refusal: "this is a detached CAdES signature; the signed document is not inside the file".
- Opening the sibling `.pdf` → a normal, fully editable PDF; the detached signature is not seen, verified, or shown, and editing it silently invalidates it.

## Desired behaviour

1. **Primary:** opening `X.pdf.p7s` finds the sibling document (strip one trailing `.p7s`, else try `X.pdf`), opens it like a `.p7m` — read-only, notice bar with signer, signing time and the digest verified **over the sibling's bytes**, marked "detached" so the user knows the signature lives in a separate file.
2. **Optional, needs a maintainer call:** opening `X.pdf` when `X.pdf.p7s` sits beside it offers the same verification (a notice, not a behaviour change). Costs a stat on every file open; may surprise users who don't care about the signature.

## Design questions

- Missing sibling → actionable error naming the expected file; both-missing vs sibling-without-`.p7s` cases.
- Sibling modified since signing → open read-only with "the content does not match what was signed" (the `digest_ok` machinery from #2126 already computes this).
- Read-only by default, or an explicit unlock? Unlike `.p7m`, the document here is the user's own file; but any edit invalidates the detached signature, so the #1449 posture (read-only + explicit action) is the natural default.
- Multiple `.p7s` files …

title: Update the vendored hayro-jbig2 to pick up merged upstream robustness fixes
author: oracola91
body:
pdfcraft vendors hayro-jbig2 under `vendor/`. A few robustness fixes for malformed JBIG2 input have since been merged upstream in LaurenzV/hayro, and the vendored copy looks to predate them:

- LaurenzV/hayro#1455 - reject reused symbol-dictionary contexts with a mismatched template
- LaurenzV/hayro#1457 - avoid integer overflows on extreme values
- LaurenzV/hayro#1278 - cap maximum symbol instances with a heuristic

Could you refresh the vendored hayro crates to a commit that includes these? It is a maintenance bump, no behaviour change for valid files.

Separately, one related fix is still open upstream and worth watching rather than acting on now: LaurenzV/hayro#1392 and its fix PR #1393, which cap the graphics-state stack depth. A later refresh would pick it up once it merges.

Happy to help confirm the vendored version if useful.

title: GoToR: relative-path remote-document open skips the approval prompt and is not path-normalized
author: oracola91
body:
Follow-up to #1265 (open local GoToR PDF links natively). The native GoToR open treats absolute and relative targets inconsistently, and the relative path is not normalized.

- For an **absolute** GoToR target the link is parked for user approval before any file is opened (`pending_remote_link`).
- For a **relative** target the file is opened immediately, with no approval prompt.
- The relative target is also joined onto the source document's parent directory with no `..` handling, so a relative spec containing `..` resolves to a `.pdf` outside the source document's folder.

Impact is limited, so this is a consistency and defense-in-depth item rather than a security hole: the result is a read-and-display of a regular `.pdf` (<=1 GiB), it is shown to the user and never sent anywhere (the app makes no network requests), and it still requires the user to click the link. But a relative target skips the gate that absolute targets get, and can point outside the source folder.

Evidence (at `main` c1a41cc):
- `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1623-1628` - absolute paths set `pending_remote_link` and return; the relative branch calls `open_resolved_remote_link(...)` directly with no prompt.
- `crates/engine/src/links.rs:203-205` - `resolve_remote_document_path` does `parent.join(path)` with no `..` stripping or confinement (it does reject `//`, `\\` and URL schemes elsewhere, and absolute paths are handled, but relative `..` is not).
- Read is bounded at `crates/engine/src/links.rs:215-233` (`read_remote_document`: regular `.pdf`, size cap), which keeps the impact to opening an unexpected local PDF.

Suggested direction: route relative GoToR targets through the same pending-approval gate as absolute ones, and lexically resolve or reject `..` in the relative join so a target cannot escape the source document's directory.

title: Summary of PDF Rendering Issues Across Multiple Test Cases
author: xAMOKx
body:
I tested PDFCraft using the Ghent PDF Output Suite 5.0, a standardised test suite developed by the Ghent Workgroup to evaluate the correct processing of PDF/X-4 documents.

The results reveal several apparent rendering problems, particularly involving overprinting, transparency, DeviceN colour spaces and image compression.

**Steps to reproduce**
- Download the freely available Ghent PDF Output Suite 5.0: https://gwg.org/resources/ghent-pdf-output-suite/
- Open the six-page test PDF in PDFCraft.
- Examine the individual test patches and compare them with the embedded reference images and expected results.

**Observed issues**
The attached screenshots show several visible failure indicators, including:
- GWG 1.1 (CMYK Overprint Mode): A visible X indicates that Overprint Mode 1 is not being respected.
- GWG 19.0–19.2 (DeviceN Overprint): Incorrect rendering of black, yellow and white overprinting, with visible X markers where solid-colour rectangles are expected.
- GWG 16.1–16.2 (Transparency Blend Modes): Multiple X markers suggest incorrect handling of transparency groups and blend modes, including isolated and non-isolated transparency.
- GWG 17.3 (JBIG2 Compression): A prominent X appears where no X should be visible.
- GWG 2.0, 4.1 and 12.0 (Spot Colour and White Overprinting): Visible X markers suggest incorrect overprint behaviour.
- GWG 13.0 (ICC Source Profile): Several visible X markers suggest that ICC source profiles are not being handled correctly.
- GWG 17.2 (JPEG2000 Compression): A visible X indicates an apparent rendering problem.

Additional test patches also warrant examination. Some results depend on colour management and overprint preview settings, so the underlying causes need to be verified.

title: Reduce File Size: let the user pick a quality before it runs (it currently re-encodes lossless line art as JPEG q60)
author: AMJ1308
body:
## Environment
- PdfCraft 0.7.1, signed and notarized macOS universal build
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1 Pro

## What happens
**Reduce File Size…** starts as soon as it's chosen, with one fixed preset: `ImageSettings::REDUCE`, which downsamples to 150 ppi above 225 ppi and encodes as **JPEG quality 60**. It applies to colour and grey images ([`crates/optimize/src/lib.rs:77`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.7.1/crates/optimize/src/lib.rs#L77), called from [`create_ui.rs:228`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.7.1/crates/ui-egui/src/create_ui.rs#L228)). Nothing asks what the file is for. Fine-grained control exists in **Optimize PDF…**, but the one-click tool most people use gives no choice.

Measured on the publicly available *2024 Ford Ranger Owner's Manual* (643 pages, 64.2 MB, 1,372 images):

| | Original | After Reduce File Size |
|---|---|---|
| File size | 61.2 MB | 8.7 MB (−86%) |
| Lossless (Flate) images | 234 | 123 |
| JPEG images | 1,138 | 1,249 |
| Pages / bookmarks / text matches for "tire pressure" | 643 / 235 / 122 | 643 / 235 / 122 ✅ |

The size reduction is excellent and nothing structural was lost. However, **111 lossless images, mostly line-art and technical illustrations, were converted to JPEG q60**. At print resolution (300 dpi) the result is visibly softer, with blurred edges on the drive-mode dial (page 350). `reduce-compare-p350-300dpi.png` shows the original on the left and the reduced copy on the right.

For an owner's manual read on screen this is fine. For a contract, an invoice with a logo, or anything printed, it isn't. Today the user only sees it after the file is saved.

## Suggestion
Before running, show a small chooser:

| Preset | Images | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Screen / email** (current behaviour) | 150 ppi, JPEG q60 | smallest file |
| **Print** | 300 ppi, JPEG q85, keep lossless images lossless | keeps line art crisp |
| **Keep image quality** | no downsampling; only recompress streams, drop thumbnails and…

author: AMJ1308
body:
## Environment
- PdfCraft 0.7.1, signed and notarized macOS universal build
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1 Pro

## What happens
1. Open any PDF and choose **E-Sign ▸ Fill & Sign ▸ Sign**. Place a saved (drawn) signature.
2. Press **⌘S**.

The saved file contains the signature as a `/Stamp` annotation with its own appearance stream. Read back with pypdf:

```
/Stamp  Rect [150, 226, 206, 258]  has /AP: True
```

Any PDF editor, including PdfCraft's own Select tool, can move or delete it. I understand this is the documented default:
- `flatten_fill_sign_on_save: false` ([`lib.rs:830`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.7.1/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L830));
- the parity note says *"The option defaults off, so a normal save leaves them editable"* ([`parity/acrobat-features.toml:5296`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.7.1/parity/acrobat-features.toml#L5296)).

## Why it matters
- **The setting is hard to find.** It sits in **Preferences**, between the comment-author name and the JavaScript options ([`js_ui.rs:467`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.7.1/crates/ui-egui/src/js_ui.rs#L467)), not in the Fill & Sign toolbar where the user is working. In a full audit of the app I didn't know it existed until I read the source.
- **Nothing tells the user.** Saving gives no hint that the signature is still a removable layer. People who sign rental agreements, leases and invoices and email them on assume the signature is part of the page.
- **The docs read the other way.** The essentials table in [`docs/target-app-parity.md:133`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.7.1/docs/target-app-parity.md#L133) lists "Fill & Sign tools; flatten on save" without "(opt-in)". That reads as if flattening happens.

## Suggestion
Keep the safe engine default, but make the choice visible where it's made:

1. **First save after placing a signature or initials:** show a one-time prompt.
   > *Lock your signature into the page?* Locked signatures can't be moved …

title: [Bug] Default paper size resets to US Letter instead of preserving A4
author: filippo-musso
body:
### Environment

* **OS:** Windows 11 x64
* **PdfCraft Version:** 0.7.1
* **Application Language:** Italian (Italy)

### Description

PdfCraft does not persist the selected paper size between sessions.

The default paper size is always set to **US Letter**, whereas I need **A4** to be the default paper size.

Even after manually selecting A4 in PdfCraft's print settings, the application resets the paper size to US Letter after closing and reopening the application.

This forces me to manually select A4 every time I print a document.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open PdfCraft.
2. Open the print page or print settings.
3. Change the paper size from **US Letter** to **A4**.
4. Close PdfCraft.
5. Reopen PdfCraft and navigate to the print page.
6. Observe that the paper size has reverted to **US Letter**.

### Expected Behavior

* The selected paper size should persist between application sessions.
* Once A4 has been selected, it should remain the default paper size when PdfCraft is reopened.
* Ideally, the application should respect the user's saved print preferences or the default paper size configured for the selected printer.

### Actual Behavior

* The paper size defaults to US Letter.
* Selecting A4 does not persist after closing the application.
* Every time PdfCraft is reopened, I must manually select A4 again.

### Impact

This behavior creates unnecessary repetitive work and increases the risk of printing documents with the wrong paper size.

For users in countries where A4 is the standard paper format, having US Letter as a persistent default is inconvenient.

title: Feature Request: Support macOS PDF Services in the Print Dialog
author: BigBobDalton
body:
First of all, thank you for developing PDFCraft. I'm enjoying using it and would like to suggest an improvement to its printing workflow on macOS.

Currently, PDFCraft appears to list only active printers registered with CUPS in its print destination selection. This means macOS PDF Services, such as **Faxbot**, are not available as selectable destinations.

Faxbot is installed as a macOS Automator Print Plugin under `~/Library/PDF Services/Faxbot.workflow`. It works correctly from other applications through the macOS PDF Services mechanism, but it does not appear in PDFCraft's printer list because it is not registered as a conventional CUPS printer.

**Feature request**

Would it be possible to support macOS PDF Services alongside conventional printers in PDFCraft?

Ideally, users could select a PDF Service such as Faxbot directly from PDFCraft's printing workflow, without first exporting the document to a PDF file and then opening or dragging it into another application.

This would also benefit users of other macOS PDF Services and workflow extensions, not just Faxbot.

I understand that PDFCraft may use a custom printer-selection interface or a CUPS-based printing API, so this may require a different integration approach. I'm interested to know whether supporting native macOS PDF Services is feasible.

**Environment**
- macOS 27.0.1 (Golden Gate)
- Apple Silicon Mac Studio
- PDF Service: Faxbot (`de.hosy.Faxer`)
- Faxbot works correctly from other applications.

Thank you for considering this request.

author: oracola91
body:
On `main` (9931329), Save and Save As both write incrementally. `save_doc_to` uses `save_bytes` for either target (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs:667`), which appends a revision to the original bytes (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:3723-3731`, `crates/cos/src/writer.rs:185-188`). A full rewrite happens only for redaction, Remove Hidden Information, Sanitize, an encryption change and repaired files. `save_full_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:3734`) exists, but the UI never calls it.

So content removed with Delete Pages, Edit Text, deleting an image, comment or attachment, changing form fields, cropping or editing metadata is still in the earlier revision of the saved file. PdfCraft's own "View revision" shows it, and so does any tool that reads earlier revisions. Many users will expect Save As to a new file to give them a clean copy.

`docs/architecture.md:51` lists "Save As with garbage collection" among the full rewrites, but the UI doesn't do that today.

Possible fixes, any of them:

1. Save As to a new path does a full rewrite for unsigned documents (signed ones have to stay incremental).
2. Call `require_full_save` after removal-type edits (delete pages, delete images, annotations or attachments, edit text), as redaction already does.
3. At least, a short note when saving a document that has earlier revisions, with a "save an optimized copy" option.
4. Align `architecture.md:51` with the behaviour.

title: Saving: overwrites the file on disk without checking it, and some writers skip the #1698 reopen check
author: oracola91
body:
Two data-safety gaps in the save path on `main` (9931329).

**1. Saves overwrite the file on disk without checking it**

- Save writes over whatever is on disk without comparing it with the version that was opened or last saved (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs:657-689`).
- The changed-on-disk notice doesn't say that Save will overwrite the newer version, and Save clears it (`file_watch.rs:354-375`).
- The same file can be open in two tabs (`open_path` at `lib.rs:1692` has no "already open" check) or in two instances.
- A second instance also lists the first one's live autosaves as crash leftovers (`recovery.rs:159-165`, no lock or liveness check), so Discard there deletes them (`recovery.rs:261-268`).

Possible fixes:
- Compare the file's stamp with the one from open or last save, and ask before overwriting.
- Focus the existing tab when a file is already open.
- Add a per-process lock or pid check in the recovery store.

**2. Some writers skip the #1698 reopen check**

Only Save and Save As run `check_save` before replacing (`editing.rs:667`). Other paths write PDFs without it:
- Sign & save (`sign_ui.rs:451`);
- the OCR batch (`ocr_ui.rs:241`; see also #1795);
- the CLI edit commands, which write `--out` with plain `std::fs::write` (`apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/main.rs:472`, `488`, `499`, `521`). That truncates first, so `--out` equal to the input plus a failed write leaves no good copy;
- automation without `--root` (`crates/automation/src/lib.rs:155`, kept so `/dev/stdout` works).

Possible fixes:
- Route PDF replaces through `write_atomically` plus `check_save`.
- In the CLI and automation, use the atomic writer for regular files and keep plain writes for character devices only.

title: Web build: a save can be marked done when nothing was saved (host bridge, download)
author: oracola91
body:
Two places on `main` (9931329) where the web build marks a document saved without knowing that it was.

**1. Host bridge (`?host=parent`)**

Saves go to the parent with `targetOrigin` set to PdfCraft's own origin (`apps/pdfcraft-web/src/main.rs:147-163`). If the embedding page is on another origin, the browser drops the message without an error. The README's embedding is same-origin, so this is a setup mistake, but an easy one to make. `post()` still returns Ok, so the document is marked saved and the leave-page warning is cleared (`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs:624-631`). The edits are then lost when the tab closes.

Possible fix: refuse host mode unless the parent is same-origin, or wait for a reply such as `pdfcraft:saved` before marking the document saved.

**2. Download**

`download()` clicks the link, revokes the object URL straight away and returns Ok (`editing.rs:981-996`), and the document is marked saved. If the user cancels the browser's save dialog, or the browser hasn't read the blob yet, the work is still marked saved and the leave-page warning is gone.

Possible fixes:
- Delay the revoke.
- Use `showSaveFilePicker` where the browser has it.
- Keep the unsaved state until the save is confirmed, or say "download started" rather than "saved".

Related: #422 (embedding API), #812 and #856 (leave-page warning).

title: Small prompts: Extract/Split of protected PDFs, editing signed documents, Remove Security
author: oracola91
body:
Three small prompts that could prevent surprises, from `main` (9931329):

1. **Extract and Split of a protected PDF.** Combine tells the user that the result won't keep the source's protection (`crates/ui-egui/src/combine_ui.rs:357-364`). Extract (`files.rs:589`) and Split (`files.rs:723`) of an encrypted document write unencrypted files with no such note. The same note there, or an option to keep the source's protection, would help.
2. **Editing a signed or certified document.** There is no heads-up before the first edit; the signature banner only changes afterwards. Rewrites that would break a signature are already refused. A one-time confirmation before the first edit, mentioning the allowed changes when the document is certified, would let the user stop before invalidating a signature.
3. **Remove Security.** It applies with only a toast (`crates/ui-egui/src/commands.rs:188-191`). Undo exists, but a confirmation would make it harder to drop protection by accident.

title: Release packages: licence and notice files missing from some packages, and no third-party notices
author: oracola91
body:
From reading the packaging scripts and NOTICE on `main` (9931329). The licence texts in the repo ask for their notices to travel with copies, and some packages don't carry them today. This is about what those texts ask for, not a legal reading.

1. **The AppImage and the macOS app ship no LICENSE or NOTICE.** The AppImage step moves `usr/share/doc` out of the AppDir (`packaging/linux/package.sh:130`). The macOS `.app` never calls `copy_docs`; only the CLI zip does (`packaging/macos/package.sh:186`).
2. **No third-party notices for the Rust dependencies.** About 765 locked packages (MIT, BSD, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0 and others) are compiled in, and no package carries their notices. A generated `THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES` file (cargo-about, or from the SBOM requested in #1845), shipped in every package and linked from About, would cover it.
3. **Licence texts for compiled-in assets** are in no package:
   - Inter, JetBrains Mono and Dancing Script under the OFL (`crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs:323-326`, `crates/fonts/src/script.rs:7,11`);
   - the egui default fonts (Ubuntu Font Licence, Hack/Bitstream Vera, Noto Emoji OFL);
   - the Foxit fonts and Adobe CMap data under BSD-3. NOTICE:40-49 has their copyright lines, but not the conditions and disclaimer.

   NOTICE:12-22 also points to `ATTRIBUTION.md` and `assets/...` paths that the packages don't include.
4. **The MSI and craft-fonts.** The portable zip copies the craft-fonts OFL files (`packaging/windows/package.ps1:139-146`), but the MSI doesn't (`packaging/windows/pdfcraft.wxs:171-190`). NOTICE:28 says the packages carry them.
5. **Lucide is ISC and MIT.** The icons derived from Feather are MIT (second part of `assets/icons/LICENSE-lucide.txt`). NOTICE:15 and `ATTRIBUTION.toml` record ISC only.
6. **Small consistency points.**
   - NOTICE:29 names Noto Sans Thai, while `ATTRIBUTION.toml` names Noto Sans Arabic for craft-fonts.
   - NOTICE:32 and :35 say hayro and lopdf come "via crates.io", but both are vendored. The ven…

title: Windows: Printer enumeration takes ~53 seconds every time Print dialog opens (v0.8.0)
author: OG-CosmicDog
body:
## Description

PdfCraft v0.8.0 has a significant delay when detecting installed Windows printers. When opening the Print dialog, physical printers do not appear immediately and take approximately 53 seconds to populate.

This happens **every time the Print dialog is opened**, not just on the first attempt after launching PdfCraft.

The issue was also present in v0.7.1, but printer detection took approximately 10 seconds. Version 0.8.0 appears to have made the delay significantly worse.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Launch PdfCraft v0.8.0 on Windows.
2. Open any PDF document.
3. Press Ctrl+P to open the Print dialog.
4. Observe that installed printers are initially missing.
5. Wait approximately 53 seconds for the printers to populate.
6. Close the Print dialog and reopen it.
7. Observe that the delay occurs again.

## Expected Behavior

Installed Windows printers should appear within a few seconds of opening the Print dialog.

## Actual Behavior

- **v0.7.1:** Approximately 10 seconds to detect printers (estimated).
- **v0.8.0:** 53.41 seconds to detect printers (measured).
- The delay occurs every time the Print dialog is opened.
- Once detection completes, the installed printers appear correctly.

## Environment

- Application: PdfCraft v0.8.0
- OS: Windows
- Printers: KONICA MINOLTA bizhub C550i, HP OfficeJet 6960, Microsoft Print to PDF, OneNote

## Additional Information

Version 0.8.0 introduced changes to the Windows printing implementation using `craft-print`. I'm not sure whether this is related, but the printer detection delay became significantly longer after updating.

title: Scanned PDFs become blurry on every zoom, even in previously viewed areas
