body:
## Bug Description

When viewing scanned or image-based PDFs, zooming in causes the image to become temporarily blurry. After waiting, the image becomes clear.

However, even when zooming out and then returning to the exact same area, the image becomes blurry again and requires another wait.

2. Zoom into an area and wait until the image becomes sharp.

## Expected Behavior

Previously viewed areas should ideally display sharply without requiring repeated rendering delays. Zooming and panning should be responsive when working with large scanned documents.

## Actual Behavior

Each zoom operation causes temporary blurriness and a noticeable delay before the image becomes sharp again, including areas already viewed.

## Additional Information

- Regular text/vector-based PDFs perform noticeably better.
- The issue is particularly noticeable with scanned engineering drawings.

title: Linear gradient fills with soft mask (/SMask) rendered as solid opaque black polygons (axial shading)
author: olekkut
body:
### Bug Description
In PDFs exported from Microsoft Word containing shapes with linear gradient transparency, **PdfCraft** renders the gradient shapes as **100% opaque solid black polygons**, completely skipping the soft mask (`/SMask`) and opacity levels.

The same document renders properly in **Google Chrome (v155, PDFium)** and **Adobe Acrobat Reader**.

---

### Comparison Screenshots

| Expected (Google Chrome PDF Viewer / PDFium) | Actual (PdfCraft 0.7.1) |
| :---: | :---: |
| ![Expected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/557a1c2f-ef15-4429-96a7-1df73ea12b7d) | ![Actual](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8c8e7dd-a389-469f-b44c-0737ff422d2f) |

---

### Technical Details & Relation to PR #2132
* **PDF Structure:** The shaded overlay shapes use an **axial shading pattern** (`/ShadingType 2`) combined with a luminosity soft mask (`/SMask`).
* This appears to be directly related to the issue described in #2128 and the ongoing work in PR #2132 (*"fix(render): a soft mask fades a gradient fill again"*), where `vello_cpu` takes a fast-path optimization for opaque gradients on covered tiles and bypasses the soft mask.
* I am sharing this minimal reproducible PDF test case exported directly from MS Word so it can be verified against PR #2132.

---

### Test File

title: [Feature Request] Add image export naming options
author: MrZwij
body:
When using the Export All Images function, PDFCraft currently exports images with this naming convention:

`{filename}_Page_{page number without leading zero}_Image_{image number with 3 leading zeroes}.{extension}`

**First request**
- Add leading zeroes to {page number} by default

**Second request**
- All leading zeroes should be appropriate for the number of digits in the number of pages or images. For example, if there are 20 pages, there should be one leading zero in {page number}. If there are 500 images, there should be two leading zeroes in {image number}.

**Third request**
These user-customizable options:

1. Include the original image name (if available)
2. Change the {filename} prefix to user-customizable text (empty text is possible).
3. Change the separators between output fields ({filename}, {page number}, etc.)
4. Option to change or remove {page number} prefix
5. Option to remove {page number}
6. Option to change or remove {image number} prefix
7. Option to remove {image number}
8. Option to reorder filename fieldsIf the user has set up their options in such a way that it would result in duplicate filenames, then automatically append a number to the end of the exported image.

I think the simplest way to implement and use this would probably be a quasi regex string that's customizable by the user, with an option explaining the various usable fields in the string. Something like this:

`{pdffilename}_pg{pagenumber}_img{imagenumber}_{originalimagename}
`

title: Feature request: native PKCS#11 hardware-token signing for PDFs
author: andrecards
body:
# Feature request: native PKCS#11 hardware-token signing for PDFs

## Summary

Add native signing with PKCS#11 tokens to PdfCraft's existing digital-signature flow. A local Linux prototype signed a PDF with an A3 token, and Poppler's `pdfsig` reported a valid cryptographic signature covering the whole document. The test does not establish a trusted certificate chain or revocation status. I can contribute a synthetic SoftHSM2 test and a focused implementation after agreeing on the API and rebasing onto current `main`.

## Proposed behavior

- Discover PKCS#11 modules and token slots, with an explicit module path override. Show a token's signing certificates only when the matching private key is available.
- Ask for the PIN once per signing operation. Keep it out of command-line arguments, logs, automation responses and saved settings. Clear it after signing, cancellation or error. Support protected authentication on the device or reader.
- Sign through the private key on the token, include available intermediate certificates, and verify the returned signature against the selected certificate before writing the PDF.
- Keep PDF writes atomic. Report an absent token, incorrect or locked PIN, ambiguous identity and unsupported per-operation authentication as actionable errors.
- Provide equivalent engine, CLI and automation access. Keep GUI strings in English source and add Brazilian Portuguese translations for every new visible string.
- Do not automatically trust the signer certificate: cryptographic validity and identity trust remain separate checks.

## Evidence and limits

A local prototype was exercised with an A3 token; `pdfsig` confirmed a valid signature and full-document coverage. Unit and integration tests use synthetic identities. No personal PDF, certificate, token serial, PIN or proprietary driver will be included in the contribution. Cross-platform hardware behavior and current-`main` integration need maintainer review and CI.

title: Severe printing performance issue – Missing "Print as Image" option
author: sistemaufficiosas-glitch
body:
Hello PdfCraft Development Team,

First of all, congratulations on your excellent project!

I run Sistema Ufficio, a professional printing and multifunction printer service business in Italy.

Today, October 14, 2026, I installed **PdfCraft version 0.7.1**, downloaded from the official distribution channel.

I was impressed by its small installation size, very fast PDF opening, and Acrobat-like editing features.

However, I encountered a serious printing performance limitation.

### Real-world comparison

- Same PDF document.
- Same printer.
- Printing initiated simultaneously from two different Windows computers.
- PdfCraft compared against Adobe Acrobat.
- PdfCraft computer equipped with 8 GB of RAM.

At the same point in time:

- **Adobe Acrobat had already processed 50 pages.**
- **PdfCraft had processed only 6 pages.**

This is a very significant difference in document processing performance.

### Missing feature: Print as Image

Adobe Acrobat provides a **Print as Image** option that can rasterize PDF pages before sending them to the printer.

PdfCraft currently does not expose an equivalent option in its print dialog.

### Requested improvements

1. Add a **Print as Image** option to the print dialog.
2. Provide selectable rasterization resolutions, such as 300 and 600 DPI.
3. Improve Windows print processing and spooling performance for complex PDF documents.
4. Optimize compatibility with professional multifunction printers.

For commercial print shops, this functionality is extremely important.

PdfCraft has great potential as an alternative to Adobe Acrobat, and I would be happy to help with further testing.

Thank you for your work!

Best regards,

**Sistema Ufficio – Italy**

title: PDF/A: device colour is found by splitting content on whitespace, so a CMYK logo in a form XObject gets an sRGB output intent and passes `pdfa_verify`
author: guillehr2
body:
### What happens

`pdfa_convert 2b` gives a document whose only CMYK content is a form XObject (a placed logo, as most layout and print tools write it) an **sRGB output intent**, identifies it as PDF/A-2b, and `pdfa_verify` then reports it **compliant**. Under ISO 19005-2 §6.2.4.3, DeviceCMYK needs a CMYK output intent (the rule #667 added), so the file claims a conformance it doesn't have.

Minimal file (one page, an RGB rectangle and a process-CMYK logo drawn through `/Logo Do`):

```
1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >> endobj
2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 /MediaBox [0 0 200 200] >> endobj
3 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /Contents 4 0 R /Resources << /XObject << /Logo 5 0 R >> >> >> endobj
4 0 obj << /Length 57 >> stream
0 0 1 rg 20 120 160 60 re f q 1 0 0 1 75 30 cm /Logo Do Q
endstream endobj
5 0 obj << /Type /XObject /Subtype /Form /BBox [0 0 50 50] /Length 27 >> stream
0.75 0 1 0 k 0 0 50 50 re f
endstream endobj
```

```sh
pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json   # doc_open → pdfa_convert 2b → doc_save → doc_open → pdfa_verify
```

- **Expected:** `DeviceCMYK is used: it needs a CMYK output intent (not added automatically)`, and no sRGB output intent.
- **Actual:** `"Added an sRGB output intent"`, then `"compliant": true` with `output_intents: ["sRGB IEC61966-2.1"]`.

### Why

`uses_device_colour` (`crates/preflight/src/lib.rs`) decides which streams are content by their dictionary (no `/Type`, `/Subtype` absent or `/Form`) and reads them by splitting the bytes on whitespace, looking for `g`/`rg`/`k` tokens. That gets content wrong both ways:

**Missed (false negatives, so a CMYK document is given an sRGB output intent):**
- form XObjects with `/Type /XObject`, which is nearly all of them, are skipped;
- tiling patterns (`/Type /Pattern`) are skipped;
- `/DeviceCMYK cs 0 0 0 1 sc` (and `CS`/`SC`) set DeviceCMYK without a `k`;
- inline images in `/CMYK`, `/DeviceCMYK` or `[/I /DeviceCMYK …]`;
- an operator right before a delimiter (`0…

title: Preferences: a real window with categories on the left
author: aalbertiarchitecte
body:
## Today

Preferences is one narrow modal (520 pt) that scrolls through everything in a single column:
interface language and size, tools panel side, appearance (with two large theme previews),
Documents and view, Reading colours, Identity, Fill & Sign, JavaScript… There is no
navigation and no search, so a setting near the bottom is hard to find, and every new setting
makes the column longer. Gap #19 in `docs/gaps.md` already notes that most of Acrobat's
twenty or so preference pages are still to come, so the column will only grow.

## Proposal

A preferences window like Acrobat's, Foxit's or Rhino's:

- **Categories in a list on the left**, the selected category's settings on the right. The
  names follow Acrobat's where a page exists there (General, Page Display, Documents,
  Commenting, Signatures, JavaScript, Units…), so the pages still missing (gap #19) have a
  place to land.
- **A larger window**, resizable, that remembers its size and the last category opened.
- **A search box** above the list: typing filters to the settings whose label matches and
  shows which category each one is in.
- **Headless:** the control channel opens it at a category (`dialog preferences:page-display`),
  so tests and agents can reach every page.

## Why it also helps contributors

`preferences_body` lives in `js_ui.rs` and is a single 230-line function that every new
setting edits, so PRs that add preferences collide there. One module per category (for
example `prefs/page_display.rs`) gives each new setting its own file.

## Scope

Moving the existing settings only: no setting changes behaviour, the settings file keeps its
keys, and existing tests keep passing. New preference pages come afterwards, one PR each.

I'd be glad to implement it after #2263 (screen resolution and calibration, #739), if this
direction suits you.

title: PdfCraft limited to ~49 Hz on Windows when using the wgpu/DX12 backend (works fine with OpenGL/glow)
author: Astrojoin
body:
When launching PdfCraft on Windows with the default graphics backend (wgpu → DirectX 12), the application’s frame rate is capped at approximately 49 Hz, even though the monitor is capable of 144 Hz and other applications run at the full refresh rate. Forcing PdfCraft to use the OpenGL backend (`PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl`) removes the cap and allows smooth 144 Hz rendering.

This suggests an issue in the wgpu/egui‑wgpu integration where the Windows Desktop Window Manager (DWM) interprets the application as unable to keep up with the monitor’s refresh rate and applies a throttling limit.

---

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Install PdfCraft (release build) on a Windows machine with a monitor set to 144 Hz (or any high‑refresh rate).  
2. Ensure no custom `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER` variable is set (so the default wgpu/DX12 backend is used).  
3. Launch PdfCraft (e.g., via its desktop shortcut).  
4. Observe the frame rate (using tools like MSI Afterburner, NVIDIA Frameview, or the built‑in FPS counter if enabled).  
5. The reported FPS will hover around 48‑52 Hz.  
6. Close PdfCraft.  
7. Set the environment variable `PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl` (system/user variable or via a shortcut).  
8. Relaunch PdfCraft.  
9. Observe the frame rate now matches the monitor’s refresh rate (~144 Hz).

### Expected Behavior
PdfCraft should render at the monitor’s refresh rate (e.g., 144 Hz) when using the default wgpu/DX12 backend, just as it does with the OpenGL backend.

### Actual Behavior
PdfCraft is limited to roughly 49 Hz when using wgpu/DX12, but runs at the full refresh rate when forced to OpenGL.

### Environment
- **OS:** Windows 10/11 (version 22H2 or later)  
- **Monitor:** 144 Hz (or other high‑refresh rate) display  
- **GPU:** NVIDIA/AMD/Intel (issue observed on multiple vendors)  
- **PdfCraft version:** Latest release (as of 2026‑10‑14)  
- **Graphics backend:** Default (wgpu → DX12) vs. forced OpenGL (`PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl`)  
- **Driver:** Latest stable drivers from GPU vendor

title: [Feature] Tab context menu: close other tabs / close tabs to the right
author: edurbs
body:
The PDF tab context menu (#1233, #1266) is a great start. Two common tab-management actions are still missing — present in browsers and IDEs (Firefox, Chrome, VS Code, IntelliJ):

- **Close other tabs** — closes every document tab except the right-clicked one
- **Close tabs to the right** — closes the tabs to the right of the right-clicked one

These go beyond Acrobat parity (Acrobat's menu has Close/Reopen/Reveal), but so does middle-click-to-close (#1853), which is already tracked. When many documents are open, closing them one by one — each with its own unsaved-changes prompt — is tedious.

Expected behaviour:

- Both actions reuse the existing close path (`request_close_tab`), so each dirty document still asks to save / cancel; cancelling keeps that document and stops the batch (as quitting does today).
- The Combine-files tab is never counted or closed by either action.
- "Close other tabs" is disabled with a single document tab; "close tabs to the right" is disabled on the rightmost tab.
- Targeting by stable `DocId`, as #1266 does, so tab identity survives earlier removals.

Implementation would extend the menu in `crates/ui-egui/src/chrome.rs` and `Action` in `crates/ui-egui/src/tab_context.rs`, with labels added to the i18n catalogs, and kittest + control-channel tests as in #1266.

I plan to work on this myself — a draft PR follows.

title: [Bug Report] [PdfCraft] Scanned PDF renders as a blank white page (CCITT G4 image with /Rows 0)
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

A scanned PDF opens in PdfCraft as a completely white page. The same file shows correctly in other viewers (Microsoft Edge, MuPDF).

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open a scanner-made PDF where each page is a 1-bit image compressed with CCITTFaxDecode (Group 4), and whose DecodeParms has /Rows 0. Example: /DecodeParms<</K -1/Columns 1656/Rows 0>>. Our file came from a Ricoh-style office scanner. The page image is an XObject named "strip0".
2. Look at the page in PdfCraft, or run: pdfcraft-cli render file.pdf --page 1 --out p1.png

Expected:
The scanned page image is shown.

Actual:
- The page is fully white, both in the app and in the CLI render.
- "text" returns nothing. That part is expected, because the file has no text layer.

Likely cause:
/Rows 0 is valid in the PDF spec. It means "use the image Height". PdfCraft seems to treat it as 0 rows and decodes an empty image.

Workaround that confirms it:
Replace the "/Rows 0" key with spaces of the same length, so the xref offsets stay valid. After that the page renders correctly in PdfCraft.

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, PdfCraft 0.7.1

title: [Bug Report] [PdfCraft] Thai text added to a PDF shows as "?????" (Add text, text box comment, Fill & Sign)
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

PdfCraft draws Thai text as "?????" on the page in every viewer. This happens with every way of adding text.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Open any PDF in PdfCraft.
2. Add Thai text, e.g. "ทดสอบภาษาไทย", with each of these tools:
   - Add text (page_add_text / edit.text)
   - Text box comment (comment_add type=textbox)
   - Fill & Sign (fill_sign_add)
3. Save the PDF, then open it in PdfCraft and in another viewer (Edge).

Expected:
The Thai text appears on the page as typed.

Actual:
- Every Thai character shows as "?" on the page, in all viewers. English text is fine.
- PdfCraft warns that the standard fonts cannot draw these characters, so the appearance shows "?".
- The text of a comment keeps the Thai in the side panel. Only what is drawn on the page is broken.

Likely cause:
Added text is drawn only with the PDF standard 14 fonts (Helvetica / Times / Courier, WinAnsi encoding), which have no Thai glyphs. A system font with Thai glyphs is never embedded.

Suggested fix:
Embed a font subset that has the glyphs, e.g. Tahoma or Leelawadee UI on Windows, or let the user pick a font. Thai also needs proper shaping for vowels and tone marks (e.g. "ที่", "น้ำ").

Impact:
Thai PDF forms cannot be filled in PdfCraft.

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, PdfCraft 0.7.1

title: Community testing: Help complete PdfCraft testing against the KillerPDF Corpus
author: jpeskov
body:
## Goal

I'd like to get more people testing PdfCraft against the [KillerPDF Corpus](https://killerpdf.net/corpus), a collection of 17,248 test PDFs split into regression and standards sets. The goal isn't to pass or fail the whole corpus. It's to find specific problems, reproduce them, get them fixed, and build up a set of regression tests along the way.

Following up on the fixture-collection suggestion in #1524, I ran about 10% of the corpus (v1.8.1) through PdfCraft as an automated compatibility and save-fidelity check. I'm not planning to keep going myself, so I'm posting what I have in case someone wants to pick it up. Progress, corrections and links to related issues can go in the comments. A parallel effort for the PDF Association's Stressful PDF Corpus is in #3088.

Individual findings will be filed as separate issues and link back here. No fix/PR is part of this.

## New to contributing? This is a good place to start

You don't need deep technical expertise to help here. A pull request asks you to understand the codebase, write a fix, add tests and get through review. A good bug report mostly asks for curiosity and care, and maintainers can turn it into a fix and a regression test.

A coding agent makes this much more approachable. If you don't already use one, [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) is a good starting point: it's open source and gives you capable models for free, which is plenty for this kind of testing. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others work well too. Point it at `RUN-RESUME.md` in the attachment below and it can do most of the setup. **You're still the reporter**, though. title: Incremental saves write absolute xref offsets for PDFs with a prefix
author: jpeskov
body:
On PdfCraft 0.8.0, editing the Subject of a PDF with bytes before its `%PDF-` header and saving incrementally returns success, but the new cross-reference offsets use absolute file positions while the prior `/Prev` remains header-relative. qpdf then reports `xref not found` and reconstructs the table. Plain incremental and prefixed full-save controls pass. The unchanged source passes the same check; the warning is introduced by the save.

## Reproduction

Download `preservation/openpreserve-format-corpus/jhove-errors/PDF-HUL-137/reserve3.pdf` from the [official KillerPDF v1.8.1 standards ZIP](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF-Corpus/releases/download/v1.8.1/killerpdf-corpus-standards-v1.8.1.zip) and verify the PDF SHA-256 is `d682898d2076bc2c49b2c8f102d88781cf2ffc88834e0996c685507f5ff33a41`. Work in a disposable directory with this file named `reserve3.pdf`, then run `pdfcraft-cli run --script repro.json --root "$PWD"`:

<details>
<summary>repro.json</summary>

```json
[
  {"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"reserve3.pdf"}},
  {"tool":"doc_set_info","args":{"doc":1,"key":"Subject","value":"Offset reproduction Subject edit"}},
  {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"full":false}}
]
```

</details>

On the pinned build, qpdf exits 0 on the original and 3 on the incrementally saved copy (`xref not found`). The plain incremental and prefixed full-save controls pass. The 128-byte prefix puts the old xref at absolute 149364/header-relative 149236; `/Prev` remains 149236, while the new xref and `startxref` are written as absolute 157497 instead of relative 157369. A copy-only correction to the new offsets passes qpdf.

Expected: retain a consistent offset convention so saving does not introduce cross-reference recovery warnings.

Environment: PdfCraft `9931329` (0.8.0), Debian 13 Linux.

Closed [#1339](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1339) concerns unchanged direct-library saves that emit an empty subsection; this report requires an edited prefixed file…

title: Saving a repaired PDF drops recoverable Info fields
author: jpeskov
body:
A metadata update after opening a damaged PDF drops other Info fields that independent readers can recover. A full save keeps only the new `/Subject` and `/ModDate`; `/Title`, `/Creator`, `/Producer`, and `/CreationDate` disappear. Requesting incremental save also loses those fields; this damaged input is rewritten rather than saved incrementally.

**Reproduction**

Download `preservation/openpreserve-format-corpus/jhove-errors/PDF-HUL-138/6.2017-0960.pdf` from the [KillerPDF v1.8.1 standards archive](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF-Corpus/releases/download/v1.8.1/killerpdf-corpus-standards-v1.8.1.zip). Its SHA-256 is `a29941595338eff03fc2b7f7d64fb688fd0f2c06c1bbb54ec4fabb75c05ce322`. Put the fixture in the working directory, save the JSON below as `repro.json`, then run:

```sh
pdfcraft-cli run --script repro.json --root "$PWD"
```

<details>
<summary>repro.json</summary>

```json
[
  {"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"6.2017-0960.pdf"}},
  {"tool":"doc_set_info","args":{"doc":1,"key":"Subject","value":"KillerPDF batch1253 metadata preservation test"}},
  {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"path":"full.pdf","full":true}}
]
```

</details>

**Expected:** The save updates `/Subject` and retains the independently recoverable Info fields.

**Actual:** The save succeeds, but the output has only the new `/Subject` and `/ModDate`. pypdf and MuPDF read the listed fields from the input; PdfCraft reports them null before saving, and MuPDF reports them empty afterward. The input has a missing `startxref`; PdfCraft rebuilds its cross-reference data from object headers.

**Environment:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), Debian 13 Linux.

This differs from [#1338](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1338), which concerns unknown trailer entries rather than Info dictionary fields.

Found while testing against the KillerPDF Corpus. Methodology and run data: [#2361](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/2361).

title: Full save drops recoverable outlines and page labels
author: jpeskov
body:
A full save drops outlines and page labels that another reader can recover from a damaged PDF. A metadata-only full save succeeds but writes catalog `/Outlines null` and `/PageLabels null`; an incremental save of the same edit retains both structures.

**Reproduction**

Download `qpdf/qpdf/qtest/qpdf/xref-compressed-in-compressed.pdf` from the [KillerPDF v1.8.1 regression archive](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF-Corpus/releases/download/v1.8.1/killerpdf-corpus-regression-v1.8.1-part10.zip). Its SHA-256 is `C99080E8D936EEB40A08D7E596F4C10B959A245FE3CB5DDB971EB7F145BAA4C2`. Put the fixture in the working directory, save the JSON below as `repro.json`, then run:

```sh
pdfcraft-cli run --script repro.json --root "$PWD"
```

<details>
<summary>repro.json</summary>

```json
[
  {"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"xref-compressed-in-compressed.pdf"}},
  {"tool":"doc_set_info","args":{"doc":1,"key":"Subject","value":"KillerPDF batch1253 metadata preservation test"}},
  {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"path":"full.pdf","full":true}}
]
```

</details>

**Expected:** The full save retains the 11 independently recovered bookmarks and 12 page-label ranges.

**Actual:** MuPDF reports both structures after opening the input and none after the full save. The corresponding incremental save retains both structures.

**Environment:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), Debian 13 Linux.

The fixture is intentionally malformed: its compressed-object reference is invalid, but MuPDF recovers the navigation structures. This concerns catalog navigation structures, unlike [#1338](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1338), which concerns unknown trailer entries.

Found while testing against the KillerPDF Corpus. Methodology and run data: [#2361](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/2361).

title: Flattening rotates and moves NoRotate widgets on rotated pages
author: jpeskov
body: Flattening a form widget marked `/NoRotate` changes its displayed orientation and position when its page has `/Rotate 90`. The widget is horizontal before flattening and vertical afterward. Poppler and MuPDF show the same change, while neighboring widgets without `/NoRotate` keep their orientation. ## Reproduce Using the [official KillerPDF v1.8.1 regression archive](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF-Corpus/releases/download/v1.8.1/killerpdf-corpus-regression-v1.8.1-part10.zip), extract `qpdf/qpdf/qtest/qpdf/manual-appearances.pdf` (PDF SHA-256 `de0605b7d4445bc8e4d9d355203f867d40e641789146a179e5e4fb08c75ec6ce`), then run: ```sh cat > flatten.json <<'JSON' [{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"qpdf/qpdf/qtest/qpdf/manual-appearances.pdf"}},{"tool":"doc_flatten","args":{"doc":1,"comments":false,"fields":true}},{"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"full":true,"path":"flattened.pdf"}}] JSON pdfcraft-cli run --script flatten.json --root . ``` Compare the `/NoRotate` widget before and after flattening. The same behavior was independently reproduced with a small self-contained widget fixture, shown below: original on the left, flattened on the right. **Expected:** `/NoRotate` widgets stay upright and in the same displayed position after flattening. **Actual:** the widget rotates with the page and shifts position after flattening. Environment: PdfCraft `9931329` (0.8.0), Debian 13 Linux x86_64. [Issue #434](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/434) and [PR #473](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/473) concern image stamps; they do not cover existing form widgets' `/NoRotate` flag during flattening. Found while testing against the KillerPDF Corpus. Methodology and run data: [#2361](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/2361).

title: CLI render omits FreeText annotations without an appearance stream
author: jpeskov
body: The standalone `pdfcraft-cli render` command omits a FreeText annotation that has no normal appearance stream (`/AP`). PdfCraft's document display renderer and independent readers draw the same annotation from its dictionary. In a minimal control PDF, the CLI output has 0 non-white pixels; PdfCraft engine rendering has 18,220, Poppler 17,556, and MuPDF 18,224. This is a display discrepancy, not a save operation. ## Reproduce The source fixture is `pdfcpu/annotations/FreeTextAnnotation.pdf` (SHA-256 `A910A7EB3ACD5D061EC335A713CFECBE5711D54395D403788D644CCB411D9786`) in the [official KillerPDF v1.8.1 regression archive](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF-Corpus/releases/download/v1.8.1/killerpdf-corpus-regression-v1.8.1-part09.zip). The corpus fixture also has rich text. This comparison uses the plain-text minimal control to remove that ambiguity: Environment: PdfCraft `9931329` (0.8.0), Debian 13 Linux x86_64. [PR #371](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/371) adds missing-appearance display support to the document display renderer; the standalone CLI render path constructs its renderer directly from input bytes and still omits this annotation. title: Edit text: one character outside the subset switches the whole line to Helvetica (different face and metrics)
author: thedelsorbo
body:
**Version:** 0.8.0 (`main`, 2026-10-15). Same synthetic fixture as #2377: [`scheda.pdf`](https://github.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/blob/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/scheda.pdf) (TrueType subsets `BAAAAA+DejaVuSans`, `CAAAAA+DejaVuSans-Bold`), script [`edits.json`](https://github.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/blob/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/edits.json).

**Steps:** `text_edit` on line 10 "Giovedì 15 ottobre " → "Venerdì 16 ottobre " (the bold subset has no `V`), and on line 20 inserting the word "Zürich" (the regular subset has no `ü`).

**Actual:** the tool answers `"font": "Helvetica-Bold"` / `"font": "Helvetica"` and the saved file gains a non-embedded Helvetica: the *entire* line is redrawn in Helvetica — different face, different widths, the line shrinks and no longer matches its neighbours. No warning says which character caused it.

![date line switched to Helvetica-Bold](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/cmp_edit_C_data.png)

![body line switched to Helvetica](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/cmp_edit_D_glifo_mancante.png)

**Expected** (what Acrobat does, and what `docs/editing-existing-text.md` describes as the goal): keep the source face for every glyph it has and substitute only the missing glyph (or, when a matching full face is available on the machine, complete the subset); and tell the user which character forced the substitution, in the same spirit as the "no silent `?`" rule (ROADMAP 2026-10-11, M14) — a silent whole-line Helvetica is the same kind of surprise. One accented letter is the normal case in Italian, French or German text, so this is hit on almost every real edit.

Related: `docs/gaps.md` gap 3 ("font reused or Helvetica substituted"), #2077 (installed fonts for editing existing text).

title: Security: redaction and Sanitize leave data in the file (tagged-PDF links, Info/XMP, earlier revisions)
author: Losminek
body:
I tried to send these privately: by e-mail on 11 October, then through Discord and the ticket form. I got no reply, and private vulnerability reporting is off on the repo. So here is a short public summary following the reporting guidance in PhotoCraft's `SECURITY.md`: component, impact and a pointer to the code, with no proof-of-concept files. All three are about data that stays in a document after the user asked to remove it. I re-checked them against `main` today (`d3a91c5`).

**1. Sanitize keeps link URLs in tagged PDFs**
`crates/redact/src/sanitize.rs` (around lines 282–334) removes a link annotation only from the page's `/Annots`. In a tagged PDF the structure tree still references the annotation, so `write_full` keeps it, URL included. Meanwhile `link_list` reports 0 links. The user is told the links are gone while the URL is still in the file.
Possible fix: also drop the annotation's references from the structure tree (OBJR entries / parent tree), or rebuild the file only from what the pages reference.

**2. `redact_apply` leaves the document Info dictionary and XMP metadata**
`crates/redact/src/lib.rs` (around 372–599) redacts page content, but a redacted string can still be in `/Info` (Title, Subject, Keywords…) and in the XMP `/Metadata` stream. Bookmarks are the same problem and are already covered by #1141 / #1145.
Possible fix: run the same matcher over `/Info` and XMP, or at least offer "remove metadata" as a follow-up step after redaction.

**3. Incremental save keeps the previous revision**
`save_bytes` writes incrementally by default (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs` around 3723–3731). After deleting a page or changing a form field, the old page and old values stay in the earlier revision inside the file. This is probably by design. Still, after a redaction or page deletion a full rewrite (or a warning) would avoid a surprise.

Related, already reported: non-atomic CLI writes (`edit X --out X`) in #1793 / #1843.

body:
`pdfcraft-cli audit` 0.8.0 now catches covers drawn as `m`/`l` paths (thanks for #1521). Three other ways of hiding text that a reader sees as redacted are still reported as clean (`count: 0`, exit 0), while the text stays extractable with `pdfcraft-cli text`:

| Cover over the text | Visible result (rendered by pdfcraft-cli render) | audit 0.8.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `0 g 70 695 330 20 re f` (filled rectangle) | hidden | found (exit 1) |
| `0 g 70 695 m 400 695 l 400 715 l 70 715 l h f` (path) | hidden | found (exit 1) |
| `0 G 20 w 70 705 m 400 705 l S` (thick black **stroke**, "marker" style) | hidden (100% dark pixels over the text box) | **not found** |
| `/Subtype /Highlight /C [0 0 0]` annotation over the text | hidden (100% dark) | **not found** |
| `1 g 70 695 330 20 re f` (**white** filled rectangle) | hidden (text invisible) | **not found** |

Reproduction: a one-page PDF with Helvetica text `BT /F1 14 Tf 72 700 Td (IBAN IT60X0542811101000000123456) Tj ET` and one of the covers above appended to the same content stream (for the annotation: `/Annots [<< /Type /Annot /Subtype /Highlight /Rect [70 695 400 715] /C [0 0 0] /F 4 /QuadPoints [70 715 400 715 70 695 400 695] >>]`). The thick stroke and the black highlight are common ways people "black out" text with a pen/marker tool; the white rectangle is the usual way text is hidden in forms.

title: Shrunk images without /Interpolate are nearest-sampled since #635: scanned text comes out ragged (fix on a branch)
author: thedelsorbo
body:
**Version:** 0.8.0 (`main`, 2026-10-15), `pdfcraft-cli render` and the desktop app.

**Summary.** Since #635 (the fix for #624), an image drawn *smaller* than its resolution is shrunk by nearest neighbour whenever it does not carry `/Interpolate true` — which is the PDF default, so nearly every scan, screenshot and exported card. Nearest neighbour keeps one sample in N and drops the rest, so scanned text comes out with ragged strokes and stems of uneven weight; at fit-to-window zooms whole stems vanish. This is what users describe as "imprecise" or "blurry" text on scanned pages, and it is a different defect from #730 (vector text).

**Reproduce.** [`scanned_card.pdf`](https://github.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/blob/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/scanned_card.pdf): a one-page A4 card as a 288 dpi JPEG (3368 × 2382 px), the way scanners and "export as image" produce it, no `/Interpolate`, no OCR layer. `pdfcraft-cli render scanned_card.pdf --dpi 61 --out out.png` (61 dpi ≈ a fit-to-window view), and compare with `pdftoppm -r 61`.

Body text at 61 dpi, 4×: PdfCraft 0.8.0 / with the fix below / Poppler:

![scanned card body text, before, after, Poppler](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/scanned_card_61dpi_before_after.png)

Mean absolute difference from a Lanczos downscale of the page image (shift-tolerant, grey levels):

| | 61 dpi (shrink 4.7×) | 96 dpi (shrink 3×) |
|---|---|---|
| PdfCraft 0.8.0 (nearest) | 4.17 | 2.23 |
| with the fix | **2.80** | **0.41** |

On a real 5760 px scanned card (not attached): 2.08 → 1.45 at 61 dpi, 0.75 → 0.16 at 96 dpi; Poppler scores 2.42 / 2.97 on the same file, so the fixed render is the closest of the three to the reference.

**Why this is a bug and not a preference.** `/Interpolate` is about smoothing an image drawn *larger* than its samples (PDF 32000-1 §8.9.6.3). When an image is drawn smaller, every device pixel covers several samples, and whether to average them is not a que…

title: parity/acrobat-features.toml has duplicate keys on main, so cargo xtask parity fails
author: magdale76
body:
`parity/acrobat-features.toml` on `main` is no longer valid TOML, so `cargo xtask parity` fails:

```
xtask parity: error: parsing parity/acrobat-features.toml: TOML parse error at line 2625, column 454
duplicate key
```

CI doesn't run `xtask parity`, so PR checks stay green and nothing flags it, but the parity report can't be produced and the pre-commit gate in `CLAUDE.md` fails for everyone.

**What happened.** Several `[[feature]]` entries now hold the same key twice: both sides of a merge on that entry were kept. For example `optimize.optimizer` has the `notes` and `evidence` from #1784 *and* the ones from the PR that touched it in parallel. As of 953ac148:

| Entry | Line | Repeated keys |
|---|---|---|
| `organize.organize-grid` | 2614 | evidence, notes |
| `organize.page-transitions` | 3192 | tools, evidence, notes |
| `form.fill-text` | 4415 | evidence, notes |
| `form.fill-sign-signature` | 5305 | evidence, notes |
| `protect.audit-faux-redactions` | 5815 | evidence, notes |
| `optimize.optimizer` | 7265 | evidence, notes |
| `optimize.downsample-images` | 7279 | evidence, notes |
| `misc.prefs-language` | 9945 | evidence, notes |
| `misc.installers` | 10103 | notes |

The first broken commit on main's first-parent history is b5dc84df (#1900); the file parses at b9f0f84f just before it. The list has grown with later merges (there were 8 entries a few minutes earlier).

**Fix.** Each entry needs its two versions combined by hand, since usually both carry real information (the union of `evidence`, and one `notes` covering both changes). A check that the file parses, in `cargo xtask ci` or in the CI workflow, would catch this at merge time.

I can open the fix PR if that helps. I'd rather not race the merge queue, though: the file changes every few minutes right now, so I'll wait for a go-ahead.

title: PDF/A: a spot colour or an indexed image over DeviceCMYK gets an sRGB output intent and passes `pdfa_verify`
author: guillehr2
body:
### What happens

`pdfa_convert 2b` gives an **sRGB output intent** to a document whose only CMYK reaches the page through a colour space rather than an operator. It then identifies the document as PDF/A-2b, and `pdfa_verify` reports it **compliant**. Two common cases are a spot colour with a DeviceCMYK alternate (how layout tools write a named ink) and an indexed image over DeviceCMYK. Under ISO 19005-2 §6.2.4.3, DeviceCMYK needs a CMYK output intent (#667), so the file claims a conformance it doesn't have.

This is the follow-up #2260 listed as out of scope. It still happens on `main` with #2260 merged.

Minimal file, `spot.pdf` (one page, an RGB rectangle and a square in a spot colour whose alternate is DeviceCMYK, selected with `/CS0 cs`):

```
1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >> endobj
2 0 obj << /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 /MediaBox [0 0 200 200] >> endobj
3 0 obj << /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /Contents 4 0 R
   /Resources << /ColorSpace << /CS0 [/Separation /Orange /DeviceCMYK
       << /FunctionType 2 /Domain [0 1] /C0 [0 0 0 0] /C1 [0 0.5 1 0] /N 1 >>] >> >> >> endobj
4 0 obj << /Length 58 >> stream
0 0 1 rg 20 120 160 60 re f /CS0 cs 1 scn 75 30 50 50 re f
endstream endobj
```

`indexed.pdf` is the same page with a two-colour image XObject in `/ColorSpace [/Indexed /DeviceCMYK 1 <00000000BF00FF00>]` in place of the spot colour.

```sh
pdfcraft-cli run --script steps_spot.json --root .   # doc_open → pdfa_verify → pdfa_convert 2b → doc_save → doc_open → pdfa_verify
```

- **Expected:** `DeviceCMYK is used: it needs a CMYK output intent (not added automatically)`, and no sRGB output intent.
- **Actual:** before converting, only `Device colour is used, but there is no PDF/A output intent` (from the RGB rectangle). After `pdfa_convert`, `"compliant": true` with `"output_intents": ["sRGB IEC61966-2.1"]`, and the same again after saving and reopening. `indexed.pdf` behaves the same way.

### Why

title: Edit text on an OCR layer: a line edit shows nothing ("not saved"), a paragraph edit draws boxes in the OCR font (fix on a branch)
author: thedelsorbo
body:
**Version:** 0.8.0 (`main`, 2026-10-15), `pdfcraft-cli` and the desktop app (both go through `Session::apply`).

**Context.** A scanned page as OCR tools write it — Tesseract, OCRmyPDF, Adobe Scan, most MFP scanners — is one page image plus an invisible text layer (`3 Tr`) in a font that is meant to be searched, not seen (Tesseract's `GlyphLessFont` encodes every character and draws a filled box for each). PdfCraft already handles rewriting such a word in `EditTextBlock` (cover in the sampled paper colour, new text in the sampled ink colour — `scan_colours`, `BlockStyle::cover`), but two paths around it make the edit come out wrong, and the user's impression is simply "my edits don't save".

**Reproduce.** [`ocr_card.pdf`](https://github.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/blob/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/ocr_card.pdf): the synthetic card from #2393 passed through Tesseract 5 (`tesseract scan.jpg out pdf`). Script: [`ocr_edits.json`](https://github.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/blob/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/ocr_edits.json) — `text_edit` of the word "Online" (line 16 / paragraph 16) to "In aula", once by `line`, once by `paragraph`, then render at 96 dpi.

1. **Line edit** (`Edit::EditTextLine` → `pdfcraft_edit::replace_line`): the invisible layer is rewritten in place, `3 Tr` and all. The file changes, `pdfcraft-cli text` and search find "In aula", the page looks exactly as before. The tool even answers `"font": "GlyphLessFont"`.
2. **Paragraph edit** (`Edit::EditTextBlock` → `rewrite_block`): the scan is covered and the new text drawn visibly — *in the layer's own font*, because `source_encodes` says it can show every character. With `GlyphLessFont` that is a row of green boxes; with other OCR fonts it is whatever their placeholder glyph is. (On a card OCR'd by another tool, same result: boxes.)

![line edit shows nothing, paragraph edit draws boxes, both fixed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thedelsorbo/pdfcraft/hinted-sfnt-glyph-runs/fixtures/ocr_edit_before_after.…

title: CI doesn't check that parity/acrobat-features.toml parses
author: magdale76
body:
Nothing in CI checks that `parity/acrobat-features.toml` parses. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`, but not `cargo xtask parity`, so a merge that leaves the file invalid passes every check. This has already happened (see the duplicate-keys issue split out of #2410).

Running `cargo xtask parity`, or a cheaper parse-only check, in CI (or in `cargo xtask ci`) would catch this at merge time.

Split out of #2410.

title: signing_with_translated_labels_through_tools fails on main: test password shorter than the new 8-character minimum
author: magdale76
body:
`signing_with_translated_labels_through_tools` in `crates/automation/tests/automation.rs` fails on `main`:

```
sign_id_create {"key":"p256","name":"Ada Lovelace","password":"secret1","path":"ada.p12"}: the password must have at least 8 characters
```

Two merges crossed:
- #1951 (f52c9288) added the test, creating a digital ID with the password `secret1` (7 characters; also used at line 4496 to sign).
- #2201 (586f2b2b, "harden .p12 digital IDs") requires at least 8 characters.

Each passed on its own. Every PR's `test` job will hit this once it is built against current `main`. `main`'s own CI runs keep being cancelled by newer pushes, so it hasn't shown up there.

Fix: use a password of 8 or more characters in both places in that test.

title: Windows: printing fails with "Failed to parse print capabilities" on Toshiba drivers (xsd:integer values with surrounding whitespace)
author: carpaaaaa
body:
## Summary

On Windows, printing to a Toshiba e-STUDIO printer fails with **"Failed to parse print capabilities"**. The driver's PrintCapabilities document contains `xsd:integer` values with leading/trailing spaces (e.g. `" 16900 "`), and the PrintSchema reader in `winprint` parses them with `str::parse::<i32>()` without trimming, so the whole document is rejected and nothing is printed.

## Environment

- PdfCraft 0.8.0, Windows x64 (Windows 11, build 26200)
- Printer: Toshiba e-STUDIO2010AC
- Driver: **TOSHIBA Universal Printer 2** (v3 driver), version 7.222.5412.176
- Other queues on the same machine print fine: HP DesignJet T850 MFP V4, Microsoft Print to PDF, OneNote (Desktop), AnyDesk Printer

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install a Toshiba e-STUDIO printer with the "TOSHIBA Universal Printer 2" driver.
2. Open any PDF in PdfCraft → Print → select the Toshiba queue → Print.
3. The error "Failed to parse print capabilities" is shown. Nothing is written to `pdfcraft.log`.

## Evidence

The driver's PrintCapabilities (fetched with `PTGetPrintCapabilities` / `PrintQueue.GetPrintCapabilitiesAsXml`, no ticket) contains these values. Namespace `ns0000` = `http://www.toshibamfp.net/xps/e-BRIDGE/2006/06/print`:

title: [BUG] [Improvement request] Add subpixel anti-aliasing and image resampling to render scanned docs at better resolution on 1080p
author: dariy-vel
body: ### Summary When viewing scanned (image-based) PDFs on a standard 24" Full HD (1080p) external monitor where `window.devicePixelRatio` is `1.0x`, text appears severely aliased, jagged, and missing thin letter strokes compared to viewers like MS Edge on the exact same monitor. Per a discussion on Discord with `@Combiler01`, opening this improvement request to enhance how PdfCraft renders and downscales scanned PDFs on `1.0x` DPI displays. ### Current Behavior vs. Expected Behavior * **Current Behavior:** PdfCraft relies strictly on `window.devicePixelRatio` (`1.0x` on a 1080p display) for its Canvas API rendering. When high-resolution scanned pages are scaled down to fit a 1:1 pixel mapping without supersampling or high-quality resampling, thin raster strokes drop out and exhibit heavy aliasing. * **Expected Behavior:** Scanned PDFs should remain crisp and legible at standard zoom levels ("Fit to Page" / <100% zoom) on 1080p displays, matching the visual clarity of Chromium/Edge's PDF viewer. ### Side-by-Side Comparison Both screenshots were taken on the **same 24" Full HD (1920x1080) monitor**, viewing the **same scanned PDF document and page**: * **PdfCraft:** * **Microsoft Edge:** ### Technical Context & Proposed Solutions As discussed with on Discord, the quality gap on 1080p monitors stems from `1.0x` pixel mapping combined with a lack of high-quality image resampling/anti-aliasing during downscaling.

title: [Bug Report] [PdfCraft] printing error
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

**PdfCraft (Windows): "Failed to parse print capabilities" when printing to Toshiba printers**

PdfCraft 0.8.0 on Windows 11 can't print to a Toshiba e-STUDIO2010AC (driver "TOSHIBA Universal Printer 2", v3). Every print attempt fails with `Failed to parse print capabilities` and nothing is sent to the printer. Other printers on the same PC (HP DesignJet, Microsoft Print to PDF) print fine.

**Cause:** the Toshiba driver's PrintCapabilities XML has a few `xsd:integer` values padded with spaces, e.g. `<psf:Value xsi:type="xsd:integer"> 16900 </psf:Value>` (in `JobBindAllDocumentsCenterGutter` and `Destination/Box/BoxNumber`). That's valid per XML Schema, because xsd:integer collapses whitespace. But winprint's PrintSchema reader (`src/ticket/document/reader.rs`, `PsfValueContext::parse`) calls `self.value.parse::<i32>()` without trimming. So one padded number makes it reject the whole capabilities document: "Invalid integer" → "Failed to parse print capabilities".

**Fix (one line):** `self.value.trim().parse()` in winprint's reader.

**Tested:** I rebuilt PdfCraft 0.8.0 with only that change (patched winprint) and printing to the Toshiba now works. The other printers are unaffected.

**Side note:** the UI only shows the top-level error, so the real cause ("Invalid integer at line:col") is lost, and nothing is written to pdfcraft.log. Showing the full error chain would make driver issues like this much easier to diagnose.

Full details + XML excerpts: https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/2430

windows 11

title: Sanitize keeps link URLs that the tagged-PDF structure tree references
author: Losminek
body:
Split out of #2380. Checked against `main` (`d3a91c5`).

`crates/redact/src/sanitize.rs` (around lines 282–334) removes a link annotation only from the page's `/Annots`. In a tagged PDF the structure tree still references the annotation, so `write_full` keeps it, URL included. Meanwhile `link_list` reports 0 links. The user is told the links are gone while the URL is still in the file.

Possible fix: also drop the annotation's references from the structure tree (OBJR entries / parent tree), or rebuild the file only from what the pages reference.

No proof-of-concept files.

title: Redaction leaves redacted strings in the Info dictionary and XMP metadata
author: Losminek
body:
Split out of #2380. Checked against `main` (`d3a91c5`).

`redact_apply` (`crates/redact/src/lib.rs`, around 372–599) redacts page content, but a redacted string can still be in the document `/Info` dictionary (Title, Subject, Keywords…) and in the XMP `/Metadata` stream. Bookmarks have the same problem and are already covered by #1141 / #1145.

Possible fix: run the same matcher over `/Info` and XMP, or at least offer "remove metadata" as a follow-up step after redaction.

No proof-of-concept files.

title: Report: a real-world corpus run of 350 PDFs against 0.8.0 — open, text vs pdftotext, page-1 render vs pdftoppm, save and extract round trips checked with qpdf and pypdf
author: KNUFFIXX
body:
This is the overview of a corpus run over real-world PDFs on Windows 11 that I repeat on every PdfCraft release; the delta to the previous release will be posted here as a comment, and every finding goes into its own issue with a synthetic fixture (https://github.com/KNUFFIXX/artcraft-fixtures, `pdfcraft/`). An earlier one-off run of ours on another machine led to #1467–#1470 and #1698–#1700.

**Corpus.** 350 PDFs from the files of a German property-management office, picked by a fixed seed from 5,044 distinct PDFs (5,581 files; 18 files over 50 MB left out) so that every producer, scan type, form, encryption and size class is in. They are private and can't be published, not even in part: real files are used to *find* problems only, and every reported problem is rebuilt as a synthetic file.

| | files |
|---|---|
| Scans | 115 (83 with an OCR text layer: JPEG 76, JPEG 2000 3, CCITT 2, JBIG2 1, mixed 1; 32 image only) |
| Office | Excel 20 · LibreOffice 13 · Word 4 · PowerPoint 1 |
| Print drivers | 16 |
| Generated | 89 (iText, TCPDF, dompdf, ReportLab, PDFlib, Aspose, Crystal Reports, Qt, wkhtmltopdf, XSL-FO, PDFBox, pdfkit, pypdf, and 26 from other generators) |
| Other producers | browsers 8 · Acrobat 2 · macOS 1 · scanner software 4 · no producer 10 |
| Forms | AcroForm 33 (2,282 fields, 3 of them signed) · XFA 1 |

title: Web build: Scan & OCR is offered in the UI but cannot work — models are missing and PDFCRAFT_MODELS has no meaning in a browser
author: Tof33
body:
On `pdfcraft-web` 0.8.0, served as a static site, the Tools panel offers **Scan & OCR**. Running it reports:

> Text recognition isn't installed: its model files are missing. Reinstall PdfCraft, or set `PDFCRAFT_MODELS` to the folder that holds them.

Neither suggestion can apply to a web build:

- `PDFCRAFT_MODELS` is an environment variable — a page in a browser has none;
- the released `pdfcraft-web-<version>.zip` contains only `index.html`, the wasm-bindgen glue and the `_bg.wasm` module. There are no model files, and `HOSTING.md` does not mention any.

The README's `cargo xtask models` ("fetch the OCR models Scan & OCR needs — release builds include them") appears to cover desktop builds only.

**Request**

Either ship the models in the web archive, or let them be discovered at runtime from files served next to `index.html` — the way PhotoCraft already discovers fonts through `fonts/manifest.txt`.

Failing that, hiding or disabling the entry in web builds would at least save users the dead end: today the feature is offered in the menu, and only reports that it cannot run once opened.

title: Web build: allow served fonts through a manifest, like PhotoCraft's fonts/manifest.txt
author: Tof33
body:
**Load a font** works, but the font is lost as soon as the page is closed:

- the wasm-bindgen glue uses no IndexedDB;
- the `pdfcraft` entry in `localStorage` holds no font.

Every session therefore restarts from the three base PDF fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier), and a user who needs a specific font has to load the same file again at every visit.

**PhotoCraft already solves this**

PhotoCraft 0.9.0 requests `fonts/manifest.txt` at startup — one line per font, `family | style | relative path`, resolved relative to the app page. Fonts served next to `index.html` then appear in its font list with no user action at all.

**Request**

The same mechanism in PdfCraft. A web deployment cannot rely on system fonts, so served fonts are the only way to make a given typeface reliably available — and the pattern already exists in the suite.

title: Web build: an embedded mode that hides the external links (Discord / GitHub / website)
author: Tof33
body:
When `pdfcraft-web` is embedded in an iframe, the welcome screen's community links (Discord, GitHub, website) cannot work:

- a sandbox without `allow-popups` blocks them;
- granting `allow-popups` is not always acceptable to the embedding page.

They stay visible and clickable, and do nothing — which reads as a broken UI rather than as a deliberate restriction.

**Request**

A URL flag — for example `?embedded` — that hides that block.

URL flags are already part of the design: `?file=` to open a document, `?webgl` and `?cpu` to pick a renderer, and `?blank` in DeckCraft to skip the sample document. This would follow the same pattern, and would help anyone embedding the app rather than running it standalone.

title: Windows Virtual PDF Printer – Print Directly to PdfCraft
author: thomaxie
body:
Feature Description

Add a Windows virtual PDF printer that allows users to select "Print to PdfCraft" directly from the print dialog of any Windows application, similar to Adobe PDF or Microsoft Print to PDF.

Current Limitation

Currently, users must:
1. Select "Save as PDF" or "Microsoft Print to PDF".
2. Save the generated PDF to disk.
3. Manually open the PDF in PdfCraft.
It adds steps, particularly for users who regularly convert web pages, documents and reports into PDFs.

Proposed Functionality
Virtual printer integration: Install an optional "Print to PdfCraft" printer in Windows, accessible from Chrome, Edge, Word, Excel and other applications.
- Automatic opening: When selected, the application generates a PDF and automatically opens it in PdfCraft.
- Save workflow: Allow users to review, edit or annotate the generated PDF before choosing where to save it.
- Print settings: Support standard paper sizes (A4, Letter), orientation, margins and page scaling where supported by the source application.
- 
Optional installation: Allow users to enable or disable the virtual printer during installation or through PdfCraft settings.

Expected User Experience
Open a document or webpage.
Press Ctrl + P.
Select Print to PdfCraft.
Click Print.
PdfCraft automatically launches with the generated PDF, ready for editing or saving.

This would make PdfCraft a great alternative for Adobe Acrobat in everyday Window environments when someone tries to print page.

For users who frequently save web-based reports, research articles, invoices and other documents, direct printing into PdfCraft would be extremely convenient.

Priority: Quality-of-life / Workflow integration
Platform: Windows 11

title: Edit text: stable identity, width and alignment for edited paragraphs
author: komo1iddin
body:
Area: M7 (Edit text), gap 3 · Spec basis: ISO 32000-2 §14.6 (marked content), §14.7–14.8 (logical structure, tagged PDF)

I'd like to agree on the direction before sending code, since this writes a new private key into files.

## 1. Problem

A paragraph ("text block") is addressed as an index into a list. `text_blocks` rebuilds that list from geometry on every call (`group_layout`). Nothing in the file or in memory ties an edited paragraph to its next appearance.

- **Indexes shift.** Every edit API takes `block: usize`:
  - `Edit::EditTextBlock`, `rewrite_block`, `clear_block` and `text_edit_layout`;
  - automation's `paragraph` (1-based);
  - the UI's `LineEditor.block` and `BlockDrag.block`.

  A rewrap or a move can merge or split blocks, because a new gap may fall under 2.5 × size, or an edge may line up with a neighbour. When that happens, the same index names another paragraph. Concrete cases today:
  - **Switching paragraphs while one is open (#2022).** The new paragraph is opened by an index from the inventory *before* the queued edit was applied.
  - **`text_edit` result.** It reports `text_blocks(page)[k - 1]` after the edit, assuming the index survived.
  - **Multi-object selection.** It is the only code that re-finds by value: same text and the same rect within 0.01. `docs/editing-multiple-objects.md` tells agents to re-list after every edit.
- **Width and alignment are lost.** `BlockStyle.width` and `align` are edit inputs only, and reading detects only "centered".
  - A justified paragraph comes back left-aligned on the next edit. This happens even while its editor is still open, because `style()` sends `align` only when it differs from the last applied look.
  - It is always left-aligned after reopening.
  - A dragged width is re-derived from the widest row's ink, so it drifts narrower. A one-row paragraph grows to the page margin on its next edit.
- **Neighbours merge.** Paragraphs separated by a blank line are grouped into one block when the baseli…

title: Design: one layout for the inline text editor and the saved result
author: komo1iddin
body:
Area: M7 (Edit text), gap 3 · Code references are to `main` at afa8e184 · Spec basis: ISO 32000-1 §9.3–9.4 (text state, text positioning), Unicode UAX #9 (bidi) and UAX #14 (line breaking)

I'd like to agree on the direction before sending code. It touches both rewrite paths and the inline editor's layouter.

## 1. Problem

Two layouts run while a paragraph is being edited, and they disagree:

- **What the user sees.** egui's `TextEdit` lays the draft out with a custom layouter (`editor_galley`, `crates/ui-egui/src/edit_text_ui.rs:1233-1300`). It uses:
  - egui's own line breaking;
  - harfrust shaping with the page's embedded faces, with Inter as the fallback;
  - a per-run calibration that spreads the difference to the PDF run's width as extra letter spacing (1201-1209).

  Galley row `i` is then pinned onto source row `i`'s baseline.
- **What is saved.** `rewrite_block` lays the draft out again, on one of two paths:
  - single-style (`crates/edit/src/text.rs:2050-2355`);
  - styled (`rewrite_styled_block`, `crates/edit/src/text_regions.rs:244`).

  Each path has its own break rules, advances, font fallback, alignment and leading.

The engine is asked about the draft on every keystroke (`text_edit_layout`, `text.rs:138-180`), but only for a union bounding box that sizes the blue frame. It already rewrites a clone and reads the result back with `text_lines`, then throws the rows away.

Concrete cases where the preview and the saved file differ today:

| # | Case | Preview | Saved |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Line breaks | egui rules: breaks at dashes and punctuation, splits long words, has no no-end rule | UAX #14 ideographic breaks plus JIS X 4051 no-start/no-end (`linebreak.rs`); never splits a word; wraps at width + 0.5 pt |
| 2 | Row placement | galley row *i* drawn on source row *i*, even when its content is a different row | engine rows from the first baseline with its own leading |
| 3 | Advances | hmtx + GPOS + additive calibration (spaces included) | `/Widths…

title: Design: a text editing session for one paragraph
author: komo1iddin
body:
Area: M7 (Edit text), gap 3 · Code references are to `main` at afa8e184 · Builds on #2504 (`ReadState`), #2508 (stable paragraph ids) and #2511 (one layout)

I'd like to agree on the direction before sending code. It changes how formatting and Esc behave in the inline editor, and it adds a session API to `pdfcraft-edit`, the engine and automation.

## 1. Problem

Editing a paragraph has no state of its own between calls. Each keystroke and each formatting change starts again from the whole page.

- **Every keystroke re-reads the page on the UI thread.** `TextBackground::prepare` calls `text_edit_layout` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs:146-180`) synchronously whenever the text or style changes. Each call:
  - interprets the page's content (`text_lines`) and groups it;
  - rewrites the paragraph into a clone, which can build Type 3 fallback fonts or embed a full face again (`embed_mapping`, `text_regions.rs:666`);
  - interprets the clone's page again to measure the result.

  None of this is reused by the next keystroke, and the editor waits for it.
- **Every Format panel change is a committed edit** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels.rs:420-431`). Each one:
  - adds an undo step labelled "Edit text";
  - writes the whole file incrementally and builds a new `RenderPool` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs:3856-3919`);
  - regroups the page, reinstalls the editor fonts (`ctx.set_fonts`) and rebuilds the textless background, because the edit generation changed.

  So choosing a font, a size and a colour, then typing, leaves four undo steps and four full writes.
- **Rewrites compound.** After a formatting commit, the next commit rewrites content that was already rewritten. Values the rewrite derives from the source rows, such as the width calibration and the leading, are now derived from its own output.
- **Esc is inconsistent.** Esc drops the typed text (`edit_text_ui.rs:1407-1421`), but formatting applied earlier in the same session stays, because it was already committed.
- **The draft is…

title: Edit text: paragraph numbers shift after an edit, so the next edit by number rewrites a different paragraph
author: komo1iddin
body:
Paragraphs are addressed by their position in the page's paragraph list. That list is regrouped from geometry after every edit. When an edit changes the grouping, the same number then refers to another paragraph. The next edit by that number replaces the wrong text, and that text is gone.

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at afa8e184. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page PDF with three paragraphs in Helvetica 12 pt (`/F1`, WinAnsi), with this content stream:
   ```
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL 1 0 0 1 72 700 Tm (Alpha paragraph, first row of text.) Tj T* (Alpha paragraph, second row.) Tj ET
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL 1 0 0 1 72 650 Tm (Bravo paragraph, a single row.) Tj ET
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL 1 0 0 1 72 600 Tm (Charlie paragraph, first row of text.) Tj T* (Charlie paragraph, second row.) Tj ET
   ```
2. `doc_open` the file, then call `text_paragraphs {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`. It returns three paragraphs: 1 = Alpha, 2 = Bravo, 3 = Charlie.
3. Add a row to Alpha:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "Alpha paragraph, first row of text.\nAlpha paragraph, second row.\nAlpha paragraph, a third row."}
   ```
4. Edit Bravo by the number step 2 returned:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 2, "text": "Bravo paragraph, edited."}
   ```
5. Call `text_paragraphs {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`.

**Expected:** Step 4 changes Bravo. Charlie is untouched.

**Actual:**
- After step 3, Alpha's new last row is closer to Bravo, so the two are regrouped as one paragraph. Step 3's result already reports a 4-line paragraph that ends with Bravo's text.
- Paragraph 2 is now Charlie, so step 4 replaces Charlie's two rows with "Bravo paragraph, edited."
- Step 5 lists two paragraphs:
  1. Alpha + Bravo;
  2. "Bravo paragraph, edited."

  Charlie's text is gone.

title: Edit text: paragraphs separated by a blank line are one paragraph, and editing the first deletes the second
author: komo1iddin
body:
Two paragraphs with one blank line between them are grouped as a single paragraph. Rows are joined while the baseline gap is under 2.5 × the font size. A blank line at ordinary leading is 2 × 1.2 = 2.4 × size, so it falls under that limit. Replacing the first paragraph's text then removes the second paragraph.

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at afa8e184. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page PDF with two paragraphs in Helvetica 12 pt (`/F1`, WinAnsi), at 14.4 pt leading with one empty row between them. This is the content stream:
   ```
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL 1 0 0 1 72 700 Tm (First paragraph, first row.) Tj T* (First paragraph, second row.) Tj ET
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL 1 0 0 1 72 656.8 Tm (Second paragraph, first row.) Tj T* (Second paragraph, second row.) Tj ET
   ```
2. `doc_open` the file, then `text_paragraphs {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`.
3. Edit the first paragraph:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "First paragraph, edited row.\nFirst paragraph, second row."}
   ```
4. Call `text_paragraphs {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`.

**Expected:** Step 2 lists two paragraphs. Step 3 changes only the first.

**Actual:**
- Step 2 lists one paragraph with all four rows (`"count": 1`).
- After step 3, the page holds only "First paragraph, edited row. First paragraph, second row." Both rows of the second paragraph are gone.

**Notes**
- **Growing paragraphs join their neighbour too.** A paragraph that gains a row moves its last baseline closer to the next paragraph and can join it on the next read. A 2-row paragraph 3 × size above a single row joins it after a third row is added. This is the first step of the index-shift case in #2516.

title: Watermark position: an anchor (top/centre/bottom × left/centre/right) and a distance in page units, chosen with a 3×3 grid
author: mtlcl410
body:
## The gap

`edit.watermark-appearance` is `partial`. Its note says what is missing: *"no offset from the page edge or in page units"*. Since #1076, a watermark can only move by an offset from the page centre, in points: `Watermark::offset`, the dialog's "Offset from centre" row, and `doc_watermark`'s `offset_x`/`offset_y`.

That makes common placements awkward. To put "CONFIDENTIAL" in the bottom-right corner, 1 cm from the edges, you have to work out half the page size minus the mark's own extent, in points. The answer is different for A4 and Letter, and wrong as soon as page sizes vary within the document.

## Acrobat

Acrobat's Add Watermark dialog, as its online help describes it, places the mark with two settings:
- **Vertical distance** *n* *units* from **Top**, **Center** or **Bottom**;
- **Horizontal distance** *n* *units* from **Left**, **Center** or **Right**.

The units are points, inches, millimetres, centimetres or picas. The distance is measured from that edge (or from the centre), so one setting works on every page size.

## Proposal

- **Engine (`pdfcraft-edit`).** Replace the centre offset with an anchor and a distance: vertical `Top | Center | Bottom` and horizontal `Left | Center | Right`, each with a distance in points. Units stay a UI concern. `Center`/`Center` with the current offset reproduces today's behaviour exactly, so existing calls keep their meaning. The mark is placed relative to the visible page box, after `/Rotate`, as now.
- **Tool (`doc_watermark`).** Add `vertical_from` / `horizontal_from` (`top|center|bottom`, `left|center|right`, default `center`) next to the existing `offset_x` / `offset_y`, which become the distances from the chosen anchor. Existing scripts keep working.
- **Dialog.** A small **3×3 grid** picks the anchor: the nine cells are exactly Acrobat's nine Top/Center/Bottom × Left/Center/Right combinations. Next to it go the two distances and a units menu (pt, in, mm, cm, picas). The preview shows the result as it doe…

title: Proposal: Offline PDF pseudonymization workflow and repeat-area redaction
author: tbr83secure-lab
body:
Hi,

First things first: great tools your buliding! I'm very excited.
I am currently building an offline, review-first pseudonymization workflow based on PdfCraft.

A short disclosure first: I am not an experienced Rust or open-source maintainer. I am developing the prototype for my own professional workflow with substantial AI-assisted coding, followed by manual testing on local documents. I am happy to share the results, patches and test findings, but I may not be the right person to maintain a larger implementation long-term.

**Background**
I already have a separate working beta pseudonymization tool. It runs locally and can detect or manually add personal information, disable false findings, assign pseudonyms and produce a mapping file.

The beta is useful, but it has a basic interface and its PDF handling is much less capable than PdfCraft. PdfCraft's native viewer, text coordinates, redaction engine and local-first architecture make it a much better foundation.

The objective is to help EU users prepare documents before using external AI services, including services operated by US providers.

The tool should reduce disclosure of personal data by removing or replacing identifying information locally before document content is submitted to an external system.

I do not intend to claim that the tool automatically makes every workflow GDPR-compliant. Pseudonymized data may still be personal data, and users still need to assess their legal basis, the provider, contractual terms and any international data transfer requirements. title: XFA dynamic form (LiveCycle 11, Spanish ISCIII grant form): instruction page overlays every body page, growable rich-text fields clip instead of paginating, exData maxLength ignored, print button script fails
author: S-Mas
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`pdfcraft-cli-0.8.0-linux-x86_64`), Linux x86_64. Driven headless through `pdfcraft-cli mcp`. I did not test the desktop app.

**Form (public):** the M-AES 2024 "Memoria de la propuesta" (mobility grant proposal) from Spain's Instituto de Salud Carlos III (ISCIII). This is the official download from the ISCIII website: https://cne.isciii.es/documents/d/guest/m-aes24_memoria-pdf-1 (sha256 `70c4973a186bb8f3d03904f30d596fa680556ee3472d0e4b8e36969afb676cbb`). It was made with Adobe LiveCycle Designer 11 and is a dynamic XFA form with `NeedsRendering` and Reader Extensions (`/Perms /UR3`). It has 4 JavaScript scripts and no FormCalc. All ISCIII funding forms (AES calls) are built this way, and in practice applicants can fill them only in Acrobat or Reader.

**Steps (MCP tools):**
1. `doc_open` the form.
2. `form_fill` with plain test text (lorem ipsum plus `áéíóú ñ «» € µ ° ± β γ ≥ ≤ ≈ → ×`):
   - `OBJETIVOS`: 5,250 characters (the field limit);
   - `ACTIVIDADES`: 10,500 characters (limit; the form says "max 2 pages");
   - `CONTRIBUCIONES`: 12,000 characters (above its 10,500 limit);
   - `EXPEDIENTE0`: `XX00/00000`.
3. `doc_save` (in place, incremental), then reopen.
4. `js_run` with `field: "PrintButton1"` (the "TERMINAR MEMORIA" button).
5. `doc_print` with `path` to produce the print-ready PDF.
