title: Edit text: a paragraph drawn at a slant rewraps wider than it is
author: komo1iddin
body:
A paragraph turned at an angle other than a multiple of 90° rewraps about one em wider than its rows. A word that doesn't fit, and would move to the next row in the same paragraph upright, stays on its row and sticks out past the paragraph's edge.

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at afa8e184. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make two one-page PDFs with the same three-row paragraph in Helvetica 12 pt (`/F1`, WinAnsi):
   - **upright:** `1 0 0 1 72 700 Tm`;
   - **30°:** `0.866025 0.5 -0.5 0.866025 100 300 Tm`.

   ```
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL <matrix> Tm (Rotated paragraph, first row of text) Tj T* (that continues on a second row and) Tj T* (ends on the third row here.) Tj ET
   ```
2. In each, add words to the paragraph:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "Rotated paragraph, first row of text that continues on a second row and now carries a few extra words before it ends on the third row here."}
   ```
3. Call `text_lines {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`.

**Expected:** Both rewrap the same way, because the paragraph is equally wide in both. The widest source row is 189.44 pt.

**Actual:**

| | Row 3 | Row 4 |
|---|---|---|
| Upright | `now carries a few extra words` | `before it ends on the third row here.` |
| 30° | `now carries a few extra words before` (196.07 pt, past the 189.44 pt edge) | `it ends on the third row here.` |

**Notes**
- **Size of the error.**
  - The paragraph's width at a slant comes out wider by the rows' height times |sin 2θ|: about 12 pt at 30° and 13.8 pt at 45° for 12 pt Helvetica.
  - 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° are exact.
  - The width doesn't keep growing: editing again with the same text gives the same rows.
- **Cause.** `TextLine::frame_rect` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`) turns the corners of the line's *upright* bounding box into the baseline's frame, and `rewrite_block_with_limit` takes a turned paragraph's width from that. …

title: Edit text: a single turned row grows past the page edge instead of wrapping
author: komo1iddin
body:
A one-row paragraph drawn turned, for example along the page's height, grows along its baseline without limit when text is added. It never wraps, so the text runs off the page. Upright one-row paragraphs stop at the page margin (crop box − 36 pt) and wrap there.

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at afa8e184. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page PDF (612 × 792 pt) with one row turned a quarter, reading upwards from y = 600:
   ```
   BT /F1 12 Tf 0 1 -1 0 300 600 Tm (A single turned row) Tj ET
   ```
2. `doc_open` the file and lengthen the row:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "A single turned row that keeps growing with many more words added until it is far longer than the page is tall, so it has to stop or wrap somewhere"}
   ```
3. Call `text_lines {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`.

**Expected:** The row grows up to the page margin along its baseline and wraps onto further rows from there, as an upright single row does at the right margin.

**Actual:**
- One row, 774 pt long, running from y = 600 to about y = 1374.
- The page's top edge is y = 792, so about 580 pt of text is outside the page and invisible.
- `text_lines` reports the row's box as `[289.2, -582.34, 303.0, 192.0]` in view space.

**Notes**
- **Where.** `rewrite_block_with_limit` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`) gives a turned single line the largest width PDF allows (14 400 pt). The comment there says it is meant to grow rather than wrap across the page's other axis. Growing is right, but it has no end.
- **Possible fix.**
  - Cap the width where the baseline, from the row's start in its own direction, leaves the crop box less the same 36 pt margin used for upright rows.
  - Below that cap, keep today's behaviour.
  - A slanted row would get the same cap along its own direction.
- **Related.** #2515 (a one-row upright paragraph grows to the margin on its next edit).

_Found and…

title: [Bug] Reveal in File Explorer opens Documents after Save As (tab path not updated until reopen)
author: tylamb1
body:
### Description
After using **Save As**, the tab's **Reveal in File Explorer** option (added in #1233 / #1266) opens the Documents folder instead of the folder where the file was saved. The tab is renamed to the new filename, but it seems to lose its file path.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open an existing PDF from disk.
2. Right-click its tab → **Reveal in File Explorer**. ✅ Explorer opens the correct folder with the file selected.
3. **Save As** to a different name/folder (in my case, a folder on a local physical drive, `R:\`).
4. Right-click the tab → **Reveal in File Explorer**.

### Expected
Explorer opens the Save As destination folder with the new file selected.

### Actual
Explorer opens **Documents**.
- The tab title updates to the new filename, but hovering the tab shows no directory/path.

### Workaround
Close the tab and reopen the saved file. Reveal in File Explorer then works correctly.

### Likely cause
Save As updates the tab's display name but not its stored file path. Reveal then passes an empty or invalid path to Explorer, which falls back to Documents.

### Environment
- PdfCraft 0.7.1
- Windows 11 Enterprise Insider Preview, version 26H2 (OS build 26340.9616)
- File saved to a local physical disk (not OneDrive or a network share)

title: Edit text: a centred one-row title grows to the right and loses its centring
author: komo1iddin
body:
A title centred on the page, drawn as a single row, keeps its left edge when words are added. The longer title is no longer centred. If it wraps, every row starts at the old left edge.

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at afa8e184. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page Letter PDF (612 pt wide) with an 18 pt title centred on the page (its centre is at x = 306) and a body paragraph below. Font: Helvetica, `/F1`, WinAnsi.
   ```
   BT /F1 18 Tf 1 0 0 1 252.477 700 Tm (Centered title) Tj ET
   BT /F1 12 Tf 1 0 0 1 72.000 640 Tm (Body text below the heading starts here and runs) Tj ET
   BT /F1 12 Tf 1 0 0 1 72.000 625.6 Tm (on for a second row of ordinary words.) Tj ET
   ```
2. `doc_open` the file, then `text_paragraphs {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`. The title is paragraph 1 and the body is paragraph 2.
3. Lengthen the title:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "Centered title with a few more words"}
   ```
4. Call `text_lines {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`.

**Expected:** The title stays centred on x = 306 and grows by the same amount to both sides. When it no longer fits between the margins, each wrapped row is centred too.

**Actual:**
- **Step 4:** the title spans x 252.5–543.6, so its centre is now at x 398.
- **Longer text** (`"Centered title with many more words added so that the single row has to become much longer than the page"`): three rows, all starting at x 252.5.

**Notes**
- **Why only single rows.**
  - A centred paragraph of *several* rows is recognised. `rewrite_styled_block` (`crates/edit/src/text_regions.rs`) treats rows whose centres line up as centred and keeps them centred.
  - That check needs more than one row, so a one-row title is always left-aligned.
  - Without an explicit `align`, a single row grows to the right up to the page margin.
- **A possible signal for one row.** Its centre lies within a small tolerance of the cr…

title: Edit text: a right-aligned one-row line grows past its right edge and wraps into a narrow column
author: komo1iddin
body:
A single row aligned to the right margin, such as a date or a page header, keeps its left edge when words are added. It grows to the right, past the edge it was aligned to, up to the page margin. Then it wraps into a column only as wide as the space left on the right, often one or two words per row.

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at afa8e184. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page Letter PDF (612 pt wide) with a date whose right edge is at x = 540 (a 72 pt right margin) and a salutation at the left margin. Font: Helvetica, `/F1`, WinAnsi.
   ```
   BT /F1 12 Tf 1 0 0 1 450.612 740 Tm (15 October 2026) Tj ET
   BT /F1 12 Tf 1 0 0 1 72.000 700 Tm (Dear reader,) Tj ET
   ```
2. `doc_open` the file, then `text_paragraphs {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`. The date is paragraph 1.
3. Lengthen the date:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "15 October 2026 with a few more words"}
   ```
4. Call `text_lines {"doc": 1, "page": 1}`.

**Expected:** The line stays right-aligned at x = 540 and grows to the left. When it no longer fits, its rows wrap and stay right-aligned.

**Actual:**
- **Step 4:** two rows, both starting at x 450.6:
  - `15 October 2026 with a` (450.6–574.7);
  - `few more words` (450.6–535.3).

  The first row now ends 35 pt past the old right edge.
- **Longer text** (`"15 October 2026 with many more words added so that the single row has to become much longer than the page"`): six rows in a 126 pt column, from x 450.6 to the 576 pt margin, with ragged right edges.

**Notes**
- **Cause.** A single upright row's width is the larger of its own width and the distance to the margin, `crop[2] − 36 − x` (`rewrite_block_with_limit`, `crates/edit/src/text.rs`). Its left edge is the anchor. A row anchored on the right is only recognised for right-to-left text (`anchored_right`).
- **A possible signal for left-to-right text.** The row's right e…

title: Edit text: Cyrillic in a Helvetica paragraph gets one Type 3 font per letter
author: komo1iddin
body:
Some paragraphs are set in a non-embedded Latin font, such as Std 14 Helvetica. When Cyrillic, Greek or other text that needs the Type 3 fallback is added to one of them and the new text keeps a line break, the Latin text stays in Helvetica. But every distinct fallback character gets a Type 3 font of its own, drawn in its own `BT … ET`. (The same edit without a line break redraws the whole paragraph in the fallback face instead: #2750.)

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at dc41044b. It was built with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` set to craft-fonts at 3d9ab3a, the ref `release.yml` uses. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page Letter PDF with a two-row paragraph in Helvetica (`/F1`, Type1, WinAnsi, not embedded):
   ```
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL 1 0 0 1 72 700 Tm (The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog) Tj T* (and keeps running through the long field.) Tj ET
   ```
2. `doc_open` it, add a Russian word to the first row (keeping the row break) and save:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog шалом\nand keeps running through the long field."}
   doc_save  {"doc": 1, "path": "a.pdf"}
   ```
3. Run `pdffonts a.pdf` and read the page's content stream.

**Expected:**
- The Latin text stays in Helvetica.
- The new characters share one Type 3 font, or one per 240 characters (the existing `MAX_TYPE3_GLYPHS`).
- A word is drawn as one run.

**Actual**
- **`a.pdf` (11 751 bytes):** `pdffonts` lists five `BIZUDPGothic-Regular` Type 3 fonts (`PCJp` to `PCJp4`) besides Helvetica, one per letter. Each letter is its own text object and repeats the full text state:
  ```
  BT /PCJp 12 Tf 0 Tc 0 Tw 100 Tz 14.4 TL 0 Ts 1 0 0 1 72 685.6 Tm <01> Tj ET
  BT /PCJp1 12 Tf 0 Tc 0 Tw 100 Tz 14.4 TL 0 Ts 1 0 0 1 82.2 685.6 Tm <01> Tj ET
  …
  ```
  Other texts in the same form:

  | New text | Type 3 fonts | Text objects | Saved …

title: Edit text: Uzbek and Kazakh Cyrillic are refused in a non-embedded font; the only fallback faces are Japanese
author: komo1iddin
body:
Adding Uzbek or Kazakh text to a paragraph set in a non-embedded font such as Helvetica fails. The fallback face has no glyphs for letters like қ, ғ, ҳ or ә. Russian, Ukrainian and Serbian text works, but it is drawn with a Japanese face.

**Environment:** macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M3 Pro, 18 GB. PdfCraft 0.8.0, `main` at dc41044b. It was built with `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` set to craft-fonts at 3d9ab3a, the ref `release.yml` uses. Mode: Headless CLI (`pdfcraft-cli run --script`).

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a one-page Letter PDF with a two-row paragraph in Helvetica (`/F1`, Type1, WinAnsi, not embedded):
   ```
   BT /F1 12 Tf 14.4 TL 1 0 0 1 72 700 Tm (The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog) Tj T* (and keeps running through the long field.) Tj ET
   ```
2. `doc_open` it and add an Uzbek word:
   ```
   text_edit {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 1, "text": "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog қизил\nand keeps running through the long field."}
   ```
3. Repeat with the Kazakh word `әже` instead of `қизил`.

**Expected:** The words are added, in a face that covers the Cyrillic used by these languages.

**Actual:**
- **Step 2:** `the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+049B`.
- **Step 3:** `the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+04D9`.
- **What works:** `Ўзбек` is accepted, because ў (U+040E/U+045E) is covered. Russian is accepted too. Both are drawn as Type 3 glyphs from BIZ UDPGothic.

**Notes**
- **Coverage of the craft-fonts faces at 3d9ab3a**, read from each face's `cmap`:

title: Freature Requirement: Signatures: let users trust a signer’s certificate (Acrobat-style “Add to Trusted Certificates”)
author: aka1prime-svg
body:
When a signed PDF’s signer isn’t in a known trust store, the signature can’t be shown as fully trusted. Acrobat handles this with a user-managed trust list: you open the signer’s certificate, choose “Add to Trusted Certificates”, and the signature’s status changes from a yellow question mark (identity unknown) to a green tick. PdfCraft doesn’t appear to have an equivalent.

## Current behavior
PdfCraft validates PAdES signatures, but I can’t find a way to mark a certificate or CA as trusted. docs/target-app-parity.md lists an OS trust store as missing for digital signatures. Signatures from self-signed or private-CA certificates therefore stay unverified.

## Requested behavior

In the signature panel or properties, show the signer’s certificate chain with a “Trust this certificate” action.
Let the user choose what to trust: the signer certificate only, or the issuing CA.
Persist the choice in an app-level trust store. Re-validate the signature immediately, so the status updates without reopening the file.
Provide a way to import trusted certificates (.cer/.crt/.pem) and to view and remove entries.
Optionally, read the OS trust store (the already-planned item) in addition to the user list.

## Why
This is a common workflow for internal or private-CA signatures. It’s also the main gap against Acrobat for signature validation on Linux, where no OS-level Adobe trust list exists.

title: Copy, paste and cut do not work for text boxes or images in the PDF editor
author: vashellsing
body:
In the PDF editor, it is not possible to copy, paste or cut text boxes or images. The only workaround is to recreate the element from scratch (and manually reapply the style) or re-insert the image through the Insert menu.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Open PdfCraft on Windows.
2. Open any PDF and enable the PDF editing mode.
3. Create a text box and style it (font, size, color, etc.).
4. Try to copy the text box using any of these methods:
   - Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V
   - Right-click on the text box → look for a "Copy" / "Paste" option
5. Repeat the same test with an image:
   - Insert an image via the Insert menu.
   - Select the image.
   - Try Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V.
   - Right-click on the image → try "Copy image" / "Copy at original size".
6. Try to cut (Ctrl + X) as well.

### Expected Behavior
- It should be possible to copy, paste and cut text boxes, keeping their exact style (font, size, color, position, etc.).
- It should be possible to copy, paste and cut images.
- Right-click on a selected object should show a working Copy / Cut / Paste context menu.
- Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V / Ctrl + X should work as expected.

### Actual Behavior
- Text boxes: no copy/paste option appears on right-click, and Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V does nothing. The user has to create a new text box and manually reapply the exact same style.
- Images: Ctrl + C / Ctrl + V does nothing. Right-click shows "Copy image" / "Copy at original size", but after clicking them, nothing is ever pasted. Cutting is also not possible.
- The only way to add an image is through the Insert menu.

### Environment
- OS: Windows 10 last version u.u
- PdfCraft version:  0.8.0 14 Oct 2026
- Architecture: x64 
### Additional Context


This makes editing very slow, because every duplicated element has to be rebuilt manually. Screenshots or a short screen recording would help, but the behavior is 100% reproducible on my side.

title: Linearized save (Fast Web View)
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
PdfCraft can't save a linearized PDF yet (`core.linearization`, P1, planned; gap 22). Acrobat's name for it is Fast Web View: a reader fetching the file over HTTP can show page 1 before the rest arrives, and Document Properties says "Fast Web View: Yes".

I'm working on this. The plan, following ISO 32000-2 Annex F:

1. **cos:** a linearized writer in a new `crates/cos/src/linearize.rs`, built on the full-rewrite writer's object walk. It writes the linearization parameter dictionary, the first-page cross-reference section and the primary hint stream, with the page offset and shared object hint tables. Then come page 1's objects, the remaining pages in order, the shared objects and the rest. Encryption goes through the same per-object path as a full save. Signed documents are refused, as a full rewrite already is.
2. **Tests:** `qpdf --check-linearization` (qpdf is already a CI oracle) on synthetic multi-page files with shared fonts and images, an encrypted one, and an incremental save on top of a linearized file. The incremental save still opens but is no longer reported as linearized. The output reopens through our own reader.
3. **engine / automation:** `linearize` on `doc_save`, `fast_web_view` on `doc_optimize`, and `linearized` in `doc_info`.
4. Parity and docs.

The first version writes classic cross-reference tables without object streams, so a linearized file can be somewhat larger than a compressed full save. The parity notes will say so.

title: Save replaces the file: read-only files are overwritten without warning, Finder tags/xattrs are dropped, hard links break
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

## Summary
Every save (incremental ⌘S included) writes a staging file and renames it over the target. Confirmed at runtime in the desktop app on macOS:

| | Before | After ⌘S |
|---|---|---|
| private file | `-rw-------` (0600) | `-rw-r--r--` (0644), see #1790 |
| read-only file | `-r--r--r--` (0444) | overwritten **without any warning**, now 0644 (no longer read-only) |
| Finder tags (`com.apple.metadata:_kMDItemUserTags`) | present | gone |
| hard link | 2 names, same inode | broken: the other name keeps the old content |
| creation date | original | reset to the save time |

A Finder-locked file (`chflags uchg`) correctly fails with "Operation not permitted (os error 1)" and keeps the edits.

## Reproduce (macOS)
```sh
cp any.pdf private.pdf && chmod 600 private.pdf
xattr -wx com.apple.metadata:_kMDItemUserTags "$(python3 -c 'import plistlib;print(plistlib.dumps(["Red\n6"],fmt=plistlib.FMT_BINARY).hex())')" private.pdf
ln private.pdf private_link.pdf
cp any.pdf readonly.pdf && chmod 444 readonly.pdf
```
Open `private.pdf` and `readonly.pdf` in PdfCraft, add a sticky note to each, press ⌘S, then:
```sh
ls -li private.pdf private_link.pdf readonly.pdf; xattr -l private.pdf
```

## Expected
- Keep the destination's permissions/ACLs and extended attributes (Finder tags and comments, etc.), e.g. copy the metadata onto the staging file before the rename (`copyfile(COPYFILE_METADATA)` on macOS, `ReplaceFileW` on Windows), or write in place when the file has other hard links.
- Ask (or refuse and offer Save As) before writing over a read-only file, as other macOS apps do.

## Code
`crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs` `write_atomically*` (0.8.0, ~L920–949) → `crates/platform/src/staging.rs` on `main`: a `create_new` staging file plus `std::fs::rename`, with no metadata copied. The permissions part was reported in #1790…

title: One unreadable entry in /Kids or /Contents silently drops everything after it (3 of 6 pages shown, no warning)
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

## Summary
In the viewer/renderer path, an array is read only up to the first entry that can't be read or resolved; the rest is dropped without a warning. One dangling reference in `/Kids` hides the rest of the document; one in `/Contents` drops the rest of the page content. MuPDF and qpdf skip the bad entry. The editing layer (COS) still sees all the pages, so viewer and editor disagree.

## Reproduce
```python
# Writes broken_kids.pdf: 6 pages; the 4th /Kids entry points to an object that doesn't exist.
# Also writes contents_broken.pdf: /Contents [ok  missing  ok] and annots_null.pdf: /Annots [a null b].
def build(objs, size):
    out = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.7\n"); offs = {}
    for num in sorted(objs):
        offs[num] = len(out); out += b"%d 0 obj\n" % num + objs[num] + b"\nendobj\n"
    x = len(out)
    out += b"xref\n0 %d\n0000000000 65535 f \n" % size
    for n in range(1, size):
        out += (b"%010d 00000 n \n" % offs[n]) if n in offs else b"0000000000 65535 f \n"
    out += b"trailer << /Size %d /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % (size, x)
    return bytes(out)

title: Remove Security fails for PDFs encrypted by MuPDF/PyMuPDF: "the edited document could not be reopened"
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

## Reproduce
```python
import pymupdf
d = pymupdf.open(); d.new_page().insert_text((72, 72), "hello", fontsize=12)
d.save("mupdf_aes256.pdf", encryption=pymupdf.PDF_ENCRYPT_AES_256, user_pw="user123", owner_pw="owner456")
print("ok")
```
```json
[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"mupdf_aes256.pdf","password":"owner456"}},
 {"tool":"doc_unprotect","args":{"doc":1}}]
```
`pdfcraft-cli run --script unprotect.json --root .` →
```
pdfcraft-cli: step 2 (doc_unprotect): the edited document could not be reopened: the document is protected by a password
```
Same in the desktop app: open the file with the owner password, then File ▸ Remove security → toast "Remove security failed: the edited document could not be reopened: the document is protected by a password".

It also fails with AES-128 and RC4-128 files written by MuPDF. It works for files protected by PdfCraft itself or by qpdf/pikepdf, and for owner-password-only files.

## Notes
MuPDF writes the `/Encrypt` dictionary inline in the trailer rather than as an indirect object; that is the visible difference from the files that work. Possibly the same as #1762, which has no details.

title: Redaction audit reports clean: a black box over one word of a long line, and unapplied redaction marks
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

## Summary
`pdfcraft-cli audit` / `doc_audit_redactions` miss two common faux-redaction cases, both with the text still extractable under the cover:
1. A black filled rectangle over one word or number of a long line → `{"count":0}`.
2. A redaction mark that was added but never applied (`redact_mark` without `redact_apply`) → `{"count": 0, "findings": []}`.

## Reproduce
```python
# fake_redaction.pdf: a long line of text with a black rectangle drawn over one word only (text still extractable).
import pymupdf
d = pymupdf.open(); p = d.new_page(width=600, height=200)
p.insert_text((30, 100), "The contract value is 98765 and the rest of this long line continues here.", fontsize=11)
r = p.search_for("98765")[0]
p.draw_rect(r + (-1, -1, 1, 1), color=(0, 0, 0), fill=(0, 0, 0))
d.save("fake_redaction.pdf"); print("ok")
```
`pdfcraft-cli audit fake_redaction.pdf` → `{"count":0,"file":"fake_redaction.pdf","findings":[]}`, exit code 0, while `98765` is still in the extracted text.

```json
[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"any.pdf"}},
 {"tool":"redact_mark","args":{"doc":1,"find":"<a word on page 1>"}},
 {"tool":"doc_audit_redactions","args":{"doc":1}}]
```
→ `{"count": 0, "findings": []}`.

## Cause
`crates/audit/src/lib.rs`: a cover counts only when it hides at least `COVER_FRACTION` (0.4) of the whole line (L80/L145 at 9931329; still 0.4 on `main`). Measuring coverage per word would catch case 1; pending `/Redact` annotations could be reported directly. Related: #2385 (stroke, highlight and white covers), #1885 (false positive).

---
_Found while testing PdfCraft 0.8.0 on macOS (desktop app driven through `--control`, plus `pdfcraft-cli`); saved files were checked with qpdf/pikepdf and MuPDF._

title: Autosave only runs when the window repaints: an idle window never writes the recovery snapshot
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

## Summary
`autosave_tick` runs from the per-frame logic (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:2876` → `recovery.rs:187`). When the app is idle (no input, no animation), no frames run, so unsaved changes are not written to the Recovery folder until the next input event. Nothing schedules a wake-up for it.

## Reproduce (macOS)
1. Open a PDF and add a sticky note (the document is now dirty).
2. Switch to another app and leave PdfCraft alone for 2+ minutes.
3. `ls ~/Library/Application\ Support/PdfCraft/Recovery` → empty.
4. Move the mouse over the PdfCraft window → the snapshot appears at once.

If the app is killed while idle (power loss, logout, memory pressure), the edits made since the last frame-driven autosave are lost, which can be far more than one minute's work.

## Expected
While any document is dirty, schedule `ctx.request_repaint_after(AUTOSAVE_SECS)` (or autosave from a timer), so snapshots are written even when the window is idle.

The recovery itself works well: after a forced kill, the next launch offered the document and restored it with its comment.

---
_Found while testing PdfCraft 0.8.0 on macOS (desktop app driven through `--control`, plus `pdfcraft-cli`); saved files were checked with qpdf/pikepdf and MuPDF._

title: Fill & Sign date and dynamic stamps default to US formats even with a pt-BR interface
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

## Summary
With macOS and PdfCraft in Brazilian Portuguese (Preferences ▸ date language shows "Igual à interface (Português (Brasil))"):

Derive the default date format from the interface or system locale (e.g. `dd/mm/yyyy` for pt-BR), and localize the dynamic stamp text and time. The format can be changed by hand, but most users keep the default.

## Code
`crates/engine/src/dates.rs:13` `DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT = "m/d/yyyy"` (unchanged on `main`). Related: #158 (date form fields), #1741 (custom dynamic stamps).

author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

title: macOS/pt-BR localization gaps: native panels in English, unlocalized decimal separators, untranslated strings
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

With the interface in Português (Brasil) on macOS:

1. **Native open/save panels are in English** ("Save As:", "Where:", "Tags:", "Cancel", "Open"). The bundle declares only `CFBundleDevelopmentRegion` = `en` (`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`), with no `CFBundleLocalizations` or `.lproj` folders, so AppKit keeps its panels in English. Declaring the supported localizations (or `CFBundleAllowMixedLocalizations`) lets NSSavePanel/NSOpenPanel follow the system language.
2. **Decimal separators are not localized:** "9.2 MB → 434.0 KB (95% menor)", "Página PDF: 209.9 × 297.0 mm", "Escala do PDF: 89.79%", "10.0 pt", "139.6 KB". pt-BR uses a comma (9,2 MB).
3. **Untranslated strings:**
   - the Print dialog button "Save as PDF";
   - the annotation hover tooltip, which shows the raw subtype ("Square") while the Comments panel says "Retângulo";
   - the combined document's name, "Combined.pdf";
   - the stamps (APPROVED, CONFIDENTIAL, "By name at time, date");
   - the tab's accessibility label "file.pdf (edited)".
4. **Wording:** "Digite seu(sua) assinatura" → "Digite sua assinatura".
5. **`LANG=C.UTF-8` on macOS forces English:** launched from a terminal with `LANG=C.UTF-8`, Auto resolves to English, while on Windows C/POSIX means "no preference" (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/mod.rs`, `language_override`, Windows-only check). Started from Finder, it correctly uses pt-BR.
6. **Paper size:** with no printer configured, the Print dialog defaults to US Letter for an A4 document (pt-BR locale) and scales it to 89.79%.

---
_Found while testing PdfCraft 0.8.0 on macOS (desktop app driven through `--control`, plus `pdfcraft-cli`); saved files were checked with qpdf/pikepdf and MuPDF._

title: Small UI issues: Cmd+G in the find field, comment editor keeps keyboard focus, text box ignores drag, Print on print-restricted PDFs, slow Comments panel with 5,000 comments
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

1. **⌘G / ⇧⌘G do nothing while the find field has focus** (Enter works). The canvas shortcuts are skipped whenever egui wants keyboard input (`crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs:1933`). In Preview and Acrobat, ⌘G works from the field.
2. **The comment editor keeps keyboard focus.** After creating a highlight, its comment editor in the Comments panel takes keyboard focus and keeps it even after other comments are drawn (rectangle, oval…). Single-key tool shortcuts (H, V) are then typed into that editor; the text is discarded later. Focus should follow the newest comment, or return to the page.
3. **Add a text box ignores a drag.** Dragging to size the box does nothing; only a click creates it (`crates/ui-egui/src/comments.rs:809`, `resp.clicked()` only). Acrobat accepts a click or a drag.
4. **Print opens on print-restricted PDFs.** On a document whose permissions forbid printing (P = 0), the Print dialog opens normally and offers "Save as PDF". Only on confirm does a toast say, in English, "the document's security settings don't allow printing…". Disabling Print, or saying so up front, would be clearer.
5. **The Comments panel slows the UI on large reviews.** On a page with 5,000 annotations, with the Comments panel open, each frame takes ~0.28 s (about 4 fps), against ~0.07 s with the panel closed. The document itself opens in 0.4 s.

---
_Found while testing PdfCraft 0.8.0 on macOS (desktop app driven through `--control`, plus `pdfcraft-cli`); saved files were checked with qpdf/pikepdf and MuPDF._

title: Engine/CLI minor issues in 0.8.0: page labels dropped, flatten leftovers, raw UTF-8 in /URI, RC4-40 permissions, CropBox text, CLI OCR models, owner password in CLI, OpenAction not reported
author: padilhaDEVELO
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (`9931329`), macOS universal build from the release DMG, macOS 26.7.1 on Apple M4. CLI: `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0 (macOS universal zip).

Each item reproduces with `pdfcraft-cli` 0.8.0:

1. **Page labels dropped.** `page_extract` (also split and combine) drops `/PageLabels`. Extracting pages 1 and 151 of a document labelled `i … A-1` gives unlabelled pages and no `/PageLabels`.
2. **Flatten leftovers.** `doc_flatten` with `fields: true` leaves `/AcroForm /CO` pointing to the removed calculated field and `/SigFlags 1`, with `/Fields []`.
3. **Raw UTF-8 in /URI.** `link_add` with `url: "https://example.com/ação"` writes raw UTF-8 into `/URI` (`b'https://example.com/a\xc3\xa7\xc3\xa3o'`). `/URI` is 7-bit ASCII, so it should be percent-encoded; other viewers show `aÃ§Ã£o`.
4. **RC4-40 permissions.** `doc_protect` with `compatibility: "rc4-40"`, `printing: "low"`, `accessibility: true` writes `P = -3388`: high-resolution printing allowed, accessibility bit clear, and no warning. R2 can't express these choices, so they should be refused or warned about.
5. **Text outside the CropBox.** It is extracted and found by search: `text --page N` returns text that isn't visible on a page whose CropBox is smaller than its MediaBox. MuPDF clips it.
6. **Huge MediaBox.** A page with `/MediaBox [0 0 1e30 1e30]` (or `/UserUnit 1e20`) makes the file "not a readable PDF: the document has no pages"; MuPDF and qpdf open it with 1 page.
7. **CLI zip without OCR models.** The macOS CLI zip ships without the OCR models: `run ocr_status` → `"available": false`, and `search_dirs` includes the CI path `/Users/runner/work/pdfcraft/pdfcraft/crates/ocr/../../assets/models`. Pointing `PDFCRAFT_MODELS` at the app's models works.

title: Form field names containing a period (.) are rejected, and existing ones are truncated
author: ominus-dev
body: Issue When designing form fields within the Prepare a form section, PdfCraft does not accept any field name that includes a period. Trying to save a name with a period results in an error message: _Change field properties failed: field names can't be empty or contain a period_ This restriction poses a problem for users creating templates for Conga or anything requiring similar PDF Templates, which depend on dotted naming conventions such as MASTER.account_firstname or ADDRESS.street1. According to Conga, this is the correct naming convention for PDF merge fields (example: DatasetName.FieldName) – Master.CONTACT_NAME. Intended behavior Field names should be allowed to include periods. Programs like Adobe Acrobat, Foxit PhantomPDF, and Foxit PDF Editor support dotted names, which are a standard way to organise hierarchical field structures. **Foxit PDF Editor example image** **PdfCraft example image** Proposed solution If there’s a technical reason for restricting periods—such as the PDF specification’s use of periods as delimiters between parent and child fields, or if they’re crucial for automation—could this restriction be made optional? Providing a toggle in Preferences to enable periods in field names would allow users who don’t need this restriction to work without issue. Related problem: existing fields get truncated When opening and editing a PDF that contains dotted field names (created with other software), PDFCraft modifies those names. Specifically, it removes everything up to and including the period, so MASTER.account_firstname appears as account_firstname. title: Paste Clipboard Images Directly into PDF (Ctrl+V, Right-Click, Middle-Click)
author: StuGazzO
body:
I'd like to suggest adding the ability to paste screenshots and images directly from the Windows clipboard into an open PDF document, without having to save them as separate image files first.

**Example Workflow**

- Capture a screenshot using Windows Snipping Tool (Win + Shift + S) or another screenshot utility.

- Switch to PdfCraft with a PDF document already open.

- Paste the screenshot directly onto the PDF page using one of the supported methods.

- Move, resize, or rotate the pasted image as needed.

- Save the modified PDF.

**Supported Paste Methods**

Ideally, all three of the following methods would be supported:

- Ctrl + V — Standard Windows keyboard shortcut for pasting.

- Right-Click → Paste — A Paste option in the context menu when right-clicking anywhere on a PDF page.

- Middle Mouse Button Click — Optionally allow middle-clicking to paste the clipboard image directly onto the PDF page.

All three methods should provide the same functionality. Since middle-click may already have an assigned function, it could be offered as a configurable option in the application settings.

**Expected Behavior**

- Accept any image available in the Windows clipboard, regardless of the application or source it was copied from.

- Insert the image at the mouse pointer's location when pasting with the mouse, or centered on the visible page when using Ctrl + V.

- Allow pasted images to be moved, resized, rotated, or deleted.

- Preserve the image's aspect ratio when resizing, with the option to adjust it if necessary.

- Preserve the original image resolution and quality wherever possible.

- Support standard Undo/Redo functionality (Ctrl + Z / Ctrl + Y).

- Ensure pasted images are retained when the PDF is saved and reopened.

title: Hangul (Korean) shows as boxes in the interface (tab titles, file names) on Linux
author: brian-moon
body:
PdfCraft 0.8.0 (.deb), Debian 12, KDE Plasma Wayland, interface language English (LANG=en_CA.UTF-8).

Opening a file named "2026년도 성가대 찬양곡 목록.pdf" shows the tab title and window title as boxes for the Korean part. The page content renders correctly.

Cause, as far as I can tell from crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs: the embedded faces (Inter, egui defaults, the Japanese craft-fonts faces) have no Hangul, and the installed-font fallbacks cover Arabic, Devanagari, Telugu, Sinhala, Tamil and (for a Chinese interface) Han, but there is no Hangul fallback. Korean fonts are installed (Nanum, Noto Sans CJK KR, Droid Sans Fallback), but none is a candidate.

Suggestion: a Hangul fallback like the other script fallbacks, probing e.g. U+AC00 (가) against common installed faces (NanumGothic, UnDotum, DroidSansFallbackFull, Malgun Gothic on Windows, Apple SD Gothic Neo on macOS). Since DroidSansFallbackFull is already in the Han candidate list, it could also be tried for Hangul regardless of the interface language.

The logs show "interface font fallback" lines only for Devanagari, Telugu and Arabic.

title: macOS: Save on a PDF opened from Apple Mail fails with "Operation not permitted" (`is_mail_temp_copy` only knows Outlook)
author: AMJ1308
body:
## Environment
- PdfCraft 0.8.0, signed and notarized macOS universal build
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple M1 Pro
- Apple Mail, with PdfCraft as the default PDF app

## Steps to reproduce
1. In Apple Mail, double-click a PDF attachment. It opens in PdfCraft.
2. Without editing anything, press **Save** (⌘S).

## What happens
```
Couldn't save ~/Library/Containers/com.apple.mail/Data/Library/Mail Downloads/<UUID>/booking.pdf: Operation not permitted (os error 1)
```
(Home folder and file name shortened.)

Apple Mail opens attachments from its sandbox container (`~/Library/Containers/com.apple.mail/Data/Library/Mail Downloads/<UUID>/`). Other apps can't write there. `write_atomically` ([`editing.rs:920`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.8.0/crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs#L920)) creates its staging file in that folder, so the save fails.

## Expected
The same behaviour PdfCraft already gives Outlook attachments: **Save asks where to keep the file** and leaves the temporary copy alone. That's the rule at [`editing.rs:589`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.8.0/crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs#L589), covered by `save_asks_where_to_keep_an_email_attachment_and_leaves_the_temporary_copy_alone` ([`editing.rs:1302`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.8.0/crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs#L1302)).

## Cause
`is_mail_temp_copy` ([`editing.rs:911`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/v0.8.0/crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs#L911)) only matches Outlook's cache folders on Windows: `/inetcache/content.outlook/`, `/temporary internet files/content.outlook/` and `/microsoft.outlookforwindows`. It has no entry for Apple Mail, so the Mail copy is treated as an ordinary file and saved in place. `main` is unchanged as of today.

## Suggestions
1. **Add Apple Mail's folder** to `is_mail_temp_copy`, for example `/library/containers/com.apple.mail/data/library/mail downloads/`. The function already lowercases the path. Extending the existing test with a macOS-style pat…

body:
# Render: MRC scan pages whose colour layer is `/DeviceGray` draw as a ghost; Chrome/pdfium draws the same pages correctly

## Summary

In a 42-page scanned textbook, 7 pages render in PdfCraft 0.8.0 as a faint grey ghost of the
text — the letter shapes are in the right places but almost invisible — while the other 35
pages render correctly. Chrome's built-in viewer (pdfium) renders **all 42 pages correctly**,
in the same browser, on the same machine, from the same file.

The pages are Mixed Raster Content: a background image, plus a small "colour layer" image whose
`/SMask` is a 1-bit JBIG2 stencil carrying the shape of the text. The split between the pages
that work and the pages that do not is exact and has one structural cause:

| | 35 pages that render correctly | 7 pages that render as a ghost |
|---|---|---|
| background `/Im0` | `/JPXDecode` **`/DeviceRGB`** 827×1169 | `/JPXDecode` **`/DeviceGray`** 827×1169 |
| colour layer `/Im1` | `/FlateDecode` **`/DeviceRGB`** 827×1169 | `/FlateDecode` **`/DeviceGray`** 827×1169 |
| `/Im1`'s `/SMask` | `/JBIG2Decode` `/ImageMask true` 2480×3507 | `/JBIG2Decode` `/ImageMask true` 2480×3507 |
| drawing operators | `/Im0 Do` then `/Im1 Do` | identical |

`/Matrix`, same `/BBox`, no transparency group, no `/ca` or `/CA`, no blend mode, no

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached `page179-layer-test.pdf` (125 KB, 6 pages) in PdfCraft 0.8.0.

title: Redaction audit reports clean when the cover is in a second content stream
author: carbongpt
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, macOS universal zip, macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon).

## Summary
`pdfcraft-cli audit` / `doc_audit_redactions` reports clean when the opaque cover is drawn in a **second content stream** on the page (`/Contents [a b]`), even when the cover hides the whole line. The same cover merged into a single content stream is found. PyMuPDF's `draw_rect`, and other editors that append drawings, write covers this way, so it is a common shape for real-world "black box" redactions.

## Reproduce
```python
import pymupdf  # 1.26
T = "Account holder: Example Name"
def base():
    d = pymupdf.open(); p = d.new_page(width=600, height=200)
    p.insert_text((30, 100), T, fontsize=12); return d, p

d, p = base(); r = p.search_for(T)[0]
p.draw_rect(r + (-1, -1, 1, 1), color=(0, 0, 0), fill=(0, 0, 0))
d.save("cover-two-streams.pdf")          # page /Contents has 2 streams

d, p = base(); r = p.search_for(T)[0]
p.draw_rect(r + (-1, -1, 1, 1), color=(0, 0, 0), fill=(0, 0, 0))
p.clean_contents()                        # merge into 1 stream
d.save("cover-one-stream.pdf")
```

| File | Content streams | `pdfcraft-cli audit` | `pdfcraft-cli text` |
|---|---|---|---|
| cover-two-streams.pdf | 2 | `{"count":0,...}`, exit 0 | `Account holder: Example Name` |
| cover-one-stream.pdf | 1 | 1 finding, exit 1 | `Account holder: Example Name` |

Both render as a solid black bar over the line.

## Expected
A finding in both cases. Per ISO 32000 the streams in a `/Contents` array are concatenated in order, so a cover in a later stream is painted after the text in an earlier one.

Possibly related: #2662 (a different trigger: a cover over one word of a long line, in a single stream).

title: Redaction audit reports clean for a black-filled Square annotation over text
author: carbongpt
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, macOS universal zip, macOS 26.6.2 (Apple silicon).

## Summary
A **Square annotation with a black interior colour** placed over text is reported clean by `pdfcraft-cli audit` / `doc_audit_redactions`, while the text under it stays extractable. Filled rectangle annotations are what markup tools (for example macOS Preview's rectangle shape with a fill) produce when someone "blacks out" text, so it is a common faux redaction. Split out from the annotation case family in #2385, which covers `/Highlight`; this one is `/Square` with `/IC [0 0 0]`.

## Reproduce
```python
import pymupdf  # 1.26
d = pymupdf.open(); p = d.new_page(width=600, height=200)
p.insert_text((30, 100), "Account holder: Example Name", fontsize=12)
a = p.add_rect_annot(p.search_for("Example Name")[0])
a.set_colors(stroke=(0, 0, 0), fill=(0, 0, 0)); a.update()
d.save("square-annot.pdf")
```

- `pdfcraft-cli audit square-annot.pdf` → `{"count":0,...,"findings":[]}`, exit 0
- `pdfcraft-cli text square-annot.pdf` → `Account holder: Example Name`
- The annotation renders as a solid black box over "Example Name".

## Expected
A finding: an opaque annotation appearance covering extractable text, as for an opaque filled rectangle in the page content.

title: Proposal: one coverage-driven system-font fallback instead of a hand-written function per script
author: shim9610
body:
## Problem

Interface text that no embedded face covers (file names, tab titles, bookmarks) still renders
as tofu for many scripts. Korean is the most reported case (#407, #1043, #2114, #2747; Thai: #1035),
and there are several open PRs that each add support for one more script (#507, #1678, #2094, …).

Looking at `crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs` and `theme.rs::installed_font_definitions` on
current `main`, the installed-font fallback is a set of separate per-script paths:

| Script | When it is loaded | How |
|---|---|---|
| Devanagari, Telugu, Sinhala, Tamil | always | `*_fallback()` + hand-written candidate list + probe char, appended to every family |
| Simplified / Traditional Chinese | only when the UI language is Chinese (#925) | `Need::Hans/Hant`, inserted before the Japanese craft-fonts faces |
| everything else | always | a single face that must contain Arabic `U+0627` |
| Hangul, Thai (no craft-fonts), Hebrew (no craft-fonts), … | never | — |

So every new script means another probe constant, another candidate list, another
`*_fallback()` function and another PR — and each script waits until someone writes one.

## Proposal

Replace the per-script functions with one coverage-driven fallback, desktop only:

1. **Detect missing glyphs.** egui 0.36 can answer this: `Fonts::has_glyphs(font_id, s)`.
   Check untrusted, data-derived strings (file names, bookmarks, tab titles, form values)
   before drawing them and collect the characters no loaded face has.
2. **Index installed faces once, off the UI thread.** Reuse the existing directory discovery
   (`system_fonts/fontconfig.rs`, the Windows/macOS font directories) and the existing
   checks (`MAX_BYTES`, `MAX_FACES`, `face_with`) to record which Unicode ranges each face covers.
3. **Load on demand.** For a missing character, pick the best covering face from the index,
   validate it (same size cap and parse check as today, so a broken file can't crash egui), and
   add it with `Context::add_font(FontIns…

title: [Feature Request] Forms: transparent fill / no border for new fields, or Make Current Properties Default for fields
author: boneyland
body:
### What I did

Prepare a form ▸ Detect form fields on an unfilled PDF. Detection placed the fields well, but every field was created with a grey border and a white fill. The white fill covers the printed form underneath, including the box lines and any shading.

I fixed it with bulk edit by setting Border color: No color and Fill color: No color on all fields. That worked, but I have to do it on every form I prepare, and again for any field I add afterwards.

### Where the default comes from

`crates/forms/src/author.rs`, `widget_dict()` (lines 499-506 on `f0c9901`) gives every new widget:

- `/MK /BC [0.55 0.55 0.55]`: grey border
- `/MK /BG [1 1 1]`: opaque white fill
- `/BS << /W 1 /S /S >>`: 1 pt solid border

Detected fields go through the same path (`Engine::auto_detect_fields` → `Edit::AddField` → `pdfcraft_forms::add_field` → `widget_dict`), as do fields drawn by hand. Image fields already remove both colours (`author.rs:613-614`), so a field with no border and no fill is already supported.

### What I'm asking for

Either of these would solve it. The second is the more general fix.

1. **Transparent default.** New fields, or at least detected fields, are created with no `/BG`, and optionally no `/BC`. Detected fields sit on top of a form that already draws its own boxes, so a border and fill drawn over them are redundant.
2. **Make Current Properties Default for form fields.** Right-click a field (or tick a box in field Properties) to make its border colour, fill colour, border width and style, font and text colour the defaults for new fields of that type. This should persist the way comment tool styles do since #365 (`comment_styles`) and #2031 (Make Properties Default in Comment Properties). Detect form fields would then use those defaults too.

### Related

title: Digital Sign Verification
author: cre8ive-marketing
body:
🐛 Bug: Digital Signature Validation Fails on Double-Click and "Validate All"

**Description**

The digital signature validation workflow is currently broken across multiple interaction points. Users are unable to trigger signature verification either individually via direct interaction or globally using the batch action button.

**Expected Behaviour**

1. Individual Validation: Double-clicking on a specific digital signature field should immediately trigger the validation process for that signature.
2. Global Validation: Clicking the "Validate All" button should iterate through all digital signatures present in the document/system and validate them concurrently or sequentially.

**Actual Behaviour**

• Double-clicking on a digital signature field does nothing (the validation routine is not invoked).
• Clicking the "Validate All" button fails to trigger verification for the signatures, and the UI state remains unchanged.

**Potential Root Causes to Investigate**

• Event Handling: The dblclick mouse event listener might not be bound to the correct signature field layer, or the event is being swallowed by an overlapping DOM element/UI container.
• Async/Promise Issues: The "Validate All" routine may be failing silently due to unhandled asynchronous promises during batch cryptographic checks.
• Thread Blocking: Cryptographic validation tasks might be blocking the main UI thread, causing the application to drop the event before updating the layout.

title: Page indicator ignores PDF page labels (/PageLabels): shows physical index while bookmarks show labels
author: anmacmillan
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.8.0 (macOS universal, `pdfcraft-0.8.0-macos-universal.dmg`). The same behaviour was seen in PrintCraft 0.2.1.

**Summary.** The page indicator ignores the document's `/PageLabels` and shows the physical page index. The bookmarks panel does read the labels, so the two disagree within the same window.

**Why it matters.** Court and tribunal bundles are commonly distributed with front matter, such as an index or contents list, that is unnumbered or numbered i, ii, and so on. The pages after it are numbered from 1 to match the printed page stamps, and submissions cite those printed numbers. Page labels exist so that a viewer can show and accept the printed number. Acrobat and PDF.js both honour them. Without this, "page 35" means two different pages depending on which part of the UI you look at.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Make a PDF whose first two pages are labelled `i` and `ii` and whose remaining pages are labelled `1`, `2`, `3` and onwards (script below).
2. Open it in PdfCraft.

**Expected.** On the first page, the page box shows `i`. On the third physical page it shows `1`, optionally with the physical position as well, e.g. "1 (3 of 180)".

**Actual.** On the first page, the page box shows `1 / 180`, the physical index. The bookmarks panel, meanwhile, correctly shows each entry's label (`i`, `1`, `55`, …).

**Suggested behaviour.** Follow Acrobat:
- show the label in the page box, with the physical position as a secondary hint where the two differ;
- interpret a typed page number as a label first, falling back to the physical index;
- optionally add a preference to turn this off.

I have not tested typed "go to page" separately.

A minimal test file can be produced with PyMuPDF:
```python
import fitz
d = fitz.open()
for _ in range(5):
    d.new_page()
d.set_page_labels([
    {"startpage": 0, "style": "r", "firstpagenum": 1},
    {"startpage": 2, "style": "D", "firstpagenum": 1},
])
d.save("labels.pdf")
```

title: Applying redactions leaves structure-tree references to the annotations and fields it removes
author: mtlcl410
body:
**What happens.** When redaction removes annotations or form fields under a mark (the apply path in `crates/redact/src/lib.rs`, and `delete_field`), it takes them off the page's `/Annots` but leaves the structure tree's object references (`/OBJR`) to them. In a tagged PDF, a full rewrite then still reaches the removed comment or widget through `StructTreeRoot`, and with it the text under the mark: a comment's `/Contents`, a field's `/V`.

**Expected.** As in Sanitize since #2532: references to annotations no page lists any more are dropped, and an element left with nothing to tag loses `/Alt`, `/ActualText`, `/T` and `/E`.

**Notes.**
- Found by @Losminek in the review of #2532 (point 2), which fixes the same gap for Sanitize.
- The helper there (`tags::drop_object_refs`, fed with the annotations listed before and after) should fit the redaction path as is.
- A test would be a tagged page with a comment and a text field under a mark, both tagged with OBJRs, checking that after applying and a full save neither the comment text nor the field value is in the file (saved without object streams).

title: Export pages to SVG
author: pauliusiv123-rgb
body:
PdfCraft can't export pages to SVG yet (`create.export-svg`, P1, planned). Acrobat offers this under Export a PDF as one vector file per page.

I'm working on this. The plan:

1. **Export:** one `.svg` per chosen page, rendered through the vendored `hayro-interpret` with the `hayro-svg` 0.7 device (Apache-2.0 OR MIT, from the same project as the hayro crates we already vendor). The existing `[patch.crates-io]` entry routes it to our patched interpreter, and all of its dependencies are already in `Cargo.lock`. Paths, fills, strokes, clips, shadings and images stay vector or embedded; text is drawn as glyph outlines, so it looks right without the fonts installed but is not selectable in the SVG.
2. **engine / automation / CLI:** SVG as a new export format next to the image formats, with page ranges and the usual `--root` confinement on the output path.
3. **Desktop:** SVG in the export format list, with its strings in every catalogue.
4. **Tests:** the SVG parses as XML, has the page's size and viewBox, honours page rotation and the CropBox, and keeps vector paths as paths. Malformed or empty pages give an error, not a panic. Parity entry and docs.

title: A closed right panel reopens on Bookmarks when the PDF sets /PageMode /UseOutlines
author: musaad-sharikh
body:
When I close the right panel (Inspector), PdfCraft keeps it closed for ordinary PDFs, as #1590/#1603 intended. A PDF whose catalog sets `/PageMode /UseOutlines` reopens it on Bookmarks every time I open it. Files from wkhtmltopdf do this, for example. Once that has happened, the panel also comes back after a restart.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any PDF and close the right panel (Inspector).
2. Open a PDF whose catalog contains `/PageMode /UseOutlines` (and an `/Outlines` tree).
3. Close the panel again, quit PdfCraft and start it again.

### Actual

At step 2 the right panel opens on Bookmarks. After step 3, the saved state contains `"right_panel_closed": true` together with `"docking_right": "Bookmarks"`, and the panel is shown again.

### Expected

A right panel the user closed stays closed, as it does for documents without an Initial View, until the user opens it again.

### Environment

PdfCraft 0.8.0, Flatpak (`ai.storyteller.pdfcraft`, stable), Linux. The same code is on `main` at f0c9901c.

### Likely cause

- The #1590 guard (`!self.right_panel_closed`) only covers the automatic Comments/Bookmarks choice in `commit_open` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1284` in v0.8.0).
- `apply_initial_view()` runs right after it and sets `self.right = Some(RightPanel::Bookmarks)` for `Navigation::Bookmarks` without checking `right_panel_closed` (`lib.rs:1060`). The same happens for Pages, Attachments and Layers.
- `restore()` then brings back `docking_right`. Because the guard needs `self.right.is_none()`, the panel stays open in later sessions.

#1996 deliberately keeps the `/PageMode /UseOutlines` behaviour, so it does not cover this case.

title: Right rail: page navigation cluster overlaps the panel buttons when the window is short in points (worse at higher Interface size, e.g. 150 %)
author: musaad-sharikh
body:
### Description

The page navigation cluster at the bottom of the right rail (page box, page count, view/page arrows, zoom %, fit, rotate, page display, zoom buttons) overlaps the panel buttons at the top of the rail whenever the window is too short in **logical points**. The page box ends up on top of the Tags/Signatures icons and the page count is drawn over an arrow icon.

Because Preferences ▸ Interface size divides the window's physical height into fewer points, a larger interface size makes the overlap appear in larger windows. At 150 % on a 1080 px tall screen, a maximized window is only ~720 pt tall, which is below the threshold on `main`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open any PDF (a 2-page file is enough).
2. Set Preferences ▸ Interface size to 150 %.
3. Make the window shorter than about 1155 px physical (on `main`) or 1050 px (on 0.8.0), for example a maximized window on a 1920×1080 display.
4. Look at the bottom of the right rail.

### Expected behavior

The rail's controls never overlap. When the rail is too short, it scrolls or drops or hides some controls, and each control stays readable and clickable.

### Actual behavior

The bottom cluster is drawn over the top buttons: the page box sits on the Tags icon, and the total page count overlaps the icon next to it. The higher the interface size, the larger the window that is affected. At 200 % on a 1080 px screen, the whole cluster runs up over most of the rail.

### Measured thresholds

Headless renders with `crates/ui-egui/examples/shot.rs` (`--scale 1`, varying `--size` height, a 2-page PDF, default layout, Accessibility Checker button not shown):

| `main` (`f0c9901c`) | ≤ 760 pt | 765 pt | 770 pt |

title: Add content ▸ Text: clicking on page text opens it for editing, so new text can't be placed next to it
author: Coffeediff
body:
### What happens

Since #1539, a click with the **Add content ▸ Text** tool on existing PDF text opens that text in the Edit text editor instead of starting a new box. The click target is the text's box plus a small margin, so on a text-heavy page (a worksheet, a form, a letter) most clicks near the text open it. That makes it hard or impossible to:

- add an answer or note right after a line of printed text
- add a label just above or below a heading
- add text over a lightly printed area, such as a line to write on

To add text there, you have to click away from the text, then drag the new box into place.

### Steps

1. Open a PDF with ordinary text.
2. Edit a PDF ▸ Add content ▸ Text.
3. Click just to the right of, or on, a line of the page's text.

**Expected:** a new empty text box at the click.
**Actual:** the page's paragraph opens for editing.

### Proposal

Keep one job per tool:

- **Add content ▸ Text always adds new text** where you click, whether or not there's page text there.
- **Edit text & images** stays the way to edit the page's own text, as it does today.
- Clicking text *you added* with the Text tool still reopens it for retyping, as #1539 made it. That case doesn't block anything, because added text is the user's own.

If page-text editing from the Text tool is wanted, a **double-click** on page text could open it, while a single click adds new text. Happy to do either.

The change is small: the `over_source` routing in `canvas.rs` for `QuickTool::AddText`, plus updating `text_tool_clicking_source_text_edits_instead_of_adding_a_copy`. I can send the PR once there's agreement on single-click-adds vs double-click-edits.

title: AutoCAD SHX text: the letter "M" renders as a box (□)
author: marcelodambrowski
body: PDFs plotted from Autodesk Civil 3D 2023 draw every capital "M" of SHX text as an empty box: "MATO NATIVO" shows as "□ATO NATIVO", "MURO" as "□URO", "POMAR" as "PO□AR", "LIMITE IMÓVEL" as "LI□ITE I□ÓVEL". Other letters are fine, and Poppler/Acrobat draw the "M" correctly. Producer: pdfplot16.hdi 16.02.172.00000 (Civil 3D 2023). The SHX text is vector geometry (stroked paths), with "AutoCAD SHX Text" comments on top. Likely cause: the SHX "M" is a single open polyline, `m` + four `l` (side, diagonal, diagonal, side), touching all four corners of its bounding box. `path_as_rect` in vendor/hayro-interpret/src/context.rs accepts any 5-element path that touches the four corners as a rectangle, so the open "M" is stroked as a closed box. Minimal reproduction (40×40 page): 0 G 2 w 5 35 m 35 35 l 5 20 l 35 5 l 5 5 l S Expected: an "M" on its side. Actual: a rectangle. Suggested fix: only take the rectangle shortcut when the path is closed (`m l l l h`, or `m l l l l` back to the start) and every side is horizontal or vertical. Screenshot attached.

title: Attach and Embedded File is the differential
author: denisdamata
body: I don't know why, but Okular doesn't support anymore "Embedded Files". That was Okular’s most important feature, which made it a replacement for the buggy Foxit. Not only can it open PDFs, but it can also add files (PDFs, images, etc.) to a PDF using clickable symbols, as shown in the figure below. There are some PDF readers, such as Stirling PDF, that allow you to add files, but they do so in a completely generic way—without an icon and without specifying the location within the PDF where the file was inserted—which makes them practically useless. This feature is what sets PDF apart, and currently—unfortunately—there is no free, open-source solution available to do this, which is why I am forced to use Master PDF. I noticed that pdfCraft has listed this feature as “milestone M12,” but it would be great if it were implemented as soon as possible.

title: Field detection: a box whose sides have an extra middle point (6-point path) is not detected
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `form_detect_fields` finds a filled cell drawn as a 4-corner closed path, but finds nothing when the same cell is written with an extra point in the middle of each vertical side (6 points). The shape on the page is identical.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows 11 x64 portable.

**Steps to reproduce.** Save as `t8.py` and run `python t8.py` (PyMuPDF), which writes `cells.pdf`:

```python
import fitz

d = fitz.open()
p = d.new_page(width=595, height=842)
w, h = 11.1, 14.7
for k in range(13):
    x = 100 + k * w
    for y, mid in ((100, False), (150, True)):
        pts = [(x, y), (x + w, y)]
        if mid:
            pts.append((x + w, y + h / 2))
        pts += [(x + w, y + h), (x, y + h)]
        if mid:
            pts.append((x, y + h / 2))
        p.draw_polyline(pts, fill=(0, 0, 0), color=None, closePath=True)
d.save("cells.pdf")
```

`steps.json`: `[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"cells.pdf"}},{"tool":"form_detect_fields","args":{"doc":1,"add":false}}]`
Then `pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root .`

**Actual.** 13 fields (kind `checkbox`, one per cell) for the 4-point row (the first row in `t8.py`, y=100 from the top); none for the 6-point row.

**Expected.** Both rows detected the same way. A middle point on a straight side does not change the shape.

**Why / use case.** The French income tax form 2042 (public, impots.gouv.fr) draws its letter cells like this (white fill, no stroke, each vertical side split in two). On page 1, 14 fields are found; I count about 355 cells with my own detection (checked on a render). Over the 6 pages, 142 are found against about 614.

**Notes.** My guess, not checked in the source: collinear intermediate points could be dropped before the four-edge test. #1596 limits closed-path rectangles to four corners plus a repeated endpoint. Related: #294, #1887 (comb rows; once the cells are detected they would still come out as one check box each).

title: Field detection: a check box is named after the next label instead of the nearer one before it
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** `form_detect_fields` names a detected check box after a neighbouring label, but in a "label, box, label, box" line it picks the label that follows the box (23 pt away) instead of the one that ends 5 pt before it. The box gets a wrong name rather than a generic one.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows 11 x64 portable.

**Steps to reproduce.** Save as `t9.py` and run `python t9.py` (PyMuPDF), which writes `labels.pdf`:

```python
import fitz

d = fitz.open()
p = d.new_page(width=595, height=842)
y = 300
p.insert_text((100, y + 8), "Monsieur", fontsize=10)
p.draw_rect(fitz.Rect(146, y, 157, y + 10), color=(0, 0, 0))
p.insert_text((180, y + 8), "Madame", fontsize=10)
p.draw_rect(fitz.Rect(222, y, 233, y + 10), color=(0, 0, 0))
d.save("labels.pdf")
```

`steps.json`: `[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"labels.pdf"}},{"tool":"form_detect_fields","args":{"doc":1,"add":false}}]`
Then `pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root .`

**Actual.** Box at x=146 (after `Monsieur`, 5 pt gap): `Madame`. Box at x=222 (after `Madame`): `Check Box1`.

**Expected.** `Monsieur` and `Madame`: the nearest label on the same line. If the rule is "label to the right of the box", that is fine too, but then a label that sits closer to the box on the other side, or that is the natural label of the next box, should not win over it.

**Why / use case.** An agent that fills fields by name ticks the wrong box. A wrong name is harder to notice than a generic one.

**Notes.** On page 1 of the public French form 2042 (impots.gouv.fr) I see the same: the `Monsieur` box of the first filer is named `Madame`, the one of the second filer `Madame2`. Related: #93 (detection names a field from the label beside it), #294.

title: Create PDF from images ignores JPEG EXIF Orientation (doc_combine, doc_create, doc_create_multiple): portrait photos come out sideways
author: erwanpaccard
body:
**Summary.** A JPEG that carries an EXIF Orientation tag is turned into a page from its stored pixels, with the tag ignored, when it goes through `doc_combine`, `doc_create` (`from: "images"`) or `doc_create_multiple`. Photos taken in portrait mode end up sideways. `page_add_image`, `stamp_custom` and `doc_watermark` apply the tag (since #485), so the library already has the logic; the "create PDF from images" paths do not use it.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows 11 x64 portable.

**Steps to reproduce.** Save as `t10.py` and run `python t10.py` (Pillow). It writes `photo.jpg` (300 x 200 stored pixels, EXIF Orientation=6, which viewers show as 200 x 300) and `plain.jpg`:

```python
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

# 300 x 200 landscape pixels, stored with EXIF Orientation=6 (viewers show it as 200 x 300 portrait)
im = Image.new("RGB", (300, 200), "white")
ImageDraw.Draw(im).text((10, 10), "TOP-LEFT of stored pixels", fill="black")
exif = Image.Exif()
exif[0x0112] = 6
im.save("photo.jpg", exif=exif)
Image.new("RGB", (300, 200), "gray").save("plain.jpg")
```

`steps.json`: `[{"tool":"doc_combine","args":{"paths":["photo.jpg","plain.jpg"],"out":"out.pdf"}}]`
Then `pdfcraft-cli run --script steps.json --root .`

**Actual.** Page 1 of `out.pdf` is 300 x 200 pt (landscape) and the embedded image is 300 x 200 px, as stored. The same happens with `doc_create` (`from: "images"`, `paths: ["photo.jpg"]`) and `doc_create_multiple` (`paths: ["photo.jpg"]`): 300 x 200 pt page, 300 x 200 px image.

**Expected.** A 200 x 300 pt page (portrait) with the image turned as the tag says, as `page_add_image` already does: on a blank page it embeds the same `photo.jpg` as 200 x 300 px.

**Why / use case.** A real DSLR portrait JPEG (Orientation=8, 4608 x 3072 stored) assembled into a PDF shows the photo lying on its side. Phone and camera photos commonly carry this tag, and an agent building a PDF from photos cannot see the result without rendering it.

title: Embedded TrueType fonts with a byte-swapped post version (00 00 00 03) are rejected, so Hebrew text renders with fallback glyphs
author: omonzon
body:
﻿**Version:** pdfcraft 0.8.0 (Windows x64 MSI), also reproduced with `pdfcraft-cli render`

## Summary

A PDF produced by ScanSoft PDF Create! (2006, from Microsoft Word) embeds its fonts as TrueType subsets (David, David Bold, Times New Roman, Guttman). Every embedded font has a `post` table whose version field is the bytes `00 00 00 03`. That is `0.0000458` as a 16.16 fixed value; the intended value is evidently 3.0 (`00 03 00 00`).

PdfCraft rejects these fonts, falls back to a substitute font, and the Hebrew text is drawn wrongly:

- some text is drawn as Latin look-alike glyphs (garbled)
- some text is not drawn at all (only punctuation remains)

Text extraction (`pdfcraft-cli text`) returns the correct Hebrew, because it uses `/ToUnicode`. Only rendering is affected. Acrobat-class viewers show the file correctly.

## Cause

`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/blob.rs`, `OpenTypeFontBlob::new` (around line 180):

```rust
// Reject fonts with invalid post table version, fixes pdf.js issue 9462.
let invalid = f.post().is_ok_and(|p| {
    !matches!(p.version().to_major_minor(), (1, 0) | (2, 0) | (2, 5) | (3, 0))
});
if invalid { return None; }
```

`FontType::new` in `font/cid.rs` then returns `None` for the embedded font, so `Type0Font::new` takes the fallback branch (`fallback = true`). `map_code` then maps CIDs through `/ToUnicode` into a substitute font, which has no glyphs for these CIDs (or different ones).

The same check affects simple `/TrueType` fonts with an embedded subset (the same file has them).

## Verification

I copied the PDF and patched only the `post` version in all 12 embedded font files (`00 00 00 03` → `00 03 00 00`). Nothing else changed. After the patch, `pdfcraft-cli render` shows the Hebrew correctly on every page I checked (page 4 in particular).

Earlier attempts that did not help: removing `/ToUnicode`, adding an explicit `/CIDToGIDMap /Identity`, and changing the simple-font encoding or flags.

## Suggested fix

The `post` table is onl…

title: Web build: automatic language ignores the browser's language
author: mccoy88f
body:
In the browser build (v0.8.0), the interface language set to *Auto* always shows English, even when the browser is set to a language the app has a catalog for. The desktop build follows the system language correctly.

**Steps:** open the web build in a browser set to Italian (`navigator.languages` = `["it-IT"]`) with no saved preferences → the interface is in English.

**Cause:** The wasm branch of `detect_system_lang()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/mod.rs` doesn't read the browser's languages, so *Auto* resolves to English.

**Suggested fix:** on wasm, use `navigator.languages` (falling back to `navigator.language`) as the system language tags. GridCraft (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n.rs`, `navigator().language()`), FilmCraft (`apps/filmcraft-web/src/lib.rs`, `navigator().languages()`), VectorCraft, WordCraft and CadCraft already do this in their browser builds.

---
Found while hosting the Craft Apps on a self-hosted ArtCraft Launcher server: https://github.com/mccoy88f/craft-launcher-docker

title: Remove security works with the user password alone when the permissions allow everything
author: mtlcl410
body:
**What happens.** `Edit::RemoveProtection` (`doc_unprotect`, File ▸ Remove security) is allowed when `unrestricted(p)` holds (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`):

```rust
/// Opened as owner, or nothing is restricted (no permissions password was set): security may
/// be changed, as in Acrobat.
fn unrestricted(p: &pdfcraft_cos::Permissions) -> bool {
    const ALL: i32 = 0b1111_0011_1100; // bits 3–6 and 9–12
    p.owner || p.bits & ALL == ALL
}
```

The second half reads "every permission bit set" as "no permissions password was set". But a file can have a separate owner password **and** every permission bit set. That's the default when PyMuPDF and pypdf encrypt with both passwords. When such a file is opened with only the user password, `p.owner` is false, but removing security is still allowed, and the saved file has no password at all.

Checked on current `main` (924c4da) with `doc_open` using the user password, then `doc_unprotect` and `doc_save`:

| file (user `user123`, owner `owner456`) | `/P` | result |
|---|---|---|
| pypdf AES-256, all permissions | `0xFFFFFFFC` | **allowed**; the saved file opens without any password |
| pypdf AES-256, print only | `0x4` | refused ("don't allow changing security") |
| protected by PdfCraft itself (default: no changes) | — | refused |

The same happens through #2702's fix for MuPDF-written files, which is how I first noticed it.

**Why it may matter.** Changing security isn't one of the `/P` permissions, so with every bit set the owner password's only remaining job is to guard the security settings themselves. The tool's own description says the document "must have been opened with its permissions password, or have none". Here it has one, and it wasn't used.

**Question for the maintainers.** Is the "all bits set" branch meant for this case, or only for files whose owner password is empty or equal to the user password? `p.owner` already tells whether the opening password authenticated as owner. Requiring it whenever the file has…

title: Edit text: text drawn inside a Form XObject isn't offered for editing (pdfpages, n-up, imposition)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** current `main` (924c4da4), Windows 11; `pdfcraft-cli` built from it.

## Summary

Edit text only sees text drawn directly in a page's content streams. Text drawn inside a **Form XObject** (`/Fm1 Do`) is extracted, searched and rendered, but it isn't offered for editing:
- `text_lines` and `text_paragraphs` don't list it, and `text_edit` refuses it with "page 1 has 0 lines".
- `object_list` shows the whole form as one artwork item. It can be moved, but its text can't be retyped.

This is a common structure:
- pages placed by LaTeX `pdfpages`
- n-up and imposition tools
- PyMuPDF `show_pdf_page`
- stamps and letterheads applied as forms
- some "print to PDF" and merge tools that wrap each source page in a form

On such files, Edit text finds nothing to edit, and the UI gives no reason why.

`parity/acrobat-features.toml` (`edit.text-edit`) and `docs/editing-existing-text.md` don't mention the limitation.

## Reproduce

```python
import pymupdf  # writes the source page as a Form XObject on the new page
s = pymupdf.open(); p = s.new_page(); p.insert_text((72, 100), "Text inside a form", fontsize=12)
d = pymupdf.open(); q = d.new_page(); q.show_pdf_page(q.rect, s, 0)
q.insert_text((72, 300), "Text on the page", fontsize=12); d.save("single.pdf")
```

`pdfcraft-cli run --script` with `doc_open`, `text_lines` and `object_list` on page 1 gives:
- `text_lines`: only `Text on the page`.
- `object_list`: `Text on the page` (kind `text`) and one `image` item (the form), with `text: null`.
- `pdfcraft-cli text single.pdf` extracts both lines.

A form shared by two pages (the same `/Fm1` on each) behaves the same way: `text_edit` on page 1 says "page 1 has 0 lines".

## What a fix has to decide

The behaviour itself is clear (Acrobat edits text inside forms), but the design has choices that belong to the maintainers:

1. **Edit in place or inline.** A form used once on one page could have its content moved into the page, wrapped in `q <form /Matrix> cm <BBox clip> ……

title: Render: knockout transparency groups (/K true) are drawn as non-knockout
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** current `main` (924c4da4), and the same on PdfCraft 0.7.1; `pdfcraft-cli render`, Windows 11.

## Summary

A transparency group with `/K true` (knockout) is drawn as if it weren't knockout. In a knockout group, each object composites with the group's initial backdrop rather than with the objects drawn before it in the group (ISO 32000-2, "Knockout groups" and the group attribute `/K`). PdfCraft blends overlapping objects in such a group with each other, so it renders `/K true` and `/K false` identically.

Knockout groups appear in exported artwork, such as Illustrator's "Knockout Group" option. With them, overlapping semi-transparent shapes in a group don't darken each other.

## Reproduce

`make_knockout.py` (standard library only) writes two PDFs. Each has a transparency group holding a red and a blue square at `ca 0.5`, half overlapping: one with `/K true`, one without.

```python

title: Export to Word drops the page background colour
author: LimitlessRam
body:
## What happened

Export to Word keeps text colour and drops the page background. A blank page whose background was set with Edit a PDF → Background opens in Word as a white page. The text stays blue.

## Steps

Seen in PdfCraft 0.7.1 on macOS (About PdfCraft: Version 7.1 (0.7.1)), recorded 13 Oct 2026.

1. Create PDF → Blank page.
2. Edit a PDF → Text. Type some text and set it blue.
3. Edit a PDF → Background. Pick a colour (he used a teal; the page turns that colour in PdfCraft) and apply it.
4. Export to Microsoft Word and open the .docx.

The Word page is white. The blue text is there. In PdfCraft the page is still teal.

Source: Kru Mark Tutorials, [PDFCraft? Someone Vibe Coded a Free Adobe Acrobat Clone (First Look)](https://youtu.be/__OvC-xOpWc), about 7:48–8:00 for the background and 9:51–10:06 for the Word document.

## Expected

The page colour is a Word page background, so the page is teal behind the blue text.

## Still the case on main

`export::Page` is width, height, blocks and images. It has no page colour. `section()` writes `w:pgSz` and `w:pgMar` only (`crates/export/src/lib.rs`). Text colour is written as `w:color`, which is the case closed in #526. This report is the page background, not the text colour.

A background drawn behind an existing file's white page fill is a separate problem, tracked by #2633. This export was from a blank page where the colour was visible in PdfCraft.
