title: [Feature Request] Ctrl + Drag to duplicate pages in the Organize Pages grid view
author: Cooval
body:
### Summary
Add the ability to duplicate pages by holding the `Ctrl` key (or `Option`/`Alt` on macOS) while dragging and dropping them in the **Organize Pages** grid view.

### Motivation / Use Case
Currently, the Organize Pages grid view allows users to reorder pages via drag-and-drop. However, when working with templates, forms, or repetitive document layouts, users often need to duplicate existing pages and place them in specific positions. 

In industry-standard tools like Adobe Acrobat, holding `Ctrl` while dragging a page thumbnail copies the page to the new drop location while leaving the original page intact in its initial position. Adding this modifier-key workflow makes page manipulation significantly faster and more intuitive than using a separate context menu action followed by a manual move.

### Proposed Behavior
1. **Trigger:** The user selects one or more page thumbnails in the **Organize Pages** grid view, holds down the `Ctrl` key (`Option`/`Alt` on macOS), and drags the selection to a new position in the grid.
2. **Visual Feedback (Optional but recommended):** While `Ctrl` is held during the drag operation, display a small `+` badge/indicator next to the cursor or dragged thumbnail preview to signal that the action will copy rather than move the page(s).
3. **Action on Drop:** 
   - If `Ctrl` is held upon releasing the mouse button, insert a duplicate of the dragged page(s) at the target drop index.
   - Keep the original page(s) untouched at their original index.
   - If `Ctrl` is released before dropping, fall back to the standard move/reorder behavior.

### Reference
- **Adobe Acrobat Pro / Standard:** In the *Organize Pages* view, `Ctrl + Drag & Drop` duplicates the selected page(s) to the target drop indicator.

When the pointer is over the top mode bar (Menu / All tools / Read / Edit / Convert / E-Sign), the cursor changes according to whatever is on the PDF page underneath the bar. title: OCR text layer leaves text render mode 3 (invisible) set, hiding text added afterwards (e.g. header & footer)
author: monkeyhut
body:
## What happens

After `ocr_recognize` has added its text layer to a page, any text added to that page afterwards is invisible. Header & footer (`doc_header_footer`) is one example: the text is in the file and `text_extract` returns it, but neither PdfCraft's renderer nor MuPDF draws it.

## Steps to reproduce (pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, Windows x64, MCP)

1. `doc_combine` with two or three PNG/JPEG images that contain some text, without `out`. This opens doc 1.
2. `ocr_recognize` `{doc: 1}`
3. `doc_header_footer` `{doc: 1, header_left: "Test", footer_center: "Page <<1>>", color: "#888888"}`
4. `doc_save` to a new path, then render a page (`pdfcraft-cli render … --dpi 150`).

Expected: header and footer are visible.
Actual: they are missing from the render. `pdfcraft-cli text` lists them.

If you swap steps 2 and 3 (header & footer first, then OCR with `skip_text_pages: false`), header and footer show up correctly.

## Cause

`text_layer` in `crates/ocr/src/lib.rs` (line 218 at `924c4da`) writes

```
/OCR BMC
BT
3 Tr
…
ET
EMC
```

The text rendering mode (`Tr`) belongs to the graphics state, and `ET` does not reset it. Because the layer is not wrapped in `q … Q`, every content stream that comes after it on the page inherits `3 Tr` (invisible). The header/footer stream does not set its own `Tr`, so it draws invisibly as well.

The content streams of the affected page look like this:

```
q %PdfCraft
q 1000.051 0 0 1000.051 0 0 cm /Im0 Do Q
Q %PdfCraft
/OCR BMC BT 3 Tr /PCHelv 1 Tf … ET EMC        <- leaves 3 Tr set
q /Artifact … BDC BT /PCHelv 10 Tf 0.533 0.533 0.533 rg … (Page 3) Tj ET EMC Q
```

## Suggested fix

Wrap the layer in save/restore:

```rust
let mut out = b"/OCR BMC\nq\nBT\n3 Tr\n/PCHelv 1 Tf\n".to_vec();
// …
out.extend_from_slice(b"ET\nQ\nEMC\n");
```

The existing test (it checks that the layer starts with `/OCR BMC` and ends with `EMC\n`) still passes. As a defensive second measure, the writers for added text (header/footer, watermark, `page_add_text`) cou…

A page's `/Contents` array is one content stream in pieces, which writers may split between any two tokens (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2). These all read the pieces joined:

title: A content stream ending inside a % comment: Edit text, the redaction audit and redaction disagree with the renderer, and redaction reveals hidden content
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, `main` @ `924c4da4` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00, MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

When one stream of a page's `/Contents` array ends inside a comment (`% …` with no end-of-line before the stream's end), PdfCraft reads the page two different ways:

- **Rendering and text extraction** continue the comment into the next stream, so whatever follows up to the next end-of-line is not drawn. hayro's `Page::page_stream` joins the streams with a space. pdftotext and MuPDF do the same.
- **Edit text, `object_list`, the redaction audit, redaction and the Office/HTML export** join the streams with `Pieces::join` (`crates/content/src/lib.rs`), which puts a **newline** between pieces. That ends the comment, so the next stream's first line becomes live content.

The consequences:
1. Edit text and `object_list` offer a paragraph whose second half is drawn nowhere.
2. `doc_audit_redactions` reports text as covered by a box that nothing draws.
3. **`redact_apply` on unrelated text on the same page makes the hidden content visible in every viewer.** It rewrites the first stream without the comment, so the next stream's text object is no longer swallowed.

ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2 only says how streams may be split (between tokens), and a comment counts as whitespace, not a token. Whichever reading is chosen, PdfCraft's renderer and its editing, audit and redaction code should agree. Today the renderer agrees with pdftotext and MuPDF, and the rest doesn't.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes three one-page PDFs whose `/Contents` holds two streams. The first stream of each ends inside a comment:

```python

title: Flattening comments removes a non-comment 3D annotation and its U3D model (evince-541-0.pdf)
author: jpeskov
body:
## Summary

Running `doc_flatten` with `comments: true, fields: false` deletes a `/Subtype /3D` annotation, along with its U3D model stream and default view. The tool is documented as merging *comment and/or form field* appearances. PdfCraft's own classifier says 3D annotations are not comments, so a comments-only flatten should leave this one alone.

The page still looks almost the same afterwards because the annotation's static poster gets baked in. The interactive 3D content is gone, though, and nothing warns that it was removed.

## Steps to reproduce

```json
[
  {"tool": "doc_open",    "args": {"path": "evince-541-0.pdf"}},
  {"tool": "doc_flatten", "args": {"doc": 1, "comments": true, "fields": false}},
  {"tool": "doc_save",    "args": {"doc": 1, "path": "flattened.pdf", "full": true}}
]
```

## Expected

Comment annotations are flattened. Non-comment annotations are kept, including the 3D annotation, its `/3DD` U3D stream and its `/3DV` view.

## Actual

The saved file contains no annotations and no 3D or U3D objects:

| | Input | Comments-only output |
|---|---|---|
| Page 1 annotations | `[(21, '3D')]`, full-page `/Rect` | `[]` |
| `/3DD` stream | `/Subtype /U3D`, 35,948 bytes | missing |
| `/3DV` default view | `24 0 R` | missing |
| File size | 197,981 bytes | 160,090 bytes |

The output passes qpdf validation, so the file is valid. The data has simply been removed.

## Likely cause

On `main`, the flatten selector picks every non-widget annotation except `Link` and `Popup` when `comments` is enabled:

```rust
// crates/edit/src/flatten.rs
Which::Comments { comments, fields } => {
    let widget = subtype == b"Widget";
    !matches!(subtype, b"Link" | b"Popup") && (!widget || fields) && (widget || comments)
}
```

`is_comment_subtype()` in `crates/annot/src/lib.rs` explicitly excludes `Screen`, `Movie`, `RichMedia`, `3D`, `PrinterMark`, `TrapNet` and `Watermark` (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6), and `non_markup_annotations_are_not_comments` tests that. The flatten…

title: Community testing: help test PdfCraft against the PDF Association Stressful PDF Corpus
author: jpeskov
body:
## Goal

I'd like to get more people testing PdfCraft against the [PDF Association's Stressful PDF Corpus](https://pdfa.org/stressful-pdf-corpus/). It's a public collection of more than 32,500 PDFs taken from bug reports across many PDF projects. Some files are malformed, some use unusual features, and others trigger compatibility problems that everyday PDFs rarely do.

The goal isn't to pass or fail the whole corpus. It's to find specific problems, reproduce them, get them fixed, and build up a set of regression tests along the way.

## New to contributing? This is a good place to start

You don't need deep technical expertise to help here. A pull request asks you to understand the codebase, write a fix, add tests and get through review. A good bug report mostly asks for curiosity and care, and maintainers can turn it into a fix and a regression test.

A coding agent makes this much more approachable. If you don't already use one, [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) is a good starting point: it's open source and gives you capable models for free, which is plenty for this kind of testing. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others work well too. It can run PdfCraft next to Poppler or MuPDF, diff the outputs, explain what's going on inside a PDF, search existing issues for duplicates, and draft the report. **You're still the reporter**, though. Rerun the command, look at the page, and make sure the problem is real before posting. If you aren't sure whether something is a bug, say so in the issue.

## Related efforts

- #2361 is a parallel community effort testing the KillerPDF corpus, with results, scripts and methodology you can reuse.
- #2458 is a 350-PDF real-world corpus run against 0.8.0.

This issue complements those efforts with a different corpus and isn't meant to replace them. Different corpora turn up different edge cases.

## Pilot results

title: [Feature Request] An option to target to specific version of PDF
author: Maniues
body:
Hi,
I have a proposal for a feature in PdfCraft to include an option to allow targeting of a specific PDF version.

An idea originates from LibreOffice Writer's PDF export feature, as presented in the screenshot.

In short, while creating a PDF, an option shall allow targeting a specific version of PDF, particularly a distinction between PDF 1.7 and PDF 2.0. While PdfCraft generated PDF 1.7, I believe in the near future it will generate 2.0 as well.

It will be useful (especially when it comes to PDF/A) to select a version of PDF.

As per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_PDF PDF is backward inclusive. PDF 1.7 contains all features of PDF 1.0 and further. So MAYBE implementing this would be limited to disallowing certain features and changing the PDF header in the exported file.

From a user perspective, PdfCraft shall open any PDF file, from 1.0 to 2.0. Exporting to a selected PDF version is a compatibility feature for operating in older systems. They are some ways to do so:

1. Use the lowest version of PDF possible. If the document doesn't make use of features introduced in PDF 1.6, save as PDF 1.5. If the document doesn't make use of PDF 1.5 features, go with PDF 1.4... To be fair, this has serious issues like Unicode support, which differs between PDF 2.0 and earlier. This is an argument that this shouldn't be implemented, since characters are used in most PDFs.
2. As mentioned in LibreOffice Writer, explicitly allow targeting specific versions. I recommend this, and this feature request is about this functionality.

I propose to allow version targeting for the following versions:
1. PDF 2.0
2. PDF 1.7
3. PDF 1.6
4. PDF 1.5 (the oldest PDF version I personally found in recent years)

After some time, support for versions 1.0-1.4 may be added to make PdfCraft a universal PDF toolkit, even better than Acrobat, but this feature shouldn't be recognized as a priority.

title: Translation catalogs and their ATTRIBUTION hashes put almost every open UI PR into conflict
author: regendorf-ux
body:
### The problem

Almost every open PR that adds a UI label goes into conflict whenever *any* other PR touching the translation catalogs merges, even when the two PRs' rows have nothing to do with each other.

Two things combine to make the conflict certain:

1. **`ATTRIBUTION.toml` pins a SHA-256 of each of the 22 catalogs** (`crates/ui-egui/src/i18n/*.tsv`, `kind = "translation"`), and `cargo xtask assets` fails when a hash doesn't match. So any PR that adds one row to a catalog must change that catalog's `sha256` line, and two such PRs always change the same 22 lines differently.
2. **New rows are appended at the end of each catalog**, so two PRs that each add a label also collide on the last lines of the same 22 files.

Since the coverage tests rightly require every new label to be translated in the same PR, nearly every UI PR touches all 22 catalogs and all 22 hash lines.

A concrete case from today: c7a6feb3 ("i18n: translate the new link and file-name messages", one row per catalog) put 18 of my 19 open PRs into conflict at once. None of them touch those messages. In each one the resolution was mechanical: keep both sides' rows, recompute 22 hashes. With roughly 200 PRs a day arriving, every contributor pays this several times a day, and so does every reviewer who waits for a branch to stop moving.

### Possible fixes (any one helps; the first removes most of it)

1. **Don't pin hashes for contributor-original translation catalogs.** Their entries could stay in `ATTRIBUTION.toml` (title, author, source, licence, usage) with `sha256` optional for `kind = "translation"` whose `source` is contributor-original. The hash protects provenance for third-party files, where a silent change matters; for files the project writes itself, git history already records every change and who made it. If a pin is still wanted, CI could recompute and commit it on `main` after merge instead of each PR carrying it.
2. **Insert rows by section instead of at the end.** The catalogs al…

title: demo-pdf fails on Windows: chrome.exe exits before the PDF is written
author: cbbozeman
body:
## Environment

- Windows 11 Enterprise (10.0.26300), x64
- rustc 1.99.1 (stable, MSVC)
- pdfcraft commit `0ac9b84` (current `main`)
- Google Chrome 154.0.8037.98 (`C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`)

## Repro

```
cargo xtask demo-pdf
```

It fails every time:

```
demo-pdf: rendering raster
demo-pdf: printing with C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe
xtask demo-pdf: error: Chrome exited with exit code: 0 without writing \\?\C:\Development\pdfcraft\dist\demo\build\chrome.pdf; see \\?\C:\Development\pdfcraft\dist\demo\build\chrome.log
error: process didn't exit successfully: `target\debug\xtask.exe demo-pdf` (exit code: 1)
```

`chrome.log` is empty. Right after the failure, `dist\demo\build\chrome.pdf` exists and is complete
(about 2.9 MB, 13 pages). Chrome wrote it, just after xtask had already given up.

## Root cause

On Windows, the `chrome.exe` process that `print_to_pdf` launches exits with code 0 while Chrome's
child processes are still writing the PDF. `print_to_pdf` (`xtask/src/demo_pdf/chrome.rs`) checks
the file once, the moment `try_wait()` reports that exit. If `is_complete(pdf)` is not yet true, it
bails right away.

To confirm: running the same command line with PowerShell's `Start-Process -Wait`, which also waits
for child processes, writes the PDF in about 3.5 s, both to a plain path and to a `\\?\` verbatim
path. So the path format and the flags are not the problem. Only the exit timing is.

Related: #954 fixed two other Windows `demo-pdf` problems (the `file:////?/` URL, and Chrome being
killed after an early incremental write). It kept the exit branch as it was, and that branch is
where this failure happens.

## Suggested fix

When Chrome exits, don't fail straight away. Poll for up to 60 s until the file exists, passes
`is_complete`, and has stopped growing (same size on two polls in a row), then return `Ok`. Bail
only if that never happens. Success on Linux and macOS is unchanged, because the file is alrea…

title: Supporting Complex XFA Forms
author: JDziurlaj
body:
I'm the author of the [Remote Ballot Marking (RBM)](https://github.com/HiltonRoscoe/RemoteBallotMarking)
tool, a remote ballot marking application built entirely on XFA and packaged as a single
self-contained PDF. I know from years of maintaining it just how complicated XFA gets once you
go past simple forms. When Mozilla landed XFA support in PDF.js, I contributed test cases from
this project, and I'd like to offer the same to PdfCraft.

I saw #60 and the `form.xfa-*` parity items, and I think RBM would make a useful conformance
exemplar as you build out dynamic XFA. Here's why.

## What it is

RBM is a dynamic XFA 3.3 application: the ballot is
laid out at open from an OASIS EML 410 (XML) data source, the voter marks contests (N-of-M and RCV,
including write-ins), and the result can be exported/transcribed (including a calculated QR
code). It is fully offline, and it ships as a series of XDP fragments stitched into one XDP
and packaged as a PDF.

The key difference from the real-world XFA found elsewhere: **RBM ships its complete sources** — template fragments, script
objects, stylesheets, and sample data — plus documentation of the internals. This gives reference of expected behavior which
is rare, most forms are shipped without documentation from the form developer.

## What it exercises

A single document that concentrates most of the hard parts of XFA:

- **Dynamic layout & data binding** (`form.xfa-dynamic`, `form.xfa-data`): Template DOM →
  Form DOM at open; repeating subforms driven by the data (`occur`); `subformSet relation="choice"`; conditional binds with SOM predicates like `$.Contest.[VotingMethod == "FPP"]` and `Exists(...)`; the data DOM updates as the voter marks, and exports back to XML.
- **Multi-column pagination**: three `contentArea`s per `pageArea`, with `keep`,
  `overflow leader/trailer`, and `breakBefore targetType="pageArea"` controlling how contests flow across columns and pages.
- **Floating fields**: hidden fields embedded into rich t…

title: An inline image whose samples contain "EI " is cut there, and its remaining samples are run as page content (render, text, Find)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, `main` @ `924c4da4` (the code below is unchanged on `0ac9b840`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3) for text and rendering, pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 for text (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

An unfiltered inline image's data length is fully determined by its parameters: `/W × /H` samples of `/BPC` bits in `/CS`, rows padded to a byte. PDF 2.0 also allows `/L`. Despite that, the renderer's content parser (`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/content/mod.rs`, `UntypedIter`) ends the image data at the first `EI` followed by whitespace, then checks with a heuristic that what follows parses as content (a text operator, or 20 valid operators).

So when the samples themselves contain `EI ` and the bytes after it happen to read as operators, two things go wrong:
- the image is cut there and drawn wrong;
- **the rest of its samples are executed as page content**.

In the fixture below, 47 grey samples contain `0EI Q BT /F1 18 Tf 72 600 Td (Injected) Tj ET q`. PdfCraft draws the word "Injected" on the page, extracts it as text, and Find finds it. MuPDF and pdftotext treat those bytes as pixels, as the image's length says they are.

The edit layer agrees with MuPDF, because `crates/content/src/lib.rs`, `unfiltered_image_end`, uses the computed length. So does the redaction interpreter. PdfCraft therefore disagrees with itself: the page shows and searches text that Edit text and redaction don't see.

This differs from #2456, where the content *after* a real `EI` is lost because of a byte above 0x7F. #2483 (open) changes the look-ahead used there but keeps "first acceptable `EI`" as the rule, so it doesn't address this.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `ei_in_samples.pdf`: four pages, each drawing a grey inline image into (100, 300)–(300, 500) and then the text "After image P*n*".
- Page 1 is the case.
- Page 2 has the same 47 samples w…

title: Edit text, redaction and export lose the rest of a page when an inline image's EI has no whitespace before it (`…>EI`, `…)EI`)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, `main` @ `924c4da4` (the code below is unchanged on `0ac9b840`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

PdfCraft's content parser (`crates/content/src/lib.rs`) finds the end of an inline image with `end_of_image`. It looks for an `EI` that is **preceded by whitespace** and followed by whitespace or a delimiter. For unfiltered images it first tries the exact length (`unfiltered_image_end`), but that also requires whitespace between the data and `EI`.

So when the data runs straight into `EI`, no end is found and the image is taken to run to the end of the content stream. Two common shapes:
- an ASCIIHex image whose end-of-data `>` is followed directly by `EI` (`2060A0E0>EI`);
- raw samples whose last byte is `)` or `]` before `EI`.

The renderer (hayro), `pdfcraft-cli text`, MuPDF and pdftotext all end the image there, and draw and read the text after it. The parser behind **Edit text (`text_paragraphs`), `object_list`, the Office/HTML export and redaction** doesn't. For them, everything after the image on that page is image data. On such a page:
- Edit text offers none of the text after the image;
- redaction refuses: "redaction could not be verified: 12 item(s) were still found under the marks, so nothing was changed". It fails safe, but that page can't be redacted at all.

This differs from #1318 / #1404 / #1418 (unreadable inline-image keys) and #2456 (a byte above 0x7F after the image), which are other ways the end goes missing.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes two four-page files. Each page draws a grey inline image into (100, 300)–(300, 500) and then the text "After image P*n*".

- **`ei_without_space.pdf`:**
  - p1: ASCIIHex `2060A0E0>EI`, the case;
  - p2: `2060A0E0> EI`;

title: Text drawn in clipping mode (`7 Tr`) is missing from text extraction, Find, word count and search-redaction, though it shows on the page
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, `main` @ `924c4da4` (the code below is unchanged on `4f6d1638`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

Text rendering mode 7 adds the glyph outlines to the clipping path without painting them. It is how gradient-, image- or pattern-filled titles are written: the text sets the clip, then a shading, an image or a fill is painted through it, and the letters show.

PdfCraft draws such a page correctly. But its reading path doesn't see the text at all, so:
- `pdfcraft-cli text` (and `text_extract`, `doc_export_text`) returns nothing for it;
- Find doesn't find it, and `text_word_count` counts 0 words;
- **`redact_mark` with `find` reports "nothing matched"**, so the text can't be found to redact. Other readers still extract it from the saved file.

Modes 4–6 (fill/stroke *and* clip) and mode 3 (invisible) are read fine. Only pure clipping is lost.

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `tr7_clip_text.pdf`:
- page 1 is the case;
- page 2 is the same with `4 Tr` (fill and clip);
- page 3 is `3 Tr` (invisible);

title: Edit a PDF loses or misplaces an image or form whose `Do` (or `cm`) is in the next content stream: not listed, not selectable, and a move sends it off the page
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, `main` @ `4f6d1638` · Windows 11 x64 · oracle: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3) (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

A page's `/Contents` array is one content stream in pieces, and a piece may end between any two tokens (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2). PdfCraft draws such pages correctly. But the image layer of Edit a PDF (`page_images`, and `object_list`, `image_hit` and `image_edit`, which build on it) parses each piece on its own. An operator whose operands end one piece and whose keyword starts the next is lost:
- **`/Im0` ‖ `Do Q`**: the image is drawn, but it isn't listed, `image_hit` on it finds nothing, and `image_edit` says "page 1 has 0 images". It can't be selected, moved or deleted.
- **`q 100 0 0 100 72 500` ‖ `cm /Im0 Do Q`**: the `cm` is dropped, so the image is listed at `[0, 791, 1, 792]` (a 1 pt square in the top-left corner) instead of where it is drawn. Clicking it finds nothing. **Moving it to a new rect writes a 100× transform: the saved image ends up at `[7500, −59708, 17500, −49708]`, far off the page.** (Delete still works.)
- **`/Fm0` ‖ `Do Q`**: the same as the first case for Form artwork.

title: Edit text redraws every row of a paragraph in its first row's state: a row in a hidden layer becomes visible, a semi-transparent row turns opaque, a horizontally scaled row is widened
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, `main` @ `4f6d1638` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

Edit text groups rows into a paragraph by their position and font. When one letter of the paragraph is changed, the whole paragraph is rewritten at its first row's `BT`, and each row's original show operators are removed. The rewrite takes its state from the first row: its CTM, its graphics state and its text state. If a later row was drawn in a different state, set by operators around that row, the row loses it:

- **A row inside `/OC /L1 BDC … EMC`, where `/L1` is a layer that is OFF.** The row is hidden. PdfCraft's own render and `text` don't show it, and neither do MuPDF and pdftotext. But Edit text includes it in the paragraph ("…the first line and the second"), so the editor shows hidden text. After any edit, the row is written outside the `BDC … EMC` and **becomes visible on the page and in every reader's text**.
- **A row drawn after `/GS0 gs` with `ca 0.3`.** It shows light grey. After the edit, it is opaque black.
- **A row after `80 Tz`.** It is 80 % wide. After the edit, it is 100 % wide.

A paragraph whose rows share their state (page 4) changes only in the edited row.

This is a different cause from #2377 (backgrounds, images and shadings painted *between* rows end up over the rewritten text) and #1680 (rows under different clips). Here nothing is painted between the rows, and there is no clip; the row's own state is lost.

The open PR for #2377, #2562 (head `77c27e5f`), doesn't change this. Built and run on the steps below, it gives the same table as `main` for pages 1–3. Its "each row uses its own inherited graphics state" applies when artwork is painted between the rows.

### What happens

The faux-redaction audit (`doc_audit_redactions`, `pdfcraft-cli audit`) counts an opaque filled rectangle drawn after a text line as covering it. It doesn't consider whether the rectangle is actually painted there. On each of these pages the text is fully visible in MuPDF and in PdfCraft's own render, yet the audit reports a `covered-text` finding, and `pdfcraft-cli audit` exits 1 ("findings exist"):

- **The box is outside the current clip** (`q 0 0 10 10 re W n … re f Q`).
- **The box is drawn by a form XObject whose `/BBox` doesn't reach the text.** A form is clipped to its BBox (ISO 32000-2 §8.10.1).
- **The box is in an optional-content layer that is OFF** (`/OC /L1 BDC … EMC`). PdfCraft's renderer and MuPDF don't draw it.
- **The text is drawn in `7 Tr` and then filled through with a dark colour.** This is how gradient- or colour-filled titles are written: the page-sized fill is clipped to the glyphs, so it is the text. The audit reports the page-sized fill as covering the text.

A clean page (5) has no finding. False findings like these make `pdfcraft-cli audit` fail in a pipeline for documents that are fine, and they train users to ignore its findings.

title: Redaction removes the glyphs but keeps the marked-content `/ActualText`, so MuPDF and pdftotext still extract the redacted text
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.8.0, `main` @ `3f5a784c` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

Text inside a marked-content sequence can carry its own replacement text. It can be given inline (`/Span <</ActualText (…)>> BDC … EMC`) or through `/Properties` (`/Span /MC0 BDC`). Text extractors output the `/ActualText` in place of the glyphs it spans. Tagged PDFs, and PDFs whose text was reordered or ligated, use it a lot.

When redaction removes glyphs inside such a sequence, it leaves the `BDC` and its `/ActualText` as they were. Any glyph left inside the sequence then makes extractors output the whole `/ActualText`, **redacted words included**:
- After search-redacting "123" in "Name John / SSN 123" (one `/ActualText`, two lines), **MuPDF and pdftotext both still extract "Name John SSN 123"** from the saved file.
- With the named form, MuPDF does.
- The black box is drawn and `redact_apply` reports success.

When every glyph in the sequence is removed, extractors print nothing. But the `/ActualText` string with the redacted words is still in the page's content stream (page 3), readable by anyone who opens the file in a text editor or any PDF library.

Redaction already removes `/ActualText` (and `/Alt` and `/E`) from structure elements whose content it touches (`crates/redact/src/tags.rs`). The marked-content operand isn't covered.

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `actualtext_redact.pdf` and `clip_title.pdf`:

body:

### What happens

Gradient-, image- or colour-filled titles are commonly written as text in a clipping render mode, followed by a fill that the glyphs clip:

```
q BT /F1 48 Tf 7 Tr 72 660 Td (Title) Tj ET 0 0 1 rg 0 0 612 792 re f Q
```

Only the letters show, in blue. Changing such a title in two ways destroys the page:

- **Edit text** rewrites the title in its own `q … Q` block, without the clipping mode. It leaves the original `BT 7 Tr … ET` behind as an empty shell. With no glyphs, that text object no longer clips, so the page-sized blue fill after it is drawn unclipped: **the whole page turns blue**, and the new title is underneath it.
- **Redaction** with a rectangle over the whole title removes all its glyphs from the clipping text object. It then clips the fill to "everything except the redaction box". So again **the page turns blue**, apart from the black box.

Content drawn later (here, "Body text") still shows. Everything the fill covers is hidden, in MuPDF as well as in PdfCraft. A plain filled title (page 4) is edited correctly.

(PdfCraft's text and Find don't see `7 Tr` text at all, #3109. Edit text does, and offers it as a paragraph.)

title: Touchpad scrolling: add speed-dependent acceleration (faster swipe scrolls disproportionately farther)
author: Thaer99ob
body:
## Description

When scrolling with a two-finger touchpad swipe, the page moves 1:1 with finger movement regardless of how fast I swipe. In web browsers, a faster swipe accelerates the scroll, so the page travels much farther than a slow swipe of the same finger distance. PDFCraft has no equivalent, so getting through long documents takes many repeated swipes.

This is separate from #1708 / #531 (momentum after lifting your fingers), which #1909 addressed. This request is about the scroll speed **while the fingers are still on the touchpad**.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open a long multi-page PDF in continuous layout.
2. Swipe slowly with two fingers over a given distance and note how far the page moves.
3. Swipe the same finger distance quickly.

## Expected behavior

The faster swipe moves the page disproportionately farther than the slow one (speed-dependent gain), as in Firefox and Chromium-based browsers.

## Actual behavior

Both swipes move the page the same amount, because scrolling tracks the finger 1:1 (#759).

## Suggestion

Since #759 deliberately made touchpad scrolling 1:1, acceleration could be an optional preference (for example "Touchpad scroll acceleration", off by default), or a gentle nonlinear gain curve applied to the precise-touchpad delta in `canvas.rs`. It should combine sensibly with the glide from #1909.

## Environment

- OS: Linux (Wayland)
- App version: Latest
## Related

- #759 (touchpad scrolling 1:1)
- #531 / #1708 (momentum scrolling), fixed by #1909

title: Arrange moves an image into another element's marked content
author: skylartaylor
body:
Found while reviewing https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2155.

`content_units` in `crates/edit/src/images.rs` ignores `BDC`/`EMC`, so Arrange treats marked-content boundaries as if they weren't there.

Repro: `/P <</MCID 0>> BDC q 100 0 0 100 50 50 cm /Im0 Do Q EMC /P <</MCID 1>> BDC BT /F1 12 Tf 72 700 Td (Text) Tj ET EMC`, then BringToFront on the image.

Result: the image is inserted inside MCID 1's `BDC…EMC` (tagged as the text), and MCID 0 is left empty. That silently corrupts the tagged-PDF structure.

Expected: units respect marked-content sequences. Either the image's `BDC…EMC` moves with it as a whole, or the move lands outside the destination's sequence, or Arrange refuses with an "unsupported" error.

title: Arrange: a top-level inline image swallows the rest of the content stream as one unit
author: skylartaylor
body:
Found while reviewing https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2155.

The `BI` branch of `content_units` in `crates/edit/src/images.rs` scans forward for an `EI` op, but the parser emits an inline image as a single `BI` op. The unit therefore runs to the end of the stream.

Effects:
- SendBackward on an image after a top-level inline image acts like SendToBack (confirmed with a probe).
- BringForward or BringToFront on an image inside the swallowed region can silently do nothing (from reading the code).

Expected: a `BI` op is a unit of its own.

title: Image Arrange and Remove Crop report success when they did nothing
author: skylartaylor
body:
Found while reviewing https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2155.

In `crates/edit/src/images.rs`:
- `arrange_image` returns `Ok(())` without changing anything in several cases: the target isn't found in any unit, there's only one unit, a `let … else { return Ok(()) }` misses, or the destination falls inside the source span. A no-op at the front or back of the stack is fine; the other cases are odd or hostile layouts and should return an "unsupported" error so the command doesn't report success.
- `remove_image_crop` returns `Ok(())` when the image has no exclusive scope, so Remove Crop "succeeds" on an image it couldn't uncrop.
- The no-panic rule: `arrange_image` still indexes with `&ops[target]` (as the `unwrap_or` fallback for the scope's start and end ops, and in the `has_other_paint` branch). It's in bounds today but breaks the no-indexing rule; use `get(..)` with an error.

title: crop_image misreads user-space crop rects inside [0,1] as image coordinates
author: skylartaylor
body:
Found while reviewing https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2155.

`crop_image_impl` in `crates/edit/src/images.rs` has an `is_normalized` heuristic: any crop rect whose coordinates all fall within `[0,1]` is treated as image UV coordinates instead of user space.

Problems (from reading the code):
- A genuine user-space crop near the page origin, e.g. `[0, 0, 0.5, 0.5]`, is misread as a fraction of the image.
- An upright user-space crop of a rotated image becomes a UV bounding box rather than the rect asked for.

Expected: one unambiguous coordinate space per API, e.g. a separate function or an explicit parameter for normalised crops.

title: Page texture can exceed max_texture_side after a page is replaced (debug assertion / abort)
author: skylartaylor
body:
Seen once in 20 local runs of the ui-egui `editing` test binary while fixing another flaky test for https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/pull/2155.

`replace_split_selection_keeps_the_unchecked_page` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/editing.rs`) hit egui's `load_texture` debug assertion: `Texture "page-DocId(1)-0" has size 1880x2350, but the maximum texture side is 2048`.

The size works out to the 400x500 replacement page rendered at scale 4.7. That scale suits the original 200x300 page; for the larger page the render would normally be tiled.

Hypothesis (not confirmed): a whole-page render requested before the replace finished is uploaded after page 0 has become the larger page. The plain-page upload branch in `crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs` doesn't check the result against `max_texture_side`.

Impact: it could abort the app on GPUs limited to 2048-pixel textures. Expected: drop results rendered for a stale page size, and never upload a texture larger than `max_texture_side` (tile or downscale it instead).

body:
## Description

I'm using PdfCraft v0.9.0 on Windows and noticed that the **Add Text** tool only provides three font options:

- Helvetica
- Times
- Courier

There is currently no visible option to select installed Windows fonts or import custom font files.

This makes it difficult to add Traditional Chinese text to existing PDF documents, as the available standard fonts do not provide the necessary CJK character coverage.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a PDF document in PdfCraft v0.9.0 on Windows.
2. Navigate to **Edit PDF**.
3. Select the **Add Text** tool.
4. Open the font dropdown menu.
5. Notice that only Helvetica, Times, and Courier are available.
6. Attempt to find an option to select or import a font that supports Traditional Chinese.

## Expected Behavior

Users should be able to select fonts installed on Windows or manually import supported `.ttf` or `.otf` font files.

For example:

- Microsoft JhengHei
- Noto Sans TC
- Noto Serif TC

This would make it possible to add Traditional Chinese text and potentially other CJK characters to PDF documents.

## Actual Behavior

The Add Text tool only offers three predefined fonts, with no visible option to select installed fonts or import custom fonts.

## Environment

- **Application:** PdfCraft v0.9.0
- **Operating System:** Windows
- **Feature:** Edit PDF → Add Text
- **Language:** Traditional Chinese (zh-TW)

## Additional Information

I noticed that the project documentation mentions font-related capabilities such as "Installed fonts" and "Load font", but these options do not appear in the Add Text interface in v0.9.0.

It would be helpful to clarify whether custom font selection is already supported elsewhere in the application or is planned for a future release.

## Suggested Improvement

Consider adding:

1. Support for selecting installed system fonts.
2. An option to import custom TTF/OTF fonts.
3. Proper CJK font embedding when saving edited PDFs.
4. A suitable fallback font for Traditional Chinese and…

title: [Bug] PDFCraft fails to render PDFs with a large number of pages
author: JoaoMarcosVilela
body:
# [Bug] PDFCraft fails to render PDFs with a large number of pages

## Bug Description
When opening a PDF document containing a large number of pages, PDFCraft fails to render the content properly. The pages appear in the interface but remain blank, without displaying their actual content.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open PDFCraft.
2. Select a PDF file containing a large number of pages.
3. Wait for the document to load.
4. Notice that the pages appear blank instead of displaying their content.

## Expected Behavior
PDFCraft should correctly render all pages of a PDF document, regardless of the number of pages, while maintaining reasonable performance and smooth navigation.

## Actual Behavior
When loading large PDF documents, PDFCraft fails to render the page content, displaying only blank pages.

## Suggested Improvements
Investigate the rendering process for large PDF documents and consider implementing performance optimizations, such as:

- **Lazy loading:** Render pages only when needed.
- **On-demand rendering:** Prioritize rendering visible pages.
- **Memory management:** Optimize memory usage when handling large documents.
- **Caching:** Improve the caching strategy for rendered pages.

## Environment
- **Application:** PDFCraft
- **Project:** ArtCraft
- **Version:** To be determined
- **Operating System:** To be determined

## Suggested Labels
`bug` `performance` `pdf-rendering`

title: [Bug] Print-to-PDF progress toast has layout and completion issues, and grayscale setting has no effect
author: hugeifixed
body: ## Description When printing a large PDF to PDF, the progress toast appears cramped, particularly around the percentage indicator. As the page count and percentage change, the text shifts and jitters instead of remaining in a stable position. Once progress reaches 100%, the toast remains there for a long time before the operation eventually finishes, making it unclear whether processing is still ongoing or has stalled. Additionally, selecting “Print in grayscale” has no effect on the generated PDF. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open a large, multipage PDF containing colored text or images. 2. Open the Print dialog. 3. Select “Print in grayscale.” 4. Start printing to PDF. 5. Observe the progress toast as the page count and percentage update. 6. Once progress reaches 100%, observe how long the toast remains before the operation finishes. 7. Open the generated PDF and check whether its content is in grayscale. ## Actual behavior - The progress text appears cramped, particularly around the percentage indicator. - Changes to the page count and percentage cause the text to shift horizontally, making it appear to jitter or “dance around.” - Progress stays at 100% for a long time before the operation eventually finishes, without explaining what is still happening. - Selecting “Print in grayscale” has no effect on the generated PDF; the output retains its colors. ## Expected behavior - The progress toast should have enough space for all progress information. - The page count and percentage should remain in **stable** positions as their values update, without crowding or shifting nearby text. - If additional work is required after progress reaches 100%, the toast should display a clear status, such as “Finalizing…”, rather than appearing stuck at 100%. - Selecting “Print in grayscale” should produce a grayscale PDF. ## Environment - Application: PdfCraft - Version: 0.9 - Operating system: Windows 11

title: Add musl Linux builds (Alpine Linux, Void musl)
author: vinod2807
body:
### What I'd like

A musl-linked Linux build, so PdfCraft runs on musl distributions — **Alpine Linux** (the most widely used musl distro, and the base of a great many containers) and **Void Linux's musl variant**. At the moment none of the published Linux artifacts can be used on either.

### Why the current artifacts don't work there

Taking the official CLI as the example, on Alpine 3.24 (x86_64):

```
$ ./pdfcraft-cli --version
/bin/ash: ./pdfcraft-cli: not found

$ file pdfcraft-cli
pdfcraft-cli: ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, version 1 (SYSV),
  dynamically linked, interpreter /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2,
  for GNU/Linux 3.2.0, stripped

$ readelf -l pdfcraft-cli | grep interpreter
  [Requesting program interpreter: /lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2]

$ readelf -d pdfcraft-cli | grep NEEDED
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libgcc_s.so.1]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libm.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [libc.so.6]
  (NEEDED) Shared library: [ld-linux-x86-64.so.2]
```

`/lib64/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` is glibc's loader. A musl system provides `/lib/ld-musl-x86_64.so.1` instead, so the kernel cannot start the process — and the shell reports that as the very confusing "not found", which reads like a missing file rather than an ABI mismatch. Same story for the `.deb` (dpkg + glibc), the `.rpm`, the AppImage (glibc + FUSE) and the Flatpak. `gcompat` is only a partial shim, not a real answer for a GUI application.

### Your FreeBSD build shows this is already a pattern you support

The FreeBSD artifact is neither glibc nor musl:

```
$ file pdfcraft-0.9.0-freebsd-x86_64/bin/pdfcraft
  ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, version 1 (FreeBSD),
  dynamically linked, interpreter /libexec/ld-elf.so.1, for FreeBSD 15.1

$ readelf -d ... | grep NEEDED
  (NEEDED) libc.so.7        # FreeBSD's own libc
  (NEEDED) libthr.so.3
  (NEEDED) libgcc_s.so.1
  (NEEDED) libm.so.5
```

That is the GUI, dynamically linked against a non-glibc libc, shipping today. So this isn't new territory …

title: Text extraction drops glyphs whose names are not in the Adobe Glyph List
author: jpeskov
body:
## Summary

When a simple font has no `/ToUnicode` (or no entry in it for a code), PdfCraft gets the text from the glyph names. If a glyph name is not in its table, the glyph is dropped from the extracted text. The page still renders correctly. Three PDFs show this: small caps with names like `c251`, the ligature names `f_i` and `f_l`, and `hyphen.case`.

title: Text extraction returns only the first pages of an 821-page book; the body text is missing
author: jpeskov
body:
## Summary

For this 821-page book, `pdfcraft-cli text` exits 0 but returns only about 4,000 characters of opening material. The body text is missing. Poppler and MuPDF return about 1.8 million characters. I think the cause is the same as in #3169: the body fonts have glyph names that PdfCraft can not map to Unicode. This book is a much bigger case, because almost the whole text is lost.

## Fixture

`batch6/poppler-gitlab/poppler-378-0.pdf` ([source PDF](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/poppler/poppler/uploads/642e34079a95558e8798e6c2aaef87a8/one.pdf)) (2,687,767 bytes, SHA-256 `7abf45ed8295fa5422ae10cf0e67ebe30a8198c7cb2e00e6c3ea21a2bfe1cd92`). Source: [PDF Association Stressful PDF Corpus](https://pdfa.org/stressful-pdf-corpus/), `batch6.tgz`.

I checked this with pypdf:

- The PDF has 821 pages. 34 pages have no `/Font` resource.
- Page 1 uses `DIN-Regular` and `DIN-Bold`. Both have a `/ToUnicode` and `/Differences`. This is the only page in the file with a font that has `/ToUnicode`.
- All other pages use `/Subtype /Type1` fonts without `/ToUnicode`. Counted over all page font resources: 1,905 have no `/Encoding`, 176 have an `/Encoding`, and 2 have `/ToUnicode`.

- Page 411 has a single content stream of 5,679 bytes after decoding. It has no Form XObjects. It draws the text in one `BT` block with `TJ` and ordinary ASCII strings, for example `[(reason)-404(to)-401(think)...]TJ`.

```sh

body:
## Summary

A newspaper page is drawn as two columns with a clip rectangle each. A glyph that crosses the edge between them is drawn in both clips, at the same place. PdfCraft keeps both copies. The headline reads `WOR RLD` and the lead reads `illusstrated`. Poppler gives the correct words.

title: Text extraction cuts the subscript `2` out of `CO2-Emissionen` and puts it on its own line
author: jpeskov
body:
## Summary

On page 28 of a German brochure, the subscript `2` in `CO2-Emissionen` is a separate, smaller text run, lowered by 2.7 pt. PdfCraft does not join it to the line. The sentence reads `CO -Emissionen` and the `2` appears on its own line. Poppler and MuPDF keep the word whole.

```text

BT  Tm 4.698 0 0 4.698 82.8534 94.2725   (2)          % /MCID 1489
Tm 8.1 0 0 8.1 85.3921 96.9455   [(-) -10 (E) 2 (m) ... ]  % /MCID 1490
```

- `CO` is 8.1 pt on baseline y = 96.95.
- The `2` is 4.698 pt (58% of 8.1) on baseline y = 94.27, which is 2.67 pt lower. It uses its own `Tm` and no `Ts` rise.
- `-Emissionen` goes back to 8.1 pt on the first baseline.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
pdfcraft-cli text poppler-577-0.pdf > poppler-577.txt

`CO2-Emissionen` in one piece, in the sentence.

PdfCraft puts `CO -Emissionen` in the sentence. The `2` is on a separate line after the sentence, before the page number `28`.

Poppler and MuPDF both return `CO2-Emissionen`. This is not a Unicode `₂` question: the digit is an ordinary `2` and it is detached.

title: Text search and search-redaction miss text when a `/ToUnicode` CMap has one malformed entry or an unresolvable `usecmap` (the whole CMap is discarded)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` · `hayro-cmap` 0.1.0 from crates.io (checksum `24d285dc…`; hayro `main` @ `2fb3fb99` has the same code) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

A font's `/ToUnicode` CMap maps character codes to Unicode. When the CMap contains one part that can't be parsed, PdfCraft's reading path discards the **whole** CMap and falls back to the font's encoding for every code. The reading path is `pdfcraft-cli text`, `text_extract`, `text_find`, and `redact_mark` with `find`.

PdfCraft's edit layer (Edit text / `text_paragraphs`, the Office export) reads the same CMap with its own parser, which skips only the bad part. So do MuPDF and pdftotext. So PdfCraft disagrees with itself:
- Edit text shows the text, and the export writes it out.
- `text_find` returns no match, and search-redaction says "nothing matched, so nothing was marked".

There are two triggers:
- **A malformed entry.** In `2 beginbfchar <41> <ZZZZ> <42> <0059> endbfchar`, the first destination isn't valid hex.
- **A `usecmap` naming a CMap that can't be resolved**, followed by valid entries. Only the predefined Adobe CMaps resolve, so this covers any other name, including the CMap's own name.

No panic and no hang in any case.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run `python repro.py .` in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes seven files of about 1 KB each. Each draws "AB" (codes 65, 66) in Helvetica with a different `/ToUnicode`. `bad_hex.pdf` and `self_usecmap.pdf` are the minimal cases.

```python
"""repro.py OUTDIR -- /ToUnicode CMap cases. A Type1 Helvetica draws "AB" (codes 65, 66); only the
/ToUnicode stream varies between files.

  normal        bfchar 65->'X' 66->'Y'  -> "XY"
  huge_bfrange  bfrange <0000> <FFFF> <0041>  (65536 codes mapped)
  nested_range  many bfranges
  self_usecmap  `usecmap` naming the CMap's own name (not resolvable) + bfchar 65->X
  cycle_usecmap `us…

title: A JPEG 2000 image with a palette renders as gray noise (palette indices are not resolved)
author: jpeskov
body:
## Summary

On page 7 of an iText PDF/A test file, a `/JPXDecode` image renders as a colour photo in Poppler and MuPDF. PdfCraft renders it as noisy grayscale. The JPEG 2000 data is palette-based, and PdfCraft decodes it without applying the palette.

## Fixture

iText [`cmp_pdfA2b_imageCheckTest4.pdf`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itext/itext-java/732d6c756417d6b7fccbc043bffbbfd8bbe5b789/pdfa/src/test/resources/com/itextpdf/pdfa/cmp/PdfA2GraphicsCheckTest/cmp_pdfA2b_imageCheckTest4.pdf) (2,419,929 bytes, SHA-256 `a66efd4ce8ccf7647c2cdc323ae66dbeff9a8956a7424380d385f049210f7961`). It is also in the KillerPDF v1.8.1 regression set.

Image `/Im1` on page 7:

- The image dictionary has `/Filter /JPXDecode`, `/Width 768` and `/Height 512`. It has **no** `/ColorSpace`.
- The JP2 header has:
  - `ihdr`: 1 component, 8 bits
  - `pclr`: a palette
  - `colr`: enumerated colour space 16 (sRGB)

So each sample is an index into an sRGB palette, not a gray value.

## Steps to reproduce

```sh
curl -L 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/itext/itext-java/732d6c756417d6b7fccbc043bffbbfd8bbe5b789/pdfa/src/test/resources/com/itextpdf/pdfa/cmp/PdfA2GraphicsCheckTest/cmp_pdfA2b_imageCheckTest4.pdf' -o input.pdf
echo 'a66efd4ce8ccf7647c2cdc323ae66dbeff9a8956a7424380d385f049210f7961  input.pdf' | sha256sum -c -
pdfcraft-cli render input.pdf --page 7 --dpi 120 --out pdfcraft.png
pdftoppm -f 7 -l 7 -r 120 -png -singlefile input.pdf poppler
```

## Expected

The photo shows in colour, as in Poppler and MuPDF. When the image dictionary has no `/ColorSpace`, the colour information in the JPEG 2000 data applies, and here that includes the palette.

## Actual

PdfCraft shows the photo as noisy grayscale. In my comparison at 96 dpi, the page-image error was about 0.120 between PdfCraft and each reference renderer, and 0.0014 between Poppler and MuPDF.

## Likely cause

`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/filter/jpx.rs` (`decode`, about line 24) always sets `resolve_palette_indices: false`. That is corr…

title: [Feature Request] Release Channels (Stable / Dev / Nightly) & In-App Delta Auto-Updater
author: hyperland956-lgtm
body:
### Description
Right now, `PdfCraft` is moving at absolute warp speed (hundreds of commits and PRs landing daily). However, for users running portable builds, the current manual update process is not only tedious, **it frequently causes file-lock panics and config crashes**:
- *Current Bug:* Extracting a new portable zip over an active folder while `pdfcraft.exe` is running triggers unhandled Windows file-lock errors (`Access is denied / Os { code: 5 }`), occasionally wiping local app state or causing a hard panic on startup due to stale cache schemas.

To support this rapid AI-driven development cycle and eliminate these manual file-replacement crashes, we need an official in-app update mechanism with stability channels.

---

### Proposed Features / Checklist

- [ ] **1. Release Channels Selection (`Stable` / `Dev` / `Nightly`):**
  - Add a setting under `Settings -> General -> Update Channel`:
    - **Stable:** Tagged official releases (e.g., `v0.8.0`), thoroughly tested.
    - **Dev:** Weekly or milestone rollups for testers wanting recent fixes.
    - **Nightly:** Cutting-edge builds straight from `main` compiled automatically via GitHub Actions every 24 hours.

- [ ] **2. In-App Silent Auto-Updater (Delta / Binary Swap):**
  - Background check against the GitHub API for updates on app startup (with a toggle to disable it for air-gapped / privacy purists).
  - When an update is available, show a subtle non-intrusive banner (*"PdfCraft v0.8.1 Nightly is ready. Restart to update"*).
  - **Smart Application Replacement:** On Windows/Linux/macOS, safely swap the binary or apply a compressed patch in-place on exit so the user doesn't hit file-lock panics in their portable folder.

- [ ] **3. Update Changelog Viewer ("What's New"):**
  - A modal or slide-out drawer showing the commit log / PR titles since the user's last version so they can see what AI-driven fixes just landed.

title: Provide an official Docker image for the web build
author: ngoc-minh-do
body:
## Feature request: official Docker image for the web build

Split from the original broader request per maintainer feedback — the **CLI image** now has its own ticket: #3206.

### Why

PdfCraft is advertised as running everywhere, but on **headless Linux** (servers, VMs, homelabs, CI) the desktop app needs a display, so the only realistic path is the **WebAssembly web build** — which is already designed for exactly this: `packaging/web/README.md` documents a fully static site (no server-side code, relative URLs, works at any path prefix, `?file=` to open a document), with the server settings it needs (`application/wasm` MIME type, gzip/Brotli, immutable cache on hashed assets, `no-cache` on `index.html`, HTTPS).

Despite that, no container image exists. `packaging/` covers desktop builds, CLI tarballs, FreeBSD and the web zip only. Every self-hoster re-implements the same glue: fetch `pdfcraft-web-<ver>.zip` at build time, unzip into NGINX, set MIME/compression/cache headers, add a healthcheck — and repeat the whole thing on every upgrade.

### The established pattern: PhotoCraft

The sibling app already merged exactly this: **storytold/photocraft#1334** ("Docker web deployment", merged 2026-10-09) added a multi-stage `Dockerfile` (builds the existing Rust/Wasm app with Trunk → serves via non-root NGINX on 8080 with `/healthz`, gzip precompression, wasm MIME types, immutable cache policy, thin LTO, arm64+amd64). A pdfcraft PR mirroring it would likely satisfy this ticket.

Docker support following the photocraft#1334 approach, ideally merged into the repo (a `Dockerfile` + `packaging/web/nginx.conf`, documented in `packaging/web/README.md`) — and/or an image built from CI on each release (version tags + `latest`, non-root, healthcheck, amd64 + arm64, musl/Alpine variant per #3166).

title: Provide an official Docker image for pdfcraft-cli (headless servers, CI and agents)
author: ngoc-minh-do
body:
## Feature request: official Docker image for `pdfcraft-cli`

Split from #3201 per maintainer request (each deployment problem gets its own ticket). This one covers the **command-line tool**, not the web build.

### Why

- `pdfcraft-cli` ships as standalone tarballs (`pdfcraft-cli-<ver>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`, …) with no server-side components — but on **headless servers, CI and agent hosts**, a container is the natural delivery: `docker run --rm <image> info doc.pdf`, or a long-lived agent sidecar for the opt-in MCP server (`pdfcraft-cli mcp`).
- There is no official image, so every user either downloads a tarball themselves or wraps it ad hoc.
- Today's Linux binaries need **glibc ≥ 2.35**, which rules out slim/musl base images — see #3166 (musl/Alpine builds) which this ticket should probably block on or pair with.

### What I'd like

1. A `pdfcraft-cli` image, built from CI on each release (the shared `craft-common-actions` release pipeline already builds the other artifacts):
   - version tags + a rolling `latest`,
   - non-root user, minimal base,
   - the CLI alone, including its opt-in MCP server (`pdfcraft-cli mcp`, stdin/stdout — no network socket),
   - arm64 alongside amd64, and ideally a musl/Alpine variant once #3166 lands.

### Related

- #423 — *"Release: a standalone Linux CLI archive"* (closed): the CLI tarballs this image would wrap — currently the only delivery vehicle
- #3201 — the web-build Docker image (the other half of this deployment ask)
- #3166 — musl/Alpine builds for slim images
- #872 / #919 — a server-side document-processing REST service would be the fuller answer for on-prem/agent workloads

title: Header/footer, Bates, watermark and Add text are invisible on a page whose content ends inside an unclosed hidden-layer sequence (`/OC … BDC` without `EMC`)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` (first measured on 0.8.0 @ `3f5a784c`; re-run on 0.9.0 with the same scripts, same results) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

PdfCraft's writers add their marks after the page's content, inside its `q … Q` wrapper (#3084 was about graphics state leaking past that wrapper). A `Q` restores graphics state, but it doesn't end a marked-content sequence.

Some files end a page's content inside a sequence that was never closed, for example `/OC /L1 BDC …` with no `EMC`. That's malformed, but it renders as intended, since everything up to the end is in the layer. On such a page, the added header, footer, Bates number, watermark or Add-text item **lands inside the open hidden-layer sequence and isn't shown**:
- not by PdfCraft;
- not by MuPDF;
- not in anyone's extracted text.

title: Edit text redraws a whole line in its first run's text state: changing one letter unhides invisible text, hides visible text, and moves or rescales the rest of the line
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 (pdftoppm wasn't available on this machine)

### What happens

A line of text is often drawn as several show operators in one text object, with a text-state operator between them:

```
BT /F1 24 Tf 72 700 Td (Shown) Tj 3 Tr ( hidden) Tj ET
```

Here `( hidden)` is invisible (rendering mode 3, ISO 32000-2 §9.3.6). Edit text joins both runs into one line, `Shown hidden`, because they share a font, size and colour. Change one letter of `Shown`, and the whole line is written again in the **first run's** text state. The second run loses its own `Tr`, `Tc`, `Tw`, `Tz` or `Ts`:

- **Invisible text becomes visible.** After `Shown` → `Shewn`, the word `hidden` is painted on the page. It shows in PdfCraft's render and in MuPDF's.
- **Visible text disappears** (line edits). With `3 Tr (Hidden) Tj 0 Tr ( shown) Tj`, editing `shown` makes the whole line invisible.
- **Outlined text is filled.** A `1 Tr` (stroke) run is redrawn filled.
- **The rest of the line moves or changes size.** A run after `3 Tc` loses its letter spacing and shrinks by 18 pt. A run after `60 Tz` is drawn 100 % wide and runs 44 pt further right. A run after `12 Tw` loses its word spacing, and a run after `2 Ts` drops to the baseline.

This happens in both kinds of text edit:
- line edits (`text_edit` with `line`, the automation tool);
- paragraph edits (`text_edit` with `paragraph`, the same path as the inline editor in Edit text).

With paragraph edits, the line counts as "invisible OCR text" when its first run is invisible. That switches the whole paragraph to visible, so `Hidden` is revealed too. A line whose runs share their state (the control page) changes only at the edited letter.

This is not #3115. #3115 is about later *rows* of a paragraph taking the first row's state, with a layer, opacity or `Tz` set between rows. Here everything is in one row and one `BT … ET`,…

title: Edit text measures vertical (`Identity-V`) text as if it were horizontal: editing one character of a column deletes the neighbouring column
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` (also PR #2590 @ `27971276`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 · font: Shippori Mincho Regular from [craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts) (OFL)

### What happens

Vertical writing uses a font whose CMap has `WMode 1`, such as `/Identity-V` (ISO 32000-2 §9.7.4.3). Each glyph moves the pen **down** by its vertical advance, not to the right. PdfCraft's renderer and reading path handle this correctly:
- the page renders like MuPDF's;
- `text_extract` reads each column in order;
- `text_find` returns tall, narrow rectangles that match the ink.

The Edit text layer (`text_lines`, `text_paragraphs` and both kinds of `text_edit`) lays the same glyphs out horizontally. A column of six 20 pt characters at x = 500 is reported as a 120 × 20 pt box running to the **right**, `[500, 54.4, 620, 74.4]`, past the right edge of the 612 pt page. Its real ink is x 490–510, y 73–190 (from the top).

Every column then looks like a row starting at the same height, so neighbouring columns "overlap". When one character of a column is edited, PdfCraft removes copies of the edited line drawn on the same baseline (fake bold, OCR layers). It counts the overlapping neighbour as such a copy, and **deletes the whole neighbouring column**. Both line and paragraph edits do this, so the inline editor (paragraph edits) does too. Columns farther away than the overlap test survive.

### Steps

1. Get a TrueType font with the characters below, for example `fonts/shippori-mincho/ShipporiMincho-Regular.ttf` from craft-fonts.
2. Save the following as `repro.py` and run `python repro.py ShipporiMincho-Regular.ttf`. It needs Python 3 and `fontTools`, which is used only to look up glyph ids. It writes `vertical.pdf`: three columns at 20 pt, in an `Identity-V` CID font that embeds the whole font. The columns are `縦書きの試験` at x = 500, `隣の列の文章` 30 pt to its left at x = 470, and `離れた列` far away at …

title: Auto-tag and "mark as decorative" rewrite page content without the cross-stream rules: hidden text appears, and a shape split across two content streams is deleted
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` (`crates/a11y` and `crates/content` are unchanged on `main` @ `5377a223`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00, pikepdf 10.17 / qpdf (operator lists)

### What happens

A page's `/Contents` can be an array of streams, and ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2 lets a writer split it between any two tokens. Two consequences follow, and PdfCraft's renderer, MuPDF, Poppler and xpdf all agree on them:

- The operands of an operator can end one stream while its keyword starts the next.
- A `%` comment at the very end of a stream (no end-of-line) continues into the next stream, up to its first end-of-line, because the streams are joined with a space.

`Pieces` in `crates/content` exists for exactly this. It also keeps the comment edges since #3081. The two accessibility writers that rewrite page content don't use it:

1. **Auto-tag** (`accessibility_autotag_apply`) joins the streams with a **newline**. That ends the comment early. The writer then replaces the page's content with one new stream, so the line the comment used to hide is now live. **Text that no viewer showed before is drawn after tagging.**
2. **Mark as decorative** (`accessibility_set_alt` with `decorative: true`) parses and rewrites only the stream that holds the figure, **on its own**:
   - Operands left at the end of that stream are dropped as stray. The next stream's `re f` is left with no operands, so **a rectangle drawn after the figure disappears**. In PdfCraft's own renderer and text extraction, everything after that `re` in the second stream is lost too (`After` is not drawn or extracted). MuPDF and pdftotext still show it.
   - The trailing comment is dropped as well, so text hidden by it **becomes visible**, as with auto-tag.

Both actions should change only the tags and marked content. A save after either one writes the change. The same pages without the split or the comment (the controls) come out unchanged.

The par…

title: The redaction audit doesn't see text drawn inside a form XObject: text blacked out by a box, or under an unapplied redaction mark, is reported clean
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` (`crates/audit` and `crates/edit/src/text.rs` are unchanged on `main` @ `50f261d7`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

The faux-redaction audit (`doc_audit_redactions`, `pdfcraft-cli audit`) checks two things:
1. text that is still extractable under an opaque box;
2. text under a `/Redact` annotation that was never applied.

It gets the page's text from the Edit-text layer (`pdfcraft_edit::text_lines`), and that layer doesn't follow `Do` into form XObjects (#2964). So **text drawn inside a form XObject is invisible to the audit.** That applies wherever the cover is drawn: on the page, in the same form, or in another form.

On each such page:
- the text is fully covered in MuPDF and in PdfCraft's own render;
- it is still returned by `pdfcraft-cli text`, by `text_find`, by MuPDF and by pdftotext;
- the audit reports nothing, and `pdfcraft-cli audit` exits as if the page were clean.

The same goes for an unapplied `/Redact` mark over form text. The audit says there is nothing left to apply, while `redact_apply` on the same document does find and remove the text.

Text in forms is common: pdfpages/n-up output, stamps, headers and footers, and page content that a producer wraps in a form XObject. The audit's job is to catch exactly this kind of black box drawn over text.

This is not #3117, which covers kinds of cover the audit doesn't recognise: images, image masks, Type 3 glyphs, `sc` colours. Here the cover is the plain `re f` box the audit does recognise, and boxes drawn inside forms are found. What's missed is the **text** under them. It is not #3118 (false positives) or #2385 (thick strokes, highlight annotations, white boxes) either.

### Steps

1. Run `repro_25.py` in an empty folder (Python 3 standard library only). It writes `audit_forms.pdf`. Each page draws `SECRET 123` at (72, 610) in 14 pt Helvetica:

| Page | Where the text is drawn | Wh…

title: Editing a tagged line whose marked content carries `/ActualText` removes the `BDC` with its `/MCID`: the new text is untagged and its structure element points at nothing
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs` is unchanged on `main` @ `50f261d7`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: pikepdf 10.17 / qpdf (content and structure), MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

In a tagged PDF, a structure element owns its content through a marked-content sequence whose property list holds an `/MCID` (ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5). The same property list often carries `/ActualText` (§14.9.4), the replacement text for what the glyphs show. LaTeX `tagpdf` writes it for maths and symbols, and other producers use it for abbreviations and decorated text:

```
/Span <</MCID 0 /ActualText (Logical words)>> BDC BT … (Shown words) Tj ET EMC
```

Edit text shows the `ActualText` as the paragraph's text, `Logical words`. When one letter of it is changed, the rewrite removes the whole `BDC … EMC`, `/MCID` included, and writes the new text **outside any marked content**. The structure tree is left as it was. So after the edit:

- the `Span` element still claims MCID 0 (`/K 0`, ParentTree key → `Span`), and the page has no MCID 0 any more;
- `accessibility_tag_content` for that element returns `text: ""`;
- PdfCraft's own Accessibility Checker, which passed before the edit, now fails `tagged-content` with "Page 1: 1 untagged content item".

Editing the same line works when its property list has no `/ActualText`. On the controls, the `BDC` and every other key are kept, and the tag content follows the edit:
- `/Span <</MCID 0>>`;
- `/P <</MCID 0 /Lang (fr-FR)>>`;
- `/Span <</MCID 0 /E (Doctor)>>`;
- a `/P <</MCID 0>>` line holding an inner ligature `/Span <</ActualText (fi)>>`. There, the inner span is dropped and the outer `P` keeps its MCID.

Dropping a stale `/ActualText` when the text changes is reasonable. Dropping the `/MCID`, and with it the content's place in the structure tree, is not.

1. Run `repro_26.py` in an empty folder (Python 3 standard library only). It writes `tagged_edit.pd…

title: Tag tools ignore an MCR's `/Stm`: "mark as decorative" and "mark as artifact" on a figure drawn in a form XObject retag a different element's content on the page
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` (`crates/a11y` is unchanged on `main` @ `50f261d7`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: pikepdf 10.17 / qpdf (content and structure), MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

A structure element can own marked content inside a form XObject. Its `/K` is then a marked-content reference whose `/Stm` names the form (ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.1, Table 357):

```
<< /Type /MCR /MCID 0 /Stm 12 0 R /Pg 10 0 R >>
```

Its MCID is numbered within the **form's** content stream, and the form has its own `/StructParents` key. Word, InDesign and Acrobat itself put tagged figures and logos in form XObjects this way. So MCID 0 in the form and MCID 0 on the page are different content, belonging to different elements.

PdfCraft's tag tools read only the MCR's `/MCID`, never its `/Stm`, and then look that MCID up in the **page's** content. On a page where the page's own content also uses that MCID, they act on the wrong content. The page renders the same before and after, but the tags no longer match what they describe:

- **`accessibility_set_alt` with `decorative: true`** on the form's figure turns the *page* figure's marked content into an `/Artifact`. That page figure belongs to another element, which keeps its `/Alt`. The form figure is removed from the tags, but its content stays marked `/Figure <</MCID 0>>`.
- **`accessibility_mark_tag_artifact`** on the form's figure does the same.
- **`accessibility_figures`** reports the form figure's location as the page figure's rectangle.
- **`accessibility_tag_content`** reports the form figure's content as the page's MCID 0. For a `P` inside a form, it returns the text of the page paragraph with the same MCID.

title: [Bug Report] [PdfCraft] Windows-specific stutter and broken deceleration during fling gestures with TOUCHPAD

Probable Root Cause / Technical Context - 
Because the hardware is capable of reporting smooth input events and Linux handles the momentum curve correctly, this points to an OS-specific software/event-loop integration issue on Windows rather than an input hardware limitation:

title: Find: replace the current match one at a time
author: earlvanze
body:
## Request

After Find locates multiple matches, add a control to replace the current match and then advance to the next match, alongside Replace All.

## Why

Users sometimes need to review each occurrence before changing it because identical text can have different intended replacements or should be left unchanged in some contexts.

## Scope

This is distinct from #1777 and PR #3078, which add Replace All. It requests an explicit one-at-a-time replacement flow with a visible current-match position and predictable undo behavior.

title: Feature request: Repeat a redaction area across multiple pages
author: widumir
body:
### Feature request
Please add an option to repeat a selected redaction area across multiple pages at the same position and size.

### Suggested workflow
1. Draw a redaction rectangle on one page.
2. Right-click the rectangle and select "Repeat on pages...".
3. Choose all pages, a page range, or specific pages.
4. Preview the resulting redaction marks before permanently applying them.

### Use case
I work with long PDFs and need to remove recurring content, such as headers, footers, or footnote sections, from the same area on multiple pages.

For example, in a 165-page document, I would like to mark the bottom section once and apply that selection to the remaining pages, rather than drawing the same rectangle manually on each page.

Text search is not a substitute: the text may differ on every page, and scanned PDFs may not contain searchable text at all.

### Expected behavior
- Repeat the selected rectangle at the same position and size on the chosen pages.
- Allow individual adjustments or removal of marks before applying the redactions.
- Permanently remove the covered content, rather than simply placing a black rectangle over it.

This would save substantial time when processing long documents.

If this functionality already exists, please let me know how to access it. Thank you for your work on PdfCraft!
