title: Create PDF from images (doc_combine, doc_create_multiple): no option to put each image on a standard page size such as A4 or Letter
author: mischiatti75-spec
body:
**Summary.** When photos are turned into a PDF (`doc_combine`, `doc_create_multiple`, `doc_create` with `from: "images"`, and *Create PDF from images* in the app), each page is as large as the image at its resolution. Phone and camera JPEGs usually carry 72 dpi or no resolution, so a 4000 × 3000 photo becomes a 4000 × 3000 pt page (about 1.41 × 1.06 m). The DPI choice added for #190 changes the size, but a set of photos with different pixel sizes still gives pages of different sizes, and none of them is a paper size. There is no option to place each image on A4 or Letter, scaled to fit.

**Environment.** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 macos-universal, macOS 26, Apple M4 Max.

**Steps to reproduce**

```python
# make_imgs.py  (pip install Pillow)
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
for name, size in (("landscape.jpg", (4000, 3000)), ("portrait.jpg", (3000, 4000))):
    im = Image.new("RGB", size, "lightgray")
    ImageDraw.Draw(im).rectangle([100, 100, size[0] - 100, size[1] - 100], outline="black", width=20)
    im.save(name, quality=85)   # no DPI stored, like many phone photos
```

```sh
python make_imgs.py
pdfcraft-cli run doc_combine 'paths=["landscape.jpg","portrait.jpg"]' out=combined.pdf --root .
pdfcraft-cli run doc_create_multiple 'paths=["landscape.jpg","portrait.jpg"]' out=multiple.pdf --root .
pdfinfo -f 1 -l 2 combined.pdf | grep size
```

**Expected.** An option to choose the page size for image pages, for example `page_size: "a4" | "letter" | [w, h]` with the image scaled to fit, centred, and the page turned to match the image's orientation; or at least one page size for the whole set. This is what scanned-photo reports and site-visit documents need, and printing them at 100 % should not crop them.

**Actual.** The page sizes follow the pixels:

```
Page    1 size: 4000 x 3000 pts
Page    2 size: 3000 x 4000 pts
```

(`multiple.pdf` is the same.) If the images are saved with 300 dpi the pages are 960 × 720 pt and 720 × 960 pt: smaller, but still not a paper size, an…

title: Save after undoing a saved security change writes a file whose objects don't match its /Encrypt
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
**What happens.** Undo past a save that changed security, then Save again: the file is written with the trailer (and `/Encrypt`) of the restored state but with the objects encrypted, or not, the way the last saved file was. @ahmadmuj found it while reviewing #2702.

Steps (engine `Session`, fixture built with our own writer, user `user`, owner `owner`, `/P -1`), on current `main` (a12fe8f4):

1. Open the encrypted file with the owner password.
2. Remove security (`Edit::RemoveProtection`), Save (`save_bytes` + `mark_saved`).
3. Undo.
4. Save (`save_bytes`), reopen with the owner password.

| variant | result |
|---|---|
| RC4-128, AES-128, AES-256, `/Encrypt` indirect | `check_save` refuses it ("no document catalog found"); the bytes have `/Encrypt` in the trailer but plaintext objects, and don't reopen (`WrongPassword` for RC4/AES-128, "no readable page tree" for AES-256) |
| same, `/Encrypt` inline (with #2702 applied, otherwise step 2 is refused, #2661) | `check_save` passes and the file is written; it opens with the owner password but every page is blank: the content stream decrypts to noise |
| opened with the user password (all permissions) | same as owner |
| without the first Save, or with `save_full_bytes` at step 4 | correct |

The reverse goes wrong the same way: on an unencrypted file, Protect, Save, Undo, Save writes a file with no `/Encrypt` whose objects are still encrypted. `check_save` passes and both pages come back blank.

**Expected.** The file from step 4 is the original, encrypted again, opening with the same passwords and showing the same text.

**Cause.** In `Session::save_bytes` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`, around line 4103) the restored snapshot is not `on_saved` and doesn't count as a `rewrite`, because `encryption_changed()` is false on the state as it was opened. So the save opens the last saved file with its own keys (unencrypted after step 2), copies the snapshot's objects into it with `overlay_changes_from` (already decrypted by the s…

title: Arabic Text Formatting and Right-to-Left (RTL) Rendering Problems When Editing PDFs
author: youcadz-droid
body:
Dear **PDFCraft** Development Team,
I would like to report a significant issue with Arabic text editing in PDFCraft.
When I edit existing PDF files containing Arabic text, the original text formatting and layout are often corrupted. The issue manifests itself in two different ways:
1. Corrupted Arabic characters: In some PDF files, editing Arabic text causes the characters to become scattered, disconnected, or incorrectly arranged, making the text unreadable.
2. Incorrect text direction: In other PDF files, the Arabic words remain correctly formed, but their order is reversed or rearranged from left to right instead of the correct right-to-left (RTL) direction required by Arabic.
These problems appear to affect the handling of Arabic text during the editing process. Potential causes include inadequate support for bidirectional text (Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm), Arabic character shaping and joining, or the preservation of text positioning and encoding in PDF documents. However, further investigation is needed to identify the exact cause.
Expected behavior:
- Arabic characters should remain correctly connected and rendered after editing.
- Text direction and word order should be preserved according to the right-to-left writing system.
- The original formatting, alignment, spacing, and layout should remain intact as much as possible.
- Edited PDFs should display Arabic text correctly when saved, reopened, or viewed in other PDF readers.
Actual behavior:
Editing Arabic text can result in broken character rendering, incorrect word ordering, and significant formatting corruption.
Arabic is widely used in educational, administrative, and professional documents. Reliable Arabic text editing is therefore essential for users working with these documents.
Could you please investigate this issue and improve PDFCraft's support for Arabic text, including RTL text direction, Arabic glyph shaping, and the preservation of the original PDF text layout?

title: Text boxes and callouts: fill colour (opaque background)
author: LinusPisano
body:
PdfCraft 0.9.0, Windows 11.

Text boxes and callouts have no background, so the drawing behind them shows through the text, which is hard to read on busy drawings. Only rectangles, ovals and polygons can have a fill today. `comment_edit` with `fill` on a text box gives *"only rectangles, ovals and polygons can be filled"*.

### Expected

- A fill colour option for text boxes and callouts (for example white, or "none"), like rectangles already have.
- With a fill set, the box is opaque and hides what is behind it.
- Ideally a default setting, so new text boxes and callouts get a white fill automatically.
- Also available in `comment_edit` (`fill`) for scripting.

### Use case

We mark up floor plans with many callouts on top of the lines, and the text needs to stay readable.

Related: #1152 (moving callout parts independently), #1491 (text box improvements).

title: Redaction keeps the redacted text in /ActualText and /Alt of tag elements reached only through /ParentTree, and the tag walk fails open past its cap
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0, `main` @ `d8b27058` (`crates/redact/src/tags.rs` unchanged on `main` @ `98cbd38a`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracle: pikepdf 10.17 (qpdf) ### What happens When redaction removes text that tagged marked content holds, `tags::clean` clears the owning structure element's `/Alt`, `/ActualText` and `/E`, which often repeat that text. It finds the owning elements by walking the structure tree from the `StructTreeRoot`'s `/K` only. An element that is reachable only through `/ParentTree` (or `/IDTree`) is never visited. It keeps `/ActualText` and `/Alt` with the redacted words, and the saved file still contains them, because the root keeps the parent tree reachable. The text on the page is gone, so the redaction looks complete, but anything that reads the tags (screen readers, `/ActualText`-aware extraction, a PDF/UA validator) still gets the redacted words. The same walk also **fails open past its cap**: `seen.len() > 2_000_000` makes it `continue` instead of stopping, so on a very large tree it returns as if every element had been checked. `drop_object_refs` in the same file had this pattern until #2532, and now removes the whole tree when it can't finish (fail-closed). Found while reviewing #3285 with @Losminek, which fixes the same `/K`-only start in `drop_object_refs` (object references to removed annotations). ### Steps 1. title: JPX images with embedded CIEJab color space render blank
author: jpeskov
body:
## Summary
PdfCraft renders a blank page when a JPX image uses CIEJab (enum 19) and its PDF image dictionary has no `/ColorSpace`. Poppler and MuPDF render the photograph.

## Fixture
The upstream [veraPDF PDF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veraPDF/veraPDF-corpus/49de56cd987929932c9e4fbbbe67d052bf44ef83/PDF_A-2b/6.2%20Graphics/6.2.8%20Images/6.2.8.3%20JPEG2000/veraPDF%20test%20suite%206-2-8-3-t04-fail-a.pdf) is also in [KillerPDF v1.8.1 part 10](https://github.com/SteveTheKiller/KillerPDF-Corpus/releases/download/v1.8.1/killerpdf-corpus-regression-v1.8.1-part10.zip), at `verapdf/PDF_A-2b/6.2 Graphics/6.2.8 Images/6.2.8.3 JPEG2000/veraPDF test suite 6-2-8-3-t04-fail-a.pdf`. It is 21,374 bytes; SHA-256 `8d35cbc64394bad6da2d19bb5b13cd8b37cd735a071d4176a2b23dfd8b272864`.

Image `/Im1` is 640 by 480, 8-bit, three-component `/JPXDecode`; its dictionary omits `/ColorSpace`. The JP2 header uses `colr` enum 19 (CIEJab) and has no `pclr` box.

## Steps to reproduce
```sh
curl -L 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/veraPDF/veraPDF-corpus/49de56cd987929932c9e4fbbbe67d052bf44ef83/PDF_A-2b/6.2%20Graphics/6.2.8%20Images/6.2.8.3%20JPEG2000/veraPDF%20test%20suite%206-2-8-3-t04-fail-a.pdf' -o input.pdf
pdfcraft-cli render input.pdf --page 1 --dpi 96 --out pdfcraft.png
pdftoppm -f 1 -l 1 -r 96 -png -singlefile input.pdf poppler
python3 -c "import fitz; d=fitz.open('input.pdf'); d[0].get_pixmap(matrix=fitz.Matrix(96/72, 96/72), alpha=False).save('mupdf.png')"
```

## Expected
PdfCraft should show the image. Poppler and MuPDF both render it.

## Actual
PdfCraft writes an all-white page and exits with status 0. The result is the same on the tested main commit and the official 0.9.0 release.

`hayro-jpeg2000` 0.3.5 recognizes enum 19 as `CieJab`, but `get_color_space` returns `Unsupported` for it in [hayro-jpeg2000 0.3.5](https://docs.rs/crate/hayro-jpeg2000/0.3.5/source/src/lib.rs#L533). PdfCraft turns that decoder error into `None` at [jpx.rs:29](https://github.com/st…

title: Deleting a page overflows the stack while pruning a deeply nested named-destination tree
author: PerchAnton
body:
Deleting a page can abort the process when the PDF's `/Names /Dests` name tree is a long chain of shallow indirect `/Kids` nodes. `prune_tree_ref` and `prune_tree_node` recurse without a depth or work bound. A seen list prevents cycles, but does not bound an acyclic chain.

Reproduced on main `932bf9c6bfdd63e2a21bb831696a3447b9def9cf`, macOS ARM64, Rust 1.95.0, the existing `low-disk` profile. An isolated regression with 16,384 nodes aborts:

```text
thread 'tests::deleting_a_page_prunes_deep_named_destination_trees' has overflowed its stack
fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
(signal: 6, SIGABRT: process abort signal)
```

A 2,048-node chain did not overflow in this configuration. The threshold depends on stack size and build settings.

To reproduce in `crates/organize/src/tests.rs`, build `doc_a()`, add a leaf `/Names [(gone) [first_page /Fit] (kept) [last_page /Fit]]`, wrap it in 16,384 separate indirect dictionaries each holding `/Kids [previous_node]`, and set the catalog's `/Names` to `<< /Dests tree_root >>`. Calling `delete_pages(&mut doc, &[0])` aborts. Each node is shallow; no deeply nested literal dictionary or external asset is needed.

Expected: deletion must not exhaust the stack. It should prune the removed page's destination and retain surviving destinations. If a traversal budget is exceeded, return an actionable error and preserve the engine document and history.

I am preparing an iterative, bounded traversal with regression coverage through the existing `page_delete` automation path.

Duplicate check: searched open and closed issues/PRs for named destinations, deletion, stack overflow and the pruning functions. #817/#851 cover dangling destinations, #1800/#1921 bound the separate import Copier, and open #2925 removes empty bookmarks. None changes this recursive name-tree walk.

title: Windows: single-instance handoff misses when SESSIONNAME is unset (Task Scheduler / service launches open a second window)
author: halr9000
body:
### What happens

On Windows, a launch of `pdfcraft.exe <file>` from **Task Scheduler** (or any context where the `SESSIONNAME` environment variable is not set — services, some remote-execution shells) cannot hand its file to the already-running PdfCraft in the same interactive session. It opens its own process/window instead, so the single-instance tab handoff from #715/#891 silently doesn't apply.

I verified this on 0.9.0 (scoop install of the official portable zip, Windows 11, interactive console session):

- Two PdfCraft processes ran at once, one bound to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PdfCraft\portable-instance.sock` and the other to `portable-instance-Console.sock` — two islands in the same user session.
- Re-running the same launch with `SESSIONNAME=Console` set hands off correctly: the second process exits and the file opens as a tab in the existing window.

### Root cause

`socket_name()` in `apps/pdfcraft/src/single_instance.rs` derives the socket suffix entirely from `%SESSIONNAME%`:

```rust
fn socket_name(session: Option<&str>) -> String {
    let session: String = session.unwrap_or_default().chars().filter(...).take(32).collect();
    if session.is_empty() { "instance.sock".to_string() } else { format!("instance-{session}.sock") }
}
```

Task Scheduler's interactive (`/IT`) tasks, and processes it spawns, do not get `SESSIONNAME` in their environment, so the launch computes `instance.sock` (portable: `portable-instance.sock`) and never finds the interactive instance's `instance-Console.sock`.

### Suggestion

Treat an absent `SESSIONNAME` as the console session — the overwhelmingly common case for a launched-with-files GUI app — or, when the exact-name socket is missing, probe the sibling `instance-Console.sock` before falling back to opening a new window. (A session-suffix mismatch then degrades to today's behavior rather than splitting the session.)

Happy to test a build. This bit me in an automation workflow where PDFs are delivered to a user's desktop via sche…

title: Switching between All tools and Read mode jumps to a different page at a fixed zoom
author: tomroth04
body:
## Summary
At a fixed zoom (e.g. 100%), switching from All tools to Read mode shows a different page than
the one being viewed, often page 1. Switching back to All tools returns to where All tools was
last left, not to the page read in Read mode. At Fit width / Fit page it does not happen.

**Version:** 0.9.0 (latest release); also reproduced on `main` at 4db6ac4
**OS:** macOS Golden Gate 27.0.1, MacBook Air (Apple M2)

## Steps to reproduce
1. Open any PDF with ~30 pages.
2. Set a fixed zoom, e.g. type 100% in the zoom field.
3. Scroll to page 18.
4. Click **Read** in the mode bar.
5. Scroll to page 6 in Read mode, then click **All tools**.

## Expected
Step 4 still shows page 18; step 5 still shows page 6.

## Actual
Step 4 shows page 1 (or wherever Read mode was last left); step 5 jumps back to page 18.

## Cause
The page view's `ScrollArea` is salted with `("page-view", view.id)` (`canvas.rs:2644`, #259),
but egui combines the salt with the parent `Ui`'s id. Since UI.9 (8ff27dc8), All tools draws the
page inside the docking workspace (`docking.rs:414`) while Read mode draws it directly in the
`CentralPanel` (`lib.rs:3182`), so each mode has its own scroll state and a mode switch loads the
other mode's stale offset.

At Fit width / Fit page the zoom changes on the switch, so the zoom anchor (`canvas.rs:2428`)
sets the offset explicitly and hides the problem. At a fixed zoom nothing sets it.

Line numbers are at 4db6ac4. Related: #1056 / #1069 (sidebar autoscroll), #189.

## Suggested fix
Give the scroll area an id that does not depend on its parent, e.g. wrap `show_viewport` in
`ui.scope_builder(egui::UiBuilder::new().id(egui::Id::new(("page-view-scope", view.id))), …)`.

A kittest test (30-page synthetic PDF, `zoom` set to 100, go to page 17, click Read, then go to
page 5 and click All tools) fails on `main` (Read shows page 0, back in All tools shows page 17)
and passes with that change. The fit-width variant passes either way. I have not run the full
UI test s…

title: Timestamp server for digital signatures (needs a decision on outbound network)
author: Tomcatt
body:
`sign.timestamp-servers` is still `planned`, but most of the work is already done. `pdfcraft-sign` builds RFC 3161 requests, checks the answers and embeds the token (`sign_with_timestamp`, `Session::sign_with_timestamp`). Validation already reports trusted timestamps. The one missing piece is the transport, and AGENTS.md says new outbound network access is the owner's decision, so I'm asking before opening a PR.

**Why:** Acrobat users signing with a CAC/PIV card often set a timestamp server, either because a form or office asks for it or so a signature keeps proving *when* it was made after the certificate expires (a CAC certificate lasts about 3 years). Without one, the signing time is just the signer's PC clock.

**Proposal, built the same way as Help ▸ Check for updates:**

- **Preferences ▸ Digital signatures ▸ Timestamp server**, a single address box, **empty by default**. While it's empty, signing never touches the network.
- `ui-egui` stays transport-free. The desktop app supplies a `TimestampTransport` closure (ureq, OS roots, 15 s timeout, 4 MiB cap), the same way it supplies `update_source`. The web build doesn't get one, so the setting stays hidden there.
- **What leaves the machine:** only the RFC 3161 request, a SHA-256 hash of the signature value plus a nonce. The document is never sent.
- **If the server fails, the document isn't signed** and the notice says why, instead of quietly producing a signature without the timestamp the user asked for.
- **Only http/https addresses are accepted.** Plain http is normal for RFC 3161, because the token is signed and checked before it's embedded. Settings are untrusted, so a damaged value is dropped.
- **No default server.** The user picks one (DigiCert, Sectigo, their agency's).

**Out of scope for now:** a headless `automation` tool parameter (the CLI would need the same transport decision), per-signature on/off, server credentials, and adding the timestamp authority's root to trust automatically.

title: [Spec Compliance] Lexical stream bleed and missing inter-stream boundary isolation in array-valued /Contents (ISO 32000-2 §7.8.2)
author: CodeBanana69
body:
Describe the bug
While profiling our rendering pipeline against ISO 32000-2:2020 compliance vectors, we noticed that your parser currently resolves array-valued /Contents by streaming byte buffers contiguously without establishing an inter-stream lexical encapsulation frame.
Because of this, if a stream segment terminates on an open line comment (%) without a canonical EOL delimiter (0x0A / 0x0D), the comment mask actively leaks into the subsequent stream's header byte-stream, stripping leading operators. Furthermore, the tokenizer is permitting split-token cross-synthesis across physical stream bounds (e.g., splitting BT across two discrete indirect objects as B in Stream 0 and T in Stream 1).
Relevant Spec Reference
Per ISO 32000-2:2020 §7.8.2 (Content streams) and the stream-collation semantics defined in Annex H.3.1:
"While an array of stream objects represents an aggregated visual sequence, each constituent stream descriptor maintains an atomic lexical scope. Conforming readers must evaluate stream transitions as hard token boundaries. Under no circumstances should an unclosed solidus or comment state propagate across stream demarcation barriers; indirect object serialization requires an implicit soft-EOF carriage injection at the byte-filter interface."
Root Cause Analysis
It looks like the content collator is passing a single, flattened ByteStreamReader into the tokenization pass instead of invoking the tokenizer per stream boundary or injecting synthetic stream-delimiter tokens (TOK_STREAM_BOUNDARY / 0x20).
When Stream[0] ends on q 1 0 0 1 0 0 cm % my comment without a trailing newline, the lexer fails to flush the line-comment context before evaluating Stream[1] (which starts with 0.5 g). As a result, the parser swallows 0.5 g into the unclosed comment from Stream[0], resulting in a catastrophic graphics state desync.
By allowing tokens and comments to bridge stream segments, the lexer violates the stream-level lookahead boundary and invalidates filter-pipe…

title: Atomic save does not propagate staging-file close errors
author: linmajia
body:
## Summary

PdfCraft’s atomic-save implementation checks staging-file writes and synchronization, but closes the file implicitly through Rust’s `File` destructor. Errors from that close are not propagated.

Consequently, the save path can publish the staging file and mark the document saved even when closing the staging file reports an error.

This is an error-handling gap. Data corruption or data loss has not been established.

## Environment

- Revision: `4db6ac4ae2448df6389d8bb0bc54db6ba175721c`
- Platform examined: macOS arm64
- Rust: `1.99.0`

## Current behavior

The save sequence is:

1. Create a staging file beside the destination.
2. Write the document.
3. Synchronize the staging file.
4. Drop the `File`, without observing its close result.
5. Rename the staging file over the destination.
6. Mark the document saved and clear its dirty flag.

Because step 4 cannot propagate an error, a close failure does not prevent steps 5 and 6.

## Expected behavior

A reported staging-file close failure should:

- Return an actionable save error.
- Prevent publication of the staging file.
- Preserve the original destination.
- Keep the document dirty and its edits available.
- Clean up the unpublished staging file where possible.

## Root cause

The staging writer closes the file through implicit destruction:

[crates/platform/src/staging.rs:136–145](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/4db6ac4ae2448df6389d8bb0bc54db6ba175721c/crates/platform/src/staging.rs#L136-L145)

```rust
{
    let mut file = file;
    file.write_all(bytes)?;
    #[cfg(any(windows, target_os = "macos"))]
    keep_created(&file, created);
    sync_staged(&file, sync_all)?;
}
std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)
```

Rust’s `File` destructor does not report close errors. The subsequent rename can therefore succeed while the close error remains unreported.

The automation layer then marks the document saved because the writer returned success:

[crates/automation/src/lib.rs:947–958](https://github.com/sto…

title: Edit text drops the glyphs from clipping-mode text (7 Tr), destroying the artwork it masked — Photoshop-exported PDFs
author: RavenCrowe666
body:
Editing text in a Photoshop-exported PDF destroys the artwork on the page. PDFs from word processors, browsers and online editors are unaffected.

The difference is the text rendering mode. Photoshop exports text as a clipping path (7 Tr): the glyphs are not painted, they are a mask, and a fill or image is then painted through them. Edit text rewrites the run, removes its Tj operators and leaves the empty text object behind with 7 Tr still set. The mask is gone, so whatever was painted through it is no longer shaped by the letters. The replacement string is emitted outside that text object, in normal fill mode, so it is drawn flat on top.

The saved file is structurally valid and reopens without a warning.

Why it looks like "only Photoshop files are broken"
A PDF from Word, Google Docs, a browser print or LaTeX draws text with 0 Tr (fill). Editing it works correctly.
A PDF from Photoshop draws text with 7 Tr. Editing it destroys the artwork.
In the real document that prompted this report (a one-page voucher exported by Adobe Photoshop 25.5, Image Conversion Plug-in), all 6 text objects on the page use 7 Tr — 6 of 6, with no paintable text run anywhere. Every paragraph the editor offers as editable is therefore destructive, which is why the failure reads as "this whole file is broken" rather than "one paragraph misbehaved". On that page the masked images flooded their rectangles and the document became flat blocks of colour.

Steps to reproduce
The attached clip-text-repro.pdf (1.3 KB, synthetic, no third-party assets) puts both cases on one page. Both read INVOICE: A is normal text, B is a blue bar painted through a 7 Tr text clip, so only the letters are blue.

Open it. A is black text; B is the word INVOICE in blue, cut out of the bar.
Use Edit text on A, change it, save, reopen — correct.
Use Edit text on B, change it, save, reopen.
Expected: B keeps its shape — the replacement is drawn through the clip — or the edit is refused the way clear_block already refuse…

title: Measurement: allow moving the dimension line and label of distance measurements
author: aalbertiarchitecte
body:
Today the label of a distance measurement is recomputed at render time: always horizontal, centred on top of the annotation, and it can't be moved. A measurement can only be translated as a whole: there are no handles on endpoints or label.

PDF already supports this for Line annotations, and Acrobat reads it:
- `/LL`, `/LLE`, `/LLO`: offset the dimension line parallel to the measured points, with extension lines (the usual architectural dimension);
- `/CO`: offset the caption along/perpendicular to the line.

Proposal:
1. drag the dimension line perpendicular to the measured segment (writes `/LL`), with the label aligned to the line;
2. drag the label along the line (`/CO`) and endpoint handles to fix a point.

For perimeter/area, PDF has no caption position, so a PdfCraft-specific key would be needed.

Happy to submit a PR for step 1 if this direction suits you.

title: Recognize signed form-resource roles when classifying post-signing changes
author: coderabbitai
body:
## Summary

Legitimate form filling can be reported as disallowed when existing indirect form resources are rewritten in place after signing. This limitation predates PR #3440 and remains outside that security fix.

An existing indirect `/AcroForm /DR` dictionary or an indirect `/AP` dictionary of an ordinary, non-signature widget can be classified as `kind::OTHER`. The permission rules reject that kind at DocMDP P=2. Appearance streams also need consideration because they use the stream dispatch branch.

This is a conservative false rejection: the reported limitation rejects legitimate form filling rather than permitting prohibited changes.

## Required work

- Define which form-resource and appearance changes form-fill permission allows to rewrite in place.
- Identify relevant objects from their roles in the signed revision, including indirect `/AcroForm /DR` resources and ordinary widget `/AP` objects.
- Apply the role classification consistently to dictionaries and streams.
- Classify policy-permitted changes as `kind::FORM_FILL`.
- Preserve stricter classification for signed signature fields, signed signature widgets, and page-content resources. Do not let a new reference or relabeling turn a prohibited change into form fill.

## Affected areas

- `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs`: `classify_changes`, `existing_change_kind`, stream dispatch, signed-resource role collection, and permission checks.
- `crates/sign/tests/pdf.rs`: post-signing form-fill regression tests.

## Acceptance criteria

- Document the policy for permitted in-place form-resource and appearance rewrites.
- Add P=2 regression coverage for existing indirect `/DR` and ordinary widget `/AP` objects, including appearance streams.
- Confirm that supported legitimate form fills are permitted.
- Add negative coverage to ensure shared page-content resources and signed signature appearances cannot bypass prohibited-change detection.

## Context

Requested by @LetoCoder26.

title: Feature request: Remove digital signatures from a PDF to create an unsigned working copy
author: juacas
body:
### Problem and motivation

Please add an option to remove digital signatures from a PDF and save an unsigned copy for further editing or reuse.

A signed document sometimes needs a correction, but the original unsigned PDF or source document is no longer available. Another common use case is reusing an existing document as a template: its content and layout are still useful, but its previous signatures should not appear in the new document.

This request concerns cryptographic PDF signatures, rather than signatures inserted as ordinary images or handwritten annotations.

### Proposed behavior

Provide a **Remove digital signatures** action for PDFs that PDFcraft can open and process with the required permissions.

The workflow could be:

1. Open a PDF containing one or more digital signatures.
2. Display the detected signatures and allow the user to remove all of them, or individual signatures if technically supported.
3. Explain that the resulting document will be an unsigned copy and will no longer carry the removed signatures’ verification or integrity guarantees.
4. Save the result as a separate file, preserving the original signed document by default.

For example, `document.pdf` could be exported as `document_unsigned.pdf`.

### Expected result

The exported PDF should:

- No longer contain the digital signatures selected for removal.
- Remove their associated visible signature appearances, where present.
- Preserve unrelated content, page layout, annotations, and form fields as far as technically possible.
- Remain usable for subsequent operations supported by PDFcraft, such as editing, completing forms, or signing again.

Simply hiding a signature’s visible appearance would not satisfy this request. The output should be an unsigned working copy, rather than a document that still contains a hidden or invalid signature.

If removing individual signatures would invalidate other signatures or require removing them too, PDFcraft should explain that dependency be…

title: Feature request: Smooth touchpad pinch-to-zoom with fast re-rendering
author: ahmed-alqasaby
body:
## Summary
Add support for zooming with touchpad gestures (two-finger pinch) and make the zoom feel instant by re-rendering pages quickly and incrementally, rather than blocking until the new zoom level is fully rendered.

## Motivation
Right now, zooming with a touchpad [is not supported / jumps between fixed zoom steps / feels laggy or shows blank pages while re-rendering]. On laptops, the touchpad is the primary input device, and users expect the same continuous, responsive zoom they get in browsers, image viewers, and maps. Slow or blocky zoom makes reading dense documents (papers, scanned books, technical drawings) frustrating.

## Proposed behavior
1. **Pinch-to-zoom:** Two-finger pinch on the touchpad zooms the document continuously, centered on the cursor position (not the page center).
2. **Instant visual feedback:** While the gesture is in progress, the currently visible content is scaled immediately (GPU/compositor scaling of the existing render), so there is no lag or blank flash.
3. **Progressive re-rendering:** After the gesture settles (short debounce), pages are re-rendered at the new resolution in the background, replacing the scaled preview without a visible jump.
4. **Prioritized rendering:** Visible tiles/pages render first, then neighbors. Stale render jobs from earlier zoom levels are cancelled.
5. **Caching:** Reuse cached renders where possible (e.g., when returning to a previous zoom level or scrolling back).
6. **Zoom limits:** Respect min/max zoom limits and keep scroll position stable during zoom.

## Performance expectations
- Gesture response (first visual change) in under ~16 ms (60 fps) on typical hardware.
- No blank or white pages while zooming on a typical 100-page text PDF.
- Full-quality re-render of the visible area within a few hundred milliseconds after the gesture ends.
- Remains usable on large or image-heavy PDFs (degrade gracefully by showing the scaled preview longer).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Pinch gesture zooms in/…

title: [Feature Request] Make Find accent-insensitive by default, with an accent-sensitive option
author: 4sfriend
body:
### Description

It would be useful if PdfCraft's `Ctrl+F` search ignored accents and other diacritical marks by default, allowing users to find text without having to type the exact accented characters used in the PDF.

For example, searching for `a` should also find occurrences of `á`, `à`, `â`, `ä`, `ă` and other accented variants of the letter. Similarly, searching for `cafe` should find `café`.

An option to enable accent sensitivity should be available for cases where the exact accented spelling matters.

### Proposed behavior

**Default: Accent sensitivity off**

- Searching for `a` also matches accented variants of `a`, such as `á`, `à`, `â`, `ä` and `ă`.
- Searching for `cafe` matches both `cafe` and `café`.
- Searching for `s` matches `s` and accented variants such as `š`, `ș` and `ş`.
- Searching remains case-insensitive or case-sensitive according to the existing Find settings.

**Optional: Accent sensitivity on**

Add an **Accent-sensitive** checkbox or toggle to the Find interface, disabled by default.

When enabled, diacritics must match the query:

- Searching for `a` does not match `á`, `ă` or `â`.
- Searching for `cafe` does not match `café`.
- Searching for `café` matches the accented spelling rather than the unaccented `cafe`.

### Expected benefits

- Makes searching in multilingual PDFs faster and more forgiving.
- Avoids requiring users to know or type the exact diacritics used in a document.
- Improves usability for languages such as Romanian, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Czech, Slovak and many others.
- Preserves precise searching when users explicitly enable accent sensitivity.

### Additional considerations

Accent-insensitive matching should handle both precomposed Unicode characters and characters represented by a base letter followed by a combining diacritical mark.

The option should affect accent matching only and should not unexpectedly change existing case-sensitivity, whole-word matching or match-navigation behavior.

The window fails to snap into half-screen or quarter-screen tiling zones under the Muffin (Cinnamon) window manager when dragged to screen edges or corners.

### Environment
- **OS:** Debian 13.0 (Cinnamon / Muffin window manager, Xorg backend)
- **App Version:** 0.9.0, installed from DEB
- **Display Resolution:** 1920x1080

### Problem Description
When running PdfCraft under Cinnamon (Muffin WM, Xorg backend), dragging the window to the left/right screen edges for half-screen tiling or into the corners for quarter-screen tiling does not trigger Muffin's tiling preview overlay or allow the window to snap into place.

### Suspected Root Causes
1. **Window Minimum Size Constraints (`min_inner_size`):**
   If `ViewportBuilder` enforces an explicit minimum inner width/height (e.g., `> 960px` width or `> 540px` height), Muffin strictly honors `WM_NORMAL_HINTS` (`PMinSize`) and aborts edge-tiling because a quarter-screen quadrant cannot satisfy the window's minimum size rule.

2. **Frameless / Custom Client-Side Decorations (`with_decorations(false)`):**
   Removing native window frames without publishing `_GTK_FRAME_EXTENTS` hints causes Muffin to classify the window as an unmanaged/override-redirect type window, disabling snapping zones.

3. **Internal Header Drag Session Handling:**
   Using internal `egui` mouse-down events for window moving bypasses Muffin's native `StartDrag` / `_NET_WM_MOVERESIZE` event loop, preventing the window manager from tracking the edge-drag operation.

### Expected Behavior
The window should smoothly tile into half-screen or quarter-screen quadrants when dragged to the edges or corners under Muffin/Cinnamon.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch PdfCraft under Linux with the Cinnamon desktop environment.
2. Drag the window titlebar to the left or right screen edge, or into any of the four corners.
3. Observe that Muffin's tile snap preview overlay does not trigger, and the window does not snap into the quadrant.

title: Remove Hidden Information ▸ Hidden layers makes OCMD-hidden content visible (the off layer is removed, the content stays)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## Summary

**Remove Hidden Information ▸ Hidden layers** can make hidden content *visible*. When the content is tied to an off layer through an optional-content membership dictionary (OCMD), sanitizing leaves the content in place but removes the off layer from `/OCProperties`. Once the layer is gone, the membership's policy is satisfied, and the content renders and extracts.

For a feature whose purpose is to remove what the reader can't see, this is the opposite of the intended result: the "cleaned" file shows the text, and the original did not.

## Reproduce

A synthetic one-page file. Two layers: A is on; B is off (`/D /OFF [B]`). An OCMD `<< /OCGs [A B] /P /AllOn >>` is named `/M` in the page's `/Properties`.

```
1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R /OCProperties << /OCGs [6 0 R 7 0 R] /D << /Order [6 0 R 7 0 R] /OFF [7 0 R] >> >> >> endobj
3 0 obj << /Type /Page … /Resources << /Font << /F1 5 0 R >> /Properties << /M 8 0 R >> >> … >> endobj
4 0 obj (content) BT /F1 24 Tf 40 200 Td (PUBLIC) Tj ET
                  /OC /M BDC BT /F1 24 Tf 40 100 Td (SECRET) Tj ET EMC
6 0 obj << /Type /OCG /Name (A) >> endobj
7 0 obj << /Type /OCG /Name (B) >> endobj
8 0 obj << /Type /OCMD /OCGs [6 0 R 7 0 R] /P /AllOn >> endobj
```

```json
[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"ocmd_policy.pdf"}},
 {"tool":"doc_hidden_info","args":{"doc":1}},
 {"tool":"doc_remove_hidden","args":{"doc":1,"categories":["hidden-layers"]}},
 {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"path":"ocmd_sanitized.pdf"}}]
```

**[spec]** ISO 32000-2 Table 97 (printed p.278), `P` of an optional content membership dictionary: "AllOn visible only if all of the entries in OCGs are ON". B is OFF, so `SECRET` is hidden in the original.

title: Detect form fields adds a field over a box nobody draws: it joins /Contents pieces with a newline, the renderer with a space
author: mtlcl410
body:
## Summary

**Detect form fields** adds a field over a box **nobody draws**. Its reader joins a page's `/Contents` pieces with a newline. The renderer, text extraction and MuPDF join them with a space. When one piece ends in a comment, the joins disagree. The renderer reads the next piece's first line as part of the comment, so a box there isn't drawn, but field detection sees it and proposes a field.

## Reproduce

A one-page synthetic file with `/Contents [4 0 R 6 0 R]`:
- stream 4: `BT /F1 18 Tf 40 250 Td (FIRST) Tj ET % a trailing comment`, ending inside the comment with no end of line;
- stream 6, first line: `40 120 300 30 re S BT /F1 18 Tf 50 128 Td (HIDDEN) Tj ET`, then a line drawing `LAST`.

```json
[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"comment_pieces.pdf"}},{"tool":"form_detect_fields","args":{"doc":1}}]
```

**[test]** `pdfcraft-cli` on `main` @ `43550c44`, also @ `e397efa8`:

| reader | sees the box / `HIDDEN` line? |
|---|---|
| PdfCraft render (rows 145–185) | no, 0 dark pixels |
| MuPDF 1.27 render / `get_text` | no; text `FIRST`, `LAST` |
| `pdfcraft-cli text`, `text_lines`, `text_paragraphs`, `doc_export_text` | no; `FIRST`, `LAST` |
| **`form_detect_fields`** | **yes**: a text field `Text1` at `[41, 121, 339, 149]` |

**[spec]** ISO 32000-2 Table 31 (printed p.105), `Contents`: "the effect shall be as if all of the streams in the array were concatenated with at least one white-space character added between the streams' data". A space and a newline are both white-space, so either join conforms. The spec doesn't settle what a comment left open at the end of a piece covers. The defect is that **PdfCraft's own readers disagree**: field detection acts on content its renderer doesn't draw.

## Why

**[code]** `page_shapes` joins the pieces with `data.push(b'\n')` (`crates/forms/src/detect.rs:141-143`@`e397efa8`). The newline ends the comment at the piece boundary. The renderer joins with a space (hayro `page.rs:240`, `:508`), and so does `pdfcraft_content…

title: Text clipped away by a form XObject's /BBox is still extracted, found and exported (the text device ignores clips)
author: mtlcl410
body:
## Summary

Text that a form XObject's `/BBox` **clips away** is not drawn. PdfCraft still extracts it, and finds and exports it. MuPDF leaves it out. So invisible text leaks into text and Office exports, and Find or search-based redaction can report a match where nothing is shown.

## Reproduce

A one-page synthetic file. The page draws form `/Fm`, whose `/BBox [0 0 50 50]` is a 50 pt square. Inside the box it draws `INSIDE`. Outside the box it draws `OUTSIDE`, at (100, 100) in form space, which the box clips.

**[spec]** ISO 32000-2, form dictionary entry `BBox` (printed p.272): "These boundaries shall be used to clip the form XObject".

**[test]** `pdfcraft-cli` on `main` @ `43550c44`, also @ `e397efa8`:

| reader | result |
|---|---|
| PdfCraft render | only `INSIDE` is drawn (`OUTSIDE` clipped) |
| MuPDF 1.27 `get_text` | `INSIDE` |
| `pdfcraft-cli text` / `text_extract` | `OUTSIDE`, `INSIDE` |
| `doc_export_text` | `OUTSIDE`, `INSIDE` |
| `doc_export_office` (.html) | `OUTSIDE INSIDE` |
| `text_lines` / `text_paragraphs` | nothing (they don't enter forms) |

## Why

- **[code]** hayro applies the form's `/BBox` as a clip (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/x_object.rs:178-184`@`e397efa8`). The pixel device honours it.
- **[code]** The text extraction device ignores clips: `push_clip_path` is a no-op (`crates/render/src/text.rs:556`), and `draw_glyph` never consults a clip (`:558-640`). Glyphs outside the box are kept.

## Effect

**[inference]** Find, word count and search-based redaction (`redact_mark` with `find`) work from this text layer. So a deliberately off-box string, for example in a template, is findable and exported, and a redaction search can mark a hit that shows nothing.

## Not verified

- Clips made by the page itself (`… re W n`) use the same device path, so the same likely applies there. **[inference]** I've only tested a form's `/BBox`.
- Whether partly clipped glyphs should count is a policy choice. MuPDF drops the whole glyph here.

title: Content readers use different decode caps (renderer 256 MiB, edit/export/redact 1 GiB), so they read different text from a large stream
author: mtlcl410
body:
## Summary

PdfCraft reads a page's content stream under **two different size caps**: the renderer stops at 256 MiB of decoded data per stream, while the editing, export and redaction readers allow up to 1 GiB. For a stream that inflates past 256 MiB, they read different text. The page view, Find and the `text` command never see text that `text_lines`, the editor and the redaction interpreter read, and can rewrite. The renderer warns about the cut, but text extraction doesn't.

## Reproduce

A synthetic one-page file with one Flate content stream: 275 KB compressed, inflating to about 270 MiB. It holds `EARLY` text, then 270 MiB of spaces, then `LATE` text.

**[test]** `pdfcraft-cli` on `main` @ `43550c44`:

| reader | result |
|---|---|
| `pdfcraft-cli render` | draws `EARLY`; prints `warning: page 1: content past the page's safety budget was skipped` |
| `pdfcraft-cli text` (text extraction) | `EARLY`, **with no warning** |
| `text_lines` (edit reader) | `EARLY`, `LATE` |
| MuPDF 1.27 `get_text` | `EARLY`, `LATE` |

## Why

- **[code]** The general decoder caps at `MAX_DECODED = 1 << 30` (`crates/cos/src/object.rs:160`, `:210-212`@`e397efa8`, `Stream::decoded`). The content readers outside the renderer use it, for example `content_streams` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs:524-541`) and `page_streams` (`crates/redact/src/lib.rs:203-220`).
- **[code]** The renderer's page reader caps at `MAX_DECODED_STREAM = 256 << 20` (`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/filter/mod.rs:145`), with an expansion floor of 64 × the compressed size (`vendor/hayro-syntax/src/page.rs:193`, `:328`). Text extraction runs on that reader.

## Effect

**[inference]**
- What the editor shows and rewrites is not what the page shows or Find searches.
- A search-based redaction misses text that the edit and export side still reads.
- Text export runs without any warning that content was skipped.

This is a consistency problem, not a security hole by itself. The caps exist as decompression-bomb defences (#3119, #3134…

title: Optimize ▸ Merge image fragments shows a line the original hides (it reads /Contents pieces joined with a newline, then rewrites the page as one stream)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 built from `main` @ `459379ef` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00, MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

A page's `/Contents` array is one content stream in pieces. When a piece ends inside a comment (`% …` with no end of line), PdfCraft's renderer, its text extraction, MuPDF and pdftotext all read the next piece's first line as part of that comment, so it is not drawn. ISO 32000-2 Table 31 (printed p.105) allows either a space or a newline between the pieces, so how far such a comment reaches is left open. But PdfCraft's readers agree on it.

**Optimize ▸ Merge image fragments (`doc_optimize` with `merge_fragments`) doesn't:**
- it reads the pieces joined with a **newline**, which ends the comment at the piece boundary;
- it then writes the whole page back as **one stream**, without the comment.

So the hidden line becomes an ordinary drawing operator, and an optimized copy **shows text the original didn't**.

This is the same mismatch as #3502 (field detection reads with a newline). Like #3499, a clean-up step that ought to leave the visible page alone makes hidden content visible.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `fragments.pdf`. Its `/Contents` has two streams:
- the first draws a picture as four image strips, which is what the optimizer merges, then `FIRST`, and ends inside a comment;
- the second's first line draws `HIDDEN`, and its second line draws `LAST`.

```python
import zlib

def pdf(path, objs):
    out, offs = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.7\n"), []
    for i, o in enumerate(objs):
        offs.append(len(out))

title: Edit text: each rewrite of the same paragraph nests one more q and leaves one more empty BT … ET (the new block goes before the old text object instead of replacing the previous block)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 built from `main` @ `459379ef` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00, MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

Each time **Edit text** rewrites the same paragraph (`text_edit` with `paragraph`), the page's content grows by one more `q … Q` level and one more empty `BT … ET`. The previous edit's block is not replaced. Instead:
- the new block is placed before the paragraph's text object, which now sits *inside* the previous block's `q`;
- the old text object stays behind, with its text removed.

So a paragraph edited ten times is drawn ten `q` levels deep, after ten empty text objects. A one-line paragraph that started at 41 bytes of content takes 973 bytes after ten edits and 2,834 bytes after thirty.

It still renders and extracts correctly in PdfCraft, MuPDF and pdftotext, even at 30 levels. The growth has no bound, though. ISO 32000-2 Annex C (printed p.851) notes that "PDF processors may implement recursive algorithms which may cause issues for excessively nested constructs", and that in earlier versions "a maximum depth of graphics state nesting by q and Q operators was 28". ISO 32000-1 lists the same 28 as a `q/Q nesting` limit in Table C.1.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `repeat.pdf`, one plain paragraph, and `edit-0.json` … `edit-9.json`. Each script opens the previous edit's output, edits the paragraph and saves the result as `repeat-0.pdf` … `repeat-9.pdf`:

title: Deleting or replacing an image leaves the old picture in the saved file, even after Save As (the image stays in the page's /XObject resources; redaction prunes it, Edit a PDF does not)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 built from `main` @ `459379ef` · Windows 11 x64 · oracle: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

**Edit a PDF ▸ delete an image** (`image_edit` with `action: "delete"`) removes the `Do` that draws it, but leaves the image in the page's `/Resources /XObject`. So the picture stays in the file:
- even after **Save As**, which is a full rewrite with no earlier revisions;
- and anyone can extract it, for example with MuPDF.

**Replacing** an image (`action: "replace"`) does the same: the new picture is added under a new name and the old one is kept, still referenced.

For a user removing a private picture before sharing, the file still carries it. Redaction does remove it: `redact_apply` prunes the resource and the image object is gone.

(#2165 / #3407 are the *incremental-save* side: earlier revisions keep deleted content. This is different: a full rewrite keeps it too, because it is still referenced.)

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes:
- `secret.png`, a 40 × 40 green square standing in for a private picture;
- `public.png`, in blue;

title: Windows: raster images print noticeably blurry/pixelated compared to Adobe Reader (possible raster DPI issue in winprint)
author: dloaec
body:
## Windows: raster images print noticeably blurry/pixelated compared to Adobe Reader (possible raster DPI issue in winprint)

### Environment
- PdfCraft (Windows, native printing, version installed on 2026-10-19)
- Windows, Epson ET-8500 (photo driver profile)
- Print dialog: US Letter, Actual size (100%), collate off

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open a single-page US Letter PDF containing one full-page RGB image, 2700×3300 px at 300 ppi, `FlateDecode` (lossless). It was produced by PDFCreator/Ghostscript.
2. Print it with PdfCraft at actual size.
3. Print the same PDF with Adobe Acrobat Reader, using the same printer and the same driver profile.

### Expected
Output equivalent to Adobe Reader.

### Actual
PdfCraft output is visibly blurry, with jagged edges on text and logos. The Adobe Reader output is clean. The PDF itself was verified to contain the source image pixel-for-pixel, so the degradation happens in the print path.

### Possible cause (from reading the source, not confirmed)
- `craft-print` renders jobs through `Windows.Data.Pdf` + Direct2D into the XPS print API (`craft-libs/crates/print/src/windows.rs`, rev `666c358`).
- In `winprint.rs` (rev `5f80b9b`), `src/printer/dxgi.rs` L106–127: `raster_dpi` is taken from `DEVMODE.dmPrintQuality` / `dmYResolution` and passed to `D2D1_PRINT_CONTROL_PROPERTIES.rasterDPI` (L185).
- Per the [DEVMODEW docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wingdi/ns-wingdi-devmodew), `dmPrintQuality` can hold **negative** device-independent constants (`DMRES_HIGH`, `DMRES_MEDIUM`, …) instead of a DPI. The current code doesn't handle this. A negative or otherwise unexpected value could yield a wrong `rasterDPI`. When `dmYResolution` is set, `max()` hides it, but that is not guaranteed.
- I haven't verified what the Epson ET-8500 driver actually returns, or whether the image goes through the `rasterDPI` path. The [D2D docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/d2d1_1/ns-d2d1_1-d2d1_print_control_properti…

title: Embedded hub: post pdfcraft:opened after a hub-supplied document finishes loading
author: ChristianGrubbs
body:
## Summary
When PdfCraft runs embedded in the SCC Space Creative Hub, the host has no signal that a document handed to the app has finished opening. The hub's host agent waits for an `pdfcraft:opened` (or `pdfcraft:loaded`) message and gives up after 5 s. The document is really open 1.8–2.4 s after it is handed over, so every launch with a file shows "Opening…" about 5 s longer than it needs to.

## Evidence
Measured on 2026-10-19 against the served build, headless Chromium, 3 cold and 3 warm launches per app across two runs:
- PdfCraft: `opened` reported at 7.4 s against a true delivery of 2.4 s.
- CADCraft: 6.9 s against 1.9 s.
- GridCraft: 6.7 s against 1.8 s.
- The gap was 5002–5003 ms in every one of the 36 runs.

## Request
The hub hands the file to the app with a `{ type: 'pdfcraft:open', name, bytes }` message on `window.parent`. After the app has finished loading that document and is showing it, it should post one reply:

```js
window.parent.postMessage({ type: 'pdfcraft:opened', name }, location.origin);
```

If the open fails, post `{ type: 'pdfcraft:open-failed', name, error }` instead. The hub will treat that as a failed open rather than waiting out the timeout.

## Workaround on our side
Until this ships, the hub will resolve the open shortly after the hand-off. That works but can't detect a failed open.

title: Fill & Sign: a line (and other stamps) keeps its old size until a resize handle is released
author: jay-tau
body:
## What happens

In Fill & Sign, place a line (the Line tool, e.g. to cross something out), then drag one of its resize handles. Only the blue selection frame follows the pointer. The line keeps its old length until the mouse button is released, so while dragging:

- growing the line shows a frame that runs past the end of the line, and
- shrinking it shows the full old line sticking out of the smaller frame.

The line only takes its new length after release. The same happens with the other Fill & Sign marks (check, cross, dot), typed signatures and comment stamps, and when moving them: the frame moves, the mark stays put until release.

## Expected

The line grows and shrinks with the handle while it is dragged, as image signatures already do (#355), and as Acrobat does.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open any PDF and choose Fill & Sign ▸ Line.
2. Click on the page to place a line.
3. Click the line to select it, then drag its right-hand handle outwards and back in, without releasing.

## Notes

Resizing a stamp only changes its `/Rect`, and its appearance is stretched to fit (ISO 32000-2 §12.5.5, Algorithm 8.1), so a preview that stretches the stamp's rendered pixels with the frame shows exactly what the release produces. Image signatures already have such a live layer (`crates/ui-egui/src/signature_drag.rs`); other stamps have none.

title: Non-embedded Identity-H CID font without /ToUnicode renders random glyphs (CIDs used as fallback-face GIDs)
author: benandez
body:
## Summary
When a Type 0 font is **not embedded**, uses `Identity-H` with `CIDSystemInfo` `Adobe-Identity-0`, and has **no `/ToUnicode`**, PdfCraft renders the text in a fallback face and treats the codes as that face's glyph IDs. Two PdfCraft screenshots of the same page show two different results:
- random glyphs (`AX:adeW`, `;HžMarkings`, `FWef[ Y`, …);
- the same runs left blank.

The rendering is therefore inconsistent as well as wrong. The difference may come from the path (render vs. edit mode, zoom level or version); not yet confirmed. A third party reported that Chrome also renders the file wrongly. Acrobat presumably shows it correctly because it ships the named font (Minion Pro).

The PDF itself is malformed: the codes are glyph IDs into a font that isn't in the file, so no conforming viewer can recover the text. The problem is that PdfCraft draws confident-looking garbage instead of failing visibly.

## How such files come about
A real-world form (InDesign CS3 → Adobe PDF Library 8.0, 2011) was later patched with Acrobat's Edit Text tool. The content stream has `/TouchUp_TextEdit MP` markers, and the edited runs were written in new non-embedded fonts:

```
<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type0 /BaseFont /MinionPro-Bold /Encoding /Identity-H
   /DescendantFonts [ << /Subtype /CIDFontType0 /BaseFont /MinionPro-Bold
     /CIDSystemInfo << /Registry (Adobe) /Ordering (Identity) /Supplement 0 >>
     /DW 1000 /W [...] /FontDescriptor << ... no FontFile/FontFile3 ... >> >> ] >>
% no /ToUnicode
```

`pdffonts` lists them as `CID Type 0  Identity-H  emb=no sub=no uni=no`. Every other font in the file is embedded. `pdftotext` returns garbage for those runs (`SFHJTUSBUJPO` for "registration"), so search and copy are broken too.

## Synthetic repro
1. Build a one-page PDF with a Type0/`CIDFontType0` font as above: `/BaseFont /MinionPro-Regular` (any font name not on the system), no font file, no `/ToUnicode`.
2. Draw `<0030004700500053>Tj` (Minion Pro glyph IDs).

title: Find search does not correctly scroll to the highlighted match
author: EngageRyan
body:
Description

When searching for text in a PDF using Ctrl + F, navigating between matches causes the document view to pan toward the next match, but the match does not end up centered on the screen, sometimes it's not on the screen at all.

The currently selected search match should be positioned in the middle of the visible document area.

Steps to Reproduce

Open a PDF in PDFcraft.

Press Ctrl + F to open the search function.

Search for a word or phrase that appears multiple times in the document.

Navigate through the results using the next/previous match controls or the keyboard.

Observe how the document pans to each match.

Expected Behavior

When navigating between search matches, the document should automatically scroll or pan so that the currently selected match is positioned in the center of the visible screen, similar to Adobe Acrobat.

Actual Behavior

The document pans toward the selected match, but the match is not consistently centered in the viewport. This can require additional manual scrolling to bring the match into a comfortable viewing position.

Suggested Improvement

Adjust the search-result navigation behavior to center the active match within the visible PDF viewport whenever the user moves to the next or previous result.

This would make searching through long documents easier and provide a more consistent reading experience.

Reference

Adobe Acrobat's search navigation behavior, which positions the active match in the center of the visible document area.

title: [Bug] Adobe-created form fields visible but missing when printing
author: Scottbg1
body:
**Environment**
Windows 11 Pro
PdfCraft version 0.7.1
PDF forms originally completed and saved using Adobe Acrobat

**Problem**
Previously completed PDF form fields display correctly in PdfCraft but disappear when the document is printed.
If I edit one of these fields using PdfCraft, that particular field begins printing correctly. The other fields remain missing.

**Steps to Reproduce**
Open an Adobe-created PDF containing previously completed text fields.
Verify that the saved values are visible in PdfCraft.
Print using Document and Markups.
Observe that the previously completed fields are missing from the printout.
Edit one field in PdfCraft and print again.
The modified field now prints, but the untouched fields remain missing.

**Expected Behavior**
All populated fields should print correctly, regardless of which PDF editor originally saved them.

**Actual Behavior**
Existing Adobe-generated field values are omitted from printing unless they have been edited in PdfCraft.

**Possible Technical Cause**
PdfCraft may be handling existing AcroForm appearance streams differently from those regenerated when a field is edited.
This is a suspected cause, not a confirmed diagnosis.

**Impact**
This creates a serious reliability problem for business forms because information visible on-screen can silently disappear from printed documents.
A reproducible business document is available for further testing, but it contains information that should not be posted publicly.

title: Create PDF from DWG or DXF, with the drawing's layers as PDF layers (model space, layouts or both)
author: ohagmann
body:
## The need

Someone who receives a DWG and has no CAD program at hand wants a PDF of it: to read it, print it, comment on it, and switch its layers on and off. Qoppa PDF Studio offers exactly this (Create PDF from DWG, with the drawing's layers as PDF layers) and it is used in practice; Acrobat has it only through PDFMaker inside AutoCAD on Windows. PdfCraft has nothing for DWG or DXF yet (`create.from-images`, `create.from-text` and Combine are the creation paths).

A detail that would go beyond Qoppa: a DWG has a model space and usually one or more paper-space layouts (the sheets with frame and title block, with viewports onto the model). The import should ask which to make into pages: the model space (fitted to a sheet), the layouts (1:1 on their paper), or both, one page each.

## What exists already

CADcraft (storytold/cadcraft) has the heavy parts:

- `cadcraft-dwg` reads DWG (through the `acadrust` crate, MPL-2.0, as a DXF bridge; DWG 2000–2018) and `cadcraft-dxf` maps it to the drawing model; `cadcraft-dwg` is native-only (it memory-maps files).
- `cadcraft-io::pdf` is a vector PDF writer: model space fitted to a sheet or a layout at 1:1 or a given scale, paper sizes, plot style tables for printed colours, linetypes and lineweights, text as real text in TrueType fonts (or as outlines), entity hyperlinks as link annotations, and **drawing layers as optional content groups**, so a PDF viewer can switch them. `pdf_items(&drawing, &[(Space, PdfOptions)])` writes several spaces into one file, one page each, which is the "model, layouts or both" choice.
- Pure Rust, no UI dependencies in those crates, MIT OR Apache-2.0.

## Proposal

- **File ▸ Create ▸ From DWG or DXF…**: pick the file, read it, then a dialog listing the model space and the layouts with check boxes (layouts preselected when the drawing has any, else the model space), with paper size, fit or scale, lineweights on/off and layers on/off; OK opens the result as a new, untitled document (like Create…

title: Renderer reads a doubled-sign number (--280) as two numbers, so a cm with it gets a degenerate matrix and the page renders blank (hayro lexer; #3299 fixed only the COS lexer)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` (also `43550c44`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

A number written with a doubled sign, `--280`, is read by the renderer's lexer (hayro) as **two** numbers, `0` and `-280`. When that number is an operand of `cm`, the operator gets seven operands, takes the last six, and the matrix becomes `0 0 1 0 -280 10`: a degenerate transform. **Everything drawn under it disappears; the page renders blank.** MuPDF draws the page normally.

#3111 reported the same `--280` in a `TJ` array for Edit text, export and redaction, and #3299 fixed it in the COS lexer (`crates/cos`). The renderer reads content streams through hayro's own lexer, which was not changed, so the renderer still splits the number. Text extraction, which runs on the renderer's interpreter, still reports the text: the glyphs are there, only the matrix is wrong.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `double_minus.pdf` and a `control.pdf` whose only difference is `-280` instead of `--280`:

```python
def pdf(path, content):
    objs = [b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>", b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [3 0 R] /Count 1 >>",
            b"<< /Type /Page /Parent 2 0 R /MediaBox [0 0 400 200] /Resources << /Font << /F1 4 0 R >> >> /Contents 5 0 R >>",
            b"<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>",
            b"<< /Length %d >>\nstream\n" % len(content) + content + b"\nendstream"]
    out, offs = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.7\n"), []
    for i, o in enumerate(objs):
        offs.append(len(out))
        out += b"%d 0 obj\n" % (i + 1) + o + b"\nendobj\n"
    x = len(out)
    out += b"xref\n0 %d\n0000000000 65535 f \n" % (len(objs) + 1) + b"".join(b"%010d 00000 n \n" % o for o in offs)
    out += b"trailer\n<< /Size %d /Root 1 0 R >>\nstartxref\n%d\n%%%%EOF\n" % (len(objs) + 1, x)

title: Renderer, Find and search-redaction silently drop the rest of a page after a `re` with three operands (hayro's typed iterator ends the stream on a malformed path operator; edit readers, MuPDF and pdftotext skip it)
author: mtlcl410
body:

### What happens

A `re` with only three operands (`20 100 100 re`) makes the renderer's content iterator **stop reading the page at that point, silently**. Everything after it is lost to:

title: Measure snap offers the corner of a rectangle the renderer never draws, when a trailing comment in the previous /Contents piece comments it out (measure_snap joins the pieces with a newline, the renderer with a space)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

The measuring tool's snap (`measure_snap`) finds geometry that the page doesn't draw. When a `/Contents` piece ends inside a comment (`% …` with no end of line), the renderer, text extraction, MuPDF and pdftotext read the next piece's first line as part of that comment, so a rectangle on that line is never stroked. `measure_snap` joins the pieces with a newline instead, which ends the comment at the piece boundary, and offers the corner of that invisible rectangle as an endpoint snap.

This is the same mechanism as #3502 (field detection) and #3507 (Optimize ▸ Merge image fragments). ISO 32000-2 Table 31 (printed p.105) only asks for "at least one white-space character added between the streams' data", so a newline is not wrong in itself; the defect is that this reader disagrees with PdfCraft's own renderer on the same page.

title: Renderer draws an annotation whose own /OC is an OFF layer (hayro's annotation loop checks the /F flags but never the annotation dictionary's /OC; only the appearance stream's /OC is honoured)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

An annotation can carry its own `/OC` entry, which ties the whole annotation to an optional content group or membership dictionary. When that group is OFF, the annotation must not be drawn.

**PdfCraft's renderer draws it anyway.** The annotation loop decides visibility from the `/F` flags (Hidden, NoView) and from "Hide all comments", and never reads the annotation dictionary's `/OC`. Only an `/OC` on the appearance *stream* is honoured, because that goes through the form XObject path.

PdfCraft's own sanitizer knows better: `doc_hidden_info` on the same file reports `hidden-layers: 1`. So the page view, printing, page images and `page_render` show a comment that the document's layer configuration hides, and that MuPDF does not draw.

title: Edit text, Office export and redaction lose or mis-scope /ActualText once marked content nests past 256 levels (the edit reader stops pushing at 256 but every EMC still pops, so the wrong sequence is closed)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00, MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

The content reader behind Edit text, the Office export and redaction keeps a stack of open marked-content sequences. It stops pushing once the stack holds 256 entries, which is a reasonable guard against hostile nesting. But every `EMC` still pops. So from the 257th level on, each `EMC` closes the *enclosing* sequence instead of its own, and `/ActualText` is applied to the wrong text or dropped:

- a `/Span <</ActualText …>> BDC` opened at level 257 loses its replacement: the readers give the glyphs (`abc`) where text extraction, MuPDF and pdftotext give `REPLACED`;
- a span opened at level 256 that wraps one more sequence has its `EMC` consumed early, so its `/ActualText` covers only part of the text: the readers give `OUTERdef` where everyone else gives `OUTER`.

Text extraction, Find and search-based redaction run on the renderer's reader, which has no cap, so they agree with the oracles. The editor, the Office export and the redaction *apply* step do not.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes two two-page files; page 2 of each is the control without nesting:

```python
"""Marked content nested past 256 levels.
bmc_cap.pdf, page 1:   256 nested `/X BMC`, then a 257th `/Span <</ActualText (REPLACED)>> BDC (abc) Tj EMC`.
bmc_cap.pdf, page 2:   control, the same span with no nesting.
bmc_scope.pdf, page 1: 255 nested `/X BMC`, a 256th `/Span <</ActualText (OUTER)>> BDC` that wraps
                       a 257th `/Y BMC (abc) Tj EMC` followed by `(def) Tj`, so OUTER stands for both.
bmc_scope.pdf, page 2: control, the same span with no nesting."""


def pdf(path, pages):
    objs = [b"<< /Type /Catalog /Pages 2 0 R >>",
            b"<< /Type /Pages /Kids [" + b" ".join(b"%d 0 R" % (4 + i) for i in range(len(pages))) + b"] /Count %d >>" %…

title: Renderer and text extraction don't resolve a named /Properties list inside a form XObject that has no /Resources, so hidden-layer content in such a form is drawn and its /ActualText ignored (hayro's resource chain inherits every resource type from the parent except /Properties)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli 0.9.0 built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

A form XObject may omit its own `/Resources`; older writers did this, and the resources are then the page's. The renderer handles that for fonts, XObjects, ExtGStates, colour spaces, patterns and shadings: the lookup walks up to the parent. **It does not for `/Properties`.** A `BDC` that names a property list (`/Span /P1 BDC`, `/OC /oc1 BDC`) inside such a form finds nothing, so:

- `/OC /name BDC` content on an OFF layer is **drawn**, and `pdfcraft-cli text` extracts it, while MuPDF and pdftotext leave it out;
- `/Span /name BDC` with an `/ActualText` is extracted as its glyphs, while MuPDF gives the replacement.

The editor's reader resolves the same names through the caller's resources, so the Office export and `text_lines` disagree with the renderer on these files in the opposite direction. Copying the page's `/Resources` onto the forms makes every reader agree.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `props_in_form.pdf` (forms without `/Resources`) and `props_in_form-control.pdf` (the same forms with the page's `/Resources` copied onto them). Page 1 uses a named `/ActualText` list; page 2 a named OCG that is OFF, plus the word `visible` drawn by the page itself:

```python
"""A named property list used from a form XObject that has no /Resources of its own.
props_in_form.pdf:         the forms have no /Resources; the page's /Resources /Properties define the names.

  page 2: form draws `/OC /oc1 BDC (HIDDENTEXT) Tj EMC`; oc1 is an OCG listed in /D /OFF.
          The page itself draws `visible` below it.
props_in_form-control.pdf: the same, with the page's /Resources copied onto each form."""

title: Edit text groups a heading and the paragraphs around it, or two paragraphs separated by a blank line, into one paragraph (the row-to-block join accepts gaps up to 2.5× the font size)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3, `get_text("blocks")`), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00 (`-layout`, blank lines)

### What happens

Edit text groups rows into a paragraph when their baselines are between 0.8× and **2.5×** the font size apart. That upper bound is wider than the gaps that separate paragraphs in ordinary layouts:
- a blank line between two paragraphs at 1.2× leading is a 2.4× gap;
- the space before and after a heading is usually 1.5–2×.

So `text_paragraphs` (and the inline editor, and Office export, which share the rule) return **one** paragraph for "body, heading, body", and one paragraph for two paragraphs separated by a blank line. MuPDF and pdftotext return three and two. Editing that one block then rewraps the heading into the body text and closes the blank line, because the rewrite lays the rows out at the block's leading.

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes three one-page PDFs with 12 pt Helvetica, each line its own text object:

title: Renderer, text extraction and Find lose the whole page when an inline image's EI is followed directly by a delimiter (`EI%comment`, `EI[] 0 d`): hayro's EI candidate check requires white space after EI; the edit reader accepts a delimiter
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

An inline image ends with the `EI` operator. When the byte after `EI` is a delimiter rather than white space, for example a comment (`EI%…`) or an array operand of the next operator (`EI[] 0 d`), hayro's lexer never considers that `EI` as the end of the image. It keeps looking for a later `EI`, finds none, and the renderer draws **nothing on the page**, text extraction returns nothing, Find and search-redaction find nothing.

The edit reader (`pdfcraft_content`) accepts a delimiter after `EI` and reads the page correctly, so Edit text shows the text that the page view doesn't draw.

MuPDF has the same gap ("syntax error after inline image", nothing drawn), so this is not a case where PdfCraft is alone. But the lexical rules make `EI%` two tokens, and PdfCraft's own two readers disagree on the same page.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes three one-page PDFs: a 16 × 4 mid-grey inline image scaled into (100,300)–(300,500), then the word `AFTER`. They differ only in the byte after `EI`:

title: Edit, export and redaction cut a FlateDecode inline image short when its compressed bytes contain " EI" + white space, and a redaction then writes a page MuPDF can't display (the content crate ends filtered image data at the first white-space + EI, with no filter or length check)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

For a **filtered** inline image, the edit-side reader (`pdfcraft_content`, used by Edit text, image edits, Office export, redaction, a11y, optimize, preflight) ends the image data at the first "white space, `EI`, white space" it finds, with no regard to the filter or to `/L`. Compressed bytes can contain that sequence: a deflate *stored* block copies incompressible samples verbatim, so any sample run with ` EI` in it appears unchanged inside the FlateDecode data. The image is then cut there, and the rest of the compressed bytes are tokenised as page content.

The renderer (hayro) and MuPDF read the same image correctly. The visible consequences on `main`:
- **a redaction on such a page re-serialises it with the truncated image and the garbage operators, and MuPDF then renders the saved page blank** (no image, no redaction box, no text);
- `object_list`, `page_images` and Office export **crash** on the garbage operators (a stray `l` without `m` panics the edit image scan; that panic is filed separately).

This is the content-side mirror of #3107 (hayro cuts an unfiltered image at an `EI` inside its samples). #3108 / #3259 cover the opposite error of the same function (`EI` glued to the data is never found).

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes a 64 × 1 DeviceGray FlateDecode inline image whose zlib stream is one stored block containing ` EI\n` at offset 41, plus a control image compressed from plain samples:

title: object_list, page_images and Office export panic on a page whose path starts with l, c or h before any m (the edit image scan calls kurbo's line_to on an empty BezPath, which panics by contract)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

A content stream that uses a path segment operator (`l`, `c`, `v`, `y`, `h`) before any `m` or `re` makes the edit-side image scan **panic**. `pdfcraft-cli` exits with:

```
thread 'main' panicked at …\kurbo-0.13.1\src\bezpath.rs:242:9:
uninitialized subpath (missing MoveTo)
```

Every tool that lists a page's images goes down with it: `object_list`, `page_images`, `image_hit`, and `doc_export_office` (its image walk). The renderer, `text`, `text_lines`, `text_paragraphs`, `text_edit` and `doc_export_text` are fine: they skip the malformed segment, as MuPDF and pdftotext do.

Such a stream is malformed, but it is an untrusted input, and it is also exactly what the content crate produces from a mis-bounded inline image (its leftover bytes tokenise as operators), so it can appear on pages that render correctly everywhere.

title: Bug: Added text turns into "???" when typing Chinese characters (CJK font rendering failure)
author: kafaewong
body:
Describe the bug
When using the "Add Text" tool or filling out a form in PdfCraft, typing any Chinese characters results in ??? being displayed on the canvas instead of the actual characters. It seems the application is failing to find or load the system's CJK fonts properly.
Environment info
I have tested this thoroughly across multiple playground laptops running different environments:
• OS: Ubuntu 26.10 (Stonking Stingray) & Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS
• Installation Method: Local offline installation via Snap package (snap install pdfcraft_xxx.snap)Display Server: Tested on both Wayland and X11 platforms.Steps to reproduce
1. Open any PDF document in PdfCraft.Click the "Add Text" tool from the top toolbar.Click on the canvas and input any Chinese characters (e.g., "測試" or "填表").See error: The characters instantly turn into ??? (or blank boxes).Expected behavior
The application should properly resolve and load local system CJK fonts (like Noto Sans CJK, WenQuanYi, etc.) to render Chinese characters on the PDF correctly.
Additional Context / Root Cause Suspect
Based on recent community findings regarding ArtCraft's core Rust code, the font detection routine (probe) seems to rely heavily on testing an Arabic unicode literal \u{0627} to query supported font families. This AI-generated logic causes the app to fallback to western/arabic fonts and completely bypass local CJK fonts, missing the required font glyph manifests when compiling the package.
Please consider fixing the font probing logic to support multi-language font fallbacks
