title: macOS Devanagari fallback list points at two files that have never existed
author: amoisttowe1
body:
## Summary

`crates/ui-egui/src/system_fonts.rs` keeps hand-written lists of installed font files to borrow for
scripts no embedded face covers (`AGENTS.md` §1.4 — read at runtime, never embedded or shipped).
**Two of the five macOS Devanagari paths point at files that do not exist, and one is Apple's real
file name misspelled**, so the face this list documents as its second choice has never been reachable.

| path listed | on macOS 26.6 (MacBook Pro, Apple M5 Max) |
| --- | --- |
| `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/DevanagariMT.ttc` | exists, 409,368 B ✅ — and it wins today |
| `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/DevanagariSangamMN.ttc` | **does not exist.** Apple's file is `Devanagari Sangam MN.ttc` — **with spaces**, the spelling this same file already uses for its Telugu and Tamil siblings (`Telugu Sangam MN.ttc`, `Tamil Sangam MN.ttc`). The correctly spelled file is here: 1,029,884 B |
| `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Kohinoor.ttc` | **does not exist.** `Kohinoor.ttc` lives one level up, at `/System/Library/Fonts/Kohinoor.ttc` (1,400,200 B) — which the list also names |
| `/Library/Fonts/Arial Unicode.ttf` | exists — a compatibility symlink into `Supplemental/`, resolving to 23,278,008 B ✅ |

So when Devanagari MT is absent, Hindi falls past the intended `Devanagari Sangam MN` instead of
using it.

## Where it came from, and how far it reaches

Both dead paths were introduced together in **#1033** ("Edit text: support Devanagari system font
fallback and Indic …", merged 2026-10-12) — its diff adds the two strings verbatim. Reading
`system_fonts.rs` at each release tag, the misspelling is present in **v0.7.1, v0.8.0 and v0.9.0**,
as it is on current `main`. In other words, these two addresses have never resolved for anyone.

## What a user would notice — stated narrowly, on purpose

**I have no screenshot or log showing breakage**, and I am not claiming one. On the Mac where I
checked, Devanagari MT exists and is chosen first, so nothing looks wrong today…

title: [Bug] Spaces in non-embedded Japanese CID fonts render as missing-glyph boxes (U+2002 fallback)
author: mskskn
body:
## Summary

Spaces in a non-embedded Japanese CID font can render as missing-glyph boxes. The Japanese text remains visible, but rows of spaces acquire visible .notdef outlines.

Confirmed on Windows x64 with a local build based on PdfCraft 0.6.0. I have not rebuilt the latest release to reproduce it, but source inspection of current main (2026-10-20) still shows the same relevant mapping and fallback selection.

This report contains only generic font identifiers, synthetic text and a proposed code change. No private documents, filenames, screenshots or document metadata are included.

## Synthetic reproduction

Use a one-page PDF with:
- Type0 /BaseFont /MS-Mincho, /Encoding /UniJIS-UCS2-HW-H.
- A non-embedded /CIDFontType2 descendant with /CIDSystemInfo << /Registry (Adobe) /Ordering (Japan1) /Supplement 4 >>.
- /DW 1000 and /W [231 [500]].
- A font descriptor naming MS-Mincho, but no FontFile/FontFile2/FontFile3.
- /F1 referencing that Type0 font.
- Content (20 pt text at x=10, y=30, on a 180 x 60 pt page):

~~~text
BT /F1 20 Tf 10 30 Td <65E500200020672C> Tj ET
~~~

This is just 日, two spaces, 本. Also test a stream containing only <002000200020>.

Render using a build with the existing craft-fonts Japanese fallback enabled.

Expected: the spaces draw no ink, while the second character stays at the position dictated by the original PDF's advances.
Actual before the local fix: spaces draw missing-glyph boxes.

## Cause

The predefined Japanese CMap / CID-to-Unicode path resolves these spaces to U+2002 EN SPACE. The selected BIZ UDMincho substitute has U+0020 and U+3000 but lacks U+2002.

In vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/cid.rs, Type0Font::map_via_unicode asks the substitute's charmap for U+2002. When this fails, the existing Adobe-collection guard correctly avoids interpreting an unrelated CID as a substitute glyph index, but the result is .notdef rather than a blank.

title: [Feature Request] Revision timeline: browse and restore earlier saved versions
author: ravenmyrrdin
body:
### [Feature Request] Revision timeline: browse and restore earlier saved versions

**Problem**
PdfCraft saves incrementally and already lets you view an earlier revision ("View revision"). What is missing is an overview of all revisions in a file, a way to compare two of them, and a way to get one back as a separate file. Acrobat only exposes earlier states for signed revisions ("View signed version").

Note: since #2174, Save As to a new file writes a clean copy without earlier revisions, so this mainly applies to documents saved in place.
**Proposal**
A "Revisions" panel that lists every incremental update in the file, with:
- revision number, save date (from the trailer/Info `ModDate` where available) and file size
- a read-only view of the document as it was at that revision
- a side-by-side or overlay comparison between two revisions
- "Restore as copy": save a chosen revision as a new file, without touching the original

Also expose it to the CLI and MCP, e.g. `doc_revisions` (list) and `doc_revision_extract` (save a revision as a new file).

**Edge cases**
- After a full rewrite (Save As / optimize) older revisions are gone; the panel should say so instead of showing nothing.
- For signed documents, mark which revision each signature covers.
- Encrypted documents: show revisions only after the document is opened with the right password.

**Use case**
Auditing who changed what and when in contracts, medical reports or forms, and recovering an earlier state after an accidental save, without needing a separate backup.

title: [Feature Request] Persistent undo history across sessions (opt-in)
author: ravenmyrrdin
body:
### [Feature Request] Persistent undo history across sessions (opt-in)

**Problem**
Undo already works after saving, which is great, but the history is lost as soon as the document is closed. Reopening a file the next day means mistakes can no longer be undone step by step.

**Proposal**
An opt-in preference "Keep undo history after closing". When enabled:
- the history is stored as a sidecar in the app data folder (not inside the PDF), keyed on a hash of the file
- on reopen, if the file is byte-identical to what was saved, the history is restored and the Edit menu shows the named steps as usual
- if the file changed outside PdfCraft, the history is discarded with a short notice
- a configurable limit (number of steps or days) and a "Clear stored history" button

**Privacy and security**
- off by default, since the history may contain text that was removed (e.g. redactions)
- never stored for encrypted documents, or stored encrypted with the document's key
- redaction steps are never kept, so redacted content cannot be recovered from the sidecar

**Use case**
Long editing jobs spread over several days (forms, page organisation, comments), where you notice a mistake only after reopening.

title: [Feature Request] Watched folders: run a saved action on every PDF dropped into a folder
author: ravenmyrrdin
body:
### [Feature Request] Watched folders: run a saved action on every PDF dropped into a folder

**Problem**
`pdfcraft-cli run --script` already makes batch processing possible, but it has to be started by hand or with an external scheduler. Many offices need a "drop it in this folder and it gets processed" workflow, fully offline.

**Proposal**
A `pdfcraft-cli watch` command (and later a GUI page) that links a folder to a JSON script:

    pdfcraft-cli watch --in ./scans --script ocr-and-protect.json --out ./done --errors ./failed

- waits until a file is fully written (size stable for N seconds) before processing
- moves the original to `--out` or `--errors`, never deletes it
- writes a log line per file (time, steps, result)
- respects `--root`, so it cannot read or write outside the given folders
- can run as a background service (systemd unit / Windows service example in the docs)

**Example scripts**
OCR + reduce file size; add Bates numbers; apply password protection; combine everything in the folder once per hour.

**Use case**
Scan stations in hospitals and small offices where documents must be processed automatically but must never leave the local network.

Related: #885 (marker-based splitting), which would fit well as a step in such a script.

I would like to suggest implementing a reading tracking cursor in PDFCraft that allows users to visually identify the word they are currently reading and move forward or backward through the text using the keyboard arrow keys.

The idea is to introduce a visual indicator that highlights the current word and allows users to navigate sequentially through the document using the ← and → keys. This would make it easier to follow the text without constantly having to reposition their gaze or use the mouse to find their place.

title: Export, OCR and print have no per-page time limit (the viewer's render pool has one)
author: oracola91
body:
The viewer renders through `RenderPool`, whose watchdog gives up on a page after `STUCK_AFTER` (20 s): it sets the interpreter's `cancelled` flag, so the page stops at its next operator, and later requests for that page get the error at once (`crates/render/src/raster.rs`).

`PageRenderer` builds its `InterpreterSettings` from `config.settings()` with no `cancelled` flag and no time limit, so a page renders until it finishes. Many paths use it:

- export (`crates/engine/src/export.rs`)
- OCR (`crates/engine/src/ocr.rs`)
- print (`crates/engine/src/print_raster.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/print_ui.rs`)
- compare, word count, text preview, signature images, the redaction and zoom previews, accessibility, the CLI and the automation tools

So a page the viewer gives up on after 20 s can keep an export, an OCR run or a print job busy for as long as it takes, and I found no cancel or time limit in `export.rs`, `ocr.rs` or `print_raster.rs`.

The shape is a design choice, so asking before sending a PR:

1. **A time limit on `PageRenderer`** (in `RenderConfig`, off by default or the same 20 s): a timer sets the same `cancelled` flag the pool uses, and `render` returns the error the pool gives. Small, since the interpreter already checks the flag.
2. **Route these callers through `RenderPool`**, so they share its watchdog and its memory of pages it gave up on.
3. **A cancel flag per operation**, so export, OCR and print can offer Cancel inside a page, with or without a time limit.

Which would you prefer, and should the CLI and automation tools get a limit too (perhaps a flag)? Happy to send the PR.

title: Web build: report the open document in the viewport title

body:
The web build sends no `ViewportCommand::Title` naming the open document (eframe would log it as `Unhandled egui viewport command: Title(…)` on the web). WordCraft, GridCraft, PhotoCraft and VectorCraft do (`<document>[ •] — <App>`).

title: Remove Hidden Information ▸ Hidden text deletes a `7 Tr` title that is used as a clip, so the fill drawn through its letters floods the whole box (redact `interp.rs` hidden-text rule)

body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

Remove Hidden Information ▸ **Hidden text** (`doc_remove_hidden` with `hidden-text`; also Sanitize Document and the Optimizer's `discard`, which call the same `sanitize::remove_hidden`) treats every glyph in text rendering mode 7 as hidden text and deletes it. Mode 7 is "Add text to path for clipping": the glyphs draw nothing themselves, but they become the clipping path for whatever is painted after them until the `Q`. A title drawn as `7 Tr` and then filled with a colour, image or shading is visible text: the user sees the fill through the letter shapes.

Deleting those glyphs leaves an empty clip-mode text object. With no glyphs shown, no clip is set, so the fill that was confined to the letters now **paints its whole rectangle**. The title disappears and a solid red box takes its place. MuPDF draws the sanitized file the same way, so the damage is in the saved file, not in PdfCraft's renderer.

`doc_hidden_info` already reports these glyphs under "Hidden text" (27 on the file below: the 9 glyphs of each of pages 1–3), so the dialog offers to remove the visible title along with the genuinely hidden text.

This is the same flood as #3123 (Edit text and redaction of a `7 Tr`/`4 Tr` title), reached through a third entry point. Mode 4 (fill **and** clip) is not affected here, because the hidden-text rule only matches 3 and 7.

The redaction interpreter walks into form XObjects at most 12 levels deep. When Apply meets a form at the 13th level, it does not refuse and does not leave the form alone: it **removes the form from the page**, whether or not anything in it was under a mark. Everything that form draws is gone from the saved file.

So one mark over a word on the page itself deletes unrelated text drawn by a deeply nested form elsewhere on the page. The same page with the chain one level shorter keeps that text.

title: Find text and redact never finds text on a hidden layer, so a "redact every match" leaves the word in the saved file (`redact_mark` searches the renderer's visible text)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

Find text and redact (`redact_mark` with `find`, `words` or `pattern`, and the UI's search) searches the same text as Find: the text the renderer extracts. The renderer leaves out content on a layer (optional content group) that is OFF. So text on a hidden layer is **never found and never marked**.

A user who searches for `SECRET` to redact every occurrence gets the matches on visible pages, applies them, and saves. The saved file still holds `SECRET` on the hidden layer: in the content stream, in plain bytes, and on screen in any viewer as soon as the layer is turned on. The layer is still listed (`doc_info` → `layers: [{"name": "Reviewer notes", "visible": false}]`), so turning it on is one click in a Layers panel. On a page where the word is *only* on a hidden layer, the search answers "nothing matched, so nothing was marked", which reads as "the word isn't on this page".

Whether Find should look at hidden layers is a product choice. For redaction it is a privacy gap: the feature's promise is "every match on every page" (`parity/acrobat-features.toml`, `protect.search-and-redact`), and redaction exists to make sure a word is gone. A rectangle mark over the same area does remove the hidden text, because Apply walks the content without a visibility test; only the search misses it.

title: Redacting a box filled with a tiling pattern removes the fill but keeps the pattern, so the text its cell draws stays in the saved file (redact never touches `/Resources /Pattern`)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3), pdftotext (xpdf) 4.00

### What happens

A tiling pattern's cell is a content stream of its own, and it can draw anything, text included. When a page fills a shape with such a pattern, what the user sees inside the shape is the cell's drawing.

Redacting that shape removes the fill from the page's content, and the page looks right: a black box, nothing behind it. But the pattern itself is left alone. It stays in the page's `/Resources /Pattern`, the page still selects it as the fill colour (`/Pattern cs /P0 scn`), and its content stream, with the text that was under the mark, is written into the saved file unchanged. Anyone who reads the file's streams gets the word back. MuPDF extracts that word from the original page as text, so this is text a reader recognises, not just pixels.

Nothing in the apply notices: it succeeds with `applied: 1`. Its verify pass re-walks the page with the same interpreter, which doesn't enter pattern cells, and the engine's after-check reads the renderer's text, which doesn't include pattern-cell text (`text_find SECRET` → 0 on the original) **[test]**.

### Steps

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `pattern_text.pdf`: one 400 × 300 pt page that shows `PUBLIC`, then fills a box with a coloured tiling pattern whose cell draws `SECRET`, so `SECRET` shows inside the box:

```python
def pdf(path, objs):
    """objs[0] is object 1 (the catalog); the xref is computed here."""
    out, offs = bytearray(b"%PDF-1.7\n"), []
    for i, o in enumerate(objs):
        offs.append(len(out))

title: Pen tablet input is ignored on native Wayland (mouse works)
author: CHEESEGRATER45
body:
## Describe the bug

On Hyprland (Wayland), PdfCraft ignores input from my pen tablet. The mouse works normally. The same happens in VectorCraft 0.13.1 and ArtCraft Launcher 0.5.1.

PhotoCraft, WordCraft, DeckCraft and GridCraft all work fine with the same pen on the same system, so the tablet and desktop setup seem OK.

## To reproduce

1. Start PdfCraft normally on a Wayland session.
2. Hover and tap with a pen tablet (not a mouse).
3. The pen does nothing in the app.

## Expected behavior

The pen moves the cursor and clicks, like it does in the other Craft apps.

## Environment

- PdfCraft 0.9.0 (AppImage x86_64)
- Arch Linux, kernel 7.2.11
- Hyprland 0.56.2 (Wayland)
- GPU: Intel RPL-P, Vulkan (wgpu renderer)
- Tablet: Wacom One Pen Tablet Medium (USB 0531:0102)

## What I checked

- `hyprctl devices` lists the Wacom under Tablets.
- `evtest` on the pen device shows ABS_PRESSURE (0-4095), ABS_TILT_X/Y, BTN_TOOL_PEN, so the kernel side is fine.
- Starting the app with `env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (so winit uses X11/XWayland) made the pen work in one test. The log then shows `winit::platform_impl::linux::x11`.

So I suspect native Wayland tablet/pen events (zwp_tablet_v2 / winit) aren't handled in this app, but I haven't looked at the code, so I could be wrong.

## Additional context

Also reported in the #pdfcraft channel on Discord. Happy to test a fix or attach logs (`~/.local/share/pdfcraft/logs/pdfcraft.log`) if useful.

body:
PdfCraft does not correctly handle Command+V when using the macOS built-in "Dvorak – QWERTY ⌘" keyboard layout.

When attempting to paste text into an editable PDF form field, Command+V opens PdfCraft's command palette instead of pasting.

- Copy text from another application.
- Open a PDF with an editable text form field in PdfCraft.

- Observe that the command palette opens rather than pasting text.
- Switch the keyboard layout to "U.S." and repeat.

**Expected behavior**
PdfCraft should honor macOS keyboard layout mappings, including the Dvorak – QWERTY ⌘ layout, so standard Command shortcuts work regardless of the selected input source.

Command+V is incorrectly interpreted as a shortcut to open the command palette.

Keyboard layout: Dvorak – QWERTY ⌘
Application: PdfCraft
Version: 0.7.1

Export to Word, HTML (and RTF and PowerPoint, which take the same list of items) puts a page's text blocks in order of their top edge, then their left edge. That isn't reading order whenever the text doesn't run in rows across the page:

title: The checker's Character encoding rule fails an Identity-H font whose CIDFont uses an Adobe character collection (Adobe-Japan1, GB1, CNS1, Korea1, KR), though ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2 maps it to Unicode
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `ec0a9650` (the same code in 0.10.0, `6fb6b7cf`) · Windows 11 x64 · oracles: pikepdf 10.17 (qpdf), MuPDF 1.27.2 (PyMuPDF 1.27.2.3)

### What happens

The Accessibility Checker's **Character encoding** rule accepts a Type 0 font without `/ToUnicode` only when its encoding is *not* Identity **and** its CIDFont uses one of the Adobe character collections. ISO 32000-2 §9.10.2 accepts it when it uses a predefined CMap other than Identity **or** its CIDFont uses one of those collections. So an `Identity-H` font over Adobe-Japan1 (and GB1, CNS1, Korea1, KR) is reported as "doesn't map its characters to Unicode". PdfCraft's own text extraction reads the text of the same font.

### Steps

body:
**Version:** PdfCraft `main` at `6fb6b7cf` (0.10.0), desktop app, Windows 11.

### What happens

On a two-column page, dragging to select text follows the renderer's block order, not the columns. Blocks come out paragraph by paragraph, alternating between the columns: L1, R1, L2, R2, …. So:

- A drag from one paragraph to the next **inside the left column** also selects the whole paragraph beside it in the right column.
- A drag from the bottom of the left column to the top of the right column, which is how a reader continues, selects the middle of the page instead.

Copy (Ctrl+C) puts exactly the selected text on the clipboard. The result is the same at 50%, 100%, 200% and 400% zoom. The page is tagged, and its structure tree reads the left column first, then the right one.

The bot on #3658 asked for "Copy from a selection" to get its own ticket, so this is that ticket, with the drags measured. The cause looks shared with #3658 (rule 3 of the renderer's reading order). The page shape differs: here every paragraph gap matters, not only one.

1. Save this as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `cols.pdf` (three paragraphs per column, at the same heights) and `cols-gap.pdf` (the left column's second paragraph starts below the right column's first one).

title: [Bug Report] [PdfCraft] Windows: Certisign desktopID KSP reports wrong size for Algorithm Group, so ICP-Brasil A3 certificates are marked "Unsupported key algorithm group"
author: fcdiass
body:
**PdfCraft:** 0.9.0, Windows 11 Pro 26200 (x64)
**Middleware:** Certisign desktopID 2.1.5.0 (`desktopID_Provider.dll` 2.1.4.1), registered both as a CSP (type 24) and as a CNG KSP
**Certificate:** ICP-Brasil RFB e-CPF A3, issuer AC Certisign RFB G5, RSA 2048

The certificate shows in the signing picker as unusable: *"its private key's algorithm couldn't be read: Unsupported key algorithm group"*.

The same certificate signs successfully on this PC in Adobe Acrobat (Reader) 26.002.22031 (64-bit) and Foxit PDF Reader 2025.2.0, entering the PIN through desktopID; Foxit validates the resulting signature as valid and the document as unmodified. They likely reach the key through the legacy CryptoAPI provider registered for it (ProviderType 24), so this shows the certificate and middleware work, not that desktopID's CNG path is otherwise sound.

The key opens fine through CNG: `CryptAcquireCertificatePrivateKey` with `CRYPT_ACQUIRE_ONLY_NCRYPT_KEY_FLAG | CRYPT_ACQUIRE_SILENT_FLAG` succeeds, and so does `NCryptOpenKey` on the provider directly. The problem is the provider's answer to `NCryptGetProperty(NCRYPT_ALGORITHM_GROUP_PROPERTY)`:

```
64-byte buffer -> rc=0, *pcbResult=3, bytes=52 00 53 00 41 00 00 00
```

It writes `"RSA\0"` (8 bytes) but reports 3, the character count instead of the byte count. `rustls-cng`'s `get_string_property` sizes its buffer from that value, so `algorithm_group()` doesn't get `"RSA"` and returns `UnsupportedKeyAlgorithmGroup`. For the record, `NCRYPT_LENGTH_PROPERTY` returns 2048 correctly, while `NCRYPT_ALGORITHM_PROPERTY` and `NCRYPT_PROVIDER_HANDLE_PROPERTY` return `NTE_NOT_SUPPORTED`.

This is a provider bug, but desktopID is common among Brazilian A3 users, and there's a workaround that needs no `unsafe`:
- in `matches_key` (`crates/sign/src/windows.rs`), when the algorithm group can't be read, fall back to the key type in the certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo (already parsed) and let a real mismatch surface at signing time;

title: /ActualText on a structure element is ignored for content inside a form XObject with /StructParents
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Follow-up to #3660 / #3689, from @mtlcl410's test report on #3689 (page E5).

## What happens
#3689 applies a structure element's `/ActualText` to the page's own marked content only (nesting depth 0). When the element's content is inside a form XObject that has a `/StructParents` entry, and the element reaches it through `<< /Type /MCR /Stm … /MCID n >>`, text extraction and Find still return the form's own glyph text (`f0rm`, not `form`).

## What the spec says
ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.4: `StructParents` "may appear … in the stream dictionary of a form or image XObject"; its value is the key of the entry for that object in the structural parent tree. The form dictionary's `StructParents` is "Required if the form XObject contains marked-content sequences that are structural content items" (Table 93). So a form's MCIDs index the parent tree entry under the form's own key, the same way the page's MCIDs index the entry under the page's key.

## Why #3689 stops at depth 0
The depth-0 rule keeps MCIDs from Type 3 glyphs, patterns, soft masks and annotation appearances out of the page's namespace. A fix should key replacements per content stream: the page's `/StructParents` at depth 0, and a form XObject's own `/StructParents` while that form is drawn, nested forms included. Anything without a key keeps its own text, as it does now.

Tagged generators often put whole paragraphs in forms, so this case is likely common.

## Done when
- Page E5 from the report reads `form` through `text_extract` and `text_find`.
- A form without `/StructParents`, an annotation appearance and a Type 3 glyph still keep their own text (`structure_replacement_text_stays_out_of_form_xobjects` and `…_annotation_appearances` keep passing).

title: Edit text merges table columns into one line; editing one word collapses the whole row (QuickBooks invoices)
author: rbachtold
body:
### What happens

QuickBooks Desktop invoices draw each table cell as its own text run, all on the same baseline. Edit text groups every run on that baseline into one line, across all four columns:

```
text_lines, page 1, line 38:
rect [88.56, 419.56, 584.64, 429.5]  CIDFont+F3  "Labor Remove Cabinets 150.00 150.00"
```

The runs start at x = 88.56 (Item Code), 174.0 (Description), and the right-aligned Price and Amount columns. The gaps between them are 60 to 300 points, far wider than a word space at 9 pt.

Changing one word rewrites the whole row as a single string, so every column after the edit moves left next to the first one.

In the app, clicking into the row also shows the text letter-spaced across the full table width while editing. After applying, the row is drawn in a wide substitute font instead of the embedded CIDFont+F3 subset.

### Steps (PdfCraft 0.9.0, Windows 10 Pro)

1. Open a QuickBooks Desktop invoice (fonts embedded as Type0 / Identity-H subsets).
2. Edit a PDF > Edit text, then click the word "Labor" in the Item Code column.
3. Change it to "Labor 2" and apply.

The same result from the CLI:

```
[{"tool":"doc_open","args":{"path":"invoice.pdf"}},
 {"tool":"text_edit","args":{"doc":1,"page":1,"line":38,"text":"Labor 2 Remove Cabinets 150.00 150.00"}},
 {"tool":"doc_save","args":{"doc":1,"path":"edited-line.pdf"}}]
```

### Expected

Only the "Labor" run changes. The other cells keep their positions and the embedded font, the way Acrobat edits one run in place.

### Possible direction

Split a visual line into separate lines (and paragraphs) where the gap between runs is much wider than the font's space width, so each table cell edits on its own. This may belong with the grouping work in #2508. #2718 looks like the same bug in an Excel-made PDF.

- Application: PdfCraft
- Version: 0.9.0
- Operating System: Windows
- Affected files: Valid unencrypted PDF 1.3 documents

This appears to be caused by PdfCraft's PDF parser/renderer being stricter than PDFium (used by Chromium browsers). Certain internal PDF-1.3 structures that are tolerated by other viewers cause PdfCraft to fail silently.

title: macOS print: jobs use the driver's default paper and tray, so the printer can hold them and nothing prints
author: thesilvjurado
body:
## Summary

On macOS, **Print** in PdfCraft says the job was sent, but nothing comes out. Preview prints the same file on the same printer.

PdfCraft sends jobs with `lp`, and CUPS fills in whatever the job doesn't specify from the queue's PPD defaults:

- **Paper:** 0.8.0 sends no paper size. 0.9.0 sends one for 7 sizes from the desktop dialog (#1583).
- **Tray:** no version sends a tray choice. The job always asks for the PPD's default tray.

On the queue below the defaults are **A4 from Tray 1**. Tray 1 is empty, so the printer holds the job ("Queued job needs resources. Tray 1 is empty."). CUPS marks the job *completed*, because LPD delivered it, so PdfCraft reports success.

Preview works because the macOS print dialog sends the selected paper and **Paper Feed: Auto Select**. Auto Select goes to CUPS as `AP_D_InputSlot` with an empty value, which suppresses the PPD's default tray, so the printer picks a tray that holds the paper.

**0.9.0 is still affected**: it fixes the paper size, but its jobs still ask for Tray 1 (see test 2 below).

## Environment

- PdfCraft 0.8.0 (macOS app). The code paths below were checked against `main` @ 22bedbf2.
- CUPS queue for a **Xerox AltaLink C8045**: Xerox macOS driver 5.19.1 (PPD with the `pstoxrps` filter), `lpd://` device URI.
- PPD defaults: `*DefaultPageSize: A4`, `*DefaultInputSlot: Tray1`. The PPD's `InputSlot` choices are Tray1–Tray6, with no `Auto`.
- Printer trays, read over IPP: Tray 1 = 11×17, **empty**; Tray 2 = Letter, empty; Trays 3–4 = Letter, full.

## Steps to reproduce

With a queue whose default tray is empty or holds the wrong paper:

```sh
lp -d <queue> -o media=Letter test.pdf                      # held at the printer (what 0.9.0 sends)
lp -d <queue> -o media=Letter -o AP_D_InputSlot= test.pdf   # prints
```

Or: open a Letter PDF in PdfCraft → Print → that printer → Print. PdfCraft and `lpstat` say the job was sent and completed, but nothing prints.

title: [Feature Request] Image layer ordering (bring to front / send to back) for selected images
author: archsueh
body:
### Feature Request

**Image layer ordering (bring to front / send to back) for selected images in "Edit text and images"**

When several images overlap on a page, the one drawn later in the content stream covers the earlier one. Acrobat Pro, PDF Studio and similar editors let you change that order: right-click a selected image → **Arrange → Bring to Front / Bring Forward / Send Backward / Send to Back**, with shortcuts (PDF Studio: `Ctrl+Shift+↑` for front, `Ctrl+↑` for forward, and the mirrored pair for back).

PdfCraft can select, move, resize, rotate, flip and crop an image, but there is no way to change which image is on top. The only workaround is to delete the image and add it again at the same place, which loses its edit history and does not help when the overlap is with content PdfCraft did not add.

**Requested behaviour**

- A context-menu entry (and a keyboard shortcut) on a selected image to move it to the front, one step forward, to the back, or one step backward within the page's drawing order.
- The same actions exposed to automation, so a script can reorder overlapping images.

### Evidence (checked against `main`)

- `crates/engine/src/lib.rs:73` — `enum ImageEdit` covers only `Move`, `Rotate`, `Flip`, `Crop`, `Replace`, `Delete`. There is no z-order variant.
- `crates/automation/src/lib.rs:500` — `image_edit` accepts `move`, `rotate`, `flip_horizontal`, `flip_vertical`, `crop`, `delete`, `replace`. No reorder action.
- `crates/engine/src/commands.rs` — no command for arranging an image's stacking order.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/commands.rs:18` — the document-view shortcuts are view/navigation keys; nothing for layer order.
- `docs/gaps.md:103` already lists **"vector and object editing; arrange and align"** as a gap against Acrobat Pro, so this is inside a known missing area.

### Impact

Overlapping images are common in practice (logos, stamps, watermarks placed over or under a figure, multi-layer scans). Without reorder, a user who brings an image …

author: Roro44G1
body:
**PdfCraft:** 0.9.0, Windows 11 x64 (MSI install)

### Summary
Romanian e-Factura invoices (generated by JasperReports 6.21.4 + OpenPDF 1.3.32, also after re-distilling with Acrobat Distiller 20) use a portrait MediaBox `[0 0 595 842]` with `/Rotate 90`, so all text is drawn turned inside the page. Editing text on these pages misbehaves:

1. **In the desktop app**, edit-text mode shows misplaced/overlapping boxes and characters rendered as solid black blocks.
2. **`text_edit` with Romanian comma-below letters** fails:
   `the BIZ UDPGothic fallback font has no glyph for U+021A` (also U+0219). The source fonts are non-embedded Helvetica / subset ArialMT, so the fallback is used, and it lacks ș ț Ș Ț — which are required for Romanian.
3. **Workaround attempt** — `text_font_import` of a full DejaVu Sans (OFL-compatible) succeeds, but `text_edit` with `font_resource` fails:
   `formatting part of turned text, or choosing a document font for it, isn't supported yet`

### Repro (CLI)
```json
[
  {"tool": "doc_open", "args": {"path": "efactura.pdf"}},
  {"tool": "text_edit", "args": {"doc": 1, "page": 1, "paragraph": 26, "text": "ASOCIAȚIA"}}
]
```
→ fallback glyph error. Adding `text_font_import` (DejaVuSans.ttf) + `"font_resource": "PCFull0"` → "turned text" error.
Editing with ASCII-only text works.

### Confirmation that rotation is the cause
After rewriting the pages to an unrotated landscape MediaBox `[0 0 842 595]` with `/Rotate 0` (contents wrapped in `q 0 -1 1 0 0 595 cm … Q`, visually identical), the same `text_font_import` + `text_edit` with `font_resource` works and ș/ț render correctly.

- Support document-font selection / partial formatting for turned text (pages with /Rotate or rotated CTM).
- Ship a fallback face covering Latin Extended-B comma-below letters (U+0218–U+021B), needed for Romanian.

When I drag an image file (PNG/JPEG/…) onto the PdfCraft window while a document is open, PdfCraft opens it as a **new tab/page** instead of placing it into the document I am editing. That is the same thing that happens when I drop a PDF.

title: Windows: taskbar and Alt+Tab show a generic icon instead of PdfCraft's
author: PyTech-be
body:
## What happens
On Windows, the running PdfCraft window shows a generic window icon in the taskbar and in Alt+Tab, instead of the PdfCraft lion icon. The title bar icon is correct.

## Cause
`native_options` in `apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs` sets the icon with `ViewportBuilder::with_icon`, which eframe passes to winit's `set_window_icon`. On Windows that only sets the small icon (`ICON_SMALL`, used by the title bar) — see `vendor/winit/src/platform_impl/windows/window.rs`. The taskbar and Alt+Tab use the big icon (`ICON_BIG`), which nobody sets.

VectorCraft had the same bug and fixed it in storytold/vectorcraft@b554330d.

## Fix
On Windows, when the app is created, set the big icon from the same 256 px PNG through winit's `WindowExtWindows::set_taskbar_icon` (`cc.winit_window()`). This needs `winit` as a Windows dependency of `apps/pdfcraft` (it is already in the tree, patched to `vendor/winit`). A PR follows on `fix/windows-taskbar-icon`.

title: Auto Tag doesn't work well for every type of pdf's
author: kishore04u
body:
1. Complex Layouts & Reading Order Multi-Column Text: It often reads straight across two columns like a single line, rather than down one column and then the next. Sidebars & Callouts: Text boxes get injected into the middle of unrelated sentences. 2. Tables Missing Borders: Tables without visible grid lines are often wrongly tagged as regular paragraphs. Complex Headers: Auto-tag cannot automatically map merged cells (colspan/rowspan) or assign table header tags () correctly. 3. Visual vs. Real Structure Fake Headings: Text made bold or large manually (without using formal Heading styles) is often tagged as plain paragraphs (

). Fake Lists: Lists typed using manual hyphens or numbers are tagged as individual sentences, breaking screen reader list navigation. 4. Scanned Pages & Math OCR Errors: Low-quality scans result in garbled text tags or skipped content. Math Formulas: Auto-tag breaks equations down into dozens of meaningless graphic figures instead of readable formulas. 5. Decorative Images It cannot distinguish decorative graphics from meaningful ones, often tagging background lines and shapes as Figures instead of hiding them as Artifacts. 6. Stripping Existing Tag Trees Completely Complete Loss of Authoring Intent: If a PDF already contains native structure from tools like Word or InDesign, deleting the existing tag tree strips out accurate semantic roles, reading order, and table headers. Running Auto-Tag on a blank slate forces Acrobat to guess everything from scratch based purely on visual appearance, usually yielding worse results than fixing the original tree.

title: [Feature Request] [PdfCraft] Feature Request: Add Regular Expression (RegEx) Support to Search and Replace
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

Description

It would be useful to support regular expressions (RegEx) in PdfCraft's existing search and replace functionality. This would allow users to find text based on patterns rather than only searching for literal words or phrases.

Proposed Functionality

Add an option to enable RegEx mode in the following operations:
Simple search
Search all
Simple replace
Replace all

When enabled, the search input should be interpreted as a regular expression. For replacement operations, capturing groups and backreferences should be supported where feasible.

Examples

invoice\s+\d+ matches invoice 123 and invoice 456.
\b[A-Z]{2}\d{4}\b matches identifiers such as AB1234.
(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2}) matches dates in YYYY-MM-DD format and allows their components to be reused in a replacement.

Expected Behaviour

Provide a toggle or checkbox to enable RegEx mode.
Validate expressions and display a helpful error message when a pattern is invalid.
Apply the same matching rules consistently across search and replace operations.
Preserve document formatting and unrelated text as much as possible when replacing matches.
Ensure replace-all operations clearly report the number of replacements made.

Expected Benefits

RegEx support would make it easier to locate structured data, identifiers, dates, and recurring text patterns, as well as perform more flexible bulk replacements.

Additional Notes

RegEx mode should be optional so that existing literal search and replace behaviour remains unchanged.

title: [Feature Request] [PdfCraft] Feature Request: Add Diacritic-Insensitive Search and Replace
author: ticket-craft
body:
### Description

Description

It would be useful to add an option to ignore diacritics when searching for or replacing text in PdfCraft.
This would allow users to find words regardless of whether accented characters are present, which is particularly helpful when working with multilingual documents.

Proposed Functionality

Add an option to ignore diacritics in the following operations:

Simple search
Search all
Simple replace
Replace all

When enabled, accented and unaccented versions of otherwise equivalent characters should match.

Examples

Searching for cafe should also find café.
Searching for resume should also find résumé.
Searching for uber should also find über.
The feature should work with Unicode text and support common diacritics across different languages.

Expected Behaviour

Provide a toggle or checkbox to enable diacritic-insensitive matching.
Keep the option disabled by default unless the existing search design suggests otherwise.
Preserve the original document text unless the user explicitly replaces a match.
Ensure replacement targets the correct character range, even when normalized text differs in length from the original.
Allow diacritic-insensitive matching to be combined with RegEx mode where technically feasible.

Expected Benefits

This feature would make searching and replacing more reliable in multilingual documents and reduce the need to try multiple spellings of the same word.

Additional Notes

Ignoring diacritics should affect text matching only. It should not automatically remove accents from the PDF or alter text that has not been selected for replacement.

The destination dictionary should be written using standard PDF `/XYZ` syntax: ```text [ page_ref /XYZ left top zoom ] 4. Tools like Foxit PDF Editor record the viewport coordinate automatically on bookmark creation, allowing granular, item-by-item navigation without requiring manual scrolling after every jump. title: [Bug / Feature Request]: "Continuous Scroll" (Rolagem contínua) view setting does not persist across application restarts (v0.10.1)
author: rezendepauloh
body: ### Description In PDFCraft v0.10.1, the page display option **"Continuous Scroll"** (localized as *"Rolagem contínua"*) does not persist in the application configuration or user session state. Every time PDFCraft is closed and reopened—or when a new document is loaded—the viewer reverts to the default non-continuous display mode (single page without vertical scrolling). As a result, the user is required to manually open the bottom/context display menu and check "Continuous Scroll" every single session. --- ### Steps to Reproduce 1. title: Feature Request: Option to toggle Middle Mouse Button behavior from Hand/Pan to standard Auto-Scroll
author: AhmadHossam2002
body:
**Description**

Currently, holding or clicking the middle mouse button (scroll wheel click) in PdfCraft hardcodes the cursor to the Hand/Pan tool to grab and drag the page.
For users accustomed to standard PDF viewers and web browsers, this overrides the expected Auto-Scroll functionality (where clicking the middle mouse button lets you scroll up and down smoothly by moving the mouse).
Because the hand tool behavior is hardcoded, it conflicts with universal navigation habits and makes document navigation clunky for those who rely heavily on auto-scroll.

**Proposed Solution:**

Please add a toggle setting in the application preferences (e.g., Settings > Navigation) that allows users to choose the default behavior for the middle mouse button:
• Option A: Hand / Pan Tool (Current Default)
• Option B: Standard Auto-Scroll / Browser Scroll

title: Feature Request: Advanced brush controls, smoothing, and shortcut improvements for Draw Tool
author: AhmadHossam2002
body:
**Description:**

To make the Draw Tool more efficient for annotation and freehand sketching, I would like to propose adding brush adjustments, stroke smoothing, and a flexible eraser shortcut. These features align the experience with standard design software (like Photoshop) and significantly speed up the workflow.

**Proposed Enhancements:**

1. Dynamic Brush Adjustments (Photoshop-style Hotkeys)

Allow users to dynamically resize and change the transparency of the brush on the fly using mouse shortcuts while the Draw Tool is active:
• Size Adjustment: Hold Alt + drag mouse left/right to decrease/increase brush size.
• Opacity/Transparency Adjustment: Hold Alt + drag mouse up/down (or a complementary shortcut) to change brush opacity.
• Visual Cue: Show a temporary on-screen preview circle reflecting the size and transparency while adjusting.

2. Stroke Smoothness / Stabilization Option

Add a "Smoothness" slider (0% to 100%) to the Draw Tool's settings panel.
• Lower settings allow for raw, precise tracking.
• Higher settings stabilize the stroke to eliminate shaky lines, creating clean, professional-looking curves.

3. Smart "E" Key Toggle / Hold Logic for Eraser

Update the E shortcut key to support dual-mode behavior:
• Tap E (Toggle): Pressing and releasing the key permanently switches the tool to the Eraser. Pressing it again (or tapping B) switches back to the Brush.
• Hold E (Temporary Switch): Holding down the E key temporarily switches to the Eraser. Releasing the key instantly reverts the tool back to the active Brush.

title: ui: the per-frame UI has no panic guard, so any UI panic closes the app with every tab
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
Neither `eframe::App::logic` nor `ui` runs under a panic guard. The guards only cover:
- command dispatch: [`commands.rs:104`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/commands.rs#L100-L112)
- pickers and file use: `pickers.rs:255/286`, `files.rs:468`
- the open worker: `open_worker.rs:145`

The panic hook in [`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs:175`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs#L175-L189) only logs.

These all run unguarded:
- dialog OK actions ([`dialogs.rs:1227-1394`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L1227-L1394))
- panel actions
- canvas gestures
- file-watch reloads
- the per-frame drawing code ([`lib.rs:2960`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L2960), [`lib.rs:3120`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L3120))

A panic in any of them ends the process, and every unsaved tab goes with it. Recovery autosave runs every 60 s (`recovery.rs:28`), so up to a minute of edits is lost. AGENTS.md §4 asks for a last-resort guard around this kind of code.

Related:
- `execute` returns `true` ("done") after a caught panic ([`commands.rs:108`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/commands.rs#L104-L111)).
- After a caught mid-command panic, `active` isn't re-validated, so the next frame's `self.views[i]` can panic again, this time unguarded.
- On wasm, panics abort, so none of the guards help there.

## Latent panics this would contain
- [`canvas.rs:5287-5293`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L5287-L5293): `texture_image` falls back to `ColorImage::from_rgba_prem…

title: compare: closing a compared snapshot tab in side-by-side view panics (index out of bounds)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
In side-by-side Compare, [`compare_ui.rs:337-358`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/compare_ui.rs#L337-L358) draws each half with `canvas::document_area(app, index, ..)`. That function can close the tab during the call: when the snapshot notice bar's **Close** was clicked, it runs `app.close_tab(i)` ([`canvas.rs:2383-2391`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L2380-L2392)).

Right after both halves are drawn, the code indexes `app.views[old]` and `app.views[new]` directly:
```rust
let offsets = [app.views[old].last_scroll, app.views[new].last_scroll];
```

## Steps
1. Open a signed PDF and choose **View signed version**. Snapshot tabs are pushed last (`sign_ui.rs:581, 630`).
2. Compare the original (old) with the snapshot (new), side by side.
3. Click **Close** on the right half's notice bar.

The next frame removes `views[new]`, and line 354 indexes past the end. The frame isn't guarded, so the app exits with every unsaved tab.

Closing the left half breaks too:
- If `old` is the last tab, line 354 panics the same way.
- Otherwise, the loop's second `document_area(app, new)` gets a shifted or out-of-range index.

## Suggested fix
Capture both `DocId`s before the loop. Resolve each index with `views.iter().position(|v| v.id == id)` before drawing each half and again after the loop, and `return` if either tab is gone.

## Test sketch
In kittest:
1. Open a.pdf and b.pdf.

title: ui: stale (page, index) comment state survives edits; Delete/Save then hit a different annotation (form widgets included)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
Several pieces of comment UI state store raw `/Annots` positions:
- `comments.selected`
- the inline `editing` state in the panel
- the composer's `ComposerKind::Edit(index)`

`DocView::document_changed` ([`canvas.rs:822-844`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L822-L844)) resets `panel_drag` and other view state, but none of these. Undo/redo clears `selected` only.

When **Delete** is pressed, [`comments.rs:1597-1600`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/comments.rs#L1597-L1601) emits `Edit::DeleteAnnotation { page, index }` without checking that the selection still exists. [`pdfcraft_annot::delete_annotation`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/annot/src/lib.rs#L1505-L1508) then deletes whatever sits at `/Annots[index]`, whatever its subtype. `set_contents` behaves the same way.

## Scenario
1. Select a comment at (p, 5).
2. Run any edit that shifts `/Annots` on that page: Apply Redactions, Flatten comments, Delete link, an Erase batch or Sanitize. The selection goes invisible.
3. Press **Delete**.

The annotation now at index 5 is removed. It may be a form field's widget or another reviewer's comment. The inline editor and composer can likewise write `SetAnnotationContents` into the wrong comment. The change can be undone, but it is silent and easily saved.

The same class of bug: `org_drag`, the Organize page drag ([`canvas.rs:5030`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/canvas.rs#L5030), drop at `:5213-5222`), holds page indices from before a change but isn't cleared in `document_changed`, unlike `panel_drag`. An undo while dragging moves pages by the old numbering.

## Suggested fix
- In `document_changed`, clear `comments.selected`, `editing`, `composer` and `gesture`, and `org_drag`.

title: ui: a file reload or OS "open" switches the document under an open dialog, so OK applies to the wrong document
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
Two things can change the active document while a modal dialog is open:
- [`file_watch.rs:382-388`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/file_watch.rs#L380-L389) reloads a clean document in place, keeping the same `DocId`, with no `modal_open()` check.
- [`lib.rs:3058`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs#L3056-L3060): `OsEvent::Open` calls `open_path` immediately, and `open_path` makes an already-open tab active (`lib.rs:1803-1804`). `startup_inbox` is gated on `modal_open()`, but this path is not. Native drag-and-drop takes the same route.

Most dialogs act on whatever is active when OK is pressed:
- Rotate, Number pages, Split, Apply redactions, Sanitize, Protect, Marks and Boxes all do ([`dialogs.rs:1289-1382`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/dialogs.rs#L1289-L1382)).
- Comment Properties' `PropsDraft` stores only `page`/`index` (`comment_props.rs:20-29`).

Only Replace Pages checks the target and generation (`still_pick_target`, `files.rs:449`).

## Scenarios
- **Reload under Comment Properties.** Comment Properties is open on a clean document that a LaTeX/Typst build or a sync client rewrites. The watcher reloads it, and OK restyles or unlocks annotation `(page, index)` of the new version, which may be a different comment.
- **OS open under Protect.** Rotate, Protect or Sanitize is open on A, and the user double-clicks B, which is already open. B becomes active under the dialog, and OK protects or sanitizes B.

## Suggested fix
- Defer `file_changed` reloads of the active document while `modal_open()` (set `disk_changed`).
- Queue `OsEvent::Open` paths until the modal closes, as `startup_inbox` does.
- Give every dialog draft a `(DocId, generation)` and check it with `still_pick_target` before applying.

- **Reload:** in the `f…

title: ui: comment text being typed does not count as unsaved work; close/quit/auto-reload discard it without asking
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
[`has_unsaved_work`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/editing.rs#L586-L595) counts `dirty`, `pending_edit`, blocked content, form drafts, `fill_text` and `line_editor`. It does not count:
- `comments.composer` text (a new note, callout or caret)
- `comments.reply`
- `comments.editing` (an inline edit of a card)
- `comments.add_box`

## Steps
1. On a clean document, type a long reply in the Comments panel.
2. Press Ctrl+W, close the window, or let a sync client touch the file. Touching the file triggers `file_changed`, then `reload_view`, then `document_replaced`, which builds a fresh `DocView`.

The typed text disappears, with no prompt and nothing in recovery.

## Suggested fix
```diff
     || v.line_editor.as_ref().map_or_else(|| false, |ed| ed.has_unsaved_text())
+    || v.comments.composer.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| !c.text.trim().is_empty())
+    || !v.comments.reply.trim().is_empty()
+    || v.comments.editing.as_ref().is_some_and(|(_, _, t)| !t.trim().is_empty())
+    || !v.comments.add_box.trim().is_empty()
```
The save prompt's **Save** path should also commit those drafts, as `save_then` already does for form typing.

## Test sketch
Open a clean fixture, set `views[0].comments.reply = "draft"` and call `request_close_tab(0)`. Assert a close request is raised and the tab stays open.

title: ui: export / Action Wizard / OCR workers never report a panic or a failed spawn, so progress sticks forever
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
Several background jobs are started with `std::thread::Builder::new()...spawn(work).ok()` and the closure isn't guarded:
- Export: [`export_ui.rs:257`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/export_ui.rs#L257)
- Action Wizard: [`actions_ui.rs:133`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/actions_ui.rs#L133)
- OCR: `ocr_ui.rs:188` and `ocr_ui.rs:274`. #1819 covers the spawn failure; this adds the panic case.

If the thread can't be spawned, or the work panics, the result is never set:
- `poll_export` keeps posting "Exporting… k of N" and repainting every 200 ms.
- The OCR and Action Wizard runs never clear, so every later attempt is refused with "already running" until restart.

Possible panic sources:
- Export runs `Document::open_with_password` and `pdfcraft_create::extract_images` (`engine/src/export.rs:46-49`) outside any guard. The engine wraps the same open in `catch_unwind` elsewhere.
- OCR runs third-party `ocrs` inference unguarded.

Optimize (`optimize_ui.rs:337-368`) and word count already handle both cases, and are a model for the fix.

## Suggested fix
- Wrap each `work` body in `pdfcraft_engine::guard`, and always set a result or error.
- If the spawn returns `Err`, clear the run state and notify the user.
- Treat a disconnected channel as a failure.

## Test sketch
Inject a panicking `work` (or a status left as if the thread died) and poll. Assert the run state is cleared and an error toast is shown.

title: ui: long-running work on the UI thread (Compare, OCR start, Find-and-Redact, label print preview, Combine conflict preview)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
Each of these runs synchronously on the UI thread and can leave the window "Not responding" on large or heavy documents. Users then tend to force-quit and lose unsaved tabs.

- **Compare.** [`compare_ui.rs:167-205`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/compare_ui.rs#L167-L205): `run_compare` text-extracts every page of both documents and rasterizes every page pair. The overlap test at `:180-186` and `:196-201` checks every visual region against all text marks of **all** pages, which is O(n·m).
- **OCR start.** [`engine/src/ocr.rs:173-189`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/engine/src/ocr.rs#L173-L189): `ocr_job` calls `pages.contains(&p)` on a `Vec` for each page, which is O(pages²) for "All pages", and parses every page's images before the worker starts. It is called from `ocr_ui.rs:168`.
- **Find-and-Redact.** [`redact_ui.rs:299-333`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/redact_ui.rs#L299-L333): extracts every page's text in the click handler and creates one `AddAnnotation` per hit, with no limit, in a single batch.
- **Label print preview.** [`print_ui.rs:335-373`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/print_ui.rs#L335-L373): renders up to 50 pages each time the page range changes, so on every keystroke.
- **Combine conflict preview.** [`combine_ui.rs:270-288`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/combine_ui.rs#L270-L288): the cache key is order-sensitive, so every reorder re-opens every listed PDF.

## Suggested fix
- Move this work to workers with progress and cancel, keyed by `edit_generation()` as word count does.
- In Compare, bucket the marks by page before the overlap test.
- In `ocr_job`, use a `HashSet` or `Vec<bool>` for the pag…

title: engine: "Convert to PDF/A" removes encryption with only the modify permission
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
`check_permission` puts `Edit::ConvertPdfA` in the group gated by `p.modify()` (around [`engine/src/lib.rs:2222`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L2170-L2232)). Protect and Remove Protection, by contrast, require `unrestricted(p)`.

The conversion itself, [`preflight::convert`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/preflight/src/lib.rs#L654-L660), starts with:
```rust
if doc.trailer().get(b"Encrypt").is_some() { doc.remove_encryption(); fixed.push("Removed encryption".into()); }
```

## Scenario
A document is opened with the **user** password. The owner allowed modify but forbade printing and copying. Convert to PDF/A, then Save, writes an unencrypted copy with no restrictions.

That is the "change security" action the engine otherwise reserves for the owner. PDF permissions are advisory (see also #2465), so this is a consistency issue rather than a hard boundary, but the engine's policy should agree with itself.

## Suggested fix
Require `unrestricted(p)` for `ConvertPdfA` when the document is encrypted. Alternatively, have `preflight::convert` return an error when `doc.permissions().is_some_and(|p| !p.owner)`.

## Test sketch
Use an R6 document with user password "u", owner password "o" and `/P` allowing modify only. Open it with "u", apply `ConvertPdfA` and expect `NotPermitted`.

title: control: on Windows the --control token file is not owner-only, and the CLI doesn't check its owner
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
- [`apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs:507-513`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/apps/pdfcraft/src/main.rs#L500-L515) restricts the staged control file only on Unix, with `#[cfg(unix)] opts.mode(0o600)`. On Windows the file inherits its folder's DACL, although the doc comment (`:488`), README and AGENTS.md §3 promise an "owner-only file".
- [`apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/main.rs:1052-1063`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/apps/pdfcraft-cli/src/main.rs#L1050-L1065): the owner and mode check is also `#[cfg(unix)]` only.

## Scenario
`pdfcraft --control C:\pc\ctl.json`. Folders created at a drive root inherit *Authenticated Users: Modify*, and so do `C:\Users\Public` and `C:\ProgramData`. Also, `~` is not expanded in cmd.exe, so the README's `~/.pdfcraft-control.json` example becomes a relative path. Another local user can then read the token and drive the app:
- `ui.open` of any path
- save and export commands
- typing
- screenshots of open documents

In the other direction, a file planted in a shared folder makes the CLI send commands to another user's listener, with no check on Windows.

## Suggested fix
- Create the file with an explicit DACL (owner, plus SYSTEM), or refuse folders whose DACL grants read access to other principals.
- In the CLI, compare the file owner's SID with the current user's.

## Test sketch
Create the control file in a temp folder whose DACL grants `Users:R`. Assert the resulting file DACL has no ACE for any SID other than the owner and SYSTEM.

title: recovery: a recovery sidecar's "path" is trusted as the save destination
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
[`recovery.rs:213-215`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/recovery.rs#L205-L220) deserializes the sidecar JSON and checks only `key`. [`recovery.rs:373-376`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/ui-egui/src/recovery.rs#L370-L378) then calls `mark_recovered(id, meta.path.clone())`, and the next Save writes to `meta.path`. The sidecar is also read with an uncapped `std::fs::read`.

## Scenario
Someone who can write the recovery folder plants `<key>.pdf` and `<key>.json` with `"path"` naming any file the user can write. The user clicks **Recover**, then Ctrl+S, and that file is overwritten with no Save As prompt.

The folder is per-user and `0700` on Unix, so this mostly matters for portable mode (`portable.rs:65-94`, `<exe dir>/PdfCraftData/Recovery`, for example on a shared drive). There the folder gets no permission tightening on Windows. Severity is low.

## Suggested fix
- Treat `meta.path` as a hint: make the first save after recovery a Save As prefilled with it, or require that a regular file already exists there and confirm before writing.
- Cap the sidecar read, e.g. `take(64 KiB)`.

title: mcp: resources/* run outside the panic guard; unbounded line reads; a non-UTF-8 line ends the server
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
- [`mcp.rs:119`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/automation/src/mcp.rs#L115-L125): only `tools/call` goes through `guarded_tool`. `resources/read` (`:414-469`) calls `doc_info`, `doc_inspect`, `text_extract`, `page_render` and `command_list` directly. Render and text extraction catch panics internally, but `doc_info` and `doc_inspect` do not, so a panic there ends the server and the session's unsaved edits.
- [`mcp.rs:87-88`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/automation/src/mcp.rs#L85-L90): `input.lines()` has no length cap. A non-UTF-8 line makes `line?` return an error, and `serve` exits.
- Most tools read agent-named files with an uncapped `std::fs::read` (e.g. `lib.rs:894`, `:1517`). `doc_batch` (512 MiB), fonts and GoToR reads are capped.

## Suggested fix
- Wrap all of `dispatch` in `guarded_tool`.
- Reuse the `read_line_limited` pattern from `ui-egui/src/control.rs:1047`.
- Answer an undecodable line with `PARSE_ERROR` and keep serving.
- Cap tool file reads the way `doc_batch` does.

## Test sketch
- Send the server `b"\xff\n"` followed by a valid `initialize`, and assert the second request gets a reply.
- Send a 64 MiB line and assert an error reply, with bounded memory.

title: engine: undo/redo swap state and then refresh unguarded, with no rollback on panic
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
`apply` runs its refresh under `guard` and rolls back on a panic ([`engine/src/lib.rs:3791-3806`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L3791-L3806)). Undo/redo ([`:3831-3858`](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/blob/416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f/crates/engine/src/lib.rs#L3831-L3858)) swap `editor.cos`/`keys` and then call `refresh_scoped` unguarded, with only `inspect_err`.

If the re-inspect panics after an undo, the UI command guard (`ui-egui/src/commands.rs:104`) or the MCP guard catches it. The editor state is then swapped while the renderer and `info` still show the old state, and `show_released` is never called.

## Suggested fix
Wrap the refresh in `guard(...)`, and on a panic swap back the same way `apply` does.

## Test sketch
Add a `#[cfg(test)]` panic-injection hook in the refresh. Call `undo()` and assert `Err`, and that `cos` and `info` are unchanged.

title: forms: values typed into Password-flag fields are stored in /V and the saved file
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
Typing into a text field with the Password flag goes through `forms_ui.rs:236-242` (`draft_edit`), then `Edit::SetFieldValue`, then `forms::set_value`, like any other field. The only uses of `flags::PASSWORD` in `crates/forms` are appearance masking (`appearance.rs:447`, `:508`) and authoring (`author.rs:968`).

So the value ends up in plain text in:
- `/V`
- the undo history
- recovery snapshots
- incremental revisions of the saved file

ISO 32000 (§12.7.5.3, Password flag) says the value of such a field should not be stored in the PDF file.

## Suggested fix
Keep the typed value in memory, for scripts and submission, but don't write `/V` for `PASSWORD` fields, or strip it at save time. Check recovery snapshots too.

## Test sketch
Fill a Password field with `hunter2` and save. Assert the saved bytes, decompressed, don't contain `hunter2`.

title: deps: cargo deny fails on RUSTSEC-2026-0382 / RUSTSEC-2026-0383 (rustls-webpki, webpki-root-certs)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
`cargo deny check` (and `cargo audit`) currently fail on two advisories:

| Advisory | Crate | Fixed in |
|---|---|---|
| RUSTSEC-2026-0382 | `rustls-webpki 0.103.15` | `>=0.103.16, <0.104.0-alpha.1` |
| RUSTSEC-2026-0383 | `webpki-root-certs 1.0.9` | `>=1.0.10` |

Both reach the tree only through `winprint`'s **build-dependencies** (craft-print → winprint → reqwest → rustls). The pinned winprint `build.rs` downloads anything only under its `pdfium` feature, which craft-print leaves off. So shipped binaries aren't affected, but the CI `deny` job is red.

## Suggested fix
```
cargo update -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-root-certs
```

Unrelated note: `rsa` is pinned to a release candidate (`0.10.0-rc.18`). Its RUSTSEC-2023-0071 ignore is justified, because it is used only for public-key operations.

title: hardening: key material and passwords are never zeroized
author: PierrunoYT
body:
## Summary
Nothing in the workspace wipes key material or passwords:
- **Signing keys:** PKCS#8 private keys (`sign/src/keys.rs:564`), decrypted PKCS#12 bags, and the generated P-256 scalar (`keys.rs:665`).
- **Encryption:** the crypt file key, and `recovered_user`, the plaintext user password (`crypt/src/lib.rs:140, 202`).
- **UI drafts:**
  - `protect_draft` keeps the typed password after Cancel or a failed apply (`dialogs.rs:1005`). It is reset only the next time the dialog opens.
  - `finish_signing` clones the whole `SignDraft`, password included.

`zeroize` is already in `Cargo.lock`.

## Suggested fix
- Use `Zeroizing<Vec<u8>>` and `Zeroizing<String>` for private keys, file keys and password buffers.
- Reset `protect_draft` on Cancel.
- Avoid cloning drafts that hold passwords.

title: Small correctness items (OCR size math, update URL check, Remove Hidden count, Reopen Closed Tab, remote GoTo tabs, Combine list drag)

title: [Bug] White text-selection I-beam cursor invisible on white PDF pages in Read and Edit modes
author: mike-elio
body:
## Description
When hovering the mouse over text on a white PDF page, the pointer changes to the text-selection I-beam cursor, but the cursor appears white or extremely light. It has insufficient contrast against the white page and becomes very difficult to see.

This happens **without clicking** on the text, and occurs in **both Read and Edit modes**.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Launch PdfCraft on Windows 11.
2. Open a PDF containing selectable text on a white page.
3. Switch to **Read** mode.
4. Move the mouse over text without clicking.
5. Observe the mouse pointer change to an almost invisible white I-beam.
6. Repeat in **Edit** mode.

## Actual behavior
The I-beam/text-selection mouse pointer is white (or too light) against the white PDF page, making it difficult to locate.

## Expected behavior
The text-selection pointer should have sufficient contrast (e.g., dark/black I-beam with a visible outline) against a white page. Ideally it should follow the OS cursor scheme or automatically adapt to the background.

## Troubleshooting already attempted
- Changed Windows 11 mouse pointer color/scheme.

title: Forms: exported form data (XFDF, FDF, XML, CSV, text) includes Password-flag field values in plain text
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft `main` at `41649514` (0.11.0), `pdfcraft-cli`, Windows 11.

### What happens

Exporting form data writes the values of fields with the Password flag in plain text, in every format: XFDF, FDF, XML, CSV and tab-delimited text. For XFA forms, the XML and XDP data exports carry the value of a `passwordEdit` field too.

This is a question rather than a clear bug. ISO 32000-2 says nothing about exports. The only text about these fields is §12.7.5.3, Table 231 (p. 540): typed characters "shall" be shown masked, and a note says PDF processors should "never store the value of the text field in the PDF file". I'm filing it so that #3926's follow-up (#3943, which keeps these values out of saved PDFs) doesn't leave the question unrecorded.

1. Save this as `repro.py` and run `python -I repro.py`. It writes `acro_password.pdf`, with a Password-flag field `pin` and a plain field `name`.

title: OCR: optional editable reconstruction for scanned PDFs
author: earlvanze
body:
## Request

Add an optional OCR output that reconstructs scanned PDF pages into editable PDF text and vector/image objects where practical, rather than retaining the scan image with an invisible text layer.

A PdfCraft community request described the desired outcome as similar to Acrobat ClearScan / Editable Text and Images.

Source: https://discord.com/channels/1359579021108842617/1558201586306650173/1562600274164457493

## Current behavior

PdfCraft OCR retains the scanned page image and adds an invisible text layer, making it searchable and selectable. That is useful, but it is not editable reconstruction.

## Proposed behavior

- Make this an opt-in output that preserves the original by default.
- Reconstruct recognized text as editable PDF text where feasible, with a clear policy for images, layout, fonts, reading order, and recognition uncertainty.
- Provide preview/review before replacing content and clearly warn about possible fidelity loss.

title: [Bug Report] Edit text shows garbled text (each character shifted by 29) when clicking a text box in a FrameMaker/Distiller 3.01 PDF
author: Jigsou
body:
## Description
In "Modify a PDF" > "Modify text and images", clicking into a text box of an existing paragraph replaces the correctly rendered text with garbled characters. The text looks fine on the page before the click, but as soon as the text box enters edit mode the editor shows a scrambled version of the same paragraph.

Example, from the legal notice paragraph near the start of the document:
- Rendered on the page: `Solid state equipment has operational characteristics differing from those of electromechanical equipment.`

Another example: the word `The` is shown as `7KH`.

Every character in the edit box is the expected character shifted by exactly 29 code points in the ASCII table: `S` (83) becomes `6` (54), `o` (111) becomes `R` (82), `T` (84) becomes `7` (55), `h` (104) becomes `K` (75), `e` (101) becomes `H` (72). This is not random corruption. It looks like the editor displays the glyph indices (or raw character codes) of an embedded TrueType subset font instead of mapping them to Unicode. This is a hypothesis from the pattern; I did not read the source code.

I did not save the document after seeing this. If the scrambled text were written back on save, the paragraph would be corrupted, so this may also be a data-loss risk.

title: Reduce File Size finishes, the native save dialog never opens, and the result is discarded without any message
author: TomTje
body:
## What happens

**Reduce File Size** runs to completion, but no save dialog ever appears, nothing is written, and the app shows no error, toast or notification. The optimized bytes are computed and then dropped.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Open a PDF.
2. **Create ▸ Reduce File Size**.
3. The progress bar runs through all images ("Optimizing… image N of M").
4. No save dialog appears. No file is written. Nothing tells the user what happened.

This is not specific to Reduce File Size: **every** action that ends in a native file dialog behaves the same way (e.g. **File ▸ Open**, **Save As**). The dialog simply never opens, and the work that asked for it is lost.

## Environment

- PdfCraft 0.11.0 (snap), Linux x86_64
- Ubuntu 24.04, XFCE on X11
- A large scanned document (~69 MB)

## Cause found on my machine

All native dialogs go through the XDG desktop portal (`rfd`, `xdg-portal` feature). On this machine the portal's GTK backend could not start:

```
$ systemctl --user status xdg-desktop-portal-gtk.service
× xdg-desktop-portal-gtk.service - Portal service (GTK/GNOME implementation)
     Active: failed (Result: exit-code) since …
  … xdg-desktop-portal-gtk[…]: cannot open display:
```

The reason was that the systemd **user manager** had no `DISPLAY` in its environment, so the service started without a display and died. With the portal working again, the same document reduces from 69.5 MB to 2.3 MB and the save dialog opens normally — so the optimizer itself was never the problem.

Workaround (import the session's `DISPLAY` into the user manager, then restart the portal):

```sh
systemctl --user import-environment DISPLAY XAUTHORITY
systemctl --user restart xdg-desktop-portal-gtk.service
systemctl --user restart xdg-desktop-portal.service
```

The import is lost when the user manager restarts, so this has to be re-applied after every login.

## What would help

1. **Tell the user.** When the native dialog cannot be shown, the app should say so instead of silently disc…

title: Windows: saved attachments do not get Mark-of-the-Web (Zone.Identifier)
author: 23z69rzihnk
body:
Context. We are evaluating PdfCraft (ArtCraft.PdfCraft 0.9.0 via winget) as a PDF reader on managed Windows clients. One of our threat scenarios is a PDF from an email that carries an embedded file.

Observation (at 88dad98). When a user saves an attachment ("Save" in the attachments panel, crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:1555), the bytes are written to the chosen path as-is. Nothing in the repository writes a Zone.Identifier alternate data stream or calls IAttachmentExecute. grep -rniE "Zone.Identifier|ZoneTransfer|IAttachmentExecute" finds nothing.

The file-name sanitizing from [storytold/pdfcraft#1114](https://github.com/storytold/pdfcraft/issues/1114) / #1630 (attachment_file_name, crates/ui-egui/src/files.rs:201) works well. It does not address the zone, though.

Why it matters. Windows and Office decide on trust from Mark-of-the-Web:

SmartScreen and the "Open File – Security Warning" prompt for .exe, .msi, .js, .hta, .lnk, …
Office Protected View, and the block on internet macros in .docm/.xlsm (enabled by default since 2022)
ISO/VHD/ZIP propagation of MotW to extracted files

A file saved from a PDF attachment is therefore treated as a local, trusted file. Acrobat, Edge, Outlook and 7-Zip all propagate MotW for this reason. The PDF itself usually carries MotW from the mail client or browser, so dropping it at the attachment boundary is a downgrade.

Suggested fix.

Windows: after writing an attachment, write the stream <path>:Zone.Identifier with [ZoneTransfer]\r\nZoneId=3\r\n. Better still, copy the zone of the source PDF when it has one (read <source>:Zone.Identifier, default to 3 when unknown). IAttachmentExecute::SetSource/Save is the official API and also triggers AV scanning, but a plain ADS write is enough and needs no unsafe.
Possibly the same for files written by "Open attachment" if they ever hit disk, and for exported images or files from untrusted documents.
A test that saves an attachment on Windows and asserts that the ADS exists.

The same applies …
