title: Signature validation: compare the signed revision's structure when classifying post-signing changes
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Hardening for signature validation's handling of changes made after signing. Full details were sent in a private vulnerability report.

Checked on `main` at 416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f.

The change classification in `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs` (around lines 1604-1662) decides which incremental-update changes a signature's DocMDP level allows. Suggested hardening:

- Compare the catalog root and the page set of the signed revision against the current revision, rather than classifying changed objects only by their type.
- Read the signature dictionary (`/ByteRange`, `/Contents`, `/Reference`) from the revision it signs, not from the latest revision.
- Apply the P=1 rules to any new signature fields and widgets.
- Add regression tests for incremental updates that change the root or page set after signing.

title: Redaction: remove every reference to redacted or deleted objects (structure tree, /CO, thumbnails, PieceInfo)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Hardening for redaction completeness. Full details were sent in a private vulnerability report.

Checked on `main` at 416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f.

Applying redaction (`crates/redact/src/lib.rs`, around lines 441-524) and deleting a form field (`crates/forms/src/author.rs`, around lines 1220-1262) should remove every reference to the removed objects. Suggested hardening:

- Call `drop_object_refs` (or an equivalent) for removed objects. That covers structure-tree `/OBJR` entries, the AcroForm `/CO` calculation order, page `/Thumb` thumbnails and `/PieceInfo` private data.
- Treat soft-mask groups, patterns and ExtGState `/Font` resources as content that redaction must sanitize.
- Add a test that redacts or deletes, saves, reopens, and asserts that no object anywhere in the file still refers to the removed content.

title: Protect: generate encryption keys and salts with getrandom instead of RandomState
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Hardening for how Protect generates encryption keys. Full details were sent in a private vulnerability report.

Checked on `main` at 416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f.

`entropy()` in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` (around lines 2294-2305) derives new file keys and salts by hashing with `std::collections::hash_map::RandomState`. `RandomState` is not a CSPRNG by contract, and how it is seeded depends on the target. Suggested hardening:

- Use `getrandom::fill` for keys, salts and generated owner passwords. `getrandom` is already in the tree, with `wasm_js`, through `sign` and `render`.
- Make Protect fail closed if no secure randomness is available.
- Add a test, on every target including wasm, that two fresh sessions protecting identical documents produce different salts.

title: JS sandbox: add a memory limit and check runtime-compiled source (eval/Function)
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Hardening for the JavaScript sandbox's resource limits.

Checked on `main` at 416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f.

The sandbox (`crates/js/src/lib.rs` around lines 1122-1125, and `crates/js/src/xfa.rs` around lines 1458-1462) limits loop iterations and recursion, but not memory. Boa allocates infallibly, so running out of memory aborts the process rather than returning an error, and `catch_unwind` cannot intercept that. Suggested hardening:

- Cap host-side copies (`strings()`, `println`/`alert`/`resetForm` output, the AcroForm `Outcome` vectors, the UI's `js_console`) by total bytes, as XFA already does with `MAX_ALERTS`/`MAX_CONSOLE`.
- Add a heap or growth limit in the vendored Boa that throws `RangeError`, or run scripts in a child process with a memory limit.
- Apply `refuse()` to runtime-compiled source through `HostHooks::ensure_can_compile_strings`, or disable `eval`/`Function`.
- Run the regression tests in a child process, since the current failure mode takes down the test binary.

title: Automation roots-only mode: refuse UNC/WebDAV/device paths before resolving them
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Hardening for path confinement when only `--automation-read-root`/`--automation-write-root` is set (roots-only mode).

Checked on `main` at 416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f.

`--root` mode refuses foreign shares before touching the filesystem (`foreign_share`, `crates/automation/src/lib.rs` around line 2108). Roots-only mode goes straight to `file_access::resolve` (around lines 125-152), which calls `std::fs::canonicalize`. Suggested hardening:

- Move the `foreign_share` / non-disk `Prefix` check into `file_access`, so both modes refuse UNC, WebDAV and device paths before any filesystem call. Return the same refusal text as for any other path outside the roots.
- Compare canonical path components exactly in the containment check (`file_access.rs` around lines 179-190), rather than with `to_lowercase()`. The drive letter can stay ASCII case-insensitive.
- Run the `tests/hostile_args.rs` loop under both confinement modes. Today it only runs with `--root`.

title: Release workflow: SHA-pin the reusable workflow that receives the signing secrets
author: PierrunoYT
body:
Hardening for the release workflow's supply chain.

Checked on `main` at 416495145354828a9efefc39df381ba3ee8f864f.

`.github/workflows/release.yml` (around lines 23-43) calls `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/release.yml@main` and passes it the code-signing secrets. Suggested hardening:

- Pin the reusable workflow to a commit SHA, and keep it updated with Dependabot or Renovate.
- Put the signing secrets behind a GitHub Environment with required reviewers.
- Require reviews and CODEOWNERS on `craft-common-actions` `main`.

Related CI hygiene items are tracked in #1114.

title: Feature request: add a document-level dark mode for PDF viewing
author: sagnikonly
body:
## Summary

PdfCraft currently supports a dark app theme, but there is no option to darken the PDF content itself while keeping the app chrome and surrounding UI unchanged.

This makes reading some PDFs in low-light conditions harder than it needs to be. A document-level dark mode would make the page background dark while preserving text contrast and readability, without forcing the entire app into dark mode.

## Problem

The app can switch to dark mode, but the PDF page rendering itself remains light. For users reading long PDFs at night, this can be uncomfortable and less readable.

## Proposed behavior

Add an option, likely in the viewer or read mode settings, to enable a PDF dark mode such as:

- a page-only dark layer or tinted rendering mode
- adjustable contrast / brightness for the rendered document
- an option to keep the app theme separate from the document theme

This should work in the main viewer without affecting document editing/export behavior.

## Expected outcome

Users should be able to turn on a dark reading mode for the document itself while keeping the surrounding app UI in the current theme.

## Notes

This request is based on the current behavior observed in the app: the app theme can be dark, but the PDF page content does not appear to have a separate dark rendering mode.

title: [Feature Request / WIP] Auto-convert MS Office documents to PDF during file merge (combine)
author: YusufMntm
body:
### Summary
Currently, combining files only supports existing PDFs and images. For users transitioning from Adobe Acrobat, an essential workflow is dragging and dropping Microsoft Office files (`.docx`, `.xlsx`, `.pptx`) directly into the merge queue and having them automatically converted to PDF in the background before merging.

### Proposed Approach
To maintain performance and keep core footprint minimal, I propose a system-level pre-processor bridge:
- **Windows:** Leverage local MS Office COM automation (if available) or fallback to headless LibreOffice (`soffice`).
- **Linux / macOS:** Utilize headless LibreOffice (`soffice --headless --convert-to pdf`).
- Graceful handling: Provide a clear notification if no conversion runtime is found in the environment rather than failing silently.

### Current Status
I have forked the repository and am actively working on an initial implementation (WIP) covering the CLI/engine conversion pipeline and file drop integration. 

I wanted to open this issue early to align with the core maintainers on the preferred architecture, dependencies, and PR acceptance criteria before submitting a pull request. Feedback is welcome!

title: XFA Engine does not handle Data Records
author: JDziurlaj
body:
Some XFA forms give you a record browser. The Data DOM holds multiple records, but the Form DOM only loads one of them at a time — the current record. The $dataWindow object controls which record is current. When the current record changes, all the fields that are bound relative to $record automatically update to show that record’s data. You don’t need a separate set of fields for every record; one set of fields is reused as the data window moves.

The attached for provides an example where:

- Loading a new photo creates (or fills) a new data record and then moves the data window to it.
- Previous / Next and the thumbnail buttons call xfa.dataWindow.gotoRecord(...).
- The big image and the detail panels are populated from $record (the current one).
- The five thumbnails are a small sliding window over the same list of records — they just read different indexes while the main form stays focused on the current record.

Records can be nominated through JavaScript/FormCalc code or declaratively (i.e. in the Configuration DOM). 

See XFA Specification v3.3, pp. 243-245 (General Case)
See XFA Specification v3.3, pp. 917-918 (Configuration DOM)

The concept of a record is not a special case, even a form with no explicit record partitioning has a $record (i.e. the entire Data DOM)

Current Behavior:

The form loads with error `Dynamic XFA form laid out from its template: 2 pages, 87 fields. title: Page with a very large image XObject (21600×14400, 1-bit) renders fully blank with no warning; same image at 10800×7200 renders
author: scottdube
body:
### Description

A single-page PDF whose only content is one large 1-bit image XObject renders as an all-white page in the app, in `pdfcraft-cli render`, and in the MCP `page_render`. `doc_info` reports no warnings or repairs. Poppler (`pdftoppm`, macOS Preview) renders the same file correctly.

The original file is a 36×24 in architectural site plan scanned at 600 dpi (21600×14400 px, CCITTFaxDecode G4, PDF 1.3). I rebuilt the same picture in several variants to isolate the cause; the pixel count is the only variable that matters:

| Variant | Image size | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Original, CCITT G4 | 21600×14400 | blank |
| Dimensions inlined, re-saved through poppler/cairo | 21600×14400 | blank |
| Same pixels as FlateDecode | 21600×14400 | blank |
| CCITT G4, downsampled | 10800×7200 | renders |
| CCITT G4 and FlateDecode, downsampled | 1800×1200 | renders |

So the threshold is somewhere between 78 Mpx and 311 Mpx, and it is codec-independent. A tell: `pdfcraft-cli render` reports `rendered page 1 at 10 dpi: 360×240 px in 0 ms` for the blank case and `284 ms` for the 10800×7200 case, so the image draw looks skipped rather than attempted and failed.

### Steps to reproduce

The script below writes two synthetic PDFs (no private content) with the same geometry: a 1-bit grid-and-diagonals pattern, FlateDecode, on a 36×24 in page.

```bash
python3 repro.py 21600 14400 big.pdf 600     # renders blank
python3 repro.py 10800 7200 ok.pdf 300       # renders
pdfcraft-cli render big.pdf --page 1 --dpi 10 --out big.png
pdfcraft-cli render ok.pdf  --page 1 --dpi 10 --out ok.png
```

`repro.py`:

```python
import sys, zlib
w, h, dst, dpi = int(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], float(sys.argv[4])
rb = (w + 7) // 8; grid = w // 12; pix = bytearray()
for y in range(h):

title: Forms JavaScript: a field's own AcroForm scripts can open the print dialog unasked
author: EricKaden
body:
## What happens

In an AcroForm form, a field's own scripts (keystroke, format, validate and calculate) run without the user asking for anything: as the user types, when a value is shown, when it's committed, and after any field a calculation reads changes. When one of them calls `this.print()`, its request reaches the app just like a button's, and the print dialog opens. So a calculate script that prints could open the dialog after every change.

Other requests are already held back in these cases:
- In XFA forms, only a click may print, open a link or open Save As (the `click_only` rule).
- In AcroForm forms, a script's `app.launchURL` goes through the link prompt before anything opens.

## Where

`crates/engine/src/js.rs`, `JsOutput::absorb`, passes every request from a field's script on to the app. #3580 drops a field script's side-panel and Save As requests there, with a line in the JavaScript console, and leaves Print as it is. This issue keeps that visible.

## Possible fix

Treat Print the same way: drop it from a field's own scripts, with a console line, and keep it for a button's Mouse Up script as now.

Found while reviewing #3580; thanks to @benandez for suggesting an issue.

title: [Feature Request] Please add official OpenCode skill support for PdfCraft
author: AHL8192
body:
Thanks for PdfCraft — PDF is the format where "it looked fine" is most expensive, so this skill is written defensively on purpose.

PdfCraft is one of those rare apps where the agent surface is a first-class citizen rather than a bolted-on API: 201 commands in 24 namespaces, 171 MCP tools (17 in `--compact` mode with `tool_search`), plus OCR, PDF/A, forms, redaction and printing. | Every session re-derives the workflow | Verified recipes to copy |

title: [Feature Request] Add Text Density / Contrast Enhancement Engine for Scanned Documents (similar to ReadEra Premium)
author: Bader-Idris
body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When opening old, scanned, or faded PDF books in PDFCraft, the fonts often look pixelated, thin, and difficult to read. Currently, PDFCraft renders these image-based documents exactly as they are scanned, without any post-processing tools to improve readability. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like to request a **Text Density / Contrast Enhancement slider** (or "Tensity" tool). This feature would dynamically adjust the darkness, weight, and contrast thresholds of image-based PDF text layers. It should artificially thicken thin, jagged, or faded fonts, forcing them to look deep, bold, and heavily "filled with ink" for a much better reading and editing experience.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Mobile e-readers already implement this beautifully. For example, the paid/premium version of **ReadEra** features a built-in contrast/weight engine that successfully thickens old, faded fonts to make them highly legible. Right now, to get the same effect in PDFCraft, users have to manually extract pages, run them through external AI image upscalers or online density changers, and re-import them, which disrupts the workflow.

**Additional context**
* **Target files:** Scanned image-only PDFs, historical books, and faded documents.
* **Expected UI:** A slider in the rendering or display settings labeled "Text Density," "Contrast Enhancement," or "Font Weight Adjustment."

title: Comments: Acrobat ignores the review statuses PdfCraft sets, and PdfCraft shows one status where Acrobat shows one per reviewer
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What happens

ISO 32000-2 §12.5.6.3 makes an annotation's state **per user**: a state reply's `T` "shall specify the user", and its `State`/`StateModel` "shall update the state of the original annotation for the specified user". It also says: "Additional state changes shall be made by adding text annotations in reply to the previous reply for a given user." PdfCraft doesn't follow this when it writes or reads states.

**Writing**
- Each status change PdfCraft writes points its `/IRT` at the comment. Per §12.5.6.3, a user's next change replies to **that user's previous state reply**.
- A state reply carries a state; it isn't a note (§12.5.6.3: "The state is not specified in the annotation itself but in a separate text annotation"). PdfCraft writes it with `/F 28` (Print, NoZoom, NoRotate) and without Hidden, so it can be shown as a stray note icon and listed as an ordinary reply. Writing it with the Hidden flag (Table 167, bit 2) keeps it a record of state.

**Reading**
- PdfCraft shows only the **latest status set by anyone**. Per §12.5.6.3 each user has their own state, so each reviewer's latest should show.
- A status set back to **None** removes the badge. None is a state of its own in Table 174 ("The user has indicated nothing about the change"), so a user who set it still has a state.
- **Marked** is per user too (Table 174: "The annotation has been marked by the user"), but PdfCraft shows any reviewer's checkmark as if it were the current user's.
- The Comments panel takes a comment's statuses only from replies whose `/IRT` names the comment (`replies_of` in `crates/ui-egui/src/comments_panel.rs`). A second change written as §12.5.6.3 requires replies to the first state reply, so the panel misses it and shows the earlier status. `comment_list` already follows the chain.

## Variants (synthetic files)

| replies on one comment | what §12.5.6.3 implies | PdfCraft today |
|---|---|---|
| Carol Completed; Bob Cancelled | two states, one per user | one badge (th…

title: App crashes on launch on Intel HD 4000 (Ivy Bridge) / Fixed by forcing dedicated NVIDIA GPU

body:
**Description:**

The crash happens when the app tries to initialize the GUI using the integrated **Intel HD Graphics 4000** on an older Ivy Bridge processor. 

I managed to fix it completely by right-clicking the executable and selecting **"Run with graphics processor" -> "High-performance NVIDIA processor"** (NVIDIA GeForce GT 720M). The app now opens instantly and works flawlessly. 

It seems the current `wgpu` or egui rendering backend is crashing due to outdated Intel legacy drivers on this specific hardware architecture.

- **CPU:** Intel Core i7-3537U @ 2.00GHz
- **Integrated GPU:** Intel HD Graphics 4000 (Driver Version: 10.18.10.4358)

title: audit: covered_text reports words painted outside the cover
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
Follow-up from CodeRabbit's outside-diff finding on #4109 (`crates/audit/src/lib.rs`, `is_cover` / `Budget::hidden_text`).

**Problem.** When a cover hides part of a text line, `covered_text` reports the whole line, including words painted outside the cover that stay visible. The finding itself (that a cover exists) is correct; only the reported text is too broad.

**Repro** (a test in `crates/audit/src/tests.rs`):

```rust
let content = b"0 g\nBT /F1 24 Tf 100 700 Td (SECRET) Tj ET\n98 688 94 32 re f\nBT /F1 24 Tf 200 700 Td (tail) Tj ET\n";
let findings = audit_redactions(&open(one_page(content, ""))).unwrap();
// today: ["SECRETtail"]; expected: ["SECRET"]
```

Before #4109 this cover was not found at all (`[]`), so #4109 is still an improvement. The over-report only affects covers that used to be missed.

**Why it needs more than an audit change.** `TextLine::ink` has one box per word, but there is no text per box. Runs get joined without a space (as in the repro), and ActualText, ligatures and bidi reordering change the text, so `ink[i]` cannot be matched to the `i`-th word of `text`. A correct fix needs `pdfcraft-edit::text_lines` to carry per-word (or per-run) text next to its box. Then `hidden_text` can report only the words that `covers` matches and that were painted after the cover.

**Acceptance.** The repro reports `"SECRET"`. Existing audit tests still pass, including `later_text_on_the_line_does_not_clear_an_earlier_cover`.

title: Edit text: Ctrl+Z with a paragraph open shows its text in a layout it never had, and doesn't undo the change
author: RiceDee
body:
1. Open a PDF with a mixed-style paragraph (a title over body text, e.g. a typical "Sample PDF" page), Edit a PDF ▸ Edit text (or Add content ▸ Text and click the text).
2. Click into the paragraph and change its formatting from Format text (alignment, bold…). The change applies at once and the paragraph stays open.
3. Press Ctrl+Z.

**Expected:** the formatting change is undone.

**Actual:** the page keeps the change, and the open editor shows the paragraph's text from before the change crammed into the box as laid out after it: text in a state it was never in.

**Cause:** `edit.undo` leaves Ctrl+Z to a focused text field, so it goes to the paragraph editor's own `TextEdit` undo history. That history still holds the text from before the formatting commit (`apply_line_format` refreshes the editor's text), and the box shares one id across paragraphs, so it can even put back another paragraph's text. The document undo never runs, and nothing closes or refreshes an editor when the document is undone.

Related: #2512 (the design for an editing session, which would make a session one undo step) and #3942 (its first, engine-only step). Neither changes this behaviour yet.

Found on 0.12.0 (Windows 11); 0.13.0 has the same code.

Discord: @Rice_Dee

title: [Feature Request] Enhanced Custom Stamps (Text Stamps & Dynamic Metadata)
author: ridhwansalim
body:
**Title:**
[Feature Request] Enhanced Custom Stamps: Text-based stamps and dynamic metadata overlay

---

### Description
Currently, custom stamps primarily support file/image uploads without dynamic author attribution or text generation options. In document review and approval workflows, stamps frequently require sign-off metadata (who approved it and when).

This request proposes two related enhancements to the custom stamp tool:
1. **Text-based stamp generator:** Allow users to type custom stamp text directly (e.g. "APPROVED", "DRAFT", "CONFIDENTIAL") in addition to file uploads.
2. **Dynamic metadata overlay:** Add checkboxes to include dynamic Author/Name, Date, and Time annotations beneath the stamp.

---

### Proposed Solution

#### 1. Custom Text Input
* In the custom stamp creation interface, introduce a choice between **Upload Image** and **Custom Text**.
* For text stamps, provide basic styling (text string, border style, color).

#### 2. Dynamic Metadata Options
Add checkboxes in the custom stamp configuration:
- [ ] **Include Name** (retrieved from PdfCraft user/system identity)
- [ ] **Include Date** (using the system/configured date format)
- [ ] **Include Time** (using the system/configured time format)

#### Output Format:
When selected, append a standardized subtext beneath the main stamp mark:
> `By {Name} at {Time}, {Date}`

*(If only specific boxes are selected, format conditionally—e.g., `By {Name}` or `at {Time}, {Date}`).*

---

### Use Case
* Standardizes quality assurance and legal/review sign-offs without requiring users to generate new static image assets for every reviewer.
* Leverages PdfCraft's local identity and formatting preferences while maintaining clean annotation appearances on documents.

title: Fix for image text editing bug in scanned/OCR content
author: Hanumanpawar95
body:
Hi,

I’ve identified the issue behind the image text edit function not working properly.

Root cause:

The edit flow was prioritizing image-selection hit testing over recognized text hit testing in scanned/document images.
As a result, when text is overlaid on an image (OCR/scanned text), the UI sometimes treats it like an image instead of editable text.
This caused the text editor not to open or the edit to apply incorrectly.
Fix:

Ensure recognized text on images is detected and opened as editable text before the image-selection path takes over.
Keep the textless page background during editing so the OCR text is edited transparently over the image instead of being blocked by the image selection layer.
Add/verify regression coverage for OCR text edits on scanned pages, especially cases where a word is placed over an image background.
This matches the bug pattern in the edit-text UI and should resolve the “image text edit not working properly” issue.

Regards, [Your Name]

title: [Feature Request] Protected View: open PDFs from the internet or e-mail in a restricted mode
author: ravenmyrrdin
body:
**Problem**
PDFs from e-mail attachments and downloads are a common way to deliver malicious content: JavaScript, links to phishing pages, embedded files, form actions that submit data or launch other documents. PdfCraft already guards several of these one by one (sandboxed JavaScript, a prompt for GoToR #2143, Mark-of-the-Web on saved attachments #3990 / #4091), but there is no single safe mode for a document that comes from an untrusted source. Acrobat has this as Protected View, and IT departments in hospitals, government and companies rely on it.

**Proposal**
A **Protected View**: a document from an untrusted source opens read-only, with everything active switched off, until the user chooses to trust it.

*When it applies*
- Windows: the file has Mark-of-the-Web (`Zone.Identifier` with ZoneId 3 or 4)
- macOS: the file has the `com.apple.quarantine` attribute
- Linux: the file has the `user.xdg.origin.url` attribute that browsers set, or lies in the Downloads folder (configurable)
- always, never, or only for marked files: a preference (Preferences › Security)

*What is switched off*
- JavaScript (document, page and field scripts, including on open)
- links and actions that open URLs, launch files or open other documents (GoToR, Launch, URI, SubmitForm, ImportData)
- opening or saving embedded files and attachments
- form filling, commenting, editing and signing
- reading, scrolling, zooming, search, copying text (if the document allows it) and printing keep working

*What the user sees*
- a clear bar above the document: "This file comes from the internet and is opened in Protected View. [Enable editing]"
- Enable editing applies to this document only; it is remembered for the file (by hash), never as a global setting
- a short explanation of which content was blocked, e.g. "This document contains JavaScript and 2 embedded files"

*For managed deployments*
- an administrator setting (MSI property, config file or policy) to force Protected View on and hide the op…

title: Word count's structure exclusions match an MCID in any content stream, not only under the page's own parent tree key
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Follow-up promised in #3740.

## Summary

Word count's structure exclusions (`TextFilter.mcids`, `crates/render/src/text.rs`) are a set of MCIDs per page. `TextFilter::excludes` matches a marked-content sequence's MCID against that set wherever the sequence is drawn: the page's own content, a form XObject with its own `/StructParents`, or an annotation appearance.

MCIDs are local to their content stream (ISO 32000-2 §14.7.5.4). A form with its own `/StructParents` numbers its sequences under its own parent tree key. So a sequence in such a form, or in an annotation appearance, that reuses an MCID the page excludes is dropped from the count. The reverse also happens: an excluded element whose content lives in a form is never matched, because the set only holds the page key's MCIDs.

`word_count.rs` builds the set from the structure tree's per-page exclusions (`excluded.remove(&page)`), keyed by page alone.

## Example

1. Page content has `/P <</MCID 0>> BDC (Body) Tj EMC`.
2. A form with `/StructParents 1` has `/Span <</MCID 0>> BDC (Other) Tj EMC`.
3. The structure tree marks the page's MCID 0 as a `Table`.

With "exclude tables", both "Body" and "Other" are dropped. "Other" isn't in a table.

## Suggested fix

Key the exclusions by parent tree key and MCID, `(key, mcid)`, the way #3740's `structure_marked_content(key, mcid)` keys structure replacements. Match against the key in effect when the sequence begins: the page's `/StructParents`, or the form's own. Content with no key (soft masks, patterns, Type 3 glyphs, forms without `/StructParents`) then matches nothing. The `exclusions` walk in `word_count.rs` would record each MCR's `/Stm` (or the page) to find its key.

This predates #3689 and #3740; neither changes it.

title: Edit text: spaces drawn as TJ gaps in a font without a space glyph read back as one space (and an indent as none)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
Follow-up from #4217 (CodeRabbit's note on `source_show`).

## Summary

Edit text writes replacement text in the paragraph's own font when it can. If that font has no encodable space, such as a TrueType subset without a space glyph or without code 32, `source_show` (`crates/edit/src/text.rs`) draws each space as a positioning-only `TJ` gap of the font's space width. After #4217, each typed space gets its own gap, so the saved line has the typed width.

The *text* does not round-trip, though. `text_lines` (and copy, Find and export) reads a gap between two runs as at most one space, and reads a gap at the start of a line as nothing. So:
- typed `ab  ba   ab` reads back as `ab ba ab`;
- a typed indent is not read back at all.

The next edit then starts from that collapsed text.

## Possible fixes

- **Wrap the run in `/ActualText`.** Put the gap run, or the whole shown string, in a marked-content sequence with `/ActualText` holding the exact text (ISO 32000-2 §14.9.4). Extraction already honours marked-content `/ActualText`. The question is how `editor_text` and re-editing treat a block that contains that sequence.
- **Draw the spaces in another face.** Show the spaces in a face of the same family that has a space glyph.
- **Count gaps in extraction.** Read a gap as several spaces when it is several space widths. This is riskier: it would change extraction for every PDF.

## Test sketch

Use the existing `a_run_of_spaces_in_a_subset_without_a_space_glyph_keeps_its_width` subset. Edit to `"  ab  ba"`, save, reopen, and assert that `text_lines` gives back `"  ab  ba"`, not just the number of `TJ` gaps.

title: Support PDF 2.0 and Modern PDF Standards
author: abhiramh23
body:
Some PDF viewers and applications have compatibility issues with newer documents, including PDF 2.0 files defined by ISO 32000-2. Improving support for modern PDF versions would increase compatibility while clearly distinguishing required goals from optional enhancements.

Must-have compatibility goals

The implementation should:

- Open and render valid PDF 2.0 documents conforming to ISO 32000-2.
- Preserve existing support for PDF 1.x documents.
- Handle common PDF 2.0 structures, metadata, and annotations without crashes, data loss, or silent rendering failures.
- Display clear, actionable warnings when documents contain unsupported or partially supported features.
- Document supported, partially supported, and unsupported PDF versions, standards, and features.
- Identify known limitations and specify whether they affect opening, rendering, editing, accessibility, archival validation, or metadata preservation.
- Preserve document content and metadata to the greatest extent possible when opening, rendering, or editing supported files.

Standards and features in scope

Required scope includes:

- PDF 1.4 through PDF 1.7, subject to the application's existing feature support.
- PDF 2.0 as defined by ISO 32000-2, including the features required to open and render valid documents.
- Common document structures, page content, fonts, images, color spaces, metadata, links, forms, and annotations.
- Graceful handling of malformed, incomplete, or unsupported content, including useful diagnostics where practical.
- Clear reporting for unsupported or partially supported features, including their likely impact on document fidelity.

PDF/A and PDF/UA are not required for the initial milestone unless they are already supported by the underlying PDF library. Where support exists, document the applicable conformance levels, validation behavior, preservation guarantees, and limitations without implying full compliance.

Optional enhancements

After the must-have goals are met, con…

Steps: open the attached repro-devicen12.pdf (849 bytes, generated, no customer data) → the page renders 100% white, zero pixels, no error anywhere. pdfcraft-cli render confirms it (render time ~0 ms = early bail-out).

title: A page can't be named by its position once page labels take its number: (1) is refused in print ranges and ignored in the page box
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `57e531cc` · Windows 11 x64

### What happens

In a Pages to Print range, a token is read as a page label first and only then as a number. That is right for labelled documents, but it leaves no way to name a page by its position once its number belongs to a label. In a document whose front matter is labelled i, ii, iii and whose body starts again at 1, `1` is the fourth page. The first page can only be reached by typing its label `i`, and a range can't say "the first three pages" without knowing how they are labelled.

The same parser reads the page ranges in Combine files, through `print::select_pages`. The page box in the navigation bar resolves what is typed the same way (label, then number) in its own code, so `(1)` there does nothing either.

Save as `repro.py` and run it in an empty folder (Python 3, standard library only). It writes `labels.pdf`: 10 pages labelled i, ii, iii, 1–7, each showing its position and its label.

title: Form scripts: messageBox and app.alert questions always answer OK, so forms can't branch on No
author: EricKaden
body:
## The problem

Form scripts ask the user things through `xfa.host.messageBox(message, title, icon, buttons)` in XFA forms and `app.alert(cMsg, nIcon, nType, cTitle)` in AcroForm forms. In PdfCraft both always return 1 (OK), even for a Yes/No question, where 1 isn't a possible answer. A script that asks "Clear this section?" can never be told No, so forms that branch on the answer always take the OK path.

Split out from this issue, as the triage bot suggested: the title, icon and buttons being ignored is #4293, and only the last message being shown is #4294.

## What the public references specify

The XFA specification (`messageBox`) and the JavaScript for Acrobat API Reference (`app.alert`) give the same values for both:

| | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| icon | Error | Warning | Question | Status | |
| buttons | OK | OK, Cancel | Yes, No | Yes, No, Cancel | |
| returned | | OK | Cancel | No | Yes |

## Proposed design

Scripts run to completion in one go, so they can't pause for a click. I'd propose answering by re-running:

1. A script asks a question that has no answer yet. The engine abandons that action, leaving the document unchanged, since edits are already all-or-nothing. It returns the question to the caller instead.
2. The app shows a dialog with the title, icon and buttons, and the user answers.
3. The app runs the same action again, with the answers given so far. The script receives them in order, so each `messageBox` or `app.alert` call returns its answer. This repeats until a run asks nothing new, and that run is the one applied.

This works wherever a user action runs scripts (button clicks, field changes, validation), in both AcroForm and XFA forms. It needs no threads and no change to how scripts run.

Around it:
- **Headless:** `js_run` and the form-filling tools take an `answers` list, so agents and tests can answer. An unanswered question comes back to the caller as a result, not an error.
- **While opening:** a question asked…

title: Form scripts: messageBox and app.alert ignore their title, icon and buttons
author: EricKaden
body:
## What happens

Form scripts show messages with `xfa.host.messageBox(message, title, icon, buttons)` in XFA forms (from JavaScript, and `$host.messageBox` from FormCalc) and with `app.alert(cMsg, nIcon, nType, cTitle)` in AcroForm forms, which also takes a single object with those keys. PdfCraft reads only the message. The title, the icon and the buttons are dropped before anything reaches the app or the headless tools:

- In the app, a warning looks the same as a status note, and the title the form gave isn't shown.
- `js_run` returns each message as a bare string in `alerts`, so an agent or a test can't tell an error from a note, or a question from a statement.

## Where

- `crates/js/src/xfa.rs`, `message_box`, and `crates/js/src/formcalc.rs` record `XfaEffect::MessageBox(String)`.
- `crates/js/src/lib.rs`, `alert`, reads only its first argument.
- `crates/engine/src/xfa.rs` turns the effect into a plain alert string.

## Expected

The XFA specification (`messageBox`) and the JavaScript for Acrobat API Reference (`app.alert`) give the same values for both:

| | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| icon | Error | Warning | Question | Status |
| buttons | OK | OK, Cancel | Yes, No | Yes, No, Cancel |

The title, icon and buttons travel with the message to the app, which shows the title and icon, and to the tools, which report them. Answering the buttons is #4291.

title: Form scripts: when one action shows several messages, only the last one appears
author: EricKaden
body:
## What happens

When one action shows several messages, the app shows only the last, as a toast. A button whose script calls `app.alert` twice, or an edit whose scripts warn about two fields, loses every message but the last. `js_run` returns them all, so only the app drops them.

## Where

`crates/ui-egui/src/js_ui.rs`, after the requests are handled: `if let Some(a) = out.alerts.last() { self.notify(a.clone()); }`

## Expected

Every message is shown, in the order the scripts raised them. In other viewers each `app.alert` or `messageBox` call opens its own dialog and waits for it to close, so every message is seen.

title: Make document timestamps reachable through a signature field for validator discovery
author: coderabbitai
body:
## Summary

`timestamp_document` in `crates/sign/src/pdf.rs` adds a `/DocTimeStamp` signature dictionary without linking it from a signature field or another catalog-reachable object. Validators that discover signatures through AcroForm fields may therefore miss the document timestamp.

As reported by @alehel during review of #4226, this behavior already exists on `main`. PR #4226 does not change `crates/sign`. The `sign.document-timestamp` entry in `parity/acrobat-features.toml` also describes the timestamp as standalone.

## Required changes

- Store the document timestamp dictionary as the `/V` of a signature field, following the signature-field layout used by `sign`. Ensure that the field is reachable from the catalog through the AcroForm field tree.
- The repository's validator has supported this layout since #621, according to @alehel. Preserve that validation behavior.
- Once the timestamp dictionary is reachable, enable `drop_unlinked: true` for the incremental write in `timestamp_document`. This should omit session-created objects that were later unlinked, without requiring a special cleanup pass before adding the timestamp dictionary.
- Review the `sign.document-timestamp` parity entry and update its description if the new layout requires it.

## Rationale

Enabling `drop_unlinked: true` with the current layout would discard the timestamp dictionary itself. The subsequent `locate` call would fail with `"ByteRange placeholder not found"`.

title: Dynamic XFA forms: a save that only fills in the form keeps its usage rights valid
author: EricKaden
body:
Follow-up to #3401, as suggested in its review: the save change it left out, as its own issue.

## The problem

Some dynamic XFA forms carry usage rights (`/Perms /UR3`), which let a free viewer fill in and save a form it otherwise couldn't save. #3401 removes them when PdfCraft lays the form out, since the layout voids them and a form with void rights opens with every field locked. That fixes the lock, but a form saved by PdfCraft then has no rights at all.
- In the free viewer, people can type into it but can't save what they typed.
- A form that passes through several people, an approval chain for example, stops working for everyone after the first person who uses PdfCraft.

## Why the rights break

Usage rights are a signature over the file's bytes, plus permissions saying what later revisions may change. Filling in the form (`/Form` `/FillIn`) is allowed, but adding pages and fields isn't. PdfCraft writes its layout of the form, the pages and the AcroForm fields, as an appended revision when the form opens (`prepare_open_unguarded`, `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`), and every save includes that revision.

## Proposal

When the file carries usage rights and the only changes are to the form's data (typed values, rows added or removed, values scripts set):
1. Save by appending to the original bytes only what filling in changes: the datasets packet (and the form packet, if presence is saved there), without the layout revision.
2. Keep `/Perms /UR3` untouched.
3. Any other change (pages, comments, signatures, attachments) saves as today, with #3401's removal and its note.

Doing this changes how a laid-out form is saved:
- The saved file no longer carries PdfCraft's layout, so PdfCraft lays it out again on every open, as it does for the original file.
- Viewers that can't read XFA show the placeholder page, as they do for the original file.
- A later step could read the rights' own permissions (`/Form`, `/Annots`, `/Signature`, `/EF`) to keep them valid for the other kin…

title: Render warnings (content truncated, image skipped) reach the CLI only: the viewer and page_render drop them
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What happens

`render_page` returns `RenderedPage.warnings`, but only the CLI shows them.

- **The desktop viewer** uploads the pixels and drops the warnings. A page whose content was cut short, or whose image was too large to decode, looks complete. The missing area is just blank.
- **The `page_render` tool** (MCP and `pdfcraft-cli run`) returns only the PNG. A script or agent can't tell that the picture is incomplete.

There are two warnings today:
- `RenderWarning::ContentTruncated` is on `main`: the nested-paint budget or form depth was reached. #3119 asks for this to be visible.
- `RenderWarning::ImageSkipped` comes with #4235 (#4071): an image is over 2^30 pixels, or its samples would be over 512 MiB, so it isn't drawn.

## What would fix it

- **Viewer:** show a page-level notice when the page has warnings, saying which kind. Something like the existing triangle-alert notices in `canvas.rs` would fit.
- **`page_render`:** return the warnings next to the PNG, for example a text or JSON part that lists them, so a headless caller sees the same thing as the CLI.
- **Tests:** a kittest that shows the notice on a page with an oversized image, and an automation test that checks `page_render` reports the warning.

## Context

CodeRabbit raised this on #4235 (`crates/render/src/raster.rs:223-225`). I left it out of that PR, which fixes the renderer side only: the image is now drawn at a reduced size, and when it's refused the renderer says so.

title: App hangs when Punto Switcher switches keyboard layout in text fields (e.g., "Replace text" comment box)
author: paulbelltower-droid
body:
**Environment:**
    PDFCraft version: 0.13
    OS: Windows 11
    Punto Switcher version: 4.4.4

**Summary:**
PDFCraft freezes ("Not Responding") when Punto Switcher auto-switches the keyboard layout while typing in a text input. Reproducible in the comment box of the "Replace text" dialog.

**Steps to reproduce:**
    Run PDFCraft with Punto Switcher auto-switch enabled.
    Open a PDF → Replace text tool → click into the comment field.
    Type a word that triggers Punto Switcher's layout conversion (e.g., "ghbdtn" → "привет").
    App hangs; must be killed via Task Manager.

Expected: Layout switch handled gracefully, app stays responsive.

**Suspected cause:**
Likely a re-entrancy deadlock on the keyboard-layout cache lock (known issue in winit-based Rust apps on Windows). The app holds a Mutex for the layout cache during key processing; Punto Switcher's global hook (pshook64.dll) synchronously dispatches WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE, whose handler tries to re-acquire the same non-reentrant mutex → self-deadlock. Same pattern as the Warp terminal freeze (fixed in their winit fork).

**Suggested fixes:**
    Don't hold the layout-cache lock across message dispatch (use ReentrantMutex, or release before processing).
    Handle WM_INPUTLANGCHANGE without re-acquiring the lock (defer update / atomic fast path).
    Check for an upstream winit fix and bump the dependency.

Workaround (for users):: add PDFCraft.exe to Punto Switcher's exclusion list.

title: Comments: an annotation in an /RT /Group shows as a reply, with its own author, text and colour (the reply type /RT is never read)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** built from `main` @ `a2ec27b4` · Windows 11 x64

### What happens

ISO 32000-2 lets a set of annotations act as one: a primary, and subordinates that point at it with `/IRT` and say `/RT /Group`. The group is one comment. Its author, text, colour and dates are the primary's, and whatever a subordinate carries for them is to be ignored.

PdfCraft never reads `/RT`. It threads every `/IRT` annotation as a reply. A group subordinate therefore shows up in the Comments panel and in `comment_list` as a reply to its primary, with its own author, text and colour, and it can't be clicked on the page at all (the page only hit-tests annotations without `/IRT`).

PdfCraft writes `/RT /Group` itself, in Replace Text (`crates/annot/src/lib.rs`, `add_text_replacement`). It makes the strikeout the primary, with empty `/Contents`, and the caret the subordinate, holding the replacement. A reader that follows §12.5.6.2 ignores the caret's text and lists the comment with no replacement. PdfCraft itself lists the caret as a reply to an empty strikeout.

body:

### What happens

Many files carry FreeText (text box) and Redact annotations without an `/AP` appearance stream, and PdfCraft draws them from their dictionaries for display (`with_missing_appearances`). Four things in those drawings don't follow the dictionary:

title: A non-embedded TrueType font such as Arial,Bold is drawn as a heavy fixed-pitch face: the stand-in's glyphs are stretched to every /Widths advance, so i and l become solid blocks
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** pdfcraft-cli built from `main` @ `a047c6ba` · code read at `a047c6ba` · Windows 11 x64

### What happens

A simple font that the document names but doesn't embed is drawn with a standard-font stand-in. For `/BaseFont /Arial,Bold` that stand-in is Helvetica-Bold, which is the right family. title: A non-embedded CID font's fallback request never carries its style: the font descriptor is read from the Type 0 dictionary, which has none, so every request asks for a regular sans-serif face
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** code read on `main` @ `0b670caf` · Windows 11 x64

### What happens

When a Type 0 font's CIDFont isn't embedded, the renderer asks the font resolver for a substitute with a `FallbackFontQuery`. That query's style fields (`is_serif`, `is_italic`, `is_small_cap`, `font_weight`, `font_family`, `font_stretch`) are read from a `/FontDescriptor` in the dictionary the query is built from. For a CID font that dictionary is the Type 0 font, which has no font descriptor. The descriptor belongs to the descendant CIDFont.

So for every non-embedded CID font the request says: not serif, not italic, weight 400. A Song, Ming, Mincho or Myeongjo font asks for the same face as a Hei or Gothic one, and `/FontWeight 700` is never seen.

### Where

**[code]** At `0b670caf`:
- `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/cid.rs:89`: `FallbackFontQuery::new(dict)`, where `dict` is the Type 0 font dictionary.
- `vendor/hayro-interpret/src/font/mod.rs:576`: `FallbackFontQuery::new` reads `dict.get::<Dict>(FONT_DESC)`, which is always absent on a Type 0 font.
- The descendant's descriptor has already been read a few lines earlier (`cid.rs:71`, `font_descriptor`). The standard-font choice, `select_standard_font(dict, &font_descriptor)`, already uses it. Only the fallback request misses it.
- Simple fonts are not affected: their descriptor sits on the font dictionary itself.

### ISO basis

ISO 32000-2:
- §9.7.6.1, Table 119 (Type 0 font dictionary) lists `Type`, `Subtype`, `BaseFont`, `Encoding`, `DescendantFonts` and `ToUnicode`, and no `FontDescriptor`.
- §9.7.4.1, Table 115 (CIDFont dictionary): `FontDescriptor` is "(Required; shall be an indirect reference) A font descriptor describing the CIDFont's default metrics other than its glyph widths".
- §9.8.1, Table 120: `FontWeight`, `FontFamily`, `FontStretch` and `Flags`; §9.8.2, Table 121: Serif is bit 2 and Italic bit 7.

### Effect

- **On `main` alone, almost nothing visible.** The only CJK substitute on `main` is `japanese_fallback` …

body:

### What happens

| A | RGB 8-bit | gradient | matches |
| B | Indexed, 4 colours, full table | four colours | matches |
| C | ImageMask, default Decode | magenta where 0 | matches |
| D | ImageMask, `/Decode [1 0]` | inverted | matches |
| E | RGB, `/Decode [1 0 1 0 1 0]` | inverted gradient | matches |
| F | colour-key `/Mask [0 0 0 0 0 0]` | black samples transparent | matches |

title: A luminosity soft mask in a DeviceCMYK group lets about an eighth of the masked paint through where the mask is 100% K
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** `main` @ c894928e · Windows 11 x64

## What happens

A luminosity soft mask whose transparency group is composited in `/DeviceCMYK` does not mask fully where the group paints 100% K. In the attached fixture the mask's group paints its left half `0 0 0 1 k` and its right half `0 0 0 0 k`, and a red rectangle is then filled under the mask over a grey backdrop. The right half is red as it should be, but the left half, which should show only the backdrop, comes out light pink: the red leaks through at about 12.5%.

The same mask written in a `/DeviceGray` group (`0 g` / `1 g`) or a `/DeviceRGB` group (`0 0 0 rg` / `1 1 1 rg`) masks fully.

The cause is how the mask's luminosity is computed. The mask group is drawn into an RGB buffer and the luminance is read from that. A `/DeviceCMYK` colour reaches the buffer through the CMYK display profile, where 100% K is a dark grey rather than black, so its luminosity comes out at about 0.125 instead of 0. A `/BC` backdrop colour in the group's DeviceCMYK space goes the same way.

## ISO basis

- ISO 32000-2 §11.5.3, *Deriving a soft mask from group luminosity*: the group's colour "shall then be converted to luminosity in one of the following ways, depending on the group's colour space". For device colour spaces: "convert the colour to DeviceGray by implementation-defined means and use the resulting gray value as the luminosity, with no compensation for gamma or other colour calibration." Its Example 2 gives the DeviceCMYK formula `Y = 1 − min(1, 0.3 × C + 0.59 × M + 0.11 × Y + K)`.
- ISO 32000-2 §10.4.2.3, *Conversion between DeviceGray and DeviceCMYK*: "the contributions of all components shall be taken into account: gray = 1.0 − min(1.0, 0.3 × cyan + 0.59 × magenta + 0.11 × yellow + black)".
- Table 142 (entries in a soft-mask dictionary), `/BC`: the backdrop colour is given in the group's colour space; its default, the space's initial value, represents black.

So 100% K is luminosity 0 (fully masked), 0% is 1 (ful…

title: Turned view (View ▸ Rotate view 90°/270°): seven tools read the zoom off the wrong side of the page, so typed text and handles are drawn at the wrong size
author: Lombardi2003
body:
## What happens

With the view turned a quarter (View ▸ Rotate view, 90° or 270°), several tools size what they draw by a zoom computed as `xf.rect.width() / xf.pw`. When the view is turned, the page's screen rectangle has its sides swapped: its width is the page's *height* on screen, so this "zoom" is off by the page's height-over-width (×1.41 on a portrait A4, ×0.71 on a landscape one).

Affected, all in `crates/ui-egui/src`:
- `fill_sign.rs`: the Fill & Sign type box draws the text you type larger (or smaller) than the text it places;
- `forms_ui.rs`: the same for typing into a form field;
- `content_ui.rs`: the same for the Add text editor;
- `measure_ui.rs`: the snapping distance;
- `prepare.rs`, `calc_order_ui.rs`, `field_table_ui.rs`: field labels, handles and overlays.

`PageXform::zoom()` (added in #3749 for the eraser) already reads the zoom off the side the page's width is on.

## Steps

1. Open a portrait page, View ▸ Rotate view 90°.
2. Fill & Sign ▸ Add text, click the page and type.
3. The text in the box is drawn about 41% larger than the text placed when you confirm.

I have a fix with a regression test ready and will open a PR for it.

title: Type 3 text in rendering mode 7 (`7 Tr`) is painted in the fill colour instead of not being rendered
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.13.0, `main` at c894928e (2026-10-24), Windows 11; `pdfcraft-cli render`.

## What happens

Text in a Type 3 font shown with text rendering mode 7 ("add text to path for clipping") is painted. Its glyphs come out filled in the current fill colour, which is black by default. When a fill follows the text object, as clip-mode text usually has, the glyphs show wherever that fill doesn't cover them. In the fixture below that is a black bar beside the red box.

## The basis

ISO 32000-2 §9.3.6 says how the rendering modes apply to a Type 3 font. Table 104 is followed by:

> Where text is drawn using a Type 3 font:
> • if text rendering mode is set to a value of 3 or 7, the text shall not be rendered.
> • if text rendering mode is set to a value other than 3 or 7, the text shall be rendered using the glyph descriptions in the Type 3 font.
> • If text rendering mode is set to a value of 4, 5, 6 or 7, nothing shall be added to the clipping path.

The same clause says that when "the only glyphs shown have no outlines … no clipping shall occur". A text object showing only Type 3 glyphs in mode 7 should therefore leave no mark and set no clip.

The renderer draws every Type 3 mode other than 3 as a fill (vendored hayro-interpret patch 42, `show_glyph`). That is right for 0, 1, 2 and 4 to 6. For mode 7 it paints glyphs that should not be rendered. Modes 4 to 7 already add nothing to the clip, which is correct, but only because `clip_glyph` logs "not implemented" for Type 3 glyphs instead of following the rule on purpose.

## Steps

1. Make a page with a Type 3 font `/TA` (`/FontMatrix [0.001 0 0 0.001 0 0]`) whose glyph `A` is `1000 0 100 0 900 800 d1 100 0 800 800 re f` (a square) and `B` is `1000 0 0 0 1000 1000 d1 0 0 m 1000 0 l 500 1000 l f` (a triangle).
2. Show it in mode 7 and then fill a box that ends inside the last glyph:

title: Renderer: a zero-height or zero-width rectangle used as a clip hides everything, and as a fill it half-covers two rows (ISO 32000-2 §10.7.4)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.13.0, `main` at c894928e (Windows 11).

## What happens

A rectangle with no height (or no width) encloses no area. PdfCraft treats it as covering no pixels:

- **As a clip** (`10 10 100 0 re W n`), it hides everything painted after it. A red fill of the whole box after that clip leaves the page blank.
- **As a fill** (`10 10 100 0 re f`), it is drawn as a thin stroke centred on the line. When the line falls on a pixel boundary, the stroke covers half of two rows, so the result is a faint two-pixel line instead of one solid pixel row. The fill and the clip of the same rectangle mark different pixels.

The same happens for a zero-width rectangle (`10 10 0 100 re`), and for a zero-height rectangle inside a rotated CTM.

## ISO basis

ISO 32000-2:2020, §10.7.4 "Scan conversion rules":

- A shape is scan-converted by "painting any pixel whose half-open square region intersects the shape, no matter how small the intersection is".
- EXAMPLE: "A zero-width or zero-height rectangle paints a line 1 pixel wide."
- "For clipping, the clipping region consists of the set of pixels that would be included by a fill operation."

§8.5.4 (clipping path operators) applies that clipping region to everything painted later. So a zero-height clip followed by a fill should paint a one-pixel line of the fill colour, the same pixels that filling the zero-height rectangle would paint.

## Steps

1. Make a one-page PDF (synthetic) whose content stream is:
   ```
   q 1 0 0 1 40 410 cm 10 10 100 0 re W n 1 0 0 rg 0 0 120 120 re f Q
   q 1 0 0 1 200 410 cm 1 0 0 rg 10 10 100 0 re f Q
   q 1 0 0 1 360 410 cm 10 10 0 100 re W n 1 0 0 rg 0 0 120 120 re f Q
   q 0.866 0.5 -0.5 0.866 300 200 cm 0 0 100 0 re W n 1 0 0 rg -50 -50 200 200 re f Q

2. `pdfcraft-cli render file.pdf --out x.png --dpi 110`

- The zero-width clip shows a one-pixel red column.

title: A Separation colour whose colourant is /All draws through its tint transform (light cyan) instead of a neutral gray
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.13.0 (`main` at c894928e), `pdfcraft-cli render`

## What happens

A Separation colour space whose colourant name is the special name `/All` is drawn through its alternate space and tint transform, as if `All` were an ordinary spot colourant. With

```
[/Separation /All /DeviceCMYK << /FunctionType 2 /Domain [0 1] /C0 [0 0 0 0] /C1 [1 0 0 0] /N 1 >>]
```

`0.5 scn` and a fill paint light cyan, the tint transform's colour. This is the space registration marks are drawn in, so crop and registration targets come out in whatever colour the writer's tint transform happens to give instead of the neutral "every ink" colour they stand for.

The vendored colour-space code says as much: a comment in `Separation::new` (`vendor/hayro-interpret/src/color.rs`) notes that `All` is ignored.

## ISO basis

ISO 32000-2 §8.6.6.4 (Separation colour spaces):

> The special colourant name All shall refer collectively to all colourants available on an output device … painting operators shall apply tint values to all available colourants at once. When outputting to an additive device, such as a computer monitor, the subtractive tint values of the All colourant shall be complemented by subtracting from 1 before applying to all available colourants.

So on screen (and in an RGB raster) a tint t paints 1 − t on each of R, G and B: tint 0 white, 0.5 a 50% gray, 1 black, whatever the alternate space and tint transform say. The same clause has `/None` paint nothing, which PdfCraft already does.

## Steps

1. Make a page that fills a box after `/CS0 cs 0.5 scn`, with `/CS0` the space above (a synthetic file built this way is attached as `colour.pdf`, box B).

- **Actual:** light cyan, the tint transform's colour (RGB 109, 206, 246 in a synthetic render at 72 dpi).

title: With /NeedAppearances, check boxes and radio buttons show the file's appearance instead of their /MK caption symbol
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.13.0 (main at b75cbd92, 2026-10-24), Windows 11

## What happens

A form whose interactive form dictionary sets `/NeedAppearances true` asks the viewer to construct the appearances of its widgets. PdfCraft already does this for text and choice fields (#3470), but check boxes and radio buttons keep the appearance streams the file carries.

In the synthetic test form, the check box field `J_check` has two widgets with `/MK << /BC [0 0 0] /CA (4) >>` (ZapfDingbats `4`, a check mark) and an `/AP /N` whose `/Yes` state is a filled square. When the box is checked, PdfCraft shows the filled square. Most other readers show a check mark, built from `/MK /CA` because the form sets `/NeedAppearances`. A copy saved by PdfCraft (still `/NeedAppearances true`) behaves the same way.

## ISO basis

- ISO 32000-2 §12.7.3, Table 224, `NeedAppearances`: "A flag specifying whether to construct appearance streams and appearance dictionaries for all widget annotations in the document". The key is deprecated in PDF 2.0 (appearance streams are required from PDF 2.0 on), but PDF 1.x forms still use it.
- Table 192, `/MK /CA`: "The widget annotation's normal caption, which shall be displayed when it is not interacting with the user". Unlike the other push-button entries, `CA` may be used with any type of button field, including check boxes.
- §12.7.5.2.3 (check boxes): the state is selected by `/AS` (or `/V`), and the standard example draws the on state as ZapfDingbats `(4) Tj`.

## Steps

1. Generate a form with `/NeedAppearances true` and a check box widget with `/MK << /BC [0 0 0] /CA (4) >>` and `/AP << /N << /Yes <filled square> /Off <empty box> >> >>`.
2. Open it in PdfCraft and check the box.
3. Save it and reopen the saved copy.

## Expected / Actual

- **Expected:** the checked box shows a check mark (the `/MK /CA` ZapfDingbats character, sized to the box, in the `/DA` colour, inside the `/BC` border and over the `/BG` background); an unchecked one shows its …

title: The € in a standard font without /Widths is drawn wider than its advance and overlaps the next glyph ("€5", "€€", "a€b" collide)
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft 0.13.0, `main` at b75cbd92 (Windows 11), `pdfcraft-cli render`.

## What happens

A page that shows the Euro sign in one of the standard 14 fonts, named without embedding and without `/Widths`, draws the € so wide that the glyph after it runs into it. In Helvetica, "€5" reads as one blob, "€€" as a single doubled shape, and the € of "a€b" touches the b. Times-Roman and Times-Bold are worse. The text is placed at the right advances (556 units in Helvetica, 500 in Times); it is the € itself that is drawn too wide, up to 722 units against an advance of 500.

The same text written by PdfCraft's own text editing ("€5" in Helvetica) shows the problem when PdfCraft reopens the file.

## ISO basis

- ISO 32000-2 §9.6.2.2: for the standard 14 fonts, `FirstChar`, `LastChar`, `Widths` and `FontDescriptor` were optional in PDF 1.0 to 1.7, and "PDF processors supporting PDF 1.0 to PDF 1.7 files shall have these fonts, or their font metrics and suitable substitution fonts, available." The substitute has to fit the standard font's metrics.
- Annex D, Table D.2: the Euro is WinAnsiEncoding code 200 (octal), that is 128.
- §9.2.4: each glyph's advance moves the next one on, so a glyph wider than its advance overlaps its neighbour.

## Steps

1. Make a one-page PDF with the font `<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica /Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding >>` (no `/Widths`) and the content `BT /F1 48 Tf 20 60 Td (\2005 \200\200 a\200b) Tj ET`.
2. `pdfcraft-cli render euro.pdf --page 1 --out x.png --dpi 150`.
3. Do the same with `/BaseFont /Times-Roman` and `/Times-Bold`.

## Expected

Each € fits within its advance: 556/1000 em in the Helvetica family, 500/1000 in Times, 600/1000 in Courier. "€5", "€€" and "a€b" read as separate glyphs with normal spacing.

## Actual

The € is drawn about 0.62 em wide in Helvetica (advance 0.556) and 0.65 em in Times-Roman (advance 0.5). It overlaps the 5, the second €, and the b.

The advances are right…

title: Find misses "office" when the page draws an fi ligature, and "example" when the word is divided by a hyphen at a line end
author: mtlcl410
body:
**Version:** PdfCraft `main` at `c894928e` (0.13.0), Windows 11, `pdfcraft-cli run` with `text_find` (Find in the app uses the same search).

### What happens

On the 14-row text copy page from #4467 (the generator is there, `copy.pdf`), Find gives:

| Query | What the page has | PdfCraft | Other readers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `office` | row 01: `of` + glyph named `/fi` + `ce` (U+FB01) | not found | found by 5 of 5 |
| `example` | row 06: `exam-` at a line end, `ple` on the next line | not found | found by 4 of 5 |
| `cafe` | row 09: `café` | not found | found by 3 of 5 |
| `first second` | row 08: two words on one baseline, drawn out of order | not found | found by 4 of 5 |
| `split words` | row 14: two words placed by `Td` | found | found by 5 of 5 |

- **Ligatures.** The page text holds the ligature character U+FB01, and the query is compared character by character, so `office` never meets `o`,`f`,`ﬁ`,`c`,`e`. The same happens with a ToUnicode map or `/ActualText` that gives U+FB00–U+FB06.
- **Divided words.** A line break counts as a space, so the text reads `exam- ple`. `example` doesn't match, and neither does `exam-ple`.
- **`cafe`.** Accent-insensitive Find is #3460, with an open pull request (#3889). It is listed here only for completeness.
- **`first second`.** The two words come out on separate lines (#4467), and that issue's fix makes them match.

### Basis

- **Ligatures.** ISO 32000-2 §9.10.3 maps ligature glyphs to the letters they stand for: "a Unicode scalar value for each character in the ligature: LATIN SMALL LETTER F (U+0066) LATIN SMALL LETTER I (U+0069) for f i". A search for the word should find it whether the page gives the letters or the ligature character. All 5 other readers do.
- **Divided words.** ISO 32000-2 §14.8.2.3 has a writer mark the hyphen that only divides a word at a line end as a soft hyphen (U+00AD), "distinct from an ordinary hard hyphen". Most PDFs don't, though, and a U+002D at a line end between two letters is usually such…

title: Relative links ignore the document's base URI, and links are active over their whole /Rect even when /QuadPoints say otherwise
author: mtlcl410
body:
PdfCraft version: 0.13.0 (main at c894928e), Windows 11.

## What happens

Two problems with link annotations that a document describes correctly:

1. **A relative URI action is refused.** A link with `/A << /S /URI /URI (page.html) >>` in a document whose catalog has `/URI << /Base (https://example.com/base/) >>` shows:
   "A link in this document tried to open an address PdfCraft won't open: the address isn't a complete web or email address. Only web (http, https) and email (mailto) links open from documents."
   The base is never read, so the relative address is checked as written.
2. **A link is active outside its `/QuadPoints`.** A link whose `/Rect` covers a whole line but whose `/QuadPoints` cover only the first word opens on a click on any word of the line. The pointer also turns into the link hand over the whole `/Rect`.

## ISO basis

- ISO 32000-2 §12.6.4.8, Table 211 (entry in a URI dictionary): `Base` is "the base URI that shall be used in resolving relative URI references. URI actions within the document may specify URIs in partial form, to be interpreted relative to this base address."

The activation region is `Rect` only when the entry "is not present, or the PDF processor does not recognise it, or if any coordinates in the QuadPoints array lie outside the region specified by Rect".

title: Forms: importing XFDF data doesn't clear a field that is empty in the data
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Export Data as XFDF writes an empty text field as `<field name="Name"></field>`, with no `<value>`, and the XFDF import skips a field that has no value. So importing the data into a filled copy of the form leaves the old text in place, and if every field in the file is empty the import fails with "nothing in the file matches this document". The same data exported as FDF (`/V ()`) or XML clears the field.

Repro: a form with an empty text field `Name`, Export Data as XFDF, type "Ada" into `Name`, Import Data from that file. `Name` still says "Ada"; it should be empty.

Cause: `walk_xfdf` only records fields that have `<value>` children.

title: Forms: a multi-select list choice containing ", " can't be imported back from XML, CSV or text
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Export Data as XML, CSV or text writes a multi-select list's choices in one cell, joined by ", ". On import the cell is split at every ", " unless the whole cell is one option. A choice that holds ", " itself, like "Smith, John", gets cut into pieces that match no option, and the whole field is rejected, so the form's own exported data can't be imported back.

Repro: a multi-select list with options "Smith, John", "Doe, Jane" and "Other", select the first two, Export Data as XML (the cell reads `Smith, John, Doe, Jane`), then Import Data from that file. The list comes back empty and the field is reported as rejected; both choices should be selected again.

Cause: `apply_values` splits the cell with `split(", ")` instead of matching it against the field's options.

title: Editing a justified paragraph drops spaces typed at the start or end of its stretched rows (an indent is lost)
author: Jayesh-Prajapati9
body:
## What happens

When you edit a **justified** paragraph, spaces typed at the start or end of a row that isn't the last one are dropped on save. So an indent typed on the first row is lost.

| Draft (Helvetica, width 300) | Left-aligned rows | Justified rows |
|---|---|---|
| `"    aaa bbb ccc\nddd eee"` | `"    aaa bbb ccc"`, `"ddd eee"` | `"aaa bbb ccc"`, `"ddd eee"` |

mercuryVM found this in review of #4217. That PR keeps every typed space in left-, centre- and right-aligned rows and in the last row of a justified paragraph. A stretched justified row keeps `main`'s behaviour on purpose, and its output is byte-identical to `main`.

## Why #4217 doesn't do it

`Tw` (word spacing) applies to every space in a `Tj`, so leading and trailing spaces inside the stretched run would also be stretched. The row would then end short of the margin, or past it.

Two approaches were tried while preparing #4217:
1. **`dx = -leading × Tw` on the row origin.** This put a re-edited row off the page.
2. **The indent as its own run, before the stretched words.** After save and reopen, that line carried `0 Tw`. The next styled-path edit (`rewrite_styled_block`) calibrated it to `200 Tz` and split the paragraph.

## A possible fix

- Move the row's start by the indent's width with `Td`, or a `TJ` adjustment, and draw only the trimmed words with `Tw`.
- Make the reopened row calibrate back to `100 Tz`. `rewrite_styled_block` would need to treat a leading offset as an indent and not as scaling.
- Decide what text extraction should give for the indent. It would be a positional gap and not U+0020, so a later edit would need to read it back as spaces for the indent to survive a second edit.

## Tests it would need

- A justified row with an indent keeps it after save and reopen, and still ends at the margin.
- Save, reopen and re-edit through the styled path: all rows `100 Tz`, one block, indent kept.

title: Clicking one of two radio buttons that share an on state turns both on, though RadiosInUnison is clear
author: mtlcl410
body:
## What happens

In a radio group whose buttons share an on state (three buttons with the on states `Yes`, `Yes`, `No`) and whose RadiosInUnison flag is clear, clicking the first `Yes` button turns on **both** `Yes` buttons. Clicking the second `Yes` then does nothing, so it can never be chosen on its own.

## What ISO 32000-2 says

- Table 229, RadiosInUnison: "If clear, the buttons are mutually exclusive (the same behaviour as HTML radio buttons)."
- §12.7.5.2.3, after EXAMPLE 2: "For radio buttons, the same behaviour shall occur only if the RadiosInUnison flag is set. If it is not set, at most one radio button in a field shall be set at a time."
- §12.7.5.2.4: where `/V` and `/AS` differ, "the value of the AS key shall be used". The two `Yes` buttons share `/V /Yes`, and only their `/AS` tells them apart.

## Expected

- RadiosInUnison clear: only the clicked button gets its on state in `/AS`. The other `Yes` button gets `/Off`. `/V` is `/Yes`.
- RadiosInUnison set: both `Yes` buttons turn on together (as today).
- NoToggleToOff clear: clicking the selected button deselects it (as today). NoToggleToOff set: it stays selected.

title: Forms: importing data into same-named check boxes always turns on the first box
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Check boxes that share one name but have different on states (`/A`, `/B`; Acrobat's "same name, different export values" check boxes) are one field, and its `/V` names the box that's on. Importing form data (XFDF, FDF or XML) whose value is `B` checks the first box (`A`) instead of the second.

Repro: open a form where such a field has its second box checked (e.g. saved from Acrobat), Export Data, uncheck it, Import Data from that file. The first box is checked; the second one should be.

Cause: the import reduces a check-box value to on/off (`FieldValue::Check(true)`), and `write_value` in forms always turns on the first widget's state, even for a text value that names another box's state.

title: Comments: importing an FDF comment with a pop-up copies the pop-up into the comment as a direct dictionary
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
When an FDF file has a comment with a pop-up (a Text annotation with `/Popup 3 0 R`, and the Popup annotation `3 0 R` with `/Parent` back to it), Import copies the whole pop-up dictionary into the comment's `/Popup` as a direct value, with its `/Parent` set to null, and no pop-up annotation ends up on the page. ISO 32000-2 Table 172 says `/Popup` shall be an indirect reference to a pop-up annotation, so the saved PDF carries it as a direct dictionary where the standard requires a reference, and the pop-up's position and open state are lost. Importing the same comment from XFDF places a real pop-up on the page.

Repro: import an FDF whose Text annotation has `/Popup n 0 R` pointing at a Popup annotation with `/Parent`, then look at the comment's `/Popup` and the page's `/Annots`.

Cause: `import_fdf` resolves every reference in the comment; it takes `/IRT` out first, but not `/Popup`.

title: A check box whose kids have different on states can only ever tick its first kid

So the field's value is the on state of the kid that is on.

title: [Bug Report] [PdfCraft] Visual glitches when scrolling/moving mouse on external monitor (Fixed with OpenGL)

body:
### Description

Problem:
Opening a PDF on the laptop screen works fine, but moving the window to an external monitor causes severe visual glitches whenever I move the mouse or scroll the page.

Solution / Workaround:
Launching the application with the OpenGL renderer via terminal completely resolved the glitches:
set PDFCRAFT_RENDERER=gl && "C:\Program Files\PdfCraft\pdfcraft.exe"
(Credit to Rice_Dee for the workaround)

System Details:
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 Laptop GPU 6GB
- Monitor 1 (Laptop): 1920x1080 @ 144Hz, Scaling: 175%
- Monitor 2 (External): 1920x1080 @ 143.98Hz, Scaling: 175%

### Operating system and version

Windows 11 (26H2, Build 26300.9711)
